Onɛ niŋ ala, asɛɛ ka ba kʋʋ o. Linɛ na faanf anɛ Na'ab la na ʋk o sanlima dansaar la tiel ka fʋ gban'e. Amaa dabpistan' linɛ gaad la wʋsa, Na'ab la pʋ buolim ka m kpɛn' o san'anɛ.”
12Ban da nɔk Esta labaar la yɛl Modekaya la, 13Modekaya da lɛbis ye ba kem yɛl o ye, “Da tɛn'ɛs ye fʋn bɛ na'ayin la zug, ba na kʋ Jew dim la wʋsa ka fʋn pɔnsɛ. 14Nannanna fʋ ya'a sin, Jew dim la yɔlisim tun'e yi zin'isi'a na, amaa fʋn nɛ fʋ saam yidim na san'am. Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ mi' linɛ zugʋ kɛ ka fʋ bɛ na'am zin'igin saŋa kaŋa?”
15Ka Esta lɛbis labaar ye ba kem yɛl Modekaya ye, 16“Kem la'as Jew dim banɛ bɛ Susa teŋin wʋsa ka ya lɔ nɔɔri sɔsi m yɛla. Da di bɛɛ nu si'el yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ nintaŋ wʋsa daba atan'. Man nɛ m zak biis la mɛ na lɔ nɔɔr nɛ ya. Ti ya'a niŋ ala naae, m na keŋ Na'ab la san'an la'an nɛ lin pʋ dɔl suor la. Ka m ya'a lɛn kpi li naanɛ.”
17Modekaya da keŋ niŋ wʋʋ Esta pa'al o si'em la.

english_text:
Esther Invites the King and Haman to a Dinner
1Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway. 2He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her.
When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter, 3the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
4Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
5The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.”
The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner, 6and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
7-8Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.”
Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
9Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry, 10but he did not say a thing.
When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh 11and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him. 12Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow. 13But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
14Haman's wife and friends said to him, “Have a gallows built about 22 meters high, and tomorrow morning ask the king to hang Mordecai there. Then later, you can have dinner with the king and enjoy yourself.”
This seemed like a good idea to Haman, and he had the gallows built.
translation_text:
Esta sɔs na'ab la sʋŋir
1Daba atan' la nya'aŋ, Esta da yɛɛ o na'am fuugʋ kpɛn' na'ayir la pʋʋgʋ zi'en Na'ab la zɔŋ za'anɔɔr tuon. Na'ab la da zin' nɛ o na'am gbauŋ zug dɔɔg la pʋʋgin ka o nindaa kpa' zɔŋ la za'anɔɔr la. 2On da nyɛ Esta ka o zi'e zakin la, Na'ab la ya'am da kpɛn' o ka o ziank o sanlima dansaar linɛ ka o zanl la tiel o san'an na. Ka Esta paae o tuonnɛ si'isi li zug la.
3Na'ab la da bu'os ye, “Esta, yɛlim fʋn bɔɔd si'el? Hali baa li zem nɛ m sʋ'ʋlim la pʋsʋkɔ, m na tisif.” 4Ka Esta lɛbis o ye, “Naa, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a na siakin, fʋn nɛ Haman naan kɛɛn na di dikanɛ ka m maal ye m tisif la.” 5Ka Na'ab la yɛl ye, “Mɔri Haman tɔ'ɔtɔ na ka ti niŋ Esta bɔɔd si'el la.”
Dinzug Na'ab la nɛ Haman da keŋ ye ba di dikanɛ ka Esta maal la. 6Ban da bɛɛ ani nuud daam la, ka Na'ab la maligim yɛl Esta ye, “Yʋ'ʋn yɛlimim fʋn bɔɔd ye m maal si'eli tisif, ka m na maal. Bɔ kimm ka fʋ bɔɔda? Hali baa fʋn bɔɔd si'el la ya'a zem nɛ m sʋ'ʋlim la pʋsʋk m na tisif.” 7Esta da lɛbis ye, “M sɔsʋg nɛ man bɔɔd si'el la anɛ anwa: 8Naa, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a sid nɔŋim yɛla ka mɛ sid na maal man bɔɔd si'eli tisim, fʋn nɛ Haman kem bɛog na di dikanɛ ka m ye m maali tisi ya la. Ka m saa na gandig fʋn bu'osid man bɔɔd si'el la yɛla.”
Haman sʋnf duoe nɛ Modekaya
9Haman da yina ka o sʋnf ma'ae nɛ hali. Amaa on da nyɛ Modekaya ka o zi'e Na'ab la za'anɔɔrin ka pʋ duoe zi'en ka kirid nɛ dabiem on Haman tuon la, o sʋnf da duoe nɛ Modekaya hali pamm. 10La'an nɛ wala, Haman da nyaŋi gban'e o mɛŋ ka yii kul.
Ka buol o zuanamɛ la'as nɛ o pu'a onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Zeres la, 11ka nwɛ'ɛd nyɔ'ɔg nɛ on mɔr arezak si'em nɛ o biisi zem si'em nɛ Na'ab la na'asid o si'em ka tis o kpɛuŋʋ gaad o taaba banɛ wʋsa bɛ na'ayin la. 12Haman da lɛn yɛli ba ye, “Ka' lin ma'aanɛ, man ma'aa ka Na'ab pu'a Esta buoli paas Na'ab la zug ka ti keŋ di dikanɛ ka o maali tis Na'ab la, ka lɛm buol man nɛ Na'ab la bɛog ya'as. 13Amaa nɛ' wʋsa pʋ niŋim malisim, man nyɛ ka Modekaya zin' Na'ab la za'anɔɔr tuon la.” 14Ka o pu'a nɛ o zuanam la wʋsa yɛl o ye, “Kɛl ka ba sɛ dabanɛ wa'am hali ka ba mɔri yun nidibi kʋʋd la, ka bɛog bɛkɛung ka fʋ saa sɔs Na'ab la ka o kɛ ka ba yul Modekaya ani n kʋʋ o. Ka fʋ nyaan dɔl Na'ab la keŋ di diib la ka li malisif.” Sa'al kaŋa da kpɛn' o kpakin ka o kɛ ka ba sɛ daad la.

english_text:
The King Honors Mordecai
1That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king. 2 When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king, 3the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?”
“Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
4About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
5The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.”
“Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
6When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?”
Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor. 7So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man, 8get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress. 9Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
10The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
11Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
12Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame. 13Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.” 14They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_text:
Modekaya paam wɔ'ɔgir
1Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la Na'ab la da pʋ gbisɛ, ka kɛ ka ba nɔk gbambanɛ ka ba sɔbid yɛla digin ka ba buon Na'anam Tiɛnr Gbana la, ye ba mɔr na karim ka o wʋm. 2Gbana la pʋʋgin ba da karim nyɛ Modekaya da yis na'ayir kpɛɛmnam ayi' gbin si'em. Ba da anɛ Bigitana nɛ Teris banɛ da gur za'anɔɔr la ka gban'e ye ba kʋ Na'ab Zeesis la. 3Ka Na'ab la bu'os ye, “Modekaya da niŋ anwana la, yɔɔd bɛɛ girimbɔ ka ba tis o?” Ka o na'ayikpɛm la lɛbis ye, “Ba da pʋ maal si'eli tis oo.” 4Ka Na'ab la bu'os ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ bɛ zakin la?” Saŋkan mɛn ka Haman mɛ kpɛn' ye o yɛl Na'ab la ka o kɛ ka ba yul Modekaya dawa'ama banɛ ka o ba' la zugʋ kʋʋ o. 5Na'ab nidib la da lɛbis o ye, “Li anɛ Haman n zi'e zakin la.” Ka Na'ab yɛl ye, “Kɛlli ka o kpɛn' na.”
6Ka Haman kpɛn' na ka Na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka ti na maali tis onɛ ka Na'ab gban'e ye o tis o girima la?” Haman da tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, “Anɔ'ɔn ka Na'ab nɔŋi paae mam, ka bɔɔd ye o tisi o sɔb girima ka li ya'a ka' manɛ?” 7O da lɛbis Na'ab la ye, “Onɛ ka Na'ab bɔɔd ye o tis o girima la, 8ba nɔkim na'am fukanɛ ka Na'ab mi' yɛ nɛ wiedkanɛ ka o mi' ban', ka na'am baŋ bɛɛ o zugin la. 9Ka nɔk fuug la nɛ wief la tis na'ayikpɛm yinne onɛ gat o taaba la wʋsa. Ka kɛ ka ba nɔk fuug la yɛɛl onɛ ka Na'ab ye o tis o girima la, ka ban'al o wief la zugʋ gilig teŋ la wʋsa, ka kɛ ka ba gaad o tuonnɛ tansidi yɛt nidib la ye, ‘Na'abi maal si'eli nwa' tis onɛ ka o nɔŋ ka ye o tis o girima!’”
10Ka Na'ab la yɛl Haman ye, “Tɔ'! Kem tɔ'ɔtɔ nɔk na'am fuug nɛ wief la niŋ wʋʋ fʋn yɛl si'em la nɔɔ tis Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid ka zin' m zɔŋŋin la. Bʋmbanɛ ka fʋ kaal la wʋsa mid ka fʋ bas baa yinne.” 11Haman sid da nɔk fuug la ka lɔ wief la. O da bɔb Modekaya nɛ fuug la ka ban'al o wief la zugʋ giligid teŋ la ka kɛ ka ba yɛt nidib la ye, “Na'abi maal si'eli nwa' tis onɛ ka o gban'e ye o tis o girima la!” 12Modekaya da giligi naae ka lɛb Na'ab la zɔŋŋin na. Amaa Haman da zaŋ si'eli lus o nindaa lɛb tɔ'ɔtɔ kul nɛ nyan, 13ka yɛl o pu'a Zeres nɛ o zuanam la linɛ wʋsa maal o.
Banɛ sa'an o la nɛ o pu'a Zeres da yɛl o ye, “Fʋn nɛ Modekaya onɛ kpa' taab la an Jew nid la zug, fʋ ye fʋ ba'asi lu nɛ. Fʋ lɛn ka' onɛ na nyaŋ o, asɛɛ fʋ ba'asi san'am!” 14Ban da nan pian'ad nɛ o la, Na'ab la sankpan'asnam da kena ye ba dɔl Haman tɔ'ɔtɔ kɛn dikanɛ ka Esta maal ka buon o la zin'igin na.

english_text:
Haman Is Punished
1The king and Haman were dining with Esther 2and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
3Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want, 4because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
5“Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
6Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!”
Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
7The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden.
Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
8Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!”
As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head. 9Then Harbona, one of the king's personal servants, said, “Your Majesty, Haman built a gallows 22 meters high beside his house, so he could hang Mordecai on it. And Mordecai is the very one who spoke up and saved your life.”
“Hang Haman from his own gallows!” the king commanded. 10At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_text:
Ban yul Haman la yɛla
1Na'ab la nɛ Haman da keŋ ye ba la'am di nɛ Esta. 2Ban da nan bɛɛ ani nuud daam la, Na'ab la da lɛm bu'os Na'apu'a Esta ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔda? Yɛlim ka m na tisif, hali baa li ya'a zem wʋʋ man sʋ'ʋlim la pʋsʋk gba fʋ na nyɛ.” 3Na'apu'a Esta da lɛbis ye, “Naa, fʋ ya'a sid siak ye fʋ na tisim man sɔs si'eli fʋ san'an, alaa mam bɔɔd si'el anɛ ye fʋ sʋŋim ka m nyɔvʋr da san'am ka mɛ faanm nidib la bas. 4Bɔzugɔ ba kuos man nɛ m nidib la tis ye ba mugusi ti ka kʋʋ ti wʋsa. Ba ya'a kuosini ti wʋʋ yammis, m sinnin nɛ, bɔzugɔ lin pʋ siak ye m daam Na'aba.” 5Na'ab Zeesis da bu'os o ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ la? Dau kanɛ ye o tʋm tʋʋm kan la bɛ yaanɛ?” 6Ka Esta lɛbis ye, “Nimbɛ'og onɛ kisi ti ka mɔɔdi ti yɛla anɛ Haman, onɛ zin' nwa'.”
Ka dabiem kpɛn' Haman, Na'ab la nɛ Esta tuon. 7Na'ab la da sʋnf da duoe hali ka o duoe ka bas o daam la ka keŋ kpɛn' na'ayir lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la. Amaa Haman n da baŋ ye Na'ab la pʋn kʋʋs o yɛla bɛ'ɛd la, ka kpɛm bɛllim Esta o nyɔvʋr yɛla. 8Na'ab la da naan lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la lɛbi kpɛn' on pa'a zin' si'eli nuud daam la ka nyɛ ka Haman bilim Esta nɔba ni on dig sɔŋ si'a zug la. Na'ab la da tans nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye, “Fʋ maan pu'ana'ab la nɛ anwaa, la'an nɛ man bɛ yin kpɛla laa?” Na'ab la ti ye o pian' naae la, ka ba pʋn pin' Haman nindaa ka li pa'al ye ba kʋʋs o bɛ'ɛd. 9Habona onɛ an Na'ab la sankpan'as yinne la da yɛl ye, “Linɛ ka ba yun nidibi li zug la ba' zi'e kpi'e Haman yin la wa'am hali. O ba'a li nɛ ye ba yul Modekaya onɛ da pian' fan' Na'ab la bas la yɛla.” Ka Na'ab ye, “Mɔr o keŋ yul o li zug!” 10Dinzug ba da nɔk Haman n keŋ yul dakanɛ ka o da ba'a zi'el ye o yul Modekaya la. Ka Na'ab la sʋnf nyaan niŋ lamm.

english_text:
A Happy Ending for the Jews
1Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials 2and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
3Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!” 4King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther, 5and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed, 6and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
7King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews. 8 I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
9On the twenty-third day of Sivan, the third month, the king's secretaries wrote the law. They obeyed Mordecai and wrote to the Jews, the rulers, the governors, and the officials of all 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. The letters were written in every language used in the kingdom, including the Jewish language. 10They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
11-13In these letters the king said:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies.
A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
14-15Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth.
After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered, 16and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
17In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_text:
Na'ab la pian' Jew dim yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa
1Daakan nɔɔ Na'ab la da nɔk Haman onɛ an Jew dim dataa la sʋ'oe zin'isi'a teŋin la tis Esta. Ka Modekaya paae Na'ab la tuon, bɔzugɔ Esta da pa'al ban kpin si'em. 2Na'ab la da pʋn dɛŋim pidig o nu'ug tikir baŋ la yis Haman san'an, ka yʋ'ʋn nɔki li tis Modekaya. Ka Esta kɛ ka o sʋ'ʋg zin'ikanɛ ka Haman da sʋ'oe la wʋsa.
3Esta da lɛn vanbin Na'ab la nɔba nii kum ka bɛllim o ye gban'abɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka Haman onɛ an Agag buudi la gban'e zaŋi keŋ Jew dim la yɛla la, kɛl ka li kpi. 4Na'ab la da tiɛn o sanlima dansaar la ka Esta si'isi li ka duoe zi'en o tuon. 5O da ye, “Naa, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a na siak, ka gɔs ka li nar, ka fʋ sʋnf mɛ sid malis nɛ mam, fʋn sɔm ka tiki fʋ nu'ug ka li kpiis gban'ar kanɛ ka Haman onɛ an Hamedata biig ka an Agag buudi gban'e ka sɔb ye o san'am Jew dim banɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlim kaŋa ni wʋsa la. 6Bɔzugɔ man ye m niŋ wala bɛ ka gɔti m nidib nɛ m du'adib ka ba san'amida?” 7Na'ab Zeesis da yɛl Na'apu'a Esta nɛ Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid la ye, “Haman n zabid nɛ Jew dim la zug, m nɔk o zin'ig la tis Esta ka kɛ ka ba yul o daug zugʋ kʋ. 8Amaa linɛ sɔb nɛ Na'ab la yʋ'ʋr ka tik nɛ o nu'ug baŋ zanbin la, si'el kae na tiaki lii. Tɔ', nannanna maligim sɔb wada si'a ya'as nɛ man Na'ab la yʋ'ʋr ka tiki li nɛ m nu'ug tikir baŋ la, ka zi'el yanamɛ bɔɔd si'em zaŋi ken Jew dim la yɛla.”
9Ba da la'as na'ayir gbansɔbidib la tɔ'ɔtɔ, nwadkanɛ tia'al atan' ka ba buon ye Sivan la, li dabisa pisi nɛ atan' daar. Ba da sɔb Modekaya yɛt ye Jew dim la maal si'el la wʋsa, tis kpɛɛmnam nɛ tuongatib nɛ nintitada banɛ bɛ tɛɛns kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi lin yi India paae Kus la. Ba da sɔb nɛ'ɛŋa sʋ'ʋlim la bɛn wʋsa, ka tɛɛns wʋsa di'e li ka li sɔbi ba mɛŋ sɔbirin, nɛ buudi la wʋsa mɛŋ pian'adin, la'an nɛ Jew dim la nɛ ba mɛŋ buudi sɔb nɛ li pian'ad. 10Modekaya da nɔk nɛ Na'ab la yʋ'ʋri sɔb ka nɔk o nu'ug tikir baŋi tik, ka nɔki tis banɛ ban'ad na'am widi banɛ ka ba zamisi ba ka mi' zɔɔb sʋ'ʋŋa la ye mɔr gbana la keŋi tɔd.
11Na'ab la da tis nɔɔr ye Jew dim banɛ bɛ teŋ la ni wʋsa mɔr suor ka ba la'asi gu' ba mɛŋ, ka zab nɛ banɛ yi buudsi'a ni na wʋsa teŋ la ni bɔɔd ye ba daam bɛɛ san'am bɛɛ kʋʋ ba nɛ ba pu'ab nɛ biis la; ka faaɛn ba dataas la la'ad. 12Dabiskanɛ ka Jew dim la da ye ba niŋ nɛ'ɛŋa Na'ab Zeesis sʋ'ʋlimin la wʋsa da anɛ nwadkanɛ paas pii nɛ ayi' la ni ka ba buonnɛ li Ada la, li dabis pii nɛ atan' daar. 13Na'ab la da tis nɔsi'a la da lieb nɛ zi'elʋg sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa ni, ka ba kɛ ka li paae nidib la ka buudi wʋsa baŋ, ka li kɛ ka Jew dim la wʋsa ti'eb dabiskan daare yɔɔ ba bi'emnam sam.
14Labaya dim banɛ da ban'ad na'am widi la da zɔɔ gilig hali wʋʋ Na'ab la tis nɔɔr si'em la. Ba da zi Na'ab la wada la keŋ mɔɔl Susa tempʋʋgin la mɛn.
15Modekaya da yi Na'ab la san'an ka yɛ na'am fuug linɛ an bʋlʋ nɛ bʋmpielig, ka sanlima baŋ tita'ar pil o zugin, ka o nɔk pien zɛn'ug linɛ ʋg nɛ gum sʋŋʋ vil o mɛŋ. Ka Susa teŋ nidib la da di'em nɛ sumalisim. 16Jew dim la san'an li da anɛ sumalisim nɛ sumpielim nɛ zusʋŋ nɛ girimtita'ari tisi ba. 17Teŋ la sʋ'ʋlim nɛ li tempʋʋs la, zin'ikanɛ wʋsa ka Na'ab la nɔzi'elʋg la paae, Jew dim la wʋsa da mɔr nɛ sumalisim ka ba maan diib nɛ di'ema.
Ka buudi bɛdegʋ banɛ ka' Jew dim la muki ba mɛŋi lieb Jew dim buudi bɔzugɔ Jew dim la yɛla da kpɛn'ɛsi ba nɛ dabiem.

english_text:
The Jews Destroy Their Enemies
1The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around, 2and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
3The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews. 4Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
5The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy. 6-10They killed 500 people in Susa, but they did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Haman had been one of the worst enemies of the Jews, and ten of his sons were among those who were killed. Their names were Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.
11Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa. 12Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
13Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
14King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa. 15Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed 300 more people. But they still did not take anything that belonged to their enemies.
16-17On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed 75,000 of their enemies, but the Jews did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Then on the fourteenth day of the month the Jews celebrated with a feast.
18 On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth. 19This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other.
The Festival of Purim
20Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces 21and told them:
Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar, 22the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
23They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration.
The Reason for the Festival of Purim
24 Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
25Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged. 26Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast. 27Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do. 28From now on, all Jewish families must remember to celebrate Purim on these two days each year.
29Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast. 30Copies of this letter were sent to Jews in the 127 provinces of King Xerxes. In the letter they said:
We pray that all of you will live in peace and safety.
31You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
32These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_text:
Jew dim paam paŋ
1Nwadkanɛ paasid pii nɛ ayi' ka ba buon Ada la, li dabis pii nɛ atan' la daar, ka ba da ye ba nɔk Na'ab la tis nɔsi'a la tʋm. Daakan la Jew dim la dataas la da tɛn'ɛs ye ba na nyaŋi ba, amaa li da tulig nɛ ka Jew dim la lɛɛ nyaŋi ba dataas la. 2Jew dim la da la'as taaba ban bɛ zin'isi'a wʋsa Na'ab Zeesis sʋ'ʋlimin la ye ba zab nɛ banɛ mɔɔdi ba san'auŋ yɛla la, sɔ' kae da nyaŋi zi'en nɛ ba, bɔzugɔ buudi la wʋsa da zɔti ba nɛ. 3Nimbɛda banɛ da bɛ teŋin la wʋsa, nɛ Gɔmenanam nɛ tuongatib nɛ na'ayir kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa da kpɛn'ɛd nɛ Jew dim la zug, bɔzugɔ ba wʋsa da zɔti Modekaya dabiem. 4Modekaya yʋ'ʋn da lieb nintita'ar na'ayin la, ka o yʋ'ʋr tiig teŋ la wʋsa, ka o paŋ paasid daar wʋsa.
5Jew dim la da san'am ka kʋʋ ba dataas la wʋsa nɛ sʋ'ʋg, ka maal banɛ kisi ba la wʋsa ban bɔɔd si'em. 6Susa tempʋʋgin la, Jew dim la da kʋ dap kɔbisnu. 7Ba mɛ da kʋ Pasandata nɛ Dalifon nɛ Asipata, 8nɛ Porata nɛ Adalia nɛ Aridata, 9nɛ Parimasita nɛ Arisai nɛ Aridaae nɛ Vaae-zata, 10banɛ an Haman biis piiga, Haman onɛ da an Jew dim la dataa, ka o saam an Hamedata la. Amaa ka lɛɛ pʋ nɔki ba nu'ugʋ si'isi ba la'adɛ.
11Banɛ da kpi Susa tempʋʋgin la, ba da yɛl Na'ab la daakan nɔɔ. 12Na'ab la da yɛl Na'apu'a Esta ye, “Jew dim la kʋ dap kɔbisnu nɛ Haman biis piiga Susa tempʋʋgin la. Ka ba yʋ'ʋn maal wala sʋ'ʋlim bama la ni? Nannanna fʋ bɔɔdim an bɔ? Sɔsim ka fʋ na nyɛ. Bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye m lɛm maali tisi fɔ? Yɛlim ka m na maali tisif.” 13Esta da lɛbis ye, “Naa, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a na siak, fʋn tisim Jew dim banɛ bɛ Susa la nɔɔr ka bɛog ba saa na tʋm wʋʋ ban pa'a tʋm kpɛla zina si'em la, ka yul Haman biis piiga la daba'ada la zug.” 14Na'ab la da tis nɔɔr ye ba sid niŋ ala, ka ba da bas nɔɔr la Susa teŋin. Ka ba ya'al Haman biis piiga la daba'ada la zug. 15Jew dim banɛ bɛ Susa teŋin la da la'as Ada nwadig la dabis pii nɛ anaasi daare kʋ dap kɔbistan' amaa ka pʋ nɔki ba nu'ugi si'isi ba laukɔ.
16Jew dim banɛ da kpɛlim Na'ab la sʋ'ʋlimin la da la'asi gu' ba mɛŋ ka nyɛ vʋ'ʋsʋm ba dataas la ni. Ba da kʋ nidib tusa pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (75,000) amaa ka lɛɛ pʋ nɔki ba nu'ugʋ si'isi ba laukɔ. 17Nɛ'ɛŋa da niŋnɛ Ada nwadig la dabis pii nɛ atan' daar, ka dabis pii nɛ anaasi daar la ka ba nɔki vʋ'ʋs ka li an diib nɛ di'ema dabisir.
Purim Di'ema Malʋŋ
18Jew dim banɛ da bɛ Susa la on da la'as taaba nɛ dabis pii nɛ atan' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi la daar ka nɔk dabis pii nɛ anu daar la vʋ'ʋs ka li an diib nɛ di'ema daar.
19Linɛ kɛ ka Jew dim banɛ bɛ teŋkpɛmis la nɔk Ada nwadig la dabis pii nɛ anaasi daar ka li an sumalisim nɛ diib dabisir nɛ dabiskanɛ ka ba tisid taaba piini.
20Modekaya da sɔb bʋmbama digil ka tɔlim gbana tis Jew dim banɛ bɛ Na'ab Zeesis teŋin la wʋsa, banɛ bɛ yamma bɛɛ lalli, 21ye o kɛ ka ba nɔk Ada nwadig dabis pii nɛ anaasi nɛ pii nɛ anu daar la wʋsa ka li an di'ema dabisa tisi ba, 22pa'an saŋa kanɛ ka Jew dim la paam yɔlisim yii ba dataas nu'usin la, nɛ nwadkanɛ ka ba sʋnsa'aŋ lieb sumalisim, ka ba kukuma lieb la'ad. O da sɔbi tisi ba ye ba mɔ ka dabisban la, ba na dit ka maan sumalisim ka tisid taaba diib ka tisid nɔŋ dim piini.
23Jew dim la siak ye ba na maan ala saŋa wʋsa wʋʋ ban pin'il si'em la, ka tʋm wʋʋ Modekaya n sɔb si'em tisi ba la. 24Bɔzugɔ Haman onɛ saamme an Hamedata ka o an Agag buudi ka an Jew dim dataa la da gban'e bɛ'ɛd ka maal pur linɛ an bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm ye o baŋ dabiskanɛ ka o na san'am Jew dim la. 25Amaa Esta da keŋ Na'ab la san'an la, Na'ab la da tis nɔɔr ye gban'abɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka Haman gban'e Jew dim la yɛla la na lɛb o mɛŋ zugin, ka ye on nɛ o biis la, ba na yuli ba nɛ dabanɛ ka o ba'a la zug. 26Dinzug ba da buon dabisban ye, Purim ka li yinɛ pian'ʋk kanɛ ka ba buon pur la ni na. Bʋn linɛ wʋsa sɔb gbauŋʋn la nɛ ban nyɛ si'el nɛ linɛ maal la zug 27ka Jew dim la da gban'e ye ba na kɛ ka li liebi ba malʋŋ ka ban nɛ ba biis nɛ banɛ bɛ nɛ ba na tiɛnd dabisbama ayi' la yɛla yʋʋm wʋsa ka da gʋ'ʋŋɛ. Ba na maannɛ li ka li dɔlli li suor nɛ saŋa kanɛ nar ye li maal la. 28Dabisbama nar ye zumaana wʋsa nɛ yir wʋsa nɛ sʋ'ʋlim nɛ tempʋʋg wʋsa tiɛndi li yɛla. Purim dabisa nwa' nar ye Jew dim wʋsa maal di'ema li daar, ka da vi' bɛɛ kɛ ka li yɛla kpi ba yaas san'anɛ.
29Alazug Na'apu'a Esta onɛ an Abihel biig la nɛ Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid la da sɔb nɛ kpi'euŋʋ paas gbauŋ kanɛ paasida ayi' la zaŋi ken Purim la yɛla. 30Modekaya da tɔlim gbana la tis Jew dim banɛ bɛ Na'ab Zeesis sʋ'ʋlim tɛɛns kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (127) la ni wʋsa. Linɛ da sɔb gbauŋʋn la da anɛ pian'asʋma ka yɛt ye ba zi'e ba nya'aŋ. 31Ka ye ba mɔɔm ka Purim dabisa la zi'en wʋʋ lin nar si'em ka dɔl wʋʋ Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid la nɛ Na'apu'a Esta gban'e si'em tisi ba la, nɛ ban zi'eli li si'em tisi ba mɛŋ nɛ ba yaas dɔl wʋʋ saŋa kanɛ ka ba lɔɔd nɔɔr ka maan sʋnsa'aŋ la. 32Esta gban'ar la da kɛ ka Purim malima la zi'en, ka ba sɔbi li niŋ gbana nii digil.

english_text:
The Greatness of Xerxes and Mordecai
1King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea. 2All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai. 3Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_text:
Modekaya lieb kpi'em
1Na'ab Zeesis da tis nɔɔr ye teŋ la nidib wʋsa yɔ lampɔ keŋ paae teŋ la wʋsa bɛn. 2O paŋ nɛ kpi'euŋ tʋʋma linɛ tʋm wʋsa la'an nɛ kpi'euŋ kanɛ wʋsa ka Modekaya da mɔr ka li anɛ Na'ab la ziank o paae ani la, ba mɛ da sɔbi li wʋsa niŋ Media nɛ Pesia na'anam la gbana la ni. 3Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid la da tia'al Na'ab Zeesis nya'aŋ, ka gat Jew dim la wʋsa, ka o taaba banɛ an Jew dim la tisid o girima bɛdegʋ, bɔzugɔ o da tʋm sʋ'ʋm tis o nidib la, ka pian'adi bɔɔd sʋ'ʋm ba bɛog yɛla.

english_text:
Job and His Family
1Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
2Job had 7 sons and 3 daughters. 3He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pair of oxen, 500 donkeys, and a large number of servants. He was the richest person in the East.
4Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking. 5After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God.
Angels, the Lord, and Satan
6 One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them, 7the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
8Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
9 “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked. 10“You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere. 11Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
12The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.”
Then Satan left.
Job Loses Everything
13Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son, 14when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass, 15a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
16That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
17Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
18That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son, 19when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
20When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God 21 and said:
“We bring nothing at birth;
we take nothing
with us at death.
The Lord alone gives and takes.
Praise the name of the Lord!”
22In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_text:
Job nɛ o yidim yɛla
1Dau sɔ' da bɛ Uz teŋin ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Job. Dau nwa' da anɛ ninvʋsʋŋ ka ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ, ka mɛ an pʋʋg yinne sɔb. O da anɛ onɛ zɔt Wina'am ka kis dinɛ wʋsa an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd. 2Dau nwa' da mɔri biribis ayɔpɔi nɛ bipumis atan', 3ka mɔr pɛ'ɛs tusa ayɔpɔi nɛ yʋgʋma tusa atan' nɛ na'akuoda tusir, nɛ bʋmis kɔbis nu nɛ sankpan'asnam bɛdegʋ. O da anɛ nintita'ari gaad nimbanɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la wʋsa. 4O biribis la da ɛɛnti maannɛ di'ema ba yaan la ti kaligi ba ya' la wʋsa; ka buoli ba tanp la ka ba kena di ka nu nɛ ba. 5Ba di'ema dabisa la ya'a gaad, Job na tʋm buoli ba ka maali ba nyain. O da ɛɛn tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, daasi'erɛɛ o biis la pa'ati tɛn'ɛs pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd Wina'am yɛla. Dinzug, o da ɛɛn duonɛ bɛkɛungʋ maal maan linɛ nyu'od bugum o biis la yinne-yinne zug.
Sʋntaana dɛŋi mak Job la yɛla
6 Daar yinne ka Wina'am biis la'as ye ba zaŋi ba mɛŋi pa'al Wina'am, ka Sʋntaana mɛ paasi ba zug. 7Ka Zugsɔb la bu'os Sʋntaana ye, “Fʋ yi yaanɛ na?” Ka o gandig ye, “Man yinɛ teŋgbauŋʋn la na, ka bɛɛ anina giligid zin'is wʋsa.”
8Ka Wina'am bu'os o ye, “Fʋ tiɛn m tʋmtʋm Job yɛlaa? Ninsaal ka' teŋgbauŋ nwa' zugʋ nwɛnɛ o. O anɛ ninvʋsʋŋ ka ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ, ka mɛ an pʋʋg yinne sɔb. O anɛ onɛ zɔt mam Wina'am ka kis dinɛ wʋsa an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.”
9 Ka Sʋntaana lɛbis Wina'am ye, “Di anɛ zaalim ka Job zɔt fʋn Na'awinnɛɛ? 10Mɛ fʋ zaŋi gu'udi gu' on nɛ o yidim nɛ on mɔr si'el wʋsa? Fʋ mɛ niŋ o zug bareka ka o pɛ'ɛs nɛ niigi du'a pɛ'ɛl teŋ la wʋsa. 11Tiɛnmi fʋ nu'ugʋ san'am o mɔrim la wʋsa ka fʋ na nyɛ ka o ki'isi fʋ, fʋ nifin.” 12Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl Sʋntaana ye, “Tɔ', on mɔr si'el wʋsa la bɛɛ fʋ nu'ugin, amaa mid ka fʋ si'is o mɛŋ.”
13Daar yinne ka Job biribis nɛ o bipumis mɔri ba di'ema o bikpɛɛm la yinne dit ka nuud, 14ka sɔ' kɛn Job san'an na yɛl o ye, “Na'akuoda la bɛɛn nɛ anina kuod ka bʋmis la ɔnbid mɔɔd anina baba 15ka Seba dim libigi ba kadi ba wʋsa keŋ. Ba kʋ tʋmtʋmnib la wʋsa, ka mam ma'aa pɔns ka kena ye m yɛlif!”
16On nan bɛɛ anina pian'ad la ka nid yinne lɛm paae na ye, “Bugum naan agɔla li na kanb pɛ'ɛs la nɛ fʋ tʋmtʋmnib la wʋsa, ka mam ma'aa pɔns ka kena ye m yɛlif!”
17On nan bɛɛ anina pian'ad la ka yinne mɛ zɔɔ paae na ye, “Kaldea dimi la'as taab zin'is atan' kpɛm bʋʋl na kadi fʋ yʋgʋma la wʋsa keŋ ka kʋʋ fʋ tʋmtʋmnib la wʋsa, ka mam ma'aa pɔns ka kena ye m yɛlif!”
18On nan bɛɛ anina pian'ad la ka nid yinne lɛm paae na yɛl ye, “Fʋ na'akim nɛ fʋ bipumis la bɛ nɛ fʋ bikpɛɛm la yinnɛ maan di'ema dit ka nuud, 19ka sisi'etita'ar naam pipirigin na kpɛn gubil yir la ka li luu bʋʋli ba ka ba kpi, ka mam ma'aa pɔns ka kena ye m yɛlif!”
20Ka Job duoe aans o fuud ka pʋn o zug ye o pa'al o sʋnsa'aŋi an si'em, ka vanbin teŋin sɔs Wina'am 21yɛt ye,
“M da naani m ma pʋʋgin yinɛ zaalim na,
zaalim mɛn ka m na lɛb.
Zugsɔb la tisim, onɛ lɛn di'e ya'as;
Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr nar nɛ girima.”
22La'an nɛ linɛ niŋ la wʋsa, Job da pʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛd bɛɛ nyɔl Wina'am ye o tʋm o bɛ'ɛdɛ.

english_text:
Job Loses His Health
1When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them, 2and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
3Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
4Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive. 5Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
6“All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.” 7Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
8Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery, 9his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
10Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God.
Job's Three Friends
11Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him. 12When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly. 13For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_text:
Sʋntaana mak Job laafi zin'igin
1Daar yinne ya'as ka Wina'am biis la'as ye ba zaŋi ba mɛŋi pa'al Wina'am, ka Sʋntaana mɛ paasi dɔlli kena. 2Ka Zugsɔb la bu'os Sʋntaana ye, “Fʋ yi yaanɛ na?” Ka Sʋntaana gandig Zugsɔb la ye, “Man yinɛ teŋgbauŋʋn la na, ka bɛɛ anina giligid zin'is wʋsa.” 3Ka Wina'am bu'os o ye, “Fʋ tiɛn m tʋmtʋm Job yɛlaa? Ninsaal kae teŋgbauŋ nwa' zugʋ nwɛn o. O anɛ ninvʋsʋŋ ka ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ, ka mɛ an pʋʋg yinne sɔb. O anɛ onɛ zɔt mam Wina'am ka kis dinɛ wʋsa an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd. Hali baa fʋn zaŋimi tugul nɛ o ka san'am o zaalim-zaalim la, o nan kpɛn zi'enɛ o burikinnim la pʋʋgin.” 4Ka Sʋntaana lɛbis ye, “Mɛ vʋm an si'el wʋsa, ninsaal kʋ maligim siaki zaŋ o vʋm tiak nɛ si'ela. 5Kɛl ka tɔɔg paae o mɛŋ niŋgbina ka fʋ na nyɛ ka o ki'isif.” 6Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl Sʋntaana ye, “Tɔ', gɔsima, m zaŋ o si'el wʋsa niŋi fʋ nu'ugin, ya'a ka' o vʋm ma'aanɛ. Da si'is o vʋm la.” 7Ka Sʋntaana yi Wina'am tuon ka kɛ ka sankpangbiriba gban'e Job niŋgbina hali yii o nɔba ni paae o zupaasʋʋg 8Ka Job nɔk sɛwia ɛnbisid o mɛŋ ka keŋ zin' tampʋʋr zug. 9Ka o pu'a yɛl o ye, “Fʋ nan kpɛn zi'enɛ fʋ burikinnimin laa? Fʋ ya'a ki'is Wina'am ka kpi, di pʋ sɔn'oe yaa?” 10Ka o lɛbis ye, “Fʋ pian'ad la nwɛnɛ pu'a kanɛ ka' ya'am nɛ. Bʋnsʋma ma'aa ka ti di'esid Zugsɔb la san'an ka lɛɛ kʋ di'e bʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ?” Yɛlbama wʋsa pʋʋgin, Job pʋ ya'ae o nɔɔri pian' Wina'am bɛ'ɛdɛ.
11Job zuanam atan' da bɛ; ba da anɛ Elifaz onɛ an Teman nid la, nɛ Bilidad onɛ an Suh nid, nɛ Zofar onɛ mɛ an Naama nid la. Ban da wʋm yɛltɔɔg dinɛ paae o la, ba da la'as taaba ye ba keŋ bɛlis o. 12Ban da nam bɛ lalli ka nyɛ o la, ba da pʋ baŋ ye onɛ la. Ba sʋnya da san'amnɛ hali ka ba pin'ili kaasid ka aansidi ba fuud ka nɔk tampɛligim niŋi ba zut ye li pa'ali ba sʋnsa'aŋ. 13Ka ba paae na la'am zin'in teŋin nɛ o daba ayɔpɔi nintaŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ. Ka ba sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ ya'ae o nɔɔri yɛl o si'ela bɔzugɔ ba da nyɛ ka o namisʋg la galis hali.

english_text:
Job's First Speech
Blot Out the Day of My Birth
1 Finally, Job cursed the day
of his birth
2by saying to God:
3Blot out the day of my birth
and the night when my parents
created a son.
4Forget about that day,
cover it with darkness,
5and send thick, gloomy shadows
to fill it with dread.
6Erase that night from the calendar
and conceal it with darkness.
7Don't let children be created
or joyful shouts be heard
ever again in that night.
8Let those with magic powers
place a curse on that day.
9Darken its morning stars
and remove all hope of light,
10because it let me be born
into a world of trouble.
Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
11Why didn't I die at birth?
12Why was I accepted
and allowed to nurse
at my mother's breast?
13Now I would be at peace
in the silent world below
14with kings and their advisors
whose palaces lie in ruins,
15and with rulers once rich
with silver and gold.
16I wish I had been born dead
and then buried, never to see
the light of day.
17In the world of the dead,
the wicked and the weary rest
without a worry.
* 18Everyone is there—
19where captives and slaves
are free at last.
Why Does God Let Me Live?
20Why does God let me live
when life is miserable
and so bitter?
21 I keep longing for death
more than I would seek
a valuable treasure.
22Nothing could make me happier
than to be in the grave.
23Why do I go on living
when God has me surrounded,
and I can't see the road?
24Moaning and groaning
are my food and drink,
25and my worst fears
have all come true.
26I have no peace or rest—
only troubles and worries.
translation_text:
Job pian' zɛrigi o du'am dabisir
1 Ka Job yʋ'ʋn ya'ae o nɔɔri pɔɔ zɛrig o du'am dabisir. 2O da yɛl ye,
3“Kɛl ka m du'am dabisir la ba'as yɔri,
hali nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ ka ba yɛl ye, ‘Ba tʋk biribiŋ pʋʋg la!’
4Kɛl ka dabiskan lieb lik
ka Wina'am onɛ bɛɛ agɔl la pʋn da tɛn'ɛsi li yɛllɛ.
Da kɛ ka nintaŋ yi daakanɛ.
5Kɛl ka dabisir la kilim lik biridi;
kɛl ka saŋgbansabilig ligili li,
ka lik nyaŋ nintaŋ dabiskaŋa nwa' ni.
6Kɛl ka lik linɛ sɔbig biridi sʋ'oe daakan yʋ'ʋŋ la.
Da kɛ ka ba kaali li paas dabisa banɛ bɛ yʋʋm la pʋʋginɛ,
bɛɛ ba pɛ'ɛsi li nwadsi'a nii.
7Pʋn da kɛ ka pu'a nɔk pʋʋg yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ;
kɛl ka sɔ' da wʋm sumalisim tʋkpiidʋgɔ.
8Kɛl ka banɛ mɔr nɔtɔɔd pɔ nɔɔri niŋ dabisir nwa',
ka teŋgban kpɛn'ɛdib bɔ bɔɔb dabisir nwa' zug.
9Kɛl ka li bɛkɛung nwadbibis lieb lik;
kɛl ka li gu'us nintaŋi gʋ'ʋŋ
ka kʋ nyɛ bɛogʋn sɔɔnrim,
10bɔzugɔ li sʋm ye li li'inimi m ma pʋʋgin
ka o da du'am ka m nyɛ yɛltɔɔd bamaa.
11Bɔzug kimm ka m da pʋ lɛbi m du'am daarɛ,
ka duoe na pʋ mɔr vɔɔnr nwa'?
12Bɔzug ka pu'adu'as la da du'asi m ma,
ka bɔ ka m ma da tisim bin'isim ka m mu'a?
13Anwaa m digin nɛ baanlimm nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.
Anwaa m gbisidin nɛ ka vʋ'ʋsid.
14M ya'a kpiinɛɛ m naan bɛɛn kpi'im teŋ,
ka la'as nɛ banɛ pʋn kpi la nɛ
na'anam nɛ ba na'ayikpɛm banɛ da sʋ'oe dunia
ka da mɛ teŋ titada la.
15Anwaa m vʋ'ʋsidin nɛ ninvʋsʋma banɛ mɔr sanlima,
ka pɛ'ɛli ba ya' nɛ anzurifa la.
16Bɔzug ka ba da pʋ pin'im
wʋʋ pu'a ɛɛn du'a bikpi'im ka ba pin' o si'em la,
bɛɛ bilia kanɛ pʋ nyɛ nɛɛsim ka lɛb si'em la?
17Kpi'im teŋ ka bugusnam pʋ lɛn tʋm bugisim tʋʋmaa,
ka banɛ tadig nyɛt vʋ'ʋsʋm.
18Anina mɛn ka banɛ da bɛ sanrega ni la mɔr yɔlisim ka bɛ baanlimm,
ka pʋ lɛn wʋm banɛ da mugusidi ba la tansʋg ya'asɛ.
19Tadimnam nɛ kpi'emnam wʋsa bɛɛ anina,
ka yammis nyɛ yɔlisim ba dima nu'usin.
20Kassa! Nɛɛsim an bɔɔ tis sʋnsa'aŋ daana?
Ka vʋm an bɔɔ tis onɛ bɛ tɔɔg pʋʋginɛ?
21 Ba ieed kum ka kum pʋ kennaa,
ba ieed kum hali nɛ nimmua
gat ban na ieed la'asʋŋ dinɛ su'a.
22Ba mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm bɛdegʋ
ka maan sumalisim ban paae yaʋgʋn la zug.
23Bɔzug ka ba tisid onɛ ka' bɛog nyɔvʋrɛ;
ka Wina'am gan'al ye ba na namis hali la?
24M sin'uŋ lieb diibi tisim,
ka m ʋʋnsʋg nwɛnɛ ku'om kpa'adnɛ.
25Gbaagba man zɔt si'el la, linɛ paam!
Linɛ ka m sid zɔt amɛŋa mɛŋa la paam.
26Ayei, m pʋ mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm, li ka' m sʋ'ʋm.
M ka' vʋ'ʋsʋm, li anɛ daauŋ ma'aa.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's First Speech
Please Be Patient and Listen
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2Please be patient and listen
to what I have to say.
* 3Remember how your words
4have guided and encouraged
many in need.
5But now you feel discouraged
when struck by trouble.
6You respect God and live right,
so don't lose hope!
7No truly innocent person
has ever died young.
8In my experience, only those
who plant seeds of evil
harvest trouble,
9and then they are swept away
by the angry breath of God.
10They may roar and growl
like powerful lions.
But when God breaks their teeth,
11they starve, and their children
are scattered.
A Secret Was Told to Me
12A secret was told to me
in a faint whisper—
13 I was overcome by sleep,
but disturbed by dreams;
14I trembled with fear,
15and my hair stood on end,
as a wind blew past my face.
16It stopped and stood still.
Then a form appeared—
a shapeless form.
And from the silence,
I heard a voice say,
17“No humans are innocent
in the eyes of God
their Creator.
18He finds fault with his servants
and even with his angels.
19Humans are formed from clay
and are fragile as moths,
so what chance do you have?
20Born after daybreak,
you die before nightfall
and disappear forever.
21Your tent pegs are pulled up,
and you leave this life,
having gained no wisdom.”
translation_text:
Elifaz pian'ʋk
1Ka Elifaz onɛ an Teman nid la lɛbis ye,
2“Nid ya'a lɛbis o nɔɔrɛ, li na daami fɔɔ?
Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi gban'e o mɛŋ ka da pian' si'ela?
3Tɛnr fʋn da pa'al nidib bɛdegʋ
ka kpɛmis tadimnam si'em.
4Fʋ sa'alʋg da sʋŋ banɛ bɔɔd liig,
ka kpɛmis banɛ giinla kɛns la.
5Ka yɛltɔɔg yʋ'ʋn paae fʋ mɛŋ ka fʋ tadig,
li di'igif nɛ ka fʋ sʋʋnr wʋsa san'am.
6Dinzugɔ fʋ Wina'am zɔtim la kʋ tisif kpi'euŋɔɔ?
Ka fʋ sida bɛllim la kʋ tisif ti'irɛɛ?
7Fʋn mɛ tɛn'ɛsim gɔsɛ, nid na zi'e sida pʋʋgin ka ba'as yɔrii?
Yaanɛ ka fʋ nam mi' wʋm ye sida dim paam san'auŋɔ?
8Mam mɛŋ kpansi gɔs
ka banɛ wʋsa kuod bɛ'ɛd ka bʋt yɛla mɛ bunnɛ bɛ'ɛd.
9Wina'am ya'a vʋ'ʋs fɛɛn, ba san'amidnɛ;
o sʋnf ya'a duoe, ba mɛlimidnɛ.
10Gbigim tun'e nwa'am ka nyuul hali,
amaa la'an nɛ wala o nyina kɔya.
11Gbigimnya'aŋ pʋ nyaŋi gban'e bʋnkɔnbʋgɔ
ka li nyaŋ o, ka o biis widig yaaŋ-yaaŋ.
12Kɛlisima, labaar kɛn man san'an na,
ka m tʋba wʋm ka li nya'amid.
13 Li kena nwɛnɛ zaansʋŋ nɛ
yʋ'ʋŋ saŋa ka nidib wʋsa gbisid.
14Ka dabiem gba'am hali ka m kirid
ka m kɔnba dammid.
15Ka pɛbisim nwɛ'ɛmi gaad
ka li kpɛn'ɛsim waad ka m niŋgbina wʋsa kpɛn' waki.
16Ka li fɔn baanlimm,
amaa ka m zi' lin an si'ela.
Ka di nwɛnɛ si'el nɛ zi'e m tuon,
ka m wʋm ka li yɛt ye,
17‘Ninvʋsaal na tun'e an pʋpiel sɔbi gaad Wina'am?
Ninsaal na tun'e an nyain gaad onɛ maal oo?
18Wina'am ya'a ye o mɛŋ-mɛŋ tʋmtʋmnib pʋʋg pʋ paada,
hali ka ye o maliaknam tʋm dinɛ pʋ nara,
19ka ninsaalib banɛ ka o nɔk ya'adi maal
ka ba na tun'e san'ami ba hali gaad ban san'amid zʋnzʋnr si'em la!
20Ba tun'e kpi bɛogʋn bɛɛ zaamnɔɔr.
Ba tun'e kpi, hali ka sɔ' ba'a kae.
21Ba ya'a yisi ba vʋm,
ba kpiidnɛ yɔɔg-yɔɔg.’”

english_text:
Eliphaz Continues
Call Out for Help
1Job, call out for help
and see if an angel comes!
2Envy and jealousy
will kill a stupid fool.
3I have seen fools take root.
But God sends a curse,
suddenly uprooting them
4and leaving their children
helpless in court.
5Then hungry and greedy people
gobble up their crops
and grab their wealth.
6Our suffering isn't caused
by the failure of crops;
7it's all part of life,
like sparks shooting skyward.
8Job, if I were you,
I would ask God for help.
9 His miracles are marvelous,
more than we can count.
10God sends showers on earth
and waters the fields.
11He protects the sorrowful
and lifts up those
who have been disgraced.
* 12God swiftly traps the wicked
13 in their own evil schemes,
and their wisdom fails.
14Darkness is their only companion,
hiding their path at noon.
15God rescues the needy
from the words of the wicked
and the fist of the mighty.
16The poor are filled with hope,
and injustice is silenced.
Consider Yourself Fortunate
17 Consider yourself fortunate
if God All-Powerful
chooses to correct you.
18 He may cause injury and pain,
but he will bandage and heal
your cuts and bruises.
19God will protect you from harm,
no matter how often
trouble may strike.
20In times of war and famine,
God will keep you safe.
21You will be sheltered,
without fear of hurtful words
or any other weapon.
22You will laugh at the threat
of destruction and famine.
And you won't be afraid
of wild animals—
23they will no longer be fierce,
and your rocky fields
will become friendly.
24Your home will be secure,
and your sheep will be safe.
25You will have more descendants
than there are blades of grass
on the face of the earth.
26You will live a very long life,
and your body will be strong
until the day you die.
27Our experience has proven
these things to be true,
so listen and learn.
translation_text:
1Ka Elifaz tɔ'ɔŋ pian'ad la ye,
“Fʋ ya'a bɔɔd, fʋn buolim si'em wʋsa, amaa anɔ'ɔnɛ na gandigi fɔ?
Maliak san'an ka fʋ ye fʋ nyɛ sʋŋir bɛɛ? Ayei!
2Asida, sʋntɔɔg kʋʋd zɔlʋg,
ka fufum kʋʋd zi'ilim daan.
3Mam mɛŋ nyɛ ka zɔlʋg ba'a nya'a,
ka li pʋ yuugɛ ka o yir ba'as yɔri.
4O biis pʋ mɔr banɛ na sʋŋi baa;
ba kadi ba saria ka ba lu
ka onɛ na sʋŋi ba kae.
5Ki kanɛ ka o kua la, nɔŋ dim na buni lii sʋ'oe,
la'an nɛ on bun sieba gɔn'ɔs sʋʋgin la,
faandib na zaŋ o mɔrim la wʋsa.
6Namisʋg pʋ naanid teŋinɛ yit naa,
ka yɛla mɛ pʋ bun teŋin naa.
7Saalib wʋsa du'anɛ nɛ yɛla
nwɛnɛ nyɔ'ɔsi yit bugumin si'em la.
8Ya'a aan mam, man naan ieen Wina'am zin'ig;
mam na zaŋi m yɛla wʋsa paae o tuon na.
9Onɛ tʋm kilima banɛ ka fʋ kʋ tun'e gban'e li gbinnɛ,
ka tʋm nyalima tʋʋma hali ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi kaalɛ.
10Onɛ kɛt ka saa niid teŋgbauŋ zug,
ka kɛt ka ku'om bɛ pɔɔdin.
11Onɛ dʋ'ʋsid tadimnam saazug,
ka bɛlisid banɛ kaasid kʋʋr.
12Onɛ san'amid zam dim gban'ar
ka ban zigid si'el wʋsa lieb zaalim.
13O bɛnd ya'am dimnɛ gban'adi ba nɛ ba mi'ilim pʋʋgin,
ka ba bɔɔdim wʋsa lieb yɔri.
14Hali baa li ya'a an nintaŋ ba niŋidnɛ nwɛnɛ ba bɛnɛ likin nɛ,
ka yiridi gin nintaŋ tisʋʋs wʋʋ li anɛ yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ.
15Onɛ gur tadimnam
ka gu'udi baa yisid banɛ nɔya tɔi wʋʋ yabid la san'an,
ka faandi ba paŋ dim nu'usin basid.
16Alazug tadimnam yʋ'ʋn mɔr ti'ir
ka banɛ tʋm dinɛ pʋ nar la pʋ lɛm mɔr nɔɔr ya'asɛ.
17 Yɛlsʋm bɛ nɛ onɛ ka Wina'am sa'al o la;
alazugɔ Wina'am ya'a tɛɛgi fʋ tʋbir
fʋn da kɛ ka li zabi fɔ.
18 Onɛ pu'alimid, onɛ mɛ lɛn ti'ebid;
onɛ tisid dɛmis, onɛ mɛ ma'ad dɛmis la.
19O na yisif yɛltɔɔd ayuobʋ pʋʋgin;
hali baa li ya'a paaf nɔɔr ayɔpɔi, o na yisif.
20Kɔ'ɔm ya'a li na, o na gurif ka fʋ kʋ kpii,
hali zaba pʋʋgin, o na lusif ka sʋ'ʋg kʋ kʋʋ fɔ.
21O na gurif ka saalib nɔya kʋ niŋif si'ela.
San'auŋ ya'a paae na fʋ kʋ zɔ dabiem.
22San'auŋ nɛ kɔ'ɔm saŋa fʋn la'adnɛ,
fʋ pʋ zɔt mɔɔgin bʋnkɔnbbɛ'ɛdɛ.
23Kugbanɛ bɛɛ fʋ pɔɔdin la kʋ lɛn san'ami fʋ zʋʋdɛ,
ka mɔɔgin bʋnkɔnbid na bɛ nɛf nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.
24Fʋ mɛŋ na baŋ ye nimma'asim bɛɛ fʋ yin,
ka fʋ bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa na bɛ, ka baa yinne kʋ kpii.
25Gɔsima, fʋ biis na zu'oe,
ka fʋ tuŋ tiɛn wʋʋ mɔɔdi galis teŋ zug si'em la.
26Fʋ na kʋdigi paae fʋ bɛn ka nyaan kpi,
nwɛnɛ ki ɛɛn bi'ig si'em ka ba nyaan bun la.
27Ti kpans ya, ka baŋ ye nɛ' anɛ sida.
Dinzug, wʋm sʋ'ʋŋa ka zaŋi lii tʋm tʋʋma fʋ bɛllimin.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
It's Impossible
1Job said:
2It's impossible to weigh
my misery and grief!
3They outweigh the sand
along the beach,
and that's why I have spoken
without thinking first.
4The fearsome arrows
of God All-Powerful
have filled my soul
with their poison.
5Do oxen and wild donkeys
cry out in distress
unless they are hungry?
6What is food without salt?
What is more tasteless
than the white of an egg?
7That's how my food tastes,
and my appetite is gone.
* 8How I wish that God
would answer my prayer
9and do away with me.
10Then I would be comforted,
knowing that in all of my pain
I have never disobeyed God.
11Why should I patiently hope
when my strength is gone?
12I am not strong as stone
or bronze,
13and I have finally reached
the end of my rope.
My Friends, I Am Desperate
14My friends, I am desperate,
and you should help me,
even if I no longer respect
God All-Powerful.
* 15But you are treacherous
16like streams that swell
with melting snow,
17then suddenly disappear
in the summer heat.
18I am like a caravan,
lost in the desert
while searching for water.
19Caravans from Tema and Sheba
20thought they would find water.
But they were disappointed,
21just as I am with you.
Only one look at my suffering,
and you run away scared.
What Have I Done Wrong?
22Have I ever asked any of you
to give me a gift
23or to purchase my freedom
from brutal enemies?
24What have I done wrong?
Show me,
and I will keep quiet.
25The truth is always painful,
but your arguments
prove nothing.
26Here I am desperate,
and you consider my words
as worthless as wind.
27Why, you would sell an orphan
or your own neighbor!
28Look me straight in the eye;
I won't lie to you.
29Stop accusing me falsely;
my reputation is at stake.
30I know right from wrong,
and I am not telling lies.
translation_text:
Job lɛbis Elifaz
1Ka Job lɛbis o ye,
2“Gbaagba! Di ya'a nyaŋidin, ba naan makini m sʋnsa'aŋ nwa',
ba naan baŋini li tɛbisim zem si'em.
3Di tɛbisim na gaad titanbin'isʋg linɛ dig atɛuk gbɛog la.
Linɛ kɛ ka m pian'ad yɔɔg-yɔɔg la.
4Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la tɔn mam nɛ o piema,
Ka piema la yabid kpɛn' m siigin.
Wina'am kɛnɛ ka o sʋnpɛɛn kpɛn'ɛsim dabiem.
5Mɔɔgin bʋŋ ya'a nyɛ yaama ɔnbida, o na kaasidaa,
bɛɛ lɔlig na ɔnbid yam ka lɛm bʋʋnna?
6Ba dit dikanɛ ka yaarim kae,
bɛɛ ya nam mi' nyɛ ka gɛlpielim mɔr mimilim?
7Man diibi an si'em la,
ka m ya'amlɛog ka' li ni baa bi'elaa.
8Mam ya'a sɔs si'ela, Wina'am na gandigi maa?
O na siaki maali m sʋʋnr bɔɔdim?
9O ya'a kpɛn zaŋ o nu'ugʋ mɛdiginim
ka li naae, li pʋ sɔn'oe yaa?
10Amaa linɛ tisidim sumbʋgʋsʋm anɛ ye,
la'an nɛ tɔɔg la wʋmim si'em la,
m pʋ ki'is Onɛ an Kasi la yɛlʋgɔ.
11Paŋ bɔ ka m mɔr ka li na tisim ti'irɛ?
Bʋnsʋŋ bɔɔ bɛ tuon ka m na maal suguru gura?
12M paŋ paae kugirɛɛ?
Ka m niŋgbiŋ anɛ kʋntzɛn'ugɔ?
13Ya'a an sida, m pʋ lɛm mɔr paŋ kanɛ ka m na sʋŋi m mɛŋa,
ka linɛ naan kɛɛn ka m nyaŋ la mɛ lɛn kae.
14Di nar ye ninkanɛ bɛ yɛltɔɔgin nyɛ sʋŋiri o zuanam san'an,
hali baa o ya'a pʋ lɛn zɔt Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la dabiem.
15Amaa man taaba nwa' anɛ banɛ pʋʋgʋ pʋ paada.
Ba nwɛnɛ kɔlkanɛ ku'om pʋ ya'asid kpiɛnrɛ.
Ba nwɛnɛ ku'osuobanɛ pɛ'ɛl nɛ ku'om
ka li pʋ yuugɛ ka ku'om la pʋbigi gaad.
16Sɛɛung ka saa niid hali
ka sakuga lii pɛ'ɛli li ka li badigid;
17amaa ʋʋn ya'a nie ku'om la pʋ lɛm pʋbida,
ka nintaŋi yit hali la ka li kʋdig bar-bar.
18Kpikpinkpinnib banɛ ban'adi ba yʋgʋma ya'a kena
ka bie ye ba nu ku'om,
ba kennɛ hali kpɛn' pipirigin ti bɔdig.
19Hali yʋgʋma banɛ yi Tema teŋin gɔɔnd
ka bɔɔd ku'om ye ba nu la,
Seeba teŋ kpikpinkpinnib ya'a kena nɛ ti'ir,
20ba sʋnya san'amidnɛ
bɔzugɔ ba na nyɛ ka ku'om kae.
21Yanam mɛ anɛ ala, ya kʋ tun'e sʋŋi ma;
ya nyɛɛm namisʋg la ka dabiem gban'e ya.
22M nam mi' sɔsi ya ye, ‘Tisiminim piini,
bɛɛ zaŋiminɛ ya mɔrim yɔ man yɛla,
23bɛɛ faanminimɛ yisi m dataas nu'usin,
bɛɛ, faanminim nimbɛ'ɛdnam mugusʋginɛ’?
24Tɔ', pa'aliminim ka m na an baanlimm ka kɛlis,
yɛliminim man gbɛlig si'el.
25Ya'a an sida, yɛlmɛŋir tɔi,
amaa ya zɛrigir la wʋsa nyɔɔd an bɔ?
26Ya bɔɔdi yɛl ye m pian'ad la mɔri gbɛlʋŋ,
ka gɔs man yɛl si'el la wʋsa ka li an pɛbisim?
27Ya maan kpiibis nwɛnɛ ba ka' vɔɔnrɛ
ka pʋ zɔti ba nimbaanliga.
Hali ya tun'e yii ya zua nya'aŋ ka kuos o.
28Amaa dimi suguru ka gɔsinim.
Ya gɔs ka m anɛ onɛ na zi'eni ya tuonnɛ ma' dama'am?
29Basimi yanamɛ yɛt si'el la.
Maligim tɛn'ɛsi sʋ'ʋŋa ka da mɔŋinim bʋʋdɛ.
30Ya tɛn'ɛs ye m ma'adnɛɛ?
Ya gɔs ka m zi' sida nɛ ziri bakidaa?”

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
1Job da lɛn yɛl ye,
“Ka' tʋʋm kpi'ema ma'aa bɛ ninsaal zug dunia nwa' nii?
O pʋ nwɛnɛ ninkanɛ tʋm baadi tʋʋmaa?
2Ka nwɛnɛ sankpan'asi tʋm tadig ka bɔɔd ye winnig li tɔ'ɔtɔ si'em la,
bɛɛ nwɛnɛ onɛ kuod baadi gur o yɔɔd si'em la,
3ala ka ba kɛ ka m bɛ yɔri bɛllim nwadis wʋsa,
ka dig yʋ'ʋŋ wʋsa liebid ka pʋ tun'e gbisida.
4M ya'a kpɛn' yʋ'ʋŋ ye m gbis,
m tɛn'ɛsidnɛ ye, ‘Saŋkanɛ ka m na nie?’
Ka bɛog mɛ pʋ nieda, ka m digi liebid bɛog nyain.
5Zunzunya nɛ dian'ad ma'aa pɛ'ɛli m niŋgbina;
m niŋgbauŋ la anɛ fɛn'ɛdi nyuusid.
6M dabisa zɔtnɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ hali
gat onɛ ʋgʋd pienni lɔbid sʋlʋg ʋgʋb daug si'em la,
ka li ba'asʋg wʋsa anɛ yɔri, ka ti'ir kae.
7M Wina'am, tɛnr ye m vʋm anɛ giŋa nwa';
ka m nif kʋ lɛn nyɛ bʋnsʋŋ linɛ na tisim sumalisim ya'asɛ.
8Nini banɛ gɔsidim la kʋ lɛn nyɛɛ ma;
fʋ na ieedi m zin'ig, ka m kʋ lɛm bɛɛ.
9Nwɛnɛ saŋgbana ɛɛnti gaad tɔ'ɔtɔ si'em la,
ala mɛn ka onɛ kpii keŋ kpi'im teŋ kʋ lɛn lɛb naa.
10O kʋ lɛn lɛb o yin na ya'asɛ,
ba mɛ kʋ lɛn tɛnri o yɛla ya'asɛ.
11Dinzugɔ m kʋ sinni m nɔɔrɛ;
m na tu'as lin mugusim si'em;
m na nyɔl hali pa'alim sʋnpɛɛnni zem si'em.
12M anɛ atɛuk ku'om bɛɛ ku'omin bʋnyua,
ka fʋ kɛ ka ba guri maa?
13M ya'a tɛn'ɛs ye m ya'a diginɛ m sɔŋ zug, m na nyɛ nimma'asim,
ka tɛn'ɛs ye m ya'a gbis, li na kɛ ka m tami m namisʋg la;
14hali nɛ din mɛnɛ, fʋ vɔlisidim nɛ zaansima,
ka ian'asidi m ya'am nɛ bʋn linɛ wʋsa ka fʋ niedi pa'annim la.
15Li kɛ ka m siak nɛ ban na yulim ka m kpi
gaad mam bɛ bɛllim si'a nwa'.
16M vʋm la ka' vɔɔnrɛ, m pʋ bɔɔd ye m vʋe saŋa wʋsaa;
basim mam baanlimm ka m bɛllim nwa' ka' vɔɔnrɛ.
17Ninsaal an bɔ ka o yɛla paki fɔ,
o an bɔ ka fʋ tɛn'ɛsid o yɛla?
18O an bɔ ka fʋ kpansid o daar woo,
ka makid o saŋa wʋsa?
19Fʋ kʋ di suguru ka fɛndigi fʋ nindaa m san'anɛɛ,
bɛɛ kɛ ka m paam vʋ'ʋsʋm bi'elaa vɔli m nintɔɔndɛ?
20Fʋn kanɛ gɔsid ninsaalib wʋsa la,
taal bɔ kimm ka m tʋm tisi fɔ?
Bɔ ka fʋ maalim bʋmbʋ'ʋdir ka bʋ'ʋdim saŋa wʋsa?
Man lieb nɛ ziidi tisi fɔɔ?
21Bɔzug ka fʋ kʋ di suguru m pɔ'ɔgir zug
ka kɛɛ m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd taali basɛ?
Bɔzugɔ, li kʋ yuugɛ ka m paae m yaanam san'an.
Fʋ na ieedim ka kʋ lɛn nyɛɛ ma.”

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
Bilidad yiiga pian'ad
1Ka Bilidad onɛ an Suh nid la lɛbis ye,
2“Fʋ ye fʋ zaŋ saŋa wala pian'?
Fʋ pian'ad la nwɛnɛ sisi'em nɛ.
3Wina'am na mɔŋ bʋʋd sɔb bʋʋdɛɛ?
Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la na zan'as linɛ an sidaa?
4Fʋ biis la da tʋm bɛ'ɛdi pɔ'ɔg o la,
o pʋ yɔɔ ba, ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la sammɛɛ?
Ayei! O kʋ maal ala! 5Amaa fʋ ya'a sɔs Wina'am sʋŋir
ka fabili tis Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la ye o zɔmif nimbaanlig,
6fʋ ya'a an pʋʋg yinne sɔb ka pʋ mɔr gba'arɛ,
hali baa di ya'a an si'em wʋsa
Wina'am mɛŋ na lɛbisi fʋ zi'eli fʋ zi'esimin.
7Fʋn daa pin'il si'em bi'ela la,
fʋ mɔrim na galis hali saŋa kanɛ kenna la.
8Bu'osim zʋmaana banɛ gaad la yɛla,
ka fʋ na zamis ya'am ti yaanam san'an.
9Bɔzugɔ tinam anɛ bɛɛga-bɛɛga biis ka zi' si'el si'ela,
ka ti dabisa mɛ pʋ zem si'el dunia nwa' nii.
10Ti yaanam la kʋ pa'alif ka yɛlif linɛ bɛɛ?
Ba kʋ zaŋi ba mi'ilim pian'af ya'am pian'adɛɛ?
11Na'apu'a-kʋ-si'is-ku'om na nyaŋi yii
nɔbig ka li ka'anɛ zin'ima'asir zin'igaa?
Kɔlkantima na nɔbig zin'ikanɛ ka ku'om kae?
12Ba ya'a nan nɔbigid ka pʋ siak ki'ebɔ,
ba zɛndigidnɛ kʋdigid tɔ'ɔtɔ nwɛnɛ mɔɔd nɛ.
13Ala ka li aɛn nɛ banɛ tam Wina'am yɛla la.
Banɛ ba'a kae nɛ Wina'am la ti'ir na ba'as yɔri.
14On zaŋ o ti'iri niŋ si'el la ka' paŋa,
on ti'e si'el la nwɛnɛ silinsi'ipaanlʋŋ nɛ.
15O dɛlnɛ o silinsi'ipaanlʋŋ la ka li kɛnsig
ka o mak ye o gammi li ka li tɔnsig.
16O nwɛnɛ mɔɔdi na bɛ nintaŋin ka ba dɔn'ɔsid ka ku'om wʋm,
ka li tɛɛn gilig lɔmbɔn'ɔg;
17ka li nya'a tɔɔn gilig tampiins nɛ kuga
ye li nyɛ zin'isʋŋ.
18Amaa ba ya'a vuoɛn li,
hali sɔ' pʋ lɛn tɛnr on bɛɛn zin'isi'a ya'asɛ.
19Fʋ nyɛ yaa, banɛ pʋ zɔt Wina'am la nyɔɔdi la,
sieba na kena n di'e ba zin'ig.
20Amaa gɔsima Wina'am kʋ maligim bas sida sɔba;
o mɛ kʋ sʋŋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dima.
21O na lɛn kɛ ka fʋ la'ad nɛ sumalisim,
hali fʋ na la' kaas kuŋ nɛ sumalisim ya'as.
22O na kɛ ka nyan di banɛ kisif la,
ka san'am pitɔɔg dim la ya'.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Job
1Ka Job lɛbis ye,
2 “Ɛɛn, m mi' ye li anɛ ala yim.
Ka ninsaal ye o niŋ wala kilim pʋpiel sɔb Wina'am tuonnɛ?
3Nid ya'a bɔɔd ye o nwa'as nɛ o,
o sɔb kʋ nyaŋi gandig o bu'osʋg yinne bu'osa tusir pʋʋginɛ.
4O ya'am la ka' makirɛ ka o paŋ ka' bɛnnɛ.
Anɔ'ɔn nam mi' mak o mɛŋ nɛ Wina'am ka di ya'annɛ?
5O sʋʋnr ɛɛn duoe ka o vɔn' zuoya lɔb,
hali ka zuoya la zi' onɛ niŋida.
6Onɛ dammid teŋgbauŋ la,
ka li mi'im zin'ig wʋsa.
7O ya'a bɔɔd, o tun'e kɛ ka nintaŋ da yii;
o mɛ tun'e kɛ ka nwadbibis kʋ nie.
8On ma'aa yadig saŋgbana la
ka kennɛ atɛuk ku'onwiis zug.
9 Onɛ maal nwadbibis buudi wʋsa zin'is atan'
ka sieba bɛ dagɔbʋg ka sieba bɛ teŋsʋk ka sieba mɛ bɛ datiuŋ;
o mɛ la'as Nɔnya'aŋ-nɛ-o-biis nɛ A-kidigim-bu'osnam.
10O tʋm nɛ tʋʋmnyalima banɛ ka ninsaal kʋ gban'e li gbinnɛ,
o kilima la ka' bɛnnɛ.
11Kassa, o dɔlli m san'anɛ gat, amaa m pʋ nyɛt oo;
o ya'a gat, m kʋ baŋ oo.
12O ya'a faaɛn si'eli gaadɛ, anɔ'ɔn na nyaŋi gu' o?
Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi bu'os o ye, ‘Bɔ ka fʋ niŋid ala?’
13Wina'am pʋ gu'ud o sʋnpɛɛnnɛ;
hali baa bʋnzɔtir linɛ bɛ ku'otita'arin buon Arahab la,
o sʋŋidib dig nɛ o nɔba teŋir.
14M ye m niŋ wala zab nɛ Wina'am?
M ye m nyɛ nɔɔr ya nwa'as nɛ o?
15Hali la'an nɛ man ka' taal la, m kʋ nyaŋi gandig oo;
m na nwɛ'ɛnɛ on kanɛ aan m sariakat la nu'ug
ye o zɔɔm nimbaanlig.
16Hali man ya'a buol o ka o siak,
mam pʋ tɛn'ɛs ye o na kɛligi m pian'adɛ.
17O na kɛ ka sisi'etita'ar nwɛ'ɛmi yutim
ka kɛ ka m fɛn'ɛd la maligim paas zaalim-zaalim.
18O kʋ kɛ ka m vʋ'ʋs baa bi'elaa
amaa ka kpɛm paasidim tɔɔg.
19Li ya'a anɛ paŋaa,
onɛ an paŋ tita'ar sɔb;
bɛɛ li ya'a anɛ sariakadib,
anɔ'ɔnɛ pa'an o sida suorɛ?
20Hali baa m ya'a ka' taalɛ,
mam mɛŋ nɔɔr kʋ tisim bʋʋdɛ;
m ya'a pʋn pʋ mɔr gbɛlʋŋɔ,
li nar ye m mɔr taal.
21La'an nɛ man ka' gbɛlʋŋ la,
m ba'a ka' nɛ m mɛŋ-mɛŋ yɛllɛ,
m mɛŋ gɔs ka m vʋm la anɛ yɔri.
22Man gɔs ka li wʋsa anɛ yinne, lin ka m ye,
‘O san'amid banɛ ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ nɛ banɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim wʋsa.’
23Yɛlmugusa ya'a ti kʋ ninkanɛ ka' taalɛ,
Wina'am la'ad o nɛ.
24Teŋ si'a ya'a li pitɔɔg dim nu'usin,
Wina'am lusid nɛ banɛ kad saria la nini.
Ya'a ka' onɛ, ka anɔ'ɔnɛ?
25Dunia nwa' pʋʋgin, m yʋma zɔt tɔ'ɔtɔ gat zɔzɔt,
ba zɔtnɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ gat ka sumalisim kae.
26Dabisa la zɔtnɛ nwɛnɛ anrʋŋ kanɛ gat tɔ'ɔtɔ nɛ,
ka nwɛnɛ silʋgʋ na naan agɔlli zuligid ye o gban'e nɔbil nɛ.
27M ya'a ye, ‘M na bas nyɔnyɔlʋg la wala,
ka basim nindalɔɔr la ka maal sumalisim.’
28La'an nɛ wala m namisʋg la kpɛn'ɛsidim nɛ dabiem,
bɔzugɔ m mi' ye fʋ kʋ tisim bʋʋdɛ.
29Ba pʋn gban'e ye m lu ya nwa',
ka bɔ ka m lɛn gɛɛndi m mɛŋ zaalim-zaalim?
30Hali baa m ya'a sʋʋ m mɛŋ nɛ ki'ibʋ nyain
ka pie m nu'us nɛ zɛɛm,
31la'an nɛ wala fʋ na lɔsim bian'arin
hali ka fubanɛ ka m yɛ la yaama yiim.
32O ka' ninsaal nwɛnɛ mam ka m na tun'e gandig oo,
bɛɛ ti mɔr taaba keŋ kɔɔtʋ nii.
33Yɛlmaan ya'a bɛɛn man nɛ on teŋsʋk
ka kpɛn'ɛsin o nu'ugʋ ti yɛl la ni,
34ka yisin balaar kanɛ ka Wina'am mɔri bʋ'ʋdim la,
ka dabiem kanɛ ka o kpɛn'ɛsidim la gaad,
35m naan pian'adin nɛ o ka dabiem kae.
Amaa din bɛ si'em nannanna nwa' la,
m kʋ nyaŋi pian' nɛ oo.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
1Ka Job lɛn yɛl ye,
Man ya'am yii m bɛllim nwa' nɛ;
kɛl ka m nyɔli m ya'am bɔɔd si'em
ka pian' nɛ m sʋntɔɔg.
2M na yɛl Wina'am ye: Da kʋʋsim bɛ'ɛdɛ,
amaa lɛɛ yɛlimi m taali an si'el kimm.
3Fʋn mugusid onɛ ka fʋ mɛŋ nu'ug maal la, li malisi fɔɔ?
Ka fʋ lɛɛ bas pitɔɔg dim ka ba tʋm bam bɔɔd si'el!
4Fʋ mɔri ninsaalib ninii?
Ninsaalibi nyɛt si'em la, ala ka fʋ mɛ nyɛtaa?
5Fʋ dabisa gimnɛ nwɛnɛ ninvʋsaal dabisaa?
Bɛɛ fʋ yʋma gimnɛ nwɛnɛ o yʋma?
6Ka dinzug ka fʋ vɛɛnsid ye fʋ nyɛɛm taal
ka ieedi m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛɛ?
7Fʋ la'am mi' ye m pʋ tʋm taalɛ,
ka mɛ mi' sʋ'ʋŋa ye sɔ' kae na faanmi fʋ nu'usinɛ.
8Fʋ mɛŋ-mɛŋ nu'us ka fʋ zaŋi maalim,
dinzug, fʋ na siaki san'ami maa?
9Tɛnr ye fʋnɛ ya'abim wʋʋ ya'ad nɛ.
Alazug, fʋ na kɛ ka m lieb titan ya'asɛɛ?
10Ka' fʋnɛ daa kpa'am wʋʋ bin'isim la niŋi m ma pʋʋgin,
ka maalim wʋʋ bam mɔr bin'isim maan waagazi si'em laa?
11Fʋnɛ daa zaŋ giinla tɔ'ɔŋi m kɔnba wʋsa
ka zaŋ niŋgbina nɛ niŋgbauŋʋ pilim.
12Fʋnɛ tisim vʋm nɛ nɔŋilim,
ka guri m siig.
13Amaa m mi' ye nɛ'ɛŋa ka fʋ daa su'a fʋ sʋʋnrin,
m mi' ye linɛ daa bɛɛ fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛrin:
14M ya'a tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd fʋ gɔsidim nɛ
ka kʋ kɛɛ m taali basɛ.
15M ya'a tʋm taal, yɛla na paam!
Hali m ya'a ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ, m kʋ nyaŋi ʋki m zug agɔlaa,
bɔzugɔ nyan nɛ fara ma'aa mɔrim.
16M ya'a ʋki m zug agɔla fʋ kemmim nɛ nwɛnɛ gbigim nɛ
ka lɛm pa'alimi fʋ paŋ la nyalima an si'em.
17Daar woo fʋ nyɛti m gbɛlima,
ka linzug ka fʋ sʋʋnr maligim pɛligid nɛ mam;
ka fʋ namisʋg gaad ala.
18“Bɔzug kimm ka fʋ kɛ ka ba du'a ma?
M ya'a da kpiinɛ m du'am saŋa ka sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ nyɛɛ ma di naan sɔn'ɔn.
19Ba ya'a pʋ du'anim,
bɛɛ m ya'a daa kpiinɛ m du'am saŋa
ka ba muminim gba li naan sɔn'ɔn.
20M dabisa dinɛ an bi'ela la pʋn pʋ naae nɛ laa?
Basim mam ka m nyɛ nimma'asim bi'ela
21ka nyaan kpii keŋ kpi'im teŋ
zin'ikanɛ ka' lɛbig naa
ka an lik biridi la.
22Teŋ kanɛ an lik biridi saŋa wʋsa
ka sʋnsa'aŋ nɛ tʋʋmyaalis galis
ka nɛɛsim gba an wʋʋ lik la.”

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Zofar
1Ka Zofar onɛ an Naama nid la lɛbis ye,
2“Nid na pian' anwana wʋsa ka ba kʋ lɛbisɛɛ?
Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye pian'ad bɛdegʋ na tisif bʋʋdɛɛ?
3Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ pian'ayɛɛd nwa' na kɛ ka nid mɔdigi sinnaa?
Fʋ na maan siaa ka ba kʋ zɛrigi fɔɔ?
4Fʋ yɛt Wina'am ye, ‘Man niŋi fʋ yɛlʋg la yadda ka gbɛlʋŋ kae,
ka bɛ nyain fʋ nini ni.’
5Amaa m naan bɔɔdin ye Wina'am mɛŋ-mɛŋ na gandig
ka ya'ae o nɔɔri pian' zɛrigif
6ka viigi pa'alif yɛlsu'ada linɛ yit ya'amin na
ka mɛ kɛ ka fʋ baŋ ye ya'am bɛ nɛ ka ya'am bɛ.
Baŋim ye Wina'am tami fʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la sieba yɛla nɛ gba.
7Fʋ na nyaŋi baŋ Wina'am nyalima gbinnɛɛ?
Fʋ na nyaŋi vɛɛnsi baŋ Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la zem si'em?
8Li dʋʋ gaad saŋgbana wʋsa,
ka bɔ kimm ka fʋ na tun'e niŋɛ?
Li zulimmi gat yaʋg,
ka fʋn mi' bɔ?
9Li wa'alim gat teŋgbauŋ
ka li labisim gat atɛuk.
10O ya'a zaŋi fʋ niŋ sanrega ni
ka mɔri fʋ dʋ kɔɔtʋ, anɔ'ɔnɛ na tun'e ki'is o?
11Bi'esʋg kae, o mi' pʋʋs ayi' dim
ka nyɛt banɛ tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd wʋsa.
12Zɔlʋg ya'a ti gban'e pian'ad gbinnɛɛ,
alaa bʋŋ na du'a ninsaal.
13La'an nɛ wala, fʋ ya'a dɔl o nɛ fʋ sʋʋnr wʋsa
ka tiɛn fʋ nu'ugʋ sɔs o,
14ka bas tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ bɛɛ fʋ sʋʋnrin la,
ka da siak ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd tʋmi fʋ yin ya'asɛ,
15ala ka fʋ na duoe fʋ zug agɔla ka nyan kae,
fʋ na zi'e kiŋ-kiŋ ka dabiem kae.
16Fʋ na tami fʋ yɛla wʋsa,
ka li nwɛnɛ saa nii gaadnɛ.
17Fʋ bɛllim na nie nyain nwɛnɛ nintaŋ nɛ
ka bʋnkanɛ an liki fʋ bɛllimin la
na nie nyain wʋʋ bɛogʋn sɔɔnrim nɛ.
18Fʋ na zin' ka dabiem kae, fʋn mɔr ti'ir la zug.
Fʋ na gɔs gɔbʋg nɛ diiug wʋsa
ka li anɛ nimma'asim ma'aa ka dabiem kae.
19Fʋ na diginɛ gbis ka onɛ na vɔlisif kae.
Nidib bɛdegʋ na bɔɔd sʋŋiri fʋ san'an.
20Amaa pitɔɔg dim ti'ir na bɔdig ka kɛɛ ba
ka ba zi' ban zɔti ken si'ela,
ba ti'ir la na ba'as nɛ kumin.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
16just as he rules over liars
and those they lie to.
17God shames counselors,
turns judges into fools,
18and makes slaves of kings.
19God removes priests and others
who have great power—
20he confuses wise,
experienced advisors,
21puts mighty kings to shame,
and takes away their power.
22God turns darkness to light;
23he makes nations strong,
then shatters their strength.
24God strikes their rulers senseless,
then leaves them to roam
through barren deserts,
25lost in the dark, staggering
like someone drunk.
translation_text:
Job
1Ka Job lɛbis ye,
2“Waii, bi'esʋg kae, ya sid anɛ a-mi'-wʋsa dim,
ya ya'a kpii, ya'am mɛ kpiya!
3Amaa baŋimi ka m mɔr ya'am nwɛnɛ yanam nɛ;
sida, ya pʋ gati ma.
Anɔ'ɔnɛ zi' yanamɛ yɛt si'el la wʋsa?
4M yʋ'ʋn lieb nɛ bʋnla'adiri tisim zuanam,
hali baa man buol Wina'am ka o gandig la.
La'an nɛ man an pʋpiel ka ka' gbɛlʋŋ la,
m lieb nɛ bʋnla'adir!
5Banɛ ka si'el-si'el pʋ paki ba la ziemid banɛ bɛ yɛla ni,
ka tusid banɛ sadigidi bɔɔd liig la.
6Bɔɔ kɛ ka banɛ faand mɔr yɔlisim?
Bɔ ka sɔ' pʋ daamid banɛ kis Wina'am la?
Ka la'am yɛl ye Wina'am bɛ nɛ ba nu'usin.
7Bu'osim bʋnkɔnbid ka ba pa'alif,
bɛɛ niis banɛ ian'ad agɔla la ka ba na yɛlif;
8bɛɛ fʋn pian' tis teŋgbauŋ la ka o na pa'alif,
bɛɛ zimi banɛ bɛ atɛukʋn la ka ba na yɛlif dinɛ bɛ.
9Banɛ ka m kaal nwa' wʋsa
mi' ye Zugsɔb la tʋm nɛ'ɛŋa nwa'.
10O nu'ugin ka bʋnvʋr wʋsa bɛ,
hali nɛ saalib wʋsa vʋm.
11Bɔzugɔ, tʋbiri wɛligid pian'ad
wʋʋ zilimi lɛmmid diib si'em la, bɛɛ m ma'aanɛɛ?
12Mɛ ya'am bɛ nɛ zuobpielim dim ni?
Li ka'anɛ kʋdigire an baŋirɛɛ?
13Ya'am nɛ paŋ anɛ Wina'am din;
mi'ilim nɛ baŋir mɛ anɛ o din.
14O ya'a nwa'ae, anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi mɛ'?
Ka ninkanɛ ka o yɔɔ o sanrega ni, anɔ'ɔn na nyaŋi yis o?
15O ya'a gu' saa lɛbis,
teŋgbauŋ la liebidnɛ kpi'emisi kpɛ'ɛŋ bar-bar.
O ya'a yɔ'ɔg saa bas
li na nii di bʋn linɛ wʋsa bɛ teŋgbauŋ la zug.
16Paŋ nɛ nyaŋir anɛ o din;
banɛ pan'asid nidib nɛ banɛ ka ba pan'asid wʋsa anɛ o din.
17Onɛ kɛt ka mi'ilim dim lieb zaalim
ka sariakatib lieb zɔn.
18Onɛ yɛɛgid na'anam banaas
ka zaŋid pien fuugʋ lɔɔdi ba sies wʋʋ yammis nɛ.
19Onɛ yisid maanmaannibi ba kpi'euŋin
ka kɛt ka paŋ dim lieb zaalim.
20Onɛ kɛt ka nidibi niŋ sieba yadda la lɛbi fɔn baanlimm
ka kɛt ka kpɛɛmnam zi' sida nɛ ziri bakida.
21Onɛ diisid na'ayikpɛm nyan
ka kɛt ka paŋ dim liebid zaalim.
22Onɛ nied dinɛ wʋsa bɛ likin
ka kɛt ka lik liebid nɛɛsim.
23Onɛ kɛt ka tɛɛns nɔbigid onɛ lɛn san'amidi ba,
onɛ yaligid tɛɛns, onɛ lɛn widigidi ba.
24Onɛ mɔŋid tɛɛns na'anam ya'am;
ka kɛt ka ba gɔɔndi gin yɔɔg-yɔɔg.
25Ba babinnɛ likin ka nɛɛsim kae
ka kɛ ka ba gɛnnim wʋʋ danuudib nɛ.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Know and Understand
1I know and understand
every bit of this.
2None of you are smarter
than I am;
there's nothing you know
that I don't.
3But I prefer to argue my case
with God All-Powerful—
4you are merely useless doctors,
who treat me with lies.
5The wisest thing you can do
is to keep quiet 6and listen
to my argument.
7Are you telling lies for God
8and not telling the whole truth
when you argue his case?
9If he took you to court,
could you fool him,
just as you fool others?
10If you were secretly unfair,
he would correct you,
11and his glorious splendor
would make you terrified.
12Your wisdom and arguments
will blow away like dust.
Be Quiet While I Speak
13Be quiet while I speak,
and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
1Ka Job lɛn keŋ tuonnɛ yɛl ye,
“Kɛlli baanlimm, ka man nini pʋn nyɛɛ li wʋsa,
ka m tʋba wʋm ka gban'e li gbin.
2Yanamɛ mi' si'el la wʋsa mam mɛ mi' mɛn;
ya pʋ gati ma.
3Amaa m sʋnf bɔɔdim anɛ ye m pian' tis Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la,
ka tu'asi m yɛl la gbinnɛ tis Wina'am.
4Dama'am ma'aa ka ya ma'adi tabin mam;
ya nwɛnɛ tima dim banɛ kʋ nyaŋi ti'eb nida.
5Ya ya'a sinni ya nɔɔr baanlimm,
li na kɛ ka ya nwɛnɛ ya'am dim nɛ.
6Kɛlisimi ka m yisi m nɔɔr pian'ʋk;
wʋmminɛ m fabʋlʋg.
7Ya niŋ wala mɔr Wina'am yʋ'ʋri pian'ad bugusim pian'adɛ?
Ya niŋ wala mɔr o yʋ'ʋri ma'ad dama'am?
8Ya na nyaŋi mɔr baregaŋ man nɛ Wina'am teŋsʋkɔɔ?
Bɛɛ ya zabi tis o?
9O ya'a vɛɛnsi ya sʋnya gɔs, li na an sʋ'ʋŋaa?
Ya na nyaŋi pan'as o nwɛnɛ yanamɛ pan'asid saalib si'em laa?
10Ayei! Ya ya'a su'a mɔr baregaŋ,
o na zɛrigi ya.
11O na'am girima la pʋ kpɛn'ɛsidi ya dabiem?
Ya pʋ zɔt dabiem nɛ on an si'em laa?
12Ya siilima la anɛ zaalim nwɛnɛ tampɛligim nɛ;
yanamɛ mɔr si'eli gu'udi ya mɛŋ la anɛ ya'ad,
li sid kʋ ya'as nwa'arɛ.
13Fɔɔnmɛ baanlimm ka kɛ ka m pian';
ka linɛ na niŋ, lin niŋ.
14Bɔzug ka m mɔr nyɔvʋri nwɛ'ɛdi kpɛɛsid wʋʋ siya'ar
ka mɔri m vʋm maan galima?
15Hali o ya'a bɔɔd, on kʋʋmim; ka m ti'ir nan kpɛm bɛ nɛ o ni.
M na tu'asi m yɛla wʋsa o tuon.
16M mi' sʋ'ʋŋa ye m sʋnkpi'euŋ la na kɛ ka m paam faangir,
bɔzugɔ onɛ zi' Wina'am pʋn kʋ li'el o san'anɛ!
17Wina'am, kɛlisimi m pian'ad nwa' sʋ'ʋŋa;
kɛl ka man yɛt si'el la kpɛn' fʋ tʋbirin.
18Man maal siri ye m tu'asi fʋ m yɛl la,
m mi' ye m na di bʋʋd.
19Sɔ' mɔr antu'a kanɛ na zɛrig mam bɛɛ?
Alaa m na sin baanlimm hali ti paae m kum.
20Wina'am, niŋim bʋnama ayi' nwa' ma'aa tisim,
ka m kʋ lɛn su'a m mɛŋi fʋ san'anɛ:
21Da lɛn nɔki fʋ kpa'asiri namisi ma,
mɛ da lɛn vɔlisidim nɛ fʋ kpi'euŋ la.
22Ala ka fʋ ya'a buolim, m na siak,
bɛɛ fʋn kɛ ka m pian' ka fʋ gandig.
23M taal nɛ m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kal aan ala?
Pa'alimi m gbɛlʋŋ nɛ m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi zu'oe si'em.
24Bɔ ka fʋ zan'as ye fʋ kʋ gɔsi ma
ka zaŋim ka m liebi fʋ dataa?
