25Fʋ na namis man kanɛ nwɛnɛ vaung ka sisi'em da'ad laa?
Fʋ na kati dɔl udugɔɔ?
26Fʋ sɔbnɛ yɛltɔɔdi gi' mam
ka kɛ ka m namisidi m biilimin sa tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.
27 Fʋ ba'a m nɔba nɛ ba'an;
fʋ guri m suoya ka gɔsid
ye fʋ baŋ man ken si'el wʋsa.
28Ala ka ninsaal bɛdigid nwɛnɛ bʋmpɔn'ɔsir nɛ,
ka nwɛnɛ fuug ka sibig mu'anɛ.”

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
1Job da lɛn yɛl ye,
“Ninsaal mɛkama dunia nwa' pʋʋgin dabisa anɛ bi'ela
ka pɛ'ɛl nɛ yɛla.
2O duodnɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ nwɛnɛ mɔpuum nɛ,
ka li pʋ yuugɛ ka o zɛndig
ka mɛlim tɔ'ɔtɔ wʋʋ ma'asim tulignɛ.
3Wina'am, fʋ na san'ami fʋ nini gɔsid ninkan buudii?
Fʋ na mɔr oŋa sɔbi fʋ tuon na ye fʋ kad o sariaa?
4Anɔ'ɔn na nyaŋi yis bʋn dinɛ an nyain dian'ad pʋʋginɛ?
Sida, li sɔb kae!
5Fʋ pʋn gban'e ninsaal nyɔvʋr bɛnnɛ naae;
fʋ mɛ gban'e on na vʋe nwadis si'em
ka o kʋ tʋʋgi li bɛnnɛ.
6Alazug, yisimi fʋ nini ka bas o baanlimm,
ka o di nyɛlʋg o vʋm dabisa la pʋʋgin nwɛnɛ onɛ tʋm lɛbir nɛ.
7Hali tiig gba mɔr ti'ir,
bɔzugɔ ba ya'a nwaae li ka bas gbi'ir, li na lɛm bus ya'as
ka li bulpaala la kʋ sʋʋgɛ.
8Hali li nya'a ya'a kʋdig si'em wʋsa,
ka li gbi'ir la kpi teŋin,
9la'an nɛ wala li ya'a wʋm ku'om nyuug, li na bus
ka li bula la na nwɛnɛ tiigi nar ye li an si'em.
10Amaa ninsaal ya'a kpi o sigid nɛ teŋin;
o bɛn ya'a ti paae ka o vʋ'ʋsʋm naae ka o gaad sɔee.
11Nwɛnɛ ku'om ɛɛn naae atɛukʋn si'em la
bɛɛ ku'om ɛɛnti kpiɛn kɔlʋgin ka li kʋdigi tans si'em la,
12ala ka ninsaal kpiid ka pʋ duoda.
Ya'a ka' saazugʋ na ti gaadɛ, saalib kʋ maligim lɛb naa
bɛɛ nie gbɛɛm pʋʋginɛ.
13Fʋ ya'a pʋn su'anim kpi'im teŋ
ka lusinim ka fʋ sʋnpɛɛn la gaadin, li pʋ sɔn'oe yaa?
Fʋ ya'a zi'elin saŋa
ka lɛn tiɛn m yɛla ya'asɛ!
14Ninsaal ya'a kpi o na lɛn vʋ'ʋg ya'asɛɛ?
Li ya'a aan ala m na mɔdig m tʋʋm kpi'ema la wʋsa ni
hali ka ti paam vʋ'ʋsʋm.
15Fʋ na buolim ka m na siak;
fʋ sʋnf na malis nɛ man onɛ ka fʋ maal nɛ fʋ nu'us la.
16Asida, fʋ na gur man sʋ'ʋŋa saŋa wʋsa
ka kʋ lɛn gi'ennɛ m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi zem si'em.
17Fʋ na zaŋi m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi su'a bɔto ni lɔ,
ka pin' m taal wʋsa.
18Amaa nwɛnɛ zuoya birigidi lit
ka kugbɛda vurigid si'em la,
19ka lɛn nwɛnɛ ku'om dit kuga
ka ku'okanɛ zɔt pied tanni ken si'em la,
ala ka fʋ san'amid ninsaal ti'ir.
20Fʋ nyaŋ o vuguri ka o mɛlim;
fʋ tiak o nindaa nwɛnɛ onɛ kpi nɛ ka o gaad sa.
21Nidib ya'a na'asid o biis, o zi'isigɛ;
ba ya'a mɛ pɔ'ɔgidi ba, o pʋ nyɛtaa.
22O mi'inɛ o mɛŋ niŋgbina zabir ma'aa
ka kaasid o mɛŋ yɛla ma'aa.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Elifaz
1Ka Elifaz onɛ an Teman nid la lɛbis ye,
2“Di nar ye ya'am sɔb lɛbis pian'ad ka pʋ tɛn'ɛsɛɛ,
bɛɛ o pɛ'ɛl o mɛŋ nɛ baŋir linɛ nwɛnɛ pɛbisimm?
3Ya'am sɔb na nwa'asid nɛ pian'ayɛɛdɛɛ,
bɛɛ o tu'asid pian'ad kanɛ ka' vɔɔnrɛ?
4Amaa fʋ pʋn pʋ lɛn zɔt Wina'am
ka mɛ kɛ ka nidib kʋ lɛn tis o girima.
5Fʋ nɔɔr pian'ad pa'annɛ fʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi zem si'em;
fʋ mɔri nɔmalisim pan'asid nidib.
6Fʋ mɛŋ nɔɔri ditif ka ka' manɛ,
fʋ mɛŋ pian'adi zɛrigidif.
7Ba da dɛŋi du'anɛ fʋn yiiga bɛɛ?
Wina'am da maan zuoya la fʋ da bɛɛ?
8Wina'am da gban'ad on na maal si'em la, fʋ da wʋm yaa?
Fʋnɛ fʋ kɔn'ɔkɔn' mɔr dunia la wʋsa ya'am?
9Fʋ mi' bɔ ka tinam zi'?
Ya'am gɔnlʋŋ bɔ ka fʋ mɔr ka tinam pʋ mɔra?
10Tinam ya'am la yit nɛ zugpielim dimin na,
ba da bɛ hali ka fʋ saam nan kae.
11Bɔzug ka fʋ zan'asid sumbʋgʋsʋm linɛ ka Wina'am tisidif la?
La'an nɛ tinamɛ pian' baanlimm tisif la wʋsaa?
12Bɔzug ka fʋ kɛ ka fʋ sʋʋnr duoe wala?
Bɔzug ka fʋ nini mu'oe hali
13ka fʋ sʋʋnr duoe nɛ Wina'am
ka fʋ pian'ad pian' linɛ pʋ nari tisid o?
14 Ninsaal sid na nyaŋi an nyainnɛɛ?
Bɛɛ pu'a du'a sɔ' na tun'e an pʋpielaa?
15Wina'am ya'a pʋ niŋ o mɛŋ-mɛŋ maliaknam yadda,
hali ka arezana ka' nyain o nini nii,
16ka ninsaal onɛ an pitɔɔg nɛ bugusim sɔb
ka nuud tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd wʋʋ ku'om la yʋ'ʋsɛ?
17Job, kɛlisim sʋ'ʋŋa ka m tu'asi pa'alif;
kɛl ka m yɛlif man nyɛ si'el.
18Banɛ an ya'am dim pa'alim sida
linɛ ka ba zamisi ba yaanam san'an ka pʋ su'a si'ela.
19Bama ka ba pɔnsi zaŋ teŋ la tisi ba
ka saan baa yinne pʋ gɛndigi ba sʋʋginɛ.
20Pʋtɔɔg sɔb na namis hali nɛ o nyɔvʋr bɛn.
Onɛ bɔɔd zaba la kʋ yuug dunia nwa' nii.
21Tʋkpiidʋg ma'aa ka o tʋba wʋm
ka li kpɛn'ɛsid o dabiem.
Saŋkanɛ ka o tɛn'ɛs ye si'el wʋsa an sʋ'ʋŋa la,
li saŋa ka faandib libigid o.
22O pʋ mɔr ti'ir ye o na nyaŋi zɔɔ yi likinɛ,
bɔzugɔ zaba sʋ'ʋg dignɛ gur o.
23O yiridnɛ gin, ka na ba'asi kilim zʋʋnd diib.
O mi' ye lik dabisir la na paae o.
24Sʋnsa'aŋ nɛ tɔɔg dabiem mɔr o
ka libig o nwɛnɛ na'abi yi tanp ye o zab nɛ o.
25Li anɛ on mɔr nyɛɛsim nɛ Wina'am
ka zabid nɛ Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la zug.
26O maal tʋbzian'asim
ka zaŋ o zaba la'akpi'ema zabid nɛ Wina'am.
27La'an nɛ on nɔb ka kpɛnda yi,
ka o siaa nɔbi pɛ'ɛl la,
28o na bɛ teŋ kanɛ an dabɔɔd,
nɛ ya' banɛ an wɛn ma'aa ka nidib kae.
29O kʋ lɛn an bʋmmɔra, bɔzugɔ o mɔrim la na naae
ka kʋ lɛn yaligi pɛ'ɛl teŋ la wʋsaa.
30O kʋ nyaŋi zɔɔ yi likin la;
bugum na zɛɛlim o ka o zɛndig wʋʋ tiig vaand nɛ.
31O mid ka o ma'aa o mɛŋi ti'e linɛ ka' vɔɔnrɛ,
bɔzugɔ o kʋ nyɛ sʋŋiri yii aninaa.
32O saŋa kʋ paae ka o pʋn zɛndig
ka o wila kʋ lɛn sɔbig lim-lim nɛ.
33O na nwɛnɛ tiig wil kanɛ ka ba fanri li wala pilɛɛd,
ka nwɛnɛ olif tikanɛ puum sʋʋg wʋsa.
34Nimbanɛ pʋ zɔt Wina'am na kilim kʋnduada,
bugum mɛ na di banɛ nɔŋ filʋŋ la ya'.
35Ba gban'adnɛ yɛla pʋʋg ka du'ad tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd;
ba pʋʋs anɛ dama'am ma'aa.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Job
1Ka Job lɛbis ye,
2“Man wʋm yɛlbama buudi hali bɛdegʋ;
ya ma' ye ya bɛlisidim nɛ
ka lɛɛ maligim kpɛn'ɛsidim yɛla ni!
3Ya yɛtim ye, ‘Fʋ pian'ayɛɛd la ka' naarɛɛ?
Bɔ kimm ka fʋ kirid ye fʋ lɛbisi ti pian'ad la?’
4Ya ya'a aan wʋʋ man an si'em nwa',
mam mɛ naan tun'e pian' tisi ya wʋʋ yanamɛ pian'ad si'em tisidim la.
5M naan nɔkini m nɔɔr nwa' pian' kpɛmisini ya,
ka bʋgʋlinɛ ya sʋʋnr nɛ m nɔŋgban pian'ad.
6La'an nɛ ala m ya'a pian', m niŋgbina zabir la kʋ gaadɛ;
m ya'a mɛ sinni m nɔɔr li kʋ gaadɛ.
7Ya'a an sida, Wina'am, fʋ kɛ ka m tadignɛ hali,
fʋ widigi m yir la wʋsa.
8Fʋ kɛ ka m lieb giinla nɛ kɔnba gʋllim,
ka li an kasɛt ye man tʋmnɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.
9Wina'am sʋʋnr pɛlig nɛ mam ka o aansidi m zɔra-zɔra.
O nyiidim nɛ hali;
m dataa la nini mu'oe nɛ mam hali.
10Saalib la'adim nɛ ka nɔkimi maali ba bʋnla'adir;
ba lɔbidim tampian'as
ka maal nɔɔr yinne kisigim.
11Wina'am zaŋimi tis nimbɛ'ɛdnam,
ka lɔbimi bas pitɔɔg dim nu'ugin.
12M daa bɛ nɛ nimma'asimin ka o kpɛn kʋʋm vuguri;
o gban'anɛ m niŋgɔɔnr ka tɛbigimɛ tud sa ka m kɔ' bur-bur.
O zaŋim nɛ ka m an wʋʋ sian'arin bʋnkɔnbʋg
13ka tɔɔndim nɛ piema zin'is wʋsa.
O kʋnsim hali paae m sianini ka pʋ zɔt nimbaanliga
ka m ziim yii pʋbid teŋin.
14Daar woo o sʋnf duodi nɛ man
ka o katimi gin wʋʋ zabzabid nɛ.
15Man sɛn sʋnsa'aŋ fuugʋ libili m niŋgbina,
ka zin' teŋin ka m ti'ir kae.
16Man kaas nɛ ka m nini mu'oe,
m nini la fʋlisi fʋlisnɛ.
17Amaa la'an nɛ wala, m mi' ye m nu'us ka' dian'adɛ,
ka m winsɔsʋg an sʋ'ʋŋa.
18Ateŋaa, da dii m ziim,
da kɛ ka m fabʋlʋg nwa' lieb zaalim.
19 Hali nannankaŋa nwa', m kasɛta sɔb bɛ nɛ arezana ni;
ɛɛn, m nu'unwɛ'ɛd la bɛ nɛ saazug.
20M ninta'am litnɛ bɔr-bɔr Wina'am tuon
ka m zuanam maannim siaa.
21M bɔɔd ye m sʋndaan naan bɛɛ nwɛ' Wina'am nu'ugʋ tisim
nwɛnɛ nid nɛ o zua nɛ.
22Yʋma fiin nwa' kpɛlim
ka mam na dɔl suokanɛ ka' lɛbig na la keŋ.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
1Ka Job yʋ'ʋn yɛl ye,
“Man vʋm la naae ya,
m dabisa pʋ lɛn lalla,
yaʋg ya'anɛ nɔɔri gurim.
2Asida sida banɛ la'ad mam la galis nɛ;
dinzugɔ m na kpɛn gɔsid banɛ pɛligidi m sʋnf la.
3O m Wina'am, kpɛn'ɛsimi fʋ nu'ugʋ m yɛl nwa' ni
ka sɔ' kae na zi'enɛ m nya'aŋa.
4Fʋnɛ lusi ba pʋtɛnda ka ba kʋ gban'e si'el-si'el gbinnɛ;
alazug, da kɛ ka ba di ya'annɛ.
5Ninkanɛ yii o zua nya'aŋ ye o di'e yɔɔd,
o sɔb biis na ba'as yɔri.
6Wina'am kɛnɛ ka man lieb bʋnla'adiri tis nidib wʋsa,
ba tʋbisidnɛ nintɔɔndi matti m nindaa.
7M sʋnsa'aŋ la kɛnɛ ka m nini sɔbid,
ka m niŋgbina naae kpɛlim kɔnba ma'aa.
8Pʋpielnam ya'a nyɛ nɛ'ɛŋa, li zabidi banɛ;
ka banɛ ka' taal sʋʋnr pɛlig nɛ banɛ pʋ zɔt Wina'am.
9La'an nɛ wala, pʋpielim dim na kpɛn zi'e ba sida ni,
ka banɛ nu'usi an nyain la maligin nyɛ kpi'euŋ.
10Amaa ya wʋsa lɛm na! Yanamɛ pian' si'el la,
maligim pian' ya'as!
Nɛ lin wʋsa m kʋ nyɛ ya'am sɔbi ya sʋʋginɛ.
11M dabisa gaad ya ka m gban'ar wʋsa san'am
ala ka m ya'amlɛog pʋn lɛn kae nɛ si'ela.
12Nimbama nwa' nɔknɛ yʋ'ʋŋ ka li lieb nintaŋ;
ka zaŋ lik ka li lieb nɛɛsim.
13M ti'ir wʋsa bɛ nɛ kpi'im teŋ,
zin'ikanɛ ka m na diginɛ gbis likin.
14M na buol Ayaʋg ye, ‘M saam’,
ka buol bʋnvʋya banɛ diti m niŋgbina la
ye, ‘M ma’, bɛɛ ‘M taʋn’.
15M ti'ir bɛ yaanɛ kimm nɛ?
Anɔ'ɔn na gɔsi nyɛ ti'iri tisi ma?
16Ti'ir na dɔllimi sig yaʋgʋnɛɛ?
Li na diginɛ m san'an kpi'im teŋaa?”

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Bilidad
1Ka Bilidad onɛ an Suh teŋin nid la lɛbis ye,
2“Bɔ saŋa ka fʋ ye fʋ bas pian'adɛ?
Zuligimi ya'am, ka kɛlis ka ti yʋ'ʋn pian'.
3Bɔ ka ya gɔs ka ti nwɛnɛ niigi ya nini ni
wʋʋ ti ka' ya'am baa bi'ela?
4Job, fʋ sʋʋnri duoe ka fʋ tɔɔnsi fʋ mɛŋi zɔrisi zɔris la!
Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye saalib wʋsa na zɔ ka bas dunia la fʋ sʋnpɛɛn la zugɔɔ?
Bɛɛ fʋ yɛl ye tampiins na vɔn?
5 Ba kpiis pitɔɔg sɔb fitir;
o bugum la kpiisnɛ ka pʋ lɛn ditta.
6Nɛɛsim dinɛ bɛɛ o dɔɔgin la lieb lik;
ka o fitir mɛ kpiis.
7O tadig nɛ ka pʋ tun'e yakid nɔbir nɛ kpi'euŋɔ;
o mɛŋ bugusim ya'am la dii o.
8O mɛŋ nɔba mɔr o kpɛn' zimi zulisin
ka di gban'e o.
9Baŋ gban'e o nɔbkpansinkpanda
ka bɛndig la mɔr o kiŋ-kiŋ.
10Ba su'a bɛnd bɛndig teŋin gur o;
baŋ dig o suorin.
11On ken zin'isi'a wʋsa
dabiem mɔr o nɛ.
12Kɔ'ɔm tadig o;
ka san'auŋ gur o ye o li.
13Ban'abɛ'ɛdi tiigi o niŋgbina wʋsa,
ka kɛ ka o nu'us nɛ o nɔba pun'oe.
14Ba yis o, o yir kanɛ ka o bɛ ka daauŋ kae la nii
mɔr o keŋ Na'aba Akum san'an.
15Bugumpielim ma'aa bɛɛ o dɔɔgin;
ka kidibir dinɛ dit bugum gilig o yir la.
16O nya'a kʋdignɛ teŋin,
ka o wila la agɔla ziank.
17Sɔ' pʋ lɛn tɛnri o yɛla dunia nwa' pʋʋginɛ,
ka o yʋ'ʋr bɔdig teŋ la zug.
18Ba kad o yis nɛɛsimin kpɛn'ɛs likin
ka mɛlis o dunia nwa' ni.
19O kʋ mɔr yaas o nidib sʋʋginɛ,
o nid baa yinne lɛn kae on da bɛ teŋ si'a la.
20Yɛl kanɛ paae o la kɛnɛ ka banɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la sʋnf vuoɛn;
ka dabiem gban'e banɛ bɛ ya-tuona la.
21Asida, lin niŋid banɛ pʋ zɔt Wina'am si'em la;
ala ka banɛ zi' Wina'am la bɛllim aɛn.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Job
1Ka Job lɛbisi yɛl ye,
2“Bʋndaar ka ya na basi m daamʋgɔ?
Ya nɔɔr pian'ad kɛ ka m kɔnba kɔɔd bur-bur!
3Nɔɔrim bʋpiiga nwa' ka ya pɔ'ɔgim;
ya tʋmim bɛ'ɛd hali, ka nyan kae.
4Di ya'a an sida ye mam yidig nɛ,
yanam kɛl ka li paanɛ mam ma'aa.
5Ya tɛn'ɛs ye ya sɔn'oe mam nɛ,
ka gɔs ka yɛlbanɛ paae mam la pa'al ye m tʋm nɛ taal.
6Ya zi' ye li anɛ Wina'am tʋm mam nɛ'ɛŋaa?
Onɛ nɔk o baŋi bɛndim.
7La'an nɛ man kaas ye, ‘O tʋmim dinɛ pʋ nar la,’
m pʋ nyɛ gandigirɛ.
La'an nɛ man ye ba sʋŋimim la,
sɔ' pʋ tisim bʋʋdɛ.
8O giŋim nɛ ka m kʋ nyaŋi gaadɛ;
o kɛ ka m suor wʋsa an lik.
9O yɛɛgi m girima ka basim zaalim
ka yisi m na'am zupibigi m zugin.
10O tɔɔnsi tɔɔnsim nɛ zin'is wʋsa;
ka vuoɛn m ti'ir wʋʋ tiig ka ba vuoɛn nɛ.
11Wina'am sʋnf pɛlig nɛ mam hali;
ka o kaalimi paas o dataas.
12O zabzabidib la la'as ye ba zab nɛ m;
ba lɔbi giligim zin'is wʋsa.
13Wina'am kɛnɛ ka m mɛŋ yidim basim;
m lieb nɛ saanne tis banɛ mi'im.
14Ka m sizuop zɔ ka basim
ka m zuanam wʋsa tami m yɛla.
15Banɛ an saam man yin, nɛ m tʋmtʋm pu'ab,
gɔsid mam ka m nwɛnɛ saan nɛ.
16M buoli m yammʋg ka o zan'as siakir;
hali m bɛllim o ka o sin.
17M vʋ'ʋsʋm nyuusidnɛ pɔn'ɔsʋgʋ m pu'a nyɔnya ni;
ka m ba'abiis pʋ bɔɔd ye ba li'eli ma.
18Hali bibibis nini kpɛn' mam nɛ;
ka ba mɔrimi la'ad.
19M zuamɛŋa gɔs man nɛ zaalim;
banɛ ka m nɔŋ la yʋ'ʋn kisigim nɛ.
20M yʋ'ʋn lieb nɛ kɔnba ma'aa;
di kpɛlim bi'ela ka m kpiin.
21Zɔminim nimbaanlig, m zuanama, zɔminim nimbaanlig,
bɔzugɔ, Wina'am nwɛ' m nɛ o mɛŋ-mɛŋ nu'ug.
22Wala ka ya namisidim nwɛnɛ Wina'am namisidim si'em la?
Yanamɛ namisim si'em la pʋ sia'alɛɛ?
23M pian'ad nwa' ya'a sɔbidinnɛ digin,
ba naan sɔbi niŋin gbauŋ pʋʋgin.
24Bɛɛ ba naan zaŋin lieŋe ki'e li tabil tampiing zug
ka li na kpɛm bɛ saŋa wʋsa.
25M mi' ye m nu'unwɛ'ɛd la vʋe
ka na duoe ka zabi m yɛla.
26Hali baa m niŋgbauŋ nwa' ya'a pun'oe,
la'an nɛ ala m na nyɛ Wina'am nɛ m nini nwa'.
27Mam mɛŋ-mɛŋ na nyɛɛ o
nɛ m nini nwa' ka ka' sɔ'ɔɔ.
M sʋnf lɔnɛ gur saŋa la!
28Ya ya'a yɛl ye, ‘Ti na kpɛn namisid Job
bɔzugɔ, yɛla nwa' wʋsa yinɛ o san'an na.’
29M yɛti ya ye ya zɔm kum
bɔzugɔ Wina'am sʋnpɛɛn ziidnɛ san'auŋ na,
ala ka ya na baŋ ye Wina'am sariakadib sid bɛ.”

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
Zofar
1Ka Zofar onɛ an Naama nid la lɛbis ye,
2“Job, fʋ pian'ad la daamim sʋʋnr
ka li an tilas ye m lɛbisif.
3Fʋn pian'am pian'asi'a la wʋsa anɛ tʋ'ʋd,
amaa m mi' mam na lɛbisif si'em.
4Asida, fʋ pʋm mi' din da an si'em kʋdimin sa;
saŋkanɛ ka ba da zaŋ ninsaali niŋ dunia zug la,
5ye ninvʋbɛ'ɛd wʋsa sumalisim pʋ ya'asid naarɛ
ka banɛ kis Wina'am kʋ nwɛ' nyɔ'ɔgʋ yuugɛ.
6Hali baa o dʋ'ʋsi-m-mɛŋ ya'a bɔɔd din duoe paae arezana,
ka o wa'am hali ka o zug paae saŋgbana ni,
7o na pun'oe nwɛnɛ o mɛŋ bin nɛ,
ka banɛ daa mi' o na bu'osid ye, ‘O bɛ yaanɛ?’
8O na mɛlim nwɛnɛ zaansʋŋ nɛ ka ba kʋ lɛn nyɛɛ o;
o na bɔdig sɔee.
9Nif kanɛ da nyɛt o la kʋ lɛn nyɛɛ o;
on da bɛ zin'isi'a la o kʋ lɛm bɛɛ ani.
10O biis na yɔ dinɛ wʋsa an nɔŋ dim bʋn la lɛbis;
ka o mɛŋ mɛ lɛbis mɔrim kanɛ wʋsa ka o zaŋ la.
11Kpi'euŋ kanɛ ka o da mɔr o dasannimin la
na lɛbi dig titanin.
12-13O zaŋ pitɔɔlim ka li malis wʋʋ diib nɛ o nɔɔrin;
ka o liennɛ li hali ka pʋ basida.
14Amaa li ya'a paae o pʋʋrin li na lieb tɔɔg;
li na tɔi lak-lak nwɛnɛ yabid nɛ.
15O na tin mɔrim kanɛ ka o di la;
Wina'am na kɛ ka o tiin li wʋsa yis na.
16O na liel wiigi zɛɛnsim,
zɛɛlʋŋ na dum o kʋ.
17O kʋ nyɛ siind nɛ bin'isim
linɛ pʋbid wʋʋ ku'osuoya badigid la malisim.
18-19O namis nɔŋ dim hali ka basi ba,
ka fan' nidib ya' banɛ ka o pʋ mɛɛ,
dinzug o kʋ dii o namisʋg la nyɔɔdɛ.
On tɔlim paam si'el la wʋsa, o kʋ dii li malisim.
20O kʋkɔma'asim la kɛnɛ ka o pʋ tigid si'ela
amaa o areza'as la kʋ nyaŋi faaɛn o.
21Si'el lɛn kae ka o na dii;
dinzug, o mɔrim la kʋ yuugɛ.
22Saŋa kan ka o mɔr si'el mɛkama la,
saŋkan nɔɔ ka yɛltɔɔd paad o;
fara nɛ yɛlmugusa na gban'e o.
23O ya'a ti dii pɛ'ɛl o pʋʋr la,
saŋkan ka Wina'am sʋnpɛɛn na lii o zug.
24Ba na kad o nɛ zan'an ka o zɔɔ yi,
ka ba yʋ'ʋn kʋns o nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug kpan.
25Kpan la zug na kʋns o sɔɔnri
tɔlig o nya'aŋ na.
Dabietita'ar na kpɛn' o
26ka on bɔ si'el wʋsa digil la san'am;
bugum dinɛ ka ninsaal pʋ nyu'oe
na di on nɛ o yin la'ad wʋsa.
27Saazug na nie o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la paalʋ,
ka teŋgbauŋ la na duoe zab nɛ o.
28Wina'am sʋnpɛɛn na zii o yiri gaad,
nwɛnɛ ku'om pʋbidi dit la'ad si'em la.
29Bugusim daan yɔɔdi an si'eli la,
lin ka Wina'am maali digili ba.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
Job
1Ka Job lɛbis ye,
2“Kɛlisimi sʋ'ʋŋa ka m pian' tisi ya;
ya ya'a siak, li na bʋgʋli m sʋʋnr.
3Dimi suguru ka kɛ ka m pian',
ka m ya'a pian' naae ka ya bɔɔd, yanam la'aminim.
4M pʋ nyɔnnɛ tisid ninsaala
dinzug m kʋ di suguru.
5Ya ya'a gɔs man an si'em la ma'aa li na lidigi ya
ka ya pin' nɔɔri zin' baanlimm.
6M ya'a tɛn'ɛs bʋn linɛ paae mam nwa',
di kpɛn'ɛsidim nɛ waad nɛ dabiem.
7Di niŋ wala ka nimbɛ'ɛdnam vʋe yuugid hali,
ka ba kpi'euŋ paasida?
8Ba nini ni ka ba biis nyɛt zi'esim linɛ an sʋ'ʋŋa,
ka ba yaas la nɔbigid hali.
9Yɛlbɛ'ɛd pʋ kpɛn'ɛdi ba yir pʋʋginɛ,
ka dabiem mɛ pʋ mɔri baa;
Wina'am mɛ pʋ namisidi baa.
10Ba na'araad dʋti ba na'anya'as
ka ba du'ad ka pʋ vɛnbisida.
11Ba biis ian'adnɛ wʋʋ pɛ'ɛs nɛ,
ka wa'ad nɛ sumalisim.
12Ba yʋ'ʋmnɛ ka nwɛ'ɛd siyada nɛ kɔna,
ka piebid wiisi maan sumalisim.
13Ba dit nɛ malisim ba vʋm saŋa wʋsa,
hali ka ti kpi nɛ nimma'asim.
14La'an nɛ wala ba yɛt Wina'am ye, ‘Basimi ti baanlimm!
Ti ba'a kae nɛ fʋn gban'e ti yɛla si'em.
15Anɔ'ɔnɛ an Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la ka ti na pʋ'ʋs o?
Ka ti ya'a pʋ'ʋs o, nyɔbɔ ka ti na paam?’
16Ba tɛn'ɛs ye ba mɛŋ paŋ ka ba paami ba mɔrim la,
amaa mam pʋ siak ban tɛn'ɛsid si'em laa.
17La'an nɛ wala wʋsa, nɔɔr ala ka ya nyɛ ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim bugum kpiisɛ?
Nɔɔr ala ka tɔɔg paae ba
bɛɛ Wina'am sʋnpɛɛn luu ba zugɔ?
18Nɔɔr ala ka o da'ae ba keŋ wʋʋ sa'ad
bɛɛ udug ka sisi'em da'ae keŋɛ?
19Ba ya'a ye, ‘Wina'am namisid biisi ba saamnam tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd zug,’
mam na lɛbis ye o ya'a namis tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la sɔb mɛŋ,
o na baŋ ye o tʋm bɛ'ɛd!
20Kɛl ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb nini nyɛɛ o san'auŋ;
kɛl ka Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la tɛɛg o tʋbir ka li wʋm o.
21O dabisa dunia nwa' ya'a ti naae,
o ba'a lɛn ka' nɛ o yaas yɛlaa.
22Sɔ' bɛɛ na tun'e pa'al Wina'am
onɛ kad tuongatib banɛ mɔr kpi'euŋ hali saria laa?
23Sɔ' mɔri laafi hali nɛ on na ti kpi;
ka o ya'a ti kpi o kpiidi nɛ nimma'asim ka dabiem kae,
24ka o niŋgbina saalim sʋ'ʋŋa
ka o kɔnba mɔr biim.
25Ka sɔ' on di namisʋg hali nɛ o kum,
ka pʋ di nyɛlʋg baa daar yinnee.
26Amaa nidib ayi' nwa' ya'a kpi ba na mumi ba wʋsa teŋin
ka zʋnzʋnya dii ba niŋgbina la.
27M mi' pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka ya tɛn'ɛsidi m yɛla,
nɛ gban'abɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka ya gban'e m yɛla la.
28Ya na yɛl ye, ‘Nintita'ar la yir bɛ yaanɛ,
ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim la da bɛ zin'isi'a la bɛ yaanɛ?’
29Ya pʋ bu'os banɛ ken suoya la wʋm ka baŋɛɛ?
Ya pʋ siak ban yɛl si'em laa?
30Wina'am sʋʋnr ya'a ti duoe ka o ye o namis nidiba,
tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim ɛɛnti nyɛnɛ yɔlisimm?
31Anɔ'ɔnɛ yɛt tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb ye o tʋm bɛ'ɛdɛ?
Anɔ'ɔnɛ yɔɔd o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la sammɛ?
32Ba ya'a mum o naae,
ba gur o yaʋg la nɛ sʋ'ʋŋa.
33Nidib na galis o dabɔɔgin,
ba na dɔl taaba keŋi pʋ'ʋs o kʋʋr la,
hali titan kanɛ ka ba zaŋi pin' o la anɛ malisim tis o.
34Alazug, ya ye ya niŋ wala bɛlis man nɛ ya antu'ayɛɛd nwa'?
Yanamɛ lɛbis si'el wʋsa anɛ faad ma'aa ka sida ka' li nii.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
Elifaz
1Ka Elifaz onɛ yi Teman la lɛbis ye,
2 “Ninsaal ya'am ya'a bɔɔd din zem si'em
amaa di ka' vɔɔnri tis Wina'am.
3Fʋ ya'a pʋn an sida sɔba,
li sʋm an bɔɔ tis Wina'am
Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la?
Bɛɛ fʋ ya'a an onɛ pʋ mɔr taala, nyɔbɔ ka o na nyɛ?
4Di anɛ fʋn zɔt Wina'am la zug ka o tansidif,
ka kati fʋ saria anwa, bɛɛ?
5Fʋ zi' ye fʋ bugusim tʋʋma la zu'onɛ galis
ka fʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la ka' bɛnnɛɛ?
6Fʋ faaɛn fʋ ba'abiis banɛ dii fʋ sam fuud ka li pʋ nara,
fʋ yɛɛs nidib la'ad ka basi ba sawɛnya.
7Fʋ daa pʋ nɔk ku'om tis banɛ ka ku'onuud kʋʋdi baa,
ka lɛm mɔŋ banɛ ka ba kɔ'ɔm zabid la diib,
8la'an nɛ fʋn da an kpi'euŋ sɔb ka mɔr kuob pamm
ka zin' anina nɛ fʋ girima wʋsa la.
9Fʋ da kad pʋkɔnya ka ba lɛb nu'uzaalis,
ka tʋm kpiibis dinɛ pʋ nara.
10Linɛ kɛ ka bɛndis giligif zin'is wʋsa,
ka dabiem ɛɛn gbirigi gban'af saŋa wʋsa la.
11Linɛ mɛ kɛ ka li an lik biridi ka fʋ pʋ nyɛta,
ka ku'om limif zin'is wʋsa la.
12Wina'am pʋ bɛ nɛ saazug saa?
Gɔsim o dʋʋ gaad nwadbibis banɛ bɛ agɔlli ian'ad pidʋ-pidʋ la.
13Amaa fʋ yɛl ye, ‘Wina'am mi' bɔ?
O na nyaŋi nyɛ likine kad nid sariaa?
14O bɛ nɛ saazug sa gin
ka saŋgbantita'ar ligil o, ka o pʋ nyɛti tii.’
15Fʋ na kpɛn dɔl suokʋdʋg
kanɛ ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim dɔl laa?
16Ba da kpi ka pʋ paae ba daarɛ,
ka li nwɛnɛ ku'om dii ba gaadnɛ.
17Ba da yɛl Wina'am ye, ‘Basimi ti baanlimm!
Bɔ ka fʋn, Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la, na nyaŋi niŋi ti?’
18Amaa gɔsima, li anɛ Wina'am pɛ'ɛli ba ya' nɛ bʋnsʋma.
Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim pʋtɛn'ɛr pʋn bɛ nɛ li kɔn'.
19Pʋpielim dim ya'a nyɛ ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim namisid
ba maannɛ sumalisim;
ka banɛ ka' taal la la'adi ba ka yɛt ye,
20‘Asida mɛnɛ, ba san'ami ti dataas la
ka bugum dii ba mɔrim la wʋsa.’
21Siakim tis Wina'am ka paam sumbʋgʋsʋm;
fʋ ya'a niŋ ala, o na niŋi fʋ zug yɛlsʋm.
22Di'em o pa'alʋg
ka zaŋi li niŋi fʋ sʋʋnrin.
23Fʋ ya'a fɛndigi lɛb Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la san'an na,
o na lɛn lɛbisi fʋ, fʋ zin'ikʋdigin la.
Fʋ ya'a yis tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi fʋ yin
24ka basi fʋ sanlimgbila la,
lɔmmi fʋ sanlim sʋma la bas tampinyɔ'ɔdin,
25ka Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la na aan fʋ sanlima,
ka an anzurifa dinɛ bɛɛ li gʋnni tisif.
26Ala ka fʋ sʋnf na malis Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la ni
ka fʋ na gɔdigi gɔs Wina'am.
27Fʋ na sɔs o, ka o na kɛlisi fʋ sɔsʋg
ka fʋ na nɔki fʋ piini tis o
wʋʋ fʋn pʋn zi'el nɔɔr si'em la.
28Fʋ ya'a gban'e si'el wʋsa, li na zi'en
ka nɛɛsim na nie fʋ suoya zan' ni.
29Yɛla ya'a sigis nidib teŋin
ka fʋ yɛl ye, ‘Wina'am, dʋ'ʋsimi ba!’
O sid na tiligi ba wʋsa.
30Hali onɛ ka' bʋʋd la, o na faaɛn o bas,
ka li anɛ fʋ nu'usi an nyain la yɛla.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.
translation_text:
Job
1Ka Job lɛbis ye,
2“Hali zina m nan kpɛn nyɔnnɛ nɛ sʋnpɛɛn;
la'an nɛ din wʋmim ka m unsid la,
Wina'am nan kpɛm mugusidim nɛ.
3M ya'a baŋin mam na nyɛɛ o zin'isi'a;
ka paae o na'am zin'igin la!
4Man naan yɛli nɛ o m yɛla la wʋsa
ka nwɛ' nɔŋgban kpi'euŋ nɛ o nɛ nimmua.
5M naan baŋin on na gandigi m yɛl la si'em,
ka kɛlis on na yɛlim si'el.
6O na zaŋ o paŋ tita'ar la zab nɛ mam bɛɛ?
Ayei, o na kɛlisi m pian'ad la.
7Ani ka ninkanɛ an pʋpielim sɔb na mɔr o antu'a kɛɛn o tuon na,
ani ka m na paam faangir m sariakat la san'an saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.
8Amaa m ya'a keŋ ya-nya'aŋ, o ka' anii;
m ya'a keŋ ya-tuona, m kʋ nyɛɛ o anii.
9O ya'a bɛ ya-datiuŋʋ tʋmmaa, m kʋ nyɛɛ o;
o ya'a fɛndigi lɛb ya-dagɔbʋgɔ, m kʋ baŋ on bɛ si'ela.
10Amaa on mi' suokanɛ ka man dɔl la;
o ya'a ti makimi naae, m na nyɛɛn wʋʋ sanlim nɛ.
11Man dɔl Wina'am suor la tituaa;
m dɔl o nɔba ka pʋ bie lɛb gɔbʋg bɛɛ datiuŋɔ.
12M pʋ bie ka bas o nɔzi'ela la;
m di'e o nɔyɛlʋg la ka li gaadi m diib.
13Nɛ wala wʋsa, on ma'aa an Wina'am ka sɔ' kae na ki'is oo
bɛɛ na tun'e kɛ ka o bas on gban'e ye o tʋm si'em la.
14On gban'e ye o tʋm mam si'em la, linɛ bɛ.
O mɛ mɔr gban'asieba man zug.
15Alazug ka m yam ian'ad o zug,
m ya'a tiɛn nɛ'ɛŋa wʋsa dabiem mɔrim nɛ.
16Wina'am kɛ ka m giinla kɛns,
Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la kɛ ka dabietita'ar kpɛn'ɛm.
17Amaa la'an nɛ wala, lik pʋ nyaŋi kɛ ka m fɔn baanlimm nɛ,
hali baa di ya'a bɔɔd lin sɔbigim biridi si'em.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
1Ka Job lɛn yɛl ye,
“Wala ka Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la pʋ gban'e dabisbanɛ ka o na kad saria?
Bɔzug ka banɛ dɔl o la zi' dabisbama nwa'?
2Bugusim dim la tɔlisidi ba pɔɔd titɔndis,
ka zuud kɔnbidi paasidi ba pɛ'ɛsin.
3Ba kad kpiibis bʋmisi keŋ sa
ka faaɛn pʋkɔɔnr lɔlig on pʋ nyaŋi yɔɔ o sam la zug.
4Ba da'ae nɔŋdimi yis suorin
ka kad tadimnam ka ba zɔɔ su'a.
5Nɔŋdaannam saadnɛ mɔɔgin
ieed diib wʋʋ bʋmis nɛ;
ba biis ginnɛ pipirisin ye ba nyɛ si'eli di.
6Ba dɔlisidi nidib pɔɔdinɛ
ki'ed kɔnbid yaama
ka wi'isid zʋʋd pitɔɔg dim pɔɔdinɛ tisidi ba.
7Ba dig yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ biel,
ba pʋ mɔr dinɛ na pili ba mɛŋ waad saŋaa.
8Ba bɛ nɛ zuoya zut ka saa bʋ'ʋdi ba
ka ba zɔti ken tampiinsin ye ba labin ka li lusi ba.
9Bugusim dim la pɔnsigid bibanɛ ka' saamnam la ba manam bin'isimin;
ka faand nɔŋ dim biisi yɔɔd sama.
10Fara dim la ginnɛ sawɛnya ban ka' fuud la zug
ba bunnɛ kpan'am dim ki, ka lɛɛ ken kɔ'ɔm.
11Ba tuod olif biili siligid kpaam
ka maan bʋnnuuda ka ken nɛ ku'onuud.
12Tempʋbɛda la ni nidib ʋʋnsidnɛ bɔɔd kum
ka sieba pu'alim ka kaasidi bɔɔd sʋŋir
amaa ka Wina'am ba'a kae nɛ baa.
13Ninsieba zan'as nɛ ye bam pʋ bɔɔd nɛɛsim,
ba pʋ gban'e nɛɛsim la gbinnɛ
ka mɛ pʋ siak ye ba dɔlli li suorɛ.
14Bɛog ya'a ti yɔe nier la, ninkʋʋd la duodnɛ
kʋʋd nɔŋ dim nɛ tadimnam;
ka yʋ'ʋŋ ka o an na'ayiigi giligid.
15Pu'abɔɔd guri ye li sɔb,
ka o zaŋ si'eli lus o nindaa
ka tɛn'ɛs ye, ‘Sɔ' kʋ nyɛɛ ma.’
16Yʋ'ʋŋ ka ba labisidi kpɛn'ɛd yaan,
ka bɛog nie ka ba yɔɔ ba mɛŋ dɔɔgin;
ka pʋ bɔɔd nɛɛsim baa bi'elaa.
17Ba zaŋ lik biridi ka li an nɛɛsim tisi ba,
ka lɛɛ zɔt nɛɛsim dabiem.
18Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim la nwɛnɛ pusinpuum
ka ku'om diti ken sa;
Wina'am nɔpɔɔr bɛɛ ba pɔɔd zug,
alazug ka sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ lɛn kennɛ ba pɔɔdin laa.
19Nintaŋi nyɛligid sakuga si'em la,
ala mɛn ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim na bɔdig dunia zug.
20Ba manam pʋn tami ba yɛla nɛ
ka zʋnzʋnya diti ba.
Sɔ' pʋ lɛn tɛnr tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim la yɛlaa,
ba nwɛnɛ tiig ka sisi'em kɔ'ɔgi bas nɛ.
21Ba mugusidi kʋnduada
ka pʋ zɔt pʋkɔnya nimbaanliga.
22Wina'am nɔkid o kpi'euŋʋ vɛ'ɛd paŋ dim la basid;
la'an nɛ ban tɛn'ɛs ye ba mɔr paŋ la,
ba vʋm bɛ nɛ Wina'am nu'ugin.
23Wina'am kɛ ka ba bɛ nwɛnɛ yɛlsi'a pʋ paki baa,
amaa o nini gɔti ba ken wʋsa.
24Ba diti ya'an daba ayi',
ka yʋ'ʋn sʋʋg wʋʋ mɔpuum nɛ,
ba nwaadi ba nɛ nwɛnɛ ki ka ba bʋn si'em la.
25Ya'a ka' alaa anɔ'ɔn na pa'al ye m ka' sida sɔba,
ka kɛ ka man tu'as si'el la wʋsa lieb yɔri?”

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
Bilidad
1Ka Bilidad onɛ yi Suh na la lɛbis ye,
2“Paŋ nɛ dabiem wʋsa anɛ Wina'am din;
o kɛ ka sumbʋgʋsʋm bɛ saazug.
3Anɔ'ɔnɛ na tun'e kaal o zabzabidib la?
Yaanɛ ka Wina'am nɛɛsim la pʋ paae?
4Ninsaal na niŋ wala an pʋpiel Wina'am tuonnɛ?
Ninsaal biig na niŋ wala pʋ mɔr taal Wina'am tuonnɛ?
5Nwadig nɛ nwadbibis nɛɛsim
ya'a an zaalim o nini ni,
6ka ninsaal onɛ nwɛnɛ titan
bɛɛ zʋnzʋnr Wina'am nifin la na an wala?”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Job
1Ka Job lɛbis ye,
2“Waii, gɔsim fʋn sʋŋ ninkanɛ ka' sʋŋid si'em!
Gɔsim sʋŋ kanɛ ka fʋ sʋŋ tadim nwa'!
3Waii, gɔsim fʋn sa'al ninkanɛ ka' ya'am si'em!
Waii, fʋ sid pa'al ye fʋ mɔr ya'am pamm!
4Anɔ'ɔn kimm lɛɛ sʋ'ʋŋif ka fʋ pian' anwana?
Anɔ'ɔnɛ tisif pʋtɛn'ɛr ka fʋ pian' pian'abama?
5Gɔsim kpi'imnam banɛ bɛ teŋin nɛ ku'om pʋʋgin la,
ba wʋsa kiridnɛ nɛ dabietita'ar.
6Hali kpi'im teŋ gba pʋ su'ad nɛ Wina'am;
li wʋsa nie nɛ nyain o nini ni.
7Wina'am yadig saŋgbauŋ la ya-datiuŋ,
ka maal teŋgbauŋ la ka li yul ka si'el pʋ mɔri li.
8Onɛ kɛ ka saŋgbana la pɛ'ɛl nɛ ku'om
ka lɛɛ kʋ tɛbigi tansi li naa.
9O tiɛnd o saŋgbana la
libin nwadpielig.
10O buoɛn atɛukʋn la ka li mɔr bɛn-bɛn
ka li bɛŋ nɛɛsim nɛ lik.
11Wina'am ya'a tans,
zan'antɔlis banɛ ti'e saŋgbauŋ la dammidnɛ nɛ dabiem.
12Wina'am zaŋ nɛ o paŋ tita'ar la nyaŋ Atɛuk;
ka zaŋ o ya'am aans bʋnzɔtir linɛ bɛ ku'otita'arinɛ buon Rahab la.
13Wina'am vʋ'ʋsʋm kɛ ka agɔl nie nyain;
ka o nu'ug kʋns wa'akanɛ ian'ad ka nwɛɛlimɛ o mɛŋ hali la.
14Gɔsima, nwa' wʋsa anɛ Wina'am tʋʋma bi'ela la,
ban nya'am yɛl ka ti wʋm si'eli nwa'!
Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na tun'e baŋ o paŋ la an si'em?”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
1Job da nan kpɛn pian'ad ye,
2“M pɔya nɛ Wina'am, onɛ mɔŋim bʋʋd la,
Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb ka kɛ ka m bɛllim lieb tɔɔg la,
3m ya'a nan kpɛm bɛɛ m nyɔvʋr zug,
ka Wina'am nan kɛ ka m vʋe,
4m nɔɔr nwa' kʋ maligin ya'ae pian' bɛ'ɛdɛ,
m zilim mɛ kʋ maligim pian' linɛ an zirii.
5M kʋ maligim siak ye yanamɛ yɛt si'el la anɛ sidaa,
hali baa kʋnya bɔkinɛ, m kʋ yɛl ye m ka' sida sɔba.
6M nam kpɛm bɛɛ m pʋpielim bɛllim la ka kʋ basɛ;
m pʋtɛn'ɛr na kpɛn an nyain hali nɛ m kum.
7Wina'am na namisi m dataas nɛ banɛ kisim la
nwɛnɛ on namisid nimbɛ'ɛdnam si'em la.
8Ti'ir bɔ ka onɛ pʋ zɔt Wina'am mɔr
saŋa kanɛ ka Wina'am di'e o nyɔvʋrɛ?
9Yɛltɔɔd ya'a ti paae o ka o kaasida,
Wina'am na wʋm o kukumaa?
10O na nyɛ sumalisim Wina'am san'anɛɛ?
O pʋn na sɔs Wina'am ʋʋn?
11M na pa'ali ya Wina'am paŋi zem si'em;
m kʋ su'a ya Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la yɛlaa.
12Ya wʋsa pʋn nyɛ linɛ naam wʋsa;
ka bɔzug ka ya pian'ad pian'ayɛɛd bama?
13Wina'am gban'e ye o tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb
nɛ pitɔɔg dim si'em nwa':
14hali baa o biis ya'a zu'oe si'em, ba wʋsa ye ba kpinɛ zaba ni;
o yaas kʋ maligim di ka li sia'ali baa.
15Ban'as na kʋʋ o bibanɛ pɔns zaba ni la
hali ka ba pʋkɔnya kʋ kaasi ba kʋʋrɛ.
16Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd daan ya'a bɔɔd on vaae anzurifa su'a si'em,
hali ka mɔr fuud ka li galis si'em,
17pʋpielim sɔb na yɛ fuud la wʋsa;
ka onɛ ka' taal mɛ di'e anzurifa la.
18Yir kanɛ ka o mɛɛd la nwɛnɛ silinsi'ipaanlʋŋ nɛ,
bɛɛ sʋgʋr ka ba ti' gur pɔɔg.
19O dig nɛ kpan'am zug, amaa ka kʋ maligim bɛɛ ala,
o nif aŋir ka li pʋn gaad sa.
20O yam na iank wʋʋ ku'om ɛɛn di nid ka li an si'em la;
ka sisi'etita'ar zii o yʋ'ʋn gaad.
21Sisi'em na yi ya-nya'aŋ na zii o gaad;
di na piis o on bɛ zin'isi'a la gaad.
22On mɔɔd ye o zɔɔ yi sisi'emin la
li na nwɛ' o yutim-yutim ka nimbaanlig kae.
23Sisi'em la vuud nɛ paŋ tita'ar hali
kpɛn'ɛsid o dabiem ka kad o yis o bɛllim zin'igin la.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
1Ka Job lɛn yɛli ba ye,
“Bʋmbɔk kanɛ ka ba tuudi nyɛt anzurifa la bɛnɛ,
ka ban nyɛligid sanlima zin'isi'a mɛ bɛ.
2Ba tuud kʋnti yisid teŋin na,
ka nyu'od kuga yisid kʋntzɛn'ug.
3Sanlim tuudib mɔri bugum kpɛn'ɛd sanlimbɔkin;
ba tuudi paad zin'ibanɛ an lik biridi wʋsa ieed sanlima.
4Ba ɛɛn gɔsnɛ nidibi kae zin'isi'a la
tu vɔndʋg hali ka li zulim
ka zaŋ nwiigi lɔɔ dɔlisi sigi bɛɛ anina ba kɔn'ɔkɔn'.
5Zʋʋd yitnɛ teŋgbauŋ zugin,
ka li teŋir-teŋir sa nwɛnɛ bugum dii kanb nɛ.
6Teŋ la tampiinsin ka kugvɛnla yit na,
ka sanlima ɛɛnti li titanin na.
7Niiŋ kae mi' zin'ig la,
ka silʋg nif mɛ nan zi' nyɛɛ li.
8Mɔɔgin bʋnkɔnbid pʋn pʋ nɔɔdi ba nɔba anii,
ka gbigim gba pʋ dɔl ani gata.
9Saalib tuudnɛ hali nwa'ad tampinkpi'ema;
ba tuudi zuoya hali paadi ba teŋir.
10Ba tuudnɛ ka nyaad vɔnya tampiinsin la,
ka nyɛt kugvɛnla nɛ linɛ ligidi zu'oe la wʋsa.
11Ba ieedi baŋid kɔldaadi pin'il si'el na,
ka mɔr dinɛ wʋsa su'a yi nɛɛsimin na.
12Ya'a an sida, ya ka ti na nyɛ ya'am?
Ka ya ka baŋir bɛ?
13Ninsaal ya'am kʋ baŋi lii;
fʋ kʋ maligim nyɛ li saalibinɛ.
14Ku'otitada nɛ Atɛuk yɛl ye,
‘Ya'am kae tinam san'anɛ.’
15Fʋ kʋ nyaŋi da' ya'am nɛ sanlim vɛnliŋ,
bɛɛ zaŋi li mak nɛ anzurifaa.
16Ofir teŋ sanlim sʋma kʋ nyaŋi da' lii,
fʋ mɛ kʋ nyaŋi da' li nɛ kugvɛnla buudi wʋsaa.
17Fʋ kʋ nyaŋi zaŋ sanlima bɛɛ gɔtiŋvɛnla mak nɛ lii,
bɛɛ da' li nɛ sanlima niŋgɔnkɔrisɛ.
18Kugpielvɛnla nɛ li buudi mɛ pʋ li'eli lii;
bɔzugɔ ya'am gaad si'el wʋsa.
19Kus teŋ kugvɛnla linɛ an dɔnbʋʋlim la kʋ nyaŋi mak nɛ lii;
fʋ mɛ kʋ nyaŋi da' li nɛ sanlimaa.
20Ka yaanɛ kimm ka ya'am yina?
Ka ya ka baŋir bɛ?
21Li su'anɛ ka bʋnvʋr kae na tun'e nyɛɛ li,
hali niis banɛ ian'ad agɔla nan zi' lin bɛ si'ela.
22Hali Asan'auŋ nɛ Kpi'im Teŋ yɛl ye;
‘Tinam mɛ kʋdim wʋmnɛ nɛ tʋba.’
23Wina'am ma'aa mi' ya'am suor,
ka mɛ mi' lin bɛ zin'isi'a.
24Bɔzugɔ, onɛ gɔsidi nyɛt teŋ-magbinnin
ka mɛ nyɛt dinɛ niŋid teŋgbauŋ zug wʋsa.
25Onɛ da maal pɛbisim nɛ li paŋ wʋsa,
ka mak ku'okanɛ bɛ saŋgbana ni la zem si'em,
26ka tis saa nɔɔr lin na ni si'em
ka maal suori tis satansʋg.
27O da gɔs ya'am sʋ'ʋŋa
ka siak ye li an sʋ'ʋm pamm.
28Ka yɛl saalib ye, ‘Nid ya'a bɔɔd ya'am, on zɔm Wina'am,
o ya'a bɔɔd baŋir on zɔm yi tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdin tɔ'ɔtɔ.’”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
1Job keŋ tuon nɛ o pian'ʋk la ye,
2“Waii, man ya'a nan kpɛn aan wʋʋ man da bɛ si'em
saŋkanɛ ka Wina'am da gɔsidim sʋ'ʋŋa la,
3ka o fitir la nie m zugin lauu
ka m kennɛ o nɛɛsimin la!
4Saŋkan ka man da nan bɛɛ m naŋnaŋin
ka Wina'am onɛ aan m zua la gur man nɛ m yidim la.
5Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la da nan bɛ nɛ m,
ka m biis mɛ bɛɛ m san'anɛ zu'oe,
6saŋkan la ka m mɔrim galis
hali ka kpaam kpa'adi yit tampiinsin na olif kpaam nɛ tisidim.
7Kpɛɛmnam ya'a da ɛɛnti la'as
ka m kena zin'inɛɛ,
8dasam da ɛɛn lɛb nɛ nya'aŋ sa
ka bʋnkʋda pɔnd nɔba m tuonnɛ na'asidim.
9Tuongatib da ɛɛn zaŋ nɛ ba nu'usi pin' ba nɔya
lɛbi fɔn baanlimm.
10Hali burikinnam da ɛɛn fɔnnɛ baanlimm
nwɛnɛ ba sɛɛn ba nɔya nɛ.
11Banɛ wʋsa da wʋmmi m labaar la da pian'adi m yɛla sʋ'ʋm,
ka banɛ wʋsa nyɛɛm siak ye m sid anɛ ninsʋŋ.
12Bɔzugɔ, nɔŋ dim ya'a da kaasidi bɔɔd sʋŋir, m sʋŋidi ba
hali nɛ kpiibis banɛ ka' sʋŋida.
13Banɛ ka li da wʋmi ba hali ka ba wʋm kum nyuug la
da kaanb kaanbsʋŋɔ tisim;
m mɛ da sʋŋ pʋkɔnya ka ba sʋnya ma'ae.
14M da yɛ pʋpielim nwɛnɛ fuug nɛ,
ka pid sida nwɛnɛ zupibig nɛ.
15Manɛ da an zʋnzɔɔs nini
nɛ pɔnda nɔba.
16Manɛ da an tadimnam saam;
ka di'e saam yɛla zi.
17M da kɔ' bugusim dim nu'us
ka faaɛn banɛ ka ba gban'e ba la bas.
18M da tɛn'ɛs ye, ‘M na yuug hali pamm,
ka nyaan kpii m mɛŋ yin.
19M da nwɛnɛ tikanɛ nya'a bɛ ku'omin saŋa wʋsa
ka o vaand pɛ'ɛl nɛ mɛligim.
20M girima la na kpɛn kennɛ tuon
ka m nyɛt kpi'euŋ paal saŋa wʋsa.’
21M ya'a da ya'ae nɔɔr ye m sa'al nidib,
ba anɛ ki' ka kɛlisid nɛ ya'amlɛog.
22M ya'a da pian' naae, sɔ' pʋ lɛm pian'ada,
bɔzugɔ, m pian'ad la da ɛɛn lii ba tʋba ni
ka bʋgʋli ba sʋʋnr.
23Ba da ɛɛn gur nɛ ya'amlɛog ye ba wʋmi m pian'ad
wʋʋ kpaadi gur sigsaa si'em la.
24M ya'a da lɔdigi m nindaa tisi ba,
ba sʋʋnr ɛɛn kpɛ'ɛŋnɛ.
25Manɛ da gban'adi ba gban'ar wʋsa tisidi ba
ka gaadi ba tuon wʋʋ na'abi gat o zabzabidib tuon si'em la,
ka bɛlisidi ba saŋkanɛ ka ba bɛ mugusʋg pʋʋgin wʋsa.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1Job da lɛn yɛl ye,
“Amaa nannanna nwa' ba la'ad mam nɛ,
hali na'akim baanlʋg
banɛ an bɛɛga-bɛɛga biis,
ka man da pʋ siakid ye
ba saamnam dɔlli m baasi
gur kɔnbid la.
2Ba da tadignɛ hali
ka ka' paŋi na tʋmi m tʋʋmaa tisidi ma.
3Nɔŋ nɛ kɔ'ɔm da mɔri ba hali
ka ba gʋ'ʋŋi ɔnbid tiis nya'a,
ka yʋ'ʋŋ ka ba gɔɔndi gin mɔɔgin nɛ pipirisin.
4Ba da vɔɔndnɛ tutuud pipirisin ɔnbid
hali ka la'am ɔnbid nya'a banɛ pʋ mɔr mimilimm.
5Nidib da kadi ba nɛ yis saalibi bɛ zin'isi'a,
ka wuunnɛ ba wʋʋ ba anɛ na'ayiis nɛ.
6Di da nyaŋi ba ka ba bɛ kɔldaad banɛ ka ku'om kae la pʋʋg,
nɛ tampinlɛma ni, hali nɛ vɔnya ni.
7Ba da bɛ nɛ mɔɔgin kaasid wʋʋ bʋnkɔnbid nɛ
ka la'asi kʋk taaba dig mɔɔgin.
8Ba da anɛ banɛ ka' vɔɔnrɛ ka sɔ' mɛ zi' ba yɛlaa,
ba da nɔk kpa'asa kadi ba yis teŋin la.
9Amaa nannanna ba biis gɔs mam nɛ zaalim
ka mɔri m yʋ'ʋri yʋ'ʋm;
m pʋ lɛm mɔr vɔɔnri tisi baa.
10Ba nɛ'ɛsid man nɛ ka pʋ bɔɔd ye ba li'eli ma;
ka tʋbisid nintɔɔndi mat man nindaa.
11Wina'am kɛ ka m lieb tadim ka ka' sʋŋid la zug,
ka nidib mɔrimi niŋid bam bɔɔd si'el.
12Ba la'as nɛ m datiuŋ baba gubigim;
ba tunɛ bʋmbu'adi m nɔba baba;
ka gban'e ye ba zab nɛ m.
13Ba vi' m suori lɛbis
ka mɔɔd ye ba kʋʋm
ka sɔ' kae na faaɛn ma.
14Ba li' m nɛ wʋʋ zabzabidibi nwa'ae zaŋguom
ka dɔl wɛlʋgʋ kpɛn' na.
15Dabiem kɛ ka m pabig.
M burikinnim la wʋsa gaadi nwɛnɛ sisi'em nɛ,
ka m mɔrim la mɛlim wʋʋ saŋgbana nɛ.
16Nannanna nwa' mam vʋm paadi li bɛn;
m namisʋg la dabisa ka' naarɛ.
17Yʋ'ʋŋ wʋsa m kɔnba nwa'adnɛ hali
ka m niŋgbina zabid ka pʋ ma'ada.
18Wina'am zaŋ nɛ o paŋ tita'ar la gban'e m niŋgɔɔnri siank
wʋʋ fuug niŋgɔɔnri muknɛ.
19O zaŋimnɛ lɔbi bas bian'arin,
ka m yʋ'ʋn lieb wʋʋ titan nɛ tampɛligim.
20M Wina'am, man kaasi buolif, ka fʋ pʋ gandigi ma;
ka m duoe zi'en ka fʋ gɔsidim ka pʋ yɛl si'ela.
21Gɔsima, fʋ namisid man nɛ;
fʋ zaŋ nɛ fʋ paŋ tita'ar la tʋmim nyɔnbid.
22Fʋ kpɛn ʋk man nɛ lɔbigi bas ka sisi'em mɔrimi keŋ sa;
ka nwɛ'ɛmi yutim-yutim sisi'etita'arin la.
23Mam mi' ye fʋ na ba'asi kʋʋm,
ka m keŋ saalib wʋsa naad zin'isi'a la.
24Sɔ' nan zi' namis ninkanɛ bɛ tɔɔg pʋʋgin
ka buon ye ba kena faaɛn o basɛ.
25M da pʋ kaasi fabil banɛ bɛ yɛla ni la yɛlaa?
M sʋʋnr da pʋ san'am nɔŋ dim yɛlaa?
26Amaa mam mɛ ya'a ti tɛn'ɛs ye sʋ'ʋm na kena la, bɛ'ɛdi kenna;
m ya'a ti tɛn'ɛs ye nɛɛsim na kena la, liki kenna.
27M sʋʋnr san'amnɛ hali ka ka' ma'arɛ;
namisʋg bɛɛ m zugin daar wʋsa.
28M gɛnnɛ nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ ka onɛ bɛlisidim kae.
M duoe zi'en wʋrʋginɛ nwɛ' kuŋ ye ba sʋŋim.
29M yʋ'ʋn nwɛnɛ zaŋku'ar sizua,
ka an viiug bɛllim taa.
30M niŋgbiŋ wʋsa sɔbig nɛ hali
ka tʋligi nwɛnɛ bugum nɛ.
31M yʋ'ʋn nwɛ'ɛdi m kɔn nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ nwɛ'ɛb ma'aa
ka piebidi m wiig kʋʋr piebʋg ma'aa.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
1Ka Job da lɛn yɛl ye,
“Mam pɔ nɛ ye m kʋ zaŋi m nini
gɔs pu'asadir nɛ yamlɛogɔ.
2Ya'a ka' ala m yɔɔd na an bɔ kimm Wina'am san'anɛ?
Bɔ ka Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la na tisimi li zugɔ?
3Li ka'anɛ san'auŋ ma'aa ka o tisid nimbɛ'ɛdnam,
ka kɛt ka banɛ tʋm bɛ'ɛd ba'asid yɔri?
4O pʋ nyɛt mam bɛ bɛllim si'aa,
hali ka mi' m nɔba yakir kallɛɛ?
5M ya'a aan pʋʋs ayi' sɔb
bɛɛ anɛ onɛ ma'adi tisidi m taaba,
6Wina'am on makim tituaa nɛ sida makir
ka o na nyɛ ka m ka' gba'arɛ.
7Man ya'a sid bienɛ ka bas suosʋŋ la,
ka kɛ ka m ya'amlɛog kpɛn' dinɛ an bɛ'ɛd,
bɛɛ nɔki m nu'ugʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛd,
8Wina'am on kɛl ka m pɔɔg zʋʋd san'am,
bɛɛ o kɛ ka sieba dii m diib la ka basim.
9M ya'amlɛog ya'a kpɛn' nɛ sɔ' pu'a
bɛɛ m ya'a digin nɛ m yak pu'a,
10Wina'am on kɛl ka mam mɛŋ pu'a mɔnnɛ tisid dau zʋŋ,
ka dap mɔr o digi.
11Nid ya'a tʋm tʋʋmfɛn'ɛsa bama buudi,
li nar ye ba kʋʋs o daana bɛ'ɛd ka tɛk o tʋbir.
12Li na nwɛnɛ bugum nɛ diimɛ paae kpi'im teŋ
ka na di mam nɛ m mɔrim wʋsa.
13M ya'a daa tʋm linɛ pʋ nari tisim tʋmtʋm dap nɛ tʋmtʋm pu'ab
ka ba fabili tisim ka m pʋ wʋm tisi ba,
14Wina'am sʋnf ya'a ti duoe nɛ ma, m na niŋ wala?
O ya'a ti bu'osim bu'osa m na niŋ wala gandigɛ?
15Ka' Wina'am kanɛ maal man la mɛ maali baa?
Ɛɛn! Onɛ sid maali ti wʋsa ti manam pʋʋsin.
16M nan zi' zan'as ye m kʋ sʋŋ nɔŋ dima,
bɛɛ kɛ ka pʋkɔnya gɔsi m nini ni ti tadig ka pʋ nyɛ si'ela.
17M da diti m kɔn'
ka zan'as ye m kʋ sʋŋ kpiibisɛɛ?
18Bɔzugɔ, m na'akinnimin sa, m gɔsi ba wʋʋ m mɛŋ-mɛŋ biis nɛ,
m biilimin sa m ba'a bɛnɛ pʋkɔnya yɛla.
19M nam mi' nyɛ sɔ' ka o bɔɔd sʋŋir
hali ka nɔŋ kɛ ka o kʋ nyaŋi paam fuugʋ lus o mɛŋ,
20ka m pʋ tis o fuugɔɔ? Ayei! Li naan kʋ dɔllin suorɛ!
Amaa m tis o fubanɛ ka ba nɔk bʋnkɔnbid kɔnbidi maal
ka li yinɛ m mɛŋ kɔnbidin na,
ka o pʋ'ʋsim nɛ o sʋʋnr wʋsa.
21M nan mi' vɔlis kpiibig
mam mɔr suobanɛ na tisim bʋʋd na'ayin la zugɔɔ? Ayei!
22M ya'a tʋm ala, m biaunk on aam li,
ka m nu'ug kɔ'ɔgi li sʋn'urin la.
23Man zɔt ye Wina'am na san'amim la zug
m pʋn kʋ siaki tʋm nɛ'ɛŋaa.
24M ya'a nɔkini m mɛŋi dɛllim nɛ sanlima
bɛɛ tɛn'ɛsi m pʋtɛn'ɛrin ye, ‘Sanlim sʋma ka man ti'e,’
25bɛɛ nwɛ'ɛdin nyɔ'ɔgʋ m mɔrim zug,
bɛɛ man tʋm paam si'el zug,
26bɛɛ m ya'a gɔsin winnigi ian'ad pil-pil la,
bɛɛ nwadig la pɛlig puki si'em la
27ka m ya'am kpɛn' ba
ka m pin'ili pʋ'ʋsidi ba,
28lina wʋsa naan aan tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ nar namisʋg
bɔzugɔ li pa'al ye m pʋ tis Wina'am onɛ an yinne la sidaa.
29M dataa ya'a daa namisid, m daa pʋ maan sumalisim,
bɛɛ o bɛ yɛla ni ka li ma'ae m sʋʋnrɛ,
30m pʋ pɔ nɔɔri niŋ o
ka li kɛ ka m kpɛn' taalinɛ.
31M yin nidib la wʋsa sɔ' kae ka kʋ yɛl ye,
‘Anɔ'ɔnɛ bɛ Job yin ka nan zi' dii tigɛ.’
32Saan sid nan zi' gbɛn yiŋa,
bɔzugɔ m di'esid saam wʋsa m yin.
33Mam pʋ su'a m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd
wʋʋ sieba niŋid si'em la.
34Mam pʋ zɔt nidibi na pian' m yɛla si'em.
M mɛ pʋ zɔt ye m yidim na diisim nyan
ka linzug kɛ ka m fɔn baanlimm ka kʋ yi yiŋa.
35Kassa, sɔ' kae na wʋm tisi maa?
M pɔya ye man yɛl si'el la wʋsa anɛ sida.
Gɔsima, m tiki m nu'ug.
Kɛl ka Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la wʋm tisim!
Sɔm man tʋm taal si'a ka li an kasɛt,
ala ka m na nyɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.
36Asida mɛnɛ, m na zaŋi li buki m biankimpiiung zug.
M na pidi li nwɛnɛ na'am zupibig nɛ.
37M na yɛl Wina'am man tʋm si'el wʋsa,
ka ʋki m zug agɔla o tuon.
38M ya'a zuun pɔɔg kanɛ ka m kuod la
bɛɛ faaɛn li yi o daana nu'ugin,
li na kaasi pa'al ye m tʋm taal.
39M ya'a di pɔɔg la zʋʋd
ka kɛ ka banɛ kua kuob la kpiid kɔ'ɔm,
40Wina'am on kɛl ka m ya'a bʋd ki nɛ mui,
mɔɔd nɛ gɔn'ɔs ma'aa on yim.”
Job antu'a naarɛ la.

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
Elihu
1Nidib atan' nwa' da pʋ lɛm pian' Job si'ela bɔzugɔ o da tɛn'ɛs ye o pʋ mɔr gbɛlʋŋɔ. 2Amaa Elihu onɛ an Barakɛl biig ka an Ram yir nid ka yi Buz na la da bɛɛ ani, ka o sʋʋnr da pɛlig nɛ Job hali, on tɛn'ɛs ye o anɛ pʋpiel ka nyɔn Wina'am la zug. 3O sʋʋnr mɛ da pɛlig nɛ Job zuanama atan' la bɔzugɔ ban da pʋ nyaŋi pa'al o gbɛlʋŋʋ an si'ela, ka li kɛ ka li nwɛnɛ Wina'am ka' bʋʋd la.
4Job zuanama atan' la da an kpɛɛmnam ka Elihu an biigi ba sʋʋgin la zug, o da sinnɛ baanlimm ka ba pian'ad. 5Amaa on da nyɛ ka ba fɔn ka pʋ lɛbisid Job ya'as la, o sʋʋnr da pɛlignɛ.
6Ka Elihu onɛ an Barakɛl biig ka yi Buz teŋin na la yɛl ye;
“Yanamɛ an kpɛɛmnam
ka man an biigi ya sʋʋgin la zug
ka m gi'igi ya ka pʋ lɛbisi m nɔɔrɛ.
7M tɛn'ɛs ye, ‘Zuobpielim na pian'ad nɛ ya'am
ka ayʋma-zu'oya mɛ an baŋir.’
8Amaa li ya'a an sida, li anɛ siig kanɛ bɛ ninsaalin,
ka Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la vʋ'ʋsi niŋ o pʋʋgin la
linɛ tisid baŋir.
9Li ka' banɛ kʋdig ma'aa mɔr ya'am
bɛɛ mi' linɛ an sidaa.
10Alazug ka m yɛl ye,
Kɛlisimi mam mɛ mɔr kʋkɔsi'a ye m lɛbis
ka mam mɛ na yɛli ya mam mi' si'el.
11Tɔ', yanamɛ pian'adin la, m mɔdiginnɛ an baanlimm,
ka kɛlisid ka ya mɔ hali
ye ya nyɛ ya'am pian'adi lɛbis o.
12M mɔdigi kɛlisi ya pian'ad la hali,
amaa ya sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ nyaŋi pa'al Job gbɛlʋŋ,
bɛɛ on tʋm si'el ka li pʋ naraa.
13Mid ka ya yɛl ye, ‘Tinamɛ mɔr ya'am si'a nwa':
ti bas o niŋ Wina'am nu'ugin,
ka onɛ mi' on na niŋ o si'em.’
14Amaa Job pʋ pian' tisi ma,
alazugɔ m kʋ gandig o wʋʋ yanamɛ lɛbis o si'em laa.”
15Ka Elihu yʋ'ʋn yɛl ye,
“Li nyaŋi ba nɛ ka ba zi' ban na lɛn lɛbisif si'ela;
ba nɔɔr lɛbnɛ biaunkin.
16Ban sadigim fɔn ka zi' ban na lɛbis o si'em la,
m kpɛm mɔdigi sinnaa?
17Mam mɛ na lɛbisi m nɔɔr;
m mɛ na yɛl mam mi' si'el.
18Bɔzugɔ, pian'ad pamm bɛɛ m sʋʋnrin,
ka m zig ye m mɔdigi gʋ'ʋŋ.
19M sʋʋnr pɛ'ɛli nɛ pian'ad
nwɛnɛ daam na pɛ'ɛl yʋʋr hali bɔɔd fudigir si'em la.
20M na pian' ka vʋ'ʋs,
m na ya'ae m nɔŋgban nɛ pian'.
21M kʋ pian' baregaŋ pian'ad
bɛɛ m pian' dʋ'ʋs sɔ'ɔɔ.
22M ya'a mi'in baregaŋ pian'ad,
Wina'am onɛ maalim la naan san'aminim.”

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
1Amaa Elihu lɛn yɛl ye,
“Job, nannanna kɛlisimi m pian'ad;
kɛlisim man ye m tu'asif si'el la sʋ'ʋŋa.
2M yʋ'ʋn na ya'ae m nɔɔri pian'
ka yɛli m nɔɔri mɔr si'el.
3M pian'ad la anɛ pʋpielim pian'ad;
li yitnɛ m sʋʋnrin na, ka faad kae.
4Wina'am Siig la maal mam;
Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la vʋ'ʋsʋm kɛ ka m vʋe.
5Fʋ ya'a na nyaŋ, fʋn gandigim;
ti'ebim sʋ'ʋŋa, ka ti gandis taaba.
6Man nɛ fʋ anɛ yinne Wina'am tuon;
ba mɛ nɔk nɛ ya'adi maalim.
7Da kɛ ka man yɛla kpɛn'ɛsif dabiem,
bɛɛ tɛn'ɛs ye m na mugusif halii.
8Amaa fʋ yɛlim nyain ka m tʋba wʋm,
asida m pʋn wʋm pian'abama wʋsa, ye,
9‘M anɛ nyain ka pʋ mɔr tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ;
m anɛ nyain ka ka' taalɛ.
10La'an nɛ wala, Wina'am ye m tʋm taal;
o zaŋim ka m lieb o dataa.
11 O gbarim nɛ bana;
ka man ken zin'isi'a wʋsa ka o gɔsidim.’
12Amaa m yɛtif ye fʋ ka' bʋʋd nɛ'ɛŋa nwa' nii,
bɔzugɔ, Wina'am gat saal woo.
13Bɔ kimm ka fʋ nyɔn
ye o pʋ gandigid ninsaal bu'osa wʋsa?
14Wina'am ɛɛn pian'anɛ pian'ad kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb,
amaa ka saal pʋ gban'adi li gbinnɛ.
15 Saalib ya'a ɛɛn gbisid yʋ'ʋŋ la,
saŋkan la ka Wina'am nied yɛla pa'annɛ ba zaansʋŋ pʋʋgin.
16O pian'adi tisidi ba ka nied yɛla pa'annɛ ba,
ka kɛn'ɛsidi ba nɛ nimmua.
17Linɛ na kɛ ka ba bas tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd
ka gu'usid nɛ ba dʋ'ʋsi-m-mɛŋ wʋsa ni.
18Ala ka o na gu' ba ka ba kʋ kpii,
bɛɛ ba sig kpi'im teŋa.
19Wina'am mɛ tun'e digil nid nɛ ban'as
hali ka li wʋm o sʋ'ʋŋa, ka zabid o hali.
20Ani ka o yaama yinɛ diib,
ka diib ya'a pʋn malis si'em o pʋ bɔɔda.
21Ka o waŋim hali naae,
ka kpɛlim kɔnbdaad ma'aa.
22Saŋkan ka o yʋ'ʋn li'el yaʋg,
ka o nyɔvʋr bɛ Akum nu'usin.
23La'an nɛ wala maliaknam tusa si'em la ni yinne
ya'a zi'en o nɔba zugʋ aan o nu'unwɛ'ɛd,
ka yɛl niŋkan sɔb linɛ nar,
24ka zɔɔ o nimbaanlig ka yɛl ye,
‘Da kɛ ka o ba'as yaʋgʋnɛɛ;
bɔzugɔ m yɔɔ o sam.’
25Ala ka o niŋgbina na lɛn kpɛ'ɛŋ;
ka o lieb nwɛnɛ on da an dasaŋ la.
26Ka o ya'a sɔs Wina'am o na zɔɔ o nimbaanlig,
o na nyɛ Wina'am nindaa ka maal sumalisim pamm;
ka Wina'am lɛbis o zi'el bɛllim sʋŋin.
27Ka o zi'en nidib tuon ka yʋ'ʋm yɛl ye,
‘Man da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd, ka niŋ linɛ pʋ nara,
amaa ba daa pʋ tɛki m tʋbir wʋʋ lin nar si'em.
28O faanm siig ka m pʋ kpii,
ka m na bɛ nɛɛsimin vʋe nɛ sumalisim.’
29Wina'am sid tʋmnɛ anwa saŋa pamm
tisid saalib;
30ka faandi ba yisid kumin
ka kɛt ka vʋm nɛɛsim niedi ba san'an.
31Job, an baanlimm ka wʋm;
kɛlisimi m pian'ad la sʋ'ʋŋa.
32Fʋ ya'a mɔr lɛbisʋg, fʋn lɛbisim.
Pian'am ka m bɔɔd ye fʋ nyɛnɛ bʋʋd.
33Ya'a ka' alaa, fʋn kɛlisim mam mɔr si'el ye m yɛlif;
an baanlimm, ka m na pa'alif ya'am.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
translation_text:
1Ka Elihu yʋ'ʋn yɛl ye,
2“Wʋmminɛ m pian'ad, yanam banɛ an ya'am dima;
kɛlisimi, yanam banɛ zamis ka mɔr mi'ilim hali la.
3 Bɔzugɔ, tʋbiri wɛligid pian'ad
wʋʋ zilimi lɛmmid diib si'em la.
4Kɛlli ka ti mɛŋ-mɛŋ kpansi baŋ linɛ an sida;
kɛlli ka ti zamisi baŋ linɛ an sʋm.
5Job yɛl ye, man ka' taalɛ:
‘Amaa Wina'am pʋ tisim m bʋʋdɛ.
6La'an nɛ man mɔr sida la,
o ye m anɛ ziri sɔb;
la'an nɛ mam pʋ tʋm taal la,
o pu'alimim bɛ'ɛd bɛ'ɛdi.’
7Fʋ nan mi' nyɛ sɔ' ka o nwɛnɛ Job, bɛɛ?
O nɔk nimpʋnannim ka li nwɛnɛ ku'om ka o nuudnɛ.
8Bugusim dim ma'aa aan o sɔnsidim taas;
ka o dɔllim taas an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdim gʋllim.
9Bɔzugɔ o yɛt ye, ‘Ninsaal ya'a bɔɔd on ma'am Wina'am sʋnf si'em
ka o kʋ dii li nyɔɔdɛ.’
10Dinzugɔ, kɛlisimi sʋ'ʋŋa yanam banɛ an ya'am dim la.
Wina'am kʋ maligin tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ
Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la kʋ niŋ linɛ pʋ nara.
11Wina'am yɔɔd tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim nɛ
ka li dɔlisid ban tʋm si'em la;
asida ban tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd si'a la na dɔlli ba.
12Ya'a an sida, Wina'am kʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛdɛ,
Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la kʋ nyɛ piel ka ye sabillɛ.
13Anɔ'ɔnɛ tis Wina'am suor ka o sʋ'oe teŋgbauŋ la?
Bɛɛ anɔ'ɔnɛ da kɛ ka o sʋ'ʋg dunia nwa' wʋsa?
14Wina'am ya'a gban'anɛ o pʋtɛn'ɛrin
ye o vaae o siig nɛ o vʋm lɛbis o mɛŋ ni,
15ninsaalib wʋsa naan mɛlimin;
ba naan lɛbin tintannin.
16Fʋ ya'a sid mɔr ya'am tun'e bakid yɛla,
fʋn kɛlisim ka wʋm man ye m yɛl si'el la.
17Ninkanɛ kis yɛlsida na tun'e an na'aba?
Ka fʋ na tun'e zɛrig Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb
ka an sida daan nɛ paŋ sɔb laa?
18Ka' Onɛ yɛt na'anam ye,
‘Ya pʋ mɔr vɔɔnrɛ,’
ka yɛt yʋ'ʋr dim ye, ‘Ya anɛ bugusim dim laa?’
19O pʋ kpɛn'ɛd kpɛɛmnam zug
bɛɛ gɔs ka kpan'am dim gat nɔŋ dima;
bɔzugɔ, onɛ maali ba wʋsa.
20Ba tun'e kpi yʋ'ʋŋ tisʋʋs nif aŋir pʋʋgin;
Wina'am kɛt ka saalib kpiid vuguri,
ka yisid kpi'euŋ dimi ba kpi'euŋ zin'igin ka li pʋ tɔiya.
21Saalibi ken zin'isi'a wʋsa, Wina'am gɔsidnɛ,
o nyɛti ba nɔbir yakir wʋsa.
22Lik zin'ig bɛɛ su'asir kae
ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim na tun'e su'aa.
23Li ka' tilas ye Wina'am dɛŋin gban'e
zi'el saŋkanɛ ka o na kad saalib sariaa.
24O ya'amin ka o yisid kpi'euŋ dimi ba zin'isin ka pʋ vɛɛnsida
ka kɛ ka sieba di'e ba zin'ig.
25On mi' ba tʋʋma la zug
ka o yisidi ba yʋ'ʋŋ vuguri,
ka ba yɛla wʋsa naae.
26Saalib nini ni ka o bʋ'ʋdi ba
ban tʋm taal la zug.
27Bɔzugɔ, ba zan'as ye ba kʋ dɔl oo,
ka ba ba'a kae o zi'ela la nii.
28Ba namisid nɔŋ dim ka ba kaasid
ka li tuak Wina'am sʋnfʋn.
29Amaa o ya'a gban'e ye o kʋ lɛbis si'ela, anɔ'ɔnɛ na zɛrig o?
O ya'a su'a o nindaa, anɔ'ɔnɛ na tun'e nyɛɛ o?
La'an nɛ wala onɛ sʋ'oe saalib nɛ sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa,
30ka na gu' ka bugusim sɔb kʋ di na'am
ka bɛnd saalibi kpɛn'ɛsi ba mɔɔgɔ.
31Amaa nid ya'a yɛl Wina'am ye,
‘M tʋm taal, m kʋ lɛm pɔ'ɔgi fɔ.
32M ya'a tʋm taal ka zi',
fʋn pa'alimim ka m kʋ lɛm paasɛ.’
33Fʋn sadigim ki'is Wina'am nɔɔr la,
fʋ tɛn'ɛs ka o na tisif fʋn bɔɔd si'elaa?
Fʋnɛ na baŋi li, ka ka' manɛ;
dinzug, yɛlim fʋn gban'e si'em.
34Nimbanɛ gban'ad pian'ad gbin la yɛl ya,
ka ya'am dim mɛ siak man yɛt si'el la ka ye,
35Job pian'adnɛ ya'am ka'alʋg pian'ad;
o pian'ad la pʋn ka' vɔɔnrɛ.
36Fʋ ya'a kpans Job pian'ad ka gɔsi li kii,
fʋ na baŋ ye li anɛ sida ye o sid anɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb.
37Li kas-kas anɛ on tʋm bɛ'ɛd ka lɛn ki'is Wina'am nɔɔr la,
ka zi'e ti tuonnɛ pian'adi takidi
maligim tukid Wina'am sʋnf.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
