11Fʋ ya'a ti digi bɔɔd kum fʋ na fabil hali,
bɔzugɔ fʋ niŋgbiŋ nɛ fʋ giinla wʋsa gɛnnɛ
12ka fʋ yʋ'ʋn yɛt ye, “Bɔ ka m daa pʋ zamis ya'am?
Bɔ ka m daa kis sɔ' na sa'ali ma?
13M daa pʋ di'e m pa'an la nɔɔrɛ.
M daa pʋ siak m karimsaamnamɛ pa'an si'el la.
14San'auŋ yʋ'ʋn bɔɔdi paam,
man ti ye m baŋ la ka nyan diim nidib sʋʋgin.”
15Numi fʋ mɛŋ bulig ku'om,
ku'okanɛ bunɛ fʋ mɛŋ buligin la.
16Da nwɛnɛ bulkanɛ pʋbid yɔɔg-yɔɔg
ka li ku'om yadigid suoraadinɛ.
17Kɛl ka fʋ bulig ku'om anɛ fʋn ma'aa din;
mid ka fʋ kɛ ka saam nuudi sʋŋidif.
18Wina'am na niŋi fʋ bulig la albareka.
Mɔr sumalisim nɛ pu'a kanɛ ka fʋ di fʋ dasannimin la.
19O vɛnlim nwɛnɛ mɔlif bɛɛ walnya'aŋ nɛ,
kɛl ka o bin'isa nɛ o niŋgbiŋ la mɔrif nyɛlʋg saŋa wʋsa.
20M biiga, bɔ ka fʋ basi fʋ mɛŋ ka pu'agɔɔndir nyaŋi fɔ?
Bɔ ka fʋ ya'amlɛog lɛɛ kpɛn' onɛ ka' fʋ pu'a?
21Wina'am nyɛt fʋn maan si'el la wʋsa,
fʋn ken zin'isi'a wʋsa nied paalʋ o san'an.
22Bugusim sɔb tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd anɛ bɛndigi lɛn tis o mɛŋ.
Ba mɛŋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi gban'adi ba ya'as.
23Ban pʋ mɔr a-gban'a-m-mɛŋ la zug ka ba kpiid.
Ba mɛŋ yalimisi kʋʋdi ba.

english_text:
Don't Be Foolish
1 My child, suppose you agree
to pay the debt of someone,
who cannot repay a loan.
2Then you are trapped
by your own words,
3and you are now in the power
of someone else.
Here is what you should do:
Go and beg for permission
to call off the agreement.
4Do this before you fall asleep
or even get sleepy.
5Save yourself, just as a deer
or a bird tries to escape
from a hunter.
6You lazy people can learn
by watching an anthill.
7Ants don't have leaders,
8but they store up food
during harvest season.
9How long will you lie there
doing nothing at all?
When are you going to get up
and stop sleeping?
10 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
11Suddenly, everything is gone,
as though it had been taken
by an armed robber.
12Worthless liars go around
13 winking and giving signals
to deceive others.
14They are always thinking up
something cruel and evil,
and they stir up trouble.
15But they will be struck
by sudden disaster
and left without a hope.
16There are six or seven
kinds of people
the Lord doesn't like:
17Those who are too proud
or tell lies or murder,
18those who make evil plans
or are quick to do wrong,
19those who tell lies in court
or stir up trouble
in a family.
20Obey the teaching
of your parents—
21always keep it in mind
and never forget it.
22Their teaching will guide you
when you walk,
protect you when you sleep,
and talk to you
when you are awake.
23The Law of the Lord is a lamp,
and its teachings
shine brightly.
Correction and self-control
will lead you through life.
24They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
25Don't let yourself be attracted
by the charm and lovely eyes
of someone like that.
26A woman who sells her love
can be bought for as little
as the price of a meal.
But making love
to another man's wife
will cost you everything.
27If you carry burning coals,
you burn your clothes;
28if you step on hot coals,
you burn your feet.
29And if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you pay the price.
30We don't put up with thieves,
not even with one who steals
for something to eat.
31And thieves who get caught
must pay back
seven times what was stolen
and lose everything.
32But if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you will destroy yourself
by your own stupidity.
33You will be beaten
and forever disgraced,
34because a jealous husband
can be furious and merciless
when he takes revenge.
35He won't let you pay him off,
no matter what you offer.
translation_text:
Da kaanb ye fʋ na yɔ sɔ' sammɛ
1M biiga, fʋ ya'a nam mi' kaanbnɛ ye fʋ di'e sɔ' samme yɔ,
ka tik nu'ugʋ tis saan;
2bɛɛ nam mi' pian'anɛ pian'ad ka li diif
ka kaanbi zi'el ka li gɛɛlif,
3ala m biiga, baŋim ye fʋ bɛ nɛ o sɔb nu'usin,
amaa fʋn na niŋ si'em yii li pʋʋginɛ nwa':
zɔm keŋ o san'an tɔ'ɔtɔ
sie fʋ mɛŋ ka nwɛ' o nu'ug.
4Niŋim tɔ'ɔtɔ ka da maan galim
bɛɛ bɔɔd ye fʋ vʋ'ʋs bɛɛ zɔɔnsim ka nyaan tʋmm.
5Zɔm yi bɛndig la pʋʋgin wʋʋ walig
bɛɛ niiŋe na nyɛ sʋlʋg ka ianki yi si'em la.
6Yanam gbanya'anama, zamisimi ya'am yi salinsa'asin,
gɔsimi ban tʋm si'el la ka gban'e li gbin.
7Ba ka' tuongat bɛɛ na'ab
bɛɛ onɛ sʋ'oe baa.
8Amaa ba la'asid diib tigir saŋa
ka su'ad zʋʋdi gur kɔ'ɔm saŋa.
9Gbanyan'a la ye o gbis daba ala?
Ka bʋndaar ka o na nie gbɛɛminɛ?
10 On yɛt si'el anɛ ye, “Kɛl ka m gbis bi'ela, ka zɔɔnsim bi'ela
ka kpɛn'ɛsi m nu'us gɛɛgʋni vʋ'ʋs.”
11Amaa on bɛ gbɛɛmin la, nɔŋ na kena wʋʋ na'ayiig nɛ
ka fara kpɛn' o nwɛnɛ faandibi kena faaɛn o nɛ.
12Nimbɛ'ɛdnam bɛɛ
banɛ ka' gban'ar la ginnɛ ma'ad ziri.
13Ba amisidi ba nini, ka sɔɔndi ba nɔba,
ka tiesid nu'us,
14ka gban'ad gban'abɛ'ɛdi ba sʋnfʋn,
ka ieed yɛla tugun nidib zin'ig wʋsa.
15Nɛ'ɛŋa zug tɔɔg na di'igi ba,
ka ba paam sapu'ad bɛ'ɛd bɛ'ɛdi
ka onɛ na ti'ebi ba kae.
16Bʋnama ayɔpɔi bɛ ka Zugsɔb la kis hali
ka pʋ bɔɔd ye o nyɛ ka ninsaal niŋi li.
17-19Bʋn ban anɛ:
nyɛɛsim gɔsig
nɛ zilim kanɛ ma'ad ziri
nɛ nu'ubanɛ kʋʋd nimbanɛ pʋ tʋm taalɛ
nɛ pʋtɛn'ɛr kanɛ gban'ad gban'abɛ'ɛd
nɛ onɛ nini mu'oe ka o kirid tɔ'ɔtɔ ye o tʋm bɛ'ɛd
nɛ onɛ dit ziri kasɛt sariakadib zin'igin
nɛ onɛ tugun ba'abiis ka ba zabid.
Dau nɛ pu'a san'auŋ sa'alʋg yɛla
20M biiga, tʋmi fʋ saamme ye fʋ tʋm si'el la,
ka da tami fʋ ma sa'alʋg laa.
21Kɛl ka ba pian'ad la bɛɛ fʋ ni saŋa wʋsa,
lɔɔmi li kɔlli fʋ niŋgɔɔnrin wʋʋ niŋgɔnkɔrig nɛ.
22Ba pa'ala la na sʋ'ʋŋif zin'ig wʋsa,
ka gurif yʋ'ʋŋ, ka mɛ sa'alif nintaŋ.
23Ba pa'ala la anɛ nɛɛsim kanɛ nie,
ba sa'alʋg la na pa'alif fʋn na bɛ si'em,
ka li anɛ nyɔvʋr suori tisif.
24Li na sʋ'ʋŋif ka fʋ yi pu'agɔɔnda nu'usin,
nɛ banɛ an nidib pu'ab ka mɔr nɔmalisim ye ba yuomif la.
25Da kɛ ka fʋ ya'am kpɛn' pu'a la vɛnlim zugɔ,
da kɛ ka o nindaa vɛnlim tiaki fʋ ya'am.
26Pu'agɔɔndir yɔɔd pʋ gat bodobodo gbil ligidii,
amaa sɔ' pu'a na san'ami fʋ nyɔvʋr wʋsa.
27Fʋ na kpa'ae bugumsaana niŋi fʋ nɔba zug
ka li kʋ la'aŋi fʋ fuugɔɔ?
28Fʋ na nɔ bugum nɛ nɔba
ka li kʋ vʋnligi fɔɔ?
29Ala mɛn ka li aaɛn tis onɛ wʋsa dig nɛ sɔ' pu'a.
Onɛ wʋsa si'is pu'a nwa' kʋ yi namisʋgʋnɛ.
30Na'ayiig ya'a zu ka li anɛ o pʋʋr yɛla,
nidib na kɛɛs o bas linzugɔɔ?
31Ba ya'a gban'e o, o na yɔ on zu si'el la lɛbis nɔɔr ayɔpɔi;
o na nɔk on mɔr si'el la wʋsa yɔ.
32Amaa dau kanɛ san'am pu'a ka' ya'am,
o kʋdim san'amid nɛ o mɛŋ.
33Bʋ'ʋd nɛ zufa'asim na aan o yɔɔd,
ka o nyan la na bɛ saŋa wʋsa;
34bɔzugɔ, fufum na kɛ ka dau sʋʋnr duoe
ka o ya'a ti ye o zab, o kʋ zɔt nimbaanliga.
35Si'el kae ka fʋ na nɔki yɔɔ o ka o di'e,
si'el kae ka fʋ na tis o ka o sʋnf ma'ae.

english_text:
The Foolishness of Unfaithfulness
1My son, pay close attention
and don't forget
what I tell you to do.
2Obey me, and you will live!
Let my instructions be
your greatest treasure.
3Keep them at your fingertips
and write them
in your mind.
4Let wisdom be your sister
and make common sense
your closest friend.
5They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
6From the window of my house,
I once happened to see
7some foolish young men.
8It was late in the evening,
sometime after dark.
9One of these young men
turned the corner
and was walking by the house
of an unfaithful wife.
10She was dressed fancy
like a woman of the street
with only one thing in mind.
11She was one of those women
who are loud and restless
and never stay at home,
12who walk street after street,
waiting to trap a man.
13She grabbed him and kissed him,
and with no sense of shame,
she said:
14“I had to offer a sacrifice,
and there is enough meat
left over for a feast.
15So I came looking for you,
and here you are!
16The sheets on my bed
are bright-colored cloth
from Egypt.
17And I have covered it
with perfume made of myrrh,
aloes, and cinnamon.
18“Let's go there
and make love all night.
19My husband is traveling,
and he's far away.
20He took a lot of money along,
and he won't be back home
before the middle
of the month.”
21And so, she tricked him
with all of her sweet talk
and her flattery.
22At once he followed her
like an ox on the way
to be slaughtered,
or like a fool on the way
to be punished
23and killed with arrows.
He was no more than a bird
rushing into a trap,
without knowing
it would cost him his life.
24My son, pay close attention
to what I have said.
25Don't even think about
that kind of woman
or let yourself be misled
by someone like her.
26Such a woman has caused
the downfall and destruction
of a lot of men.
27Her house is a one-way street
leading straight down
to the world of the dead.
translation_text:
1M biiga, tɛnr man yɛlif si'el la,
ka da tam man zi'elif ye fʋ tʋm si'em la.
2Maalim man pa'al si'el la, ka fʋ na vʋe.
Gu'usim sʋ'ʋŋa ka dɔlli m pa'ala la,
wʋʋ fʋn gu'usid nɛ fʋ nif bielif yɛla si'em la.
3Kɛl ka m pa'ala la bɛɛ fʋ ni saŋa wʋsa;
lɔɔmi li tabili fʋ nu'ubibis,
ka sɔbi li digili fʋ sʋnfʋn.
4Yɛlim ya'am ye, “Fʋ anɛ m taʋn,”
ka buol baŋir ye fʋ sizua.
5Ba na sʋŋif ka fʋ luak pu'agɔɔnda,
nɛ pu'a banɛ dɔl dapi pian'ad zufa'asim pian'ad la.
Pu'agɔɔndir la yɛla
6Daar yinne ka m daa vɛɛsi m takoro ni
gɔsid yiŋ ye m nyɛ linɛ bɛ.
7M daa nyɛ dasam bɛdegʋ banɛ ya'am pʋ bi' nannɛ,
amaa yinne daa bɛɛ ani an gɛdʋg.
8O daa dɔlnɛ tempʋʋgin suor la gati
ti paae lɔdsi'a ka pu'a sɔ' yir bɛɛ ani.
O daa dɛn'ɛdnɛ yir la gat
9ka nintaŋ bɔɔd liib
ka li sɔbid nyɔs-nyɔs.
10Ka pu'a la sia'al o,
ka maal o mɛŋ wʋʋ pu'agɔɔndir nɛ,
ka pin'ili bɛlisid o.
11O daa anɛ pu'a kanɛ zugʋ kpi'em ka pʋ zɔt nyannɛ,
ka bɛ pal la zugʋ ken saŋa wʋsa,
12ka zi'e lɔdigin,
bɛɛ suoraug la zug, bɛɛ da'an la gur.
13O daa kuak dasaŋ la, ka muak o,
ka gɔs o nindaa kii, ka ye,
14“M maali m maan zina,
ka maan la ni'im bɛ.
15Dinzug ka m yina ieedif;
m ieef nɛ hali ka yʋ'ʋn nyɛɛf nwa'!
16M da'anɛ gadʋ pien sʋma Egipt teŋin
nɔki ligili m gadʋg la.
17M nɔknɛ tudaar sʋma puusi li
ka li anɛ bʋnnyubisa buudi wʋsa.
18Kpɛn'ɛm na digin nɛ mam yʋ'ʋŋa
ka bɛog ti nie, ka ti wʋsa na di malisim.
19M sid ka' yinnɛ,
o duoe nɛ suori keŋ lallisa.
20On nɔk ligidsi'a la pʋ pɔɔda,
o na paae bakuai ayi'.”
21Pu'a la daa pan'as o nɛ nɔŋgban malisiŋ,
ka zaŋ antu'a malisiŋi gban'e o.
22Ka o kpɛn yuk tɔ'ɔtɔ dɔl pu'a la nya'aŋ wʋʋ naaf ka ba mɔri wa'ae kʋʋb,
bɛɛ waligi ianki sig baŋin
23ka ba kʋns o sʋnf nɛ piim si'em la.
O daa nwɛnɛ niiŋe na ian'adi ken bɛndigin
ka zi' ye o nyɔvʋr bɛnnɛ la.
24Alazugɔ, m biisɛ, kɛlisimi man yɛt si'el la sʋ'ʋŋa
ka yɔ'ɔgi ya tʋbaa wʋm nɛ nimmua.
25Mid ka ya kɛ ka ya ya'amlɛog kpɛn' pu'a bannam buudii,
pʋn da bie lɛbi ba san'an baa bi'elaa.
26O nyaŋi san'am dap bɛdegʋ.
Ya'a kpɛlim banɛ kpi la, fʋ kʋ nyaŋi kaali baa.
27Fʋ ya'a keŋ o yin, fʋn baŋim ye fʋ bɛ nɛ suori ken kpi'im teŋ.
Li anɛ suogiŋ kanɛ ziidi fʋ ken kumin.

english_text:
In Praise of Wisdom
1 With great understanding,
Wisdom is calling out
2as she stands at the crossroads
and on every hill.
3She stands by the city gate
where everyone enters the city,
and she shouts:
4“I am calling out
to each one of you!
5Good sense and sound judgment
can be yours.
6Listen, because what I say
is worthwhile and right.
7I always speak the truth
and refuse to tell a lie.
8Every word I speak is honest,
not one is misleading
or deceptive.
9“If you have understanding,
you will see that my words
are just what you need.
10Let instruction and knowledge
mean more to you than silver
or the finest gold.
11 Wisdom is worth much more
than precious jewels
or anything else you desire.”
Wisdom Speaks
12I am Wisdom—Common Sense
is my closest friend;
I possess knowledge
and sound judgment.
13If you respect the Lord,
you will hate evil.
I hate pride and conceit
and deceitful lies.
14I am strong, and I offer
sensible advice
and sound judgment.
15By my power kings govern,
and rulers make laws
that are fair.
16Every honest leader rules
with help from me.
17I love everyone who loves me,
and I will be found by all
who honestly search.
18I can make you rich and famous,
important and successful.
19What you receive from me
is more valuable
than even the finest gold
or the purest silver.
20I always do what is right,
21and I give great riches
to everyone who loves me.
22 From the beginning,
I was with the Lord.
I was there before he began
23to create the earth.
At the very first,
the Lord gave life to me.
24When I was born,
there were no oceans
or springs of water.
25My birth was before
mountains were formed
or hills were put in place.
26It happened long before God
had made the earth
or any of its fields
or even the dust.
27 I was there when the Lord
put the heavens in place
and stretched the sky
over the surface of the sea.
28I was with him when he placed
the clouds in the sky
and created the springs
that fill the ocean.
29I was there when he set
boundaries for the sea
to make it obey him,
and when he laid foundations
to support the earth.
30I was right beside the Lord,
helping him plan and build.
I made him happy each day,
and I was happy at his side.
31I was pleased with his world
and pleased with its people.
32 Pay attention, my children!
Follow my advice,
and you will be happy.
33Listen carefully
to my instructions,
and you will be wise.
34Come to my home each day
and listen to me.
You will find happiness.
35By finding me, you find life,
and the Lord will be pleased
with you.
36But if you don't find me,
you hurt only yourself,
and if you hate me,
you are in love with death.
translation_text:
Ya'am yɛla
1 Kɛlisimi! Aya'am buon la.
Abaŋir yis o mɛŋ paalʋ na.
2O nwɛnɛ pu'a zi'e suor kanɛ bɛ kʋkʋn zug
nɛ suokita ni.
3O zi'enɛ suokanɛ dɔlli kpɛn'ɛd tempʋʋgin la,
ani ka o zi'e buon nidib la ye,
4“Gɔsimi, m pian'adi tisidi ya wʋsa;
m buonnɛ yanam banɛ wʋsa bɛ dunia ni!
5Yanam ya'am pɔɔdim dima, bɔɔmi ya'am.
Yanam banɛ an zɔnnɛ, mɔɔmi ka gban'e pian'ad gbin.
6Kɛlisimi ka m mɔri yɛlsʋm sieba ye m yɛl;
man yɛt si'el la wʋsa dɔlli suor.
7Man nɔɔr tu'asidnɛ sida;
man kisnɛ ziri pian'ad.
8Linɛ yiti m nɔɔrin na wʋsa mɔri sʋŋir;
ziri baa yinne kae, ka li mɛ kʋ kɛ ka sɔ' kpɛn' mɔɔgɔ.
9Li nienɛ nyain tis banɛ gban'ad si'el gbin;
ka an tituaa tis banɛ mɔr mi'ilim sʋ'ʋŋa.
10Gaŋimi man pa'ala la, ka bas anzurifa,
ieemi baŋir ka kɛ sanlima.
11Man anɛ Aya'am, m gat bʋnsʋma wʋsa;
fʋn mɔr ya'amlɛog nɛ si'el wʋsa kʋ nyaŋi nɔki mak nɛ mam.
12Man anɛ Aya'am, m gban'ad si'el gbin;
man mɔr baŋir nɛ pʋtɛn'ɛsʋma.
13Zugsɔb la zɔtim anɛ fʋn na kis tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.
Man kis nyɛɛsim nɛ tita'alim,
nɛ suobɛ'ɛd nɛ ziri pian'ad wʋsa.
14M ya'a gban'e si'el m tʋmnɛ ala kimm.
Man gban'ad si'el gbin, ka mɛ mɔr paŋ.
15Man sʋŋid na'anam ka ba gɔsidi ba teŋ
ka pa'an tuongatib ka ba gban'ad wadsʋma.
16Manɛ sʋŋid tuongatib wʋsa dunia nwa' pʋʋgin
la'an nɛ kpi'emnam nɛ ninsʋma wʋsa.
17Man nɔŋnɛ banɛ nɔŋim la;
onɛ wʋsa ieed mam sid na nyɛɛm.
18Arezak nɛ na'asi bɛ nɛ man san'an,
kpan'am nɛ mɔrim linɛ pʋ naad bɛ nɛ man ni.
19Linɛ ka fʋ na paam man san'an la gat sanlima,
ka tisid bʋnsʋma ka li kʋ nyaŋi mak nɛ anzurifa sʋŋɔ.
20Mam bɛ nɛ pʋpielim bɛllim;
ka dɔl sida suor tituaa,
21ka tisid banɛ nɔŋim la kpan'am,
ka kɛt ka arezak pɛ'ɛnnɛ ba yir.
22 Man ka Zugsɔb la da dɛŋin maal yiiga;
on da nam pʋ maal si'el-si'el la ka mam pʋm bɛ.
23Pin'ilʋgʋn sa ka o maal mam,
manɛ an yiiga ka dunia nyaan pin'il.
24Ba da du'a man yiiga ka atɛuk nyaan maal,
saŋa kanɛ ka ku'om nam pʋ bun la.
25Zuoya nɛ kʋkʋna da nan kae la,
ka mam pʋm bɛ.
26Saŋa kan ka Wina'am nam pʋ maal dunia
nɛ teŋgbauŋ nɛ titanbin'isi.
27On da zi'el saŋgbauŋʋ li zin'igin la, m da bɛɛ ani,
saŋa kanɛ ka o da buoɛn ku'om nɛ teŋ bɛn la.
28O da kɛ ka saŋgbauŋ zi'en ki',
ka kɛ ka atɛuk pin'ili bun nɛ paŋ,
29ka zi'el nɔɔri tis atɛuk ku'om
ye li da pɛ'ɛli gaad on pa'al si'em la;
onɛ mɛ da pin'il dunia ɛɛnbir la.
30Saŋkan ka man da bɛɛ o san'an wʋʋ onɛ mi' mɛɛb yɛla nɛ.
Daar wʋsa manɛ da kɛt ka o mɔr sumalisim,
ka m mɛŋ da maan sumalisim o san'an saŋa wʋsa.
31M sʋnf da malis nɛ dunia la wʋsa
ka m nini tig nɛ ninsaal buudi.
32M biisɛ, nannanna kɛlisimini m pian'ad nwa';
albareka bɛ nɛ banɛ dɔl man yɛl si'el la.
33Kɛlisimini m pa'ala la ka paam ya'am,
mid ka ya nɛ'ɛsi lii bas.
34Albareka bɛ nɛ onɛ wʋsa wʋmi m pian'ad
ka bɛɛ m san'an daar wʋsa,
ka zi'e m za'anɔɔrini gur.
35Banɛ ieemi nyɛ la mɔr nyɔvʋr,
ka Zugsɔb la sʋnf mɛ na ma'ae nɛ ba.
36Banɛ pʋ nyɛ mam la na san'ami ba mɛŋ;
onɛ wʋsa pʋ bɔɔd mam bɔɔd nɛ kum.”

english_text:
Wisdom Gives a Feast
1Wisdom has built her house
with its seven columns.
2She has prepared the meat
and set out the wine.
Her feast is ready.
3She has sent her servant women
to announce her invitation
from the highest hills:
4“Everyone who is ignorant
or foolish is invited!
5All of you are welcome
to my meat and wine.
6If you want to live,
give up your foolishness
and let understanding
guide your steps.”
True Wisdom
7Correct a worthless bragger,
and all you will get
are insults and injuries.
8Any bragger you correct
will only hate you.
But if you correct someone
who has common sense,
you will be loved.
9If you have good sense,
instruction will help you
to have even better sense.
And if you live right,
education will help you
to know even more.
10 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of wisdom.
To have understanding,
you must know the Holy God.
11I am Wisdom. If you follow me,
you will live a long time.
12Good sense is good for you,
but if you brag,
you hurt yourself.
A Foolish Invitation
13Stupidity is reckless,
senseless, and foolish.
14She sits in front of her house
and on the highest hills
in the town.
15She shouts to everyone
who passes by,
16“If you are stupid,
come on inside!”
And to every fool she says,
17“Stolen water tastes best,
and the food you eat in secret
tastes best of all.”
18None who listen to Stupidity
understand that her guests
are as good as dead.
translation_text:
Aya'am nɛ yalimis yɛla
1Aya'am mɛɛ o yir,
ka ba' zan'antɔlis ayɔpɔi ka li zi'e sappi.
2O dʋg ni'im sʋ'ʋŋa ka maal damalisiŋ
ka li kpɛlim nidib la na kena di.
3O tʋm o tʋmtʋm pu'ab tempʋʋgin
ye ba buol nidib na ka ba di.
O zi'e teŋ la zin'ikanɛ dʋ la nii
kaasid agɔla yɛt ye,
4“Yanam banɛ ya'am nam pʋ bi' la, kemi na!”
Ka yɛl banɛ an zɔn la ye,
5“Kemi na dii m diib la
ka nu dankanɛ ka m digil la.
6Basim ya'amka'alʋg tʋʋma ka fʋ na vʋe;
ka dɔl baŋir suor sʋ'ʋŋa.”
7Fʋ ya'a sa'al nintʋ'ʋsim sɔb fʋ di'edi tʋ'ʋd;
fʋ ya'a sa'al nimbɛ'og o na zɛrigif.
8Da sa'al nintʋ'ʋsa ka o na kisigif;
amaa fʋ ya'a sa'al ya'am sɔb o na nɔŋif.
9Fʋ ya'a yɛl ya'am dim si'el li maligim paasidi ba nɛ ya'am.
Fʋ ya'a yɛl pʋpielnam si'el li paasidi ba nɛ baŋir.
10 Zugsɔb zɔtim an ya'am pin'ilʋg,
fʋ ya'a mi' Onɛ an Kasi la li anɛ baŋir.
11Ya'am paasidnɛ fʋ vʋm yʋma
ka fʋ na yuug dunia nwa' ni.
12Fʋ ya'a mɔr ya'am, fʋn nɔɔ na dii li malisim;
fʋ mɛ ya'a ka' ya'am, fʋn nɔɔ na di fara.
13Pu'ayaliŋ maannɛ vuud,
o zi' si'ela ka mɛ pʋ zɔt nyannɛ.
14O zi'inɛ o yir za'anɔɔrin,
bɛɛ digil o kʋk tempʋʋginɛ zin',
15ka buon banɛ gat
ka ba nini mu'oe nɛ ba tʋʋma la ye,
16“Yanam nimbanɛ ka' ya'am la, kpɛn'ɛmi na!”
Ka yɛt zɔn la ye,
17“Fʋ ya'a zu ku'om nu li malis nɛ.
Fʋ mɛ ya'a zu diibi su'a di, li malis nɛ hali.”
18Banɛ ka o buon la zi' ye nimbanɛ kpɛn'ɛd o yin la kpiidnɛ,
ba kʋ tun'e baŋ ye banɛ pʋn kpɛn' la bɛ yaʋgʋn kʋdim-kʋdim saa.

english_text:
Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some proverbs
of Solomon:
Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
make them sad.
2What you gain by doing evil
won't help you at all.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
3If you obey the Lord,
you won't go hungry;
if you are wicked,
God won't let you have
what you want.
4Laziness leads to poverty;
hard work makes you rich.
5At harvest season
it's smart to work hard,
but stupid to sleep.
6Everyone praises good people,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
7Good people are remembered
long after they are gone,
but the wicked
are soon forgotten.
8If you have good sense,
you will listen and obey;
if all you do is talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
9You will be safe,
if you always do right,
but you will get caught,
if you are dishonest.
10Deceit causes trouble,
and foolish talk
will bring you to ruin.
11The words of good people
are a source of life,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
12 Hatred stirs up trouble;
love overlooks the wrongs
that others do.
13If you have good sense,
it will show when you speak.
But if you are stupid,
you will be beaten
with a stick.
14If you have good sense,
you will learn all you can,
but foolish talk
will soon destroy you.
15Great wealth can be a fortress,
but poverty
is no protection at all.
16If you live right,
the reward is a good life;
if you are evil,
all you have is sin.
17Accept correction,
and you will find life;
reject correction,
and you will miss the road.
18You can hide your hatred
by telling lies,
but you are a fool
to spread lies.
19You will say the wrong thing
if you talk too much—
so be sensible and watch
what you say.
20The words of a good person
are like pure silver,
but the thoughts
of an evil person
are almost worthless.
21Many are helped
by useful instruction,
but fools are killed
by their own stupidity.
22When the Lord blesses you
with riches,
you have nothing to regret.
23Fools enjoy doing wrong,
but anyone with good sense
enjoys acting wisely.
24What evil people dread most
will happen to them,
but good people will get
what they want most.
25Those crooks will disappear
when a storm strikes,
but God will keep safe
all who obey him.
26Having a lazy person on the job
is like a mouth full of vinegar
or smoke in your eyes.
27If you respect the Lord,
you will live longer;
if you keep doing wrong,
your life will be cut short.
28If you obey the Lord,
you will be happy,
but there is no future
for the wicked.
29The Lord protects everyone
who lives right,
but he destroys anyone
who does wrong.
30Good people will stand firm,
but the wicked will disappear
from the land.
31Honest people speak sensibly,
but deceitful liars
will be silenced.
32If you obey the Lord,
you will always know
the right thing to say.
But no one will trust you
if you tell lies.
translation_text:
Solomon siilima
1Nɛ'ɛŋa anɛ Solomon siilima:
Bikanɛ mɔr ya'am ziankid o saam zug;
ka zɔn diisidi ba manam nyan.
2Fʋ ya'a dɔl zam suori paam kpan'am li kʋ sʋŋi fɔɔ,
amaa pʋpielim yisidif nɛ kumin.
3Zugsɔb la kʋ kɛ ka pʋpiel ken nɛ kɔ'ɔm,
ka mɛ kʋ kɛ ka nimbɛ'og nyɛ on bɔɔd si'ela.
4Gbanya'am kɛtnɛ ka fʋ lieb nɔŋdaan,
amaa fʋ ya'a tʋm hali, li na kɛ ka fʋ lieb arezak daan.
5Ya'am sɔb la'asid o ki nɛ bunib saŋa,
sieba mɛ ya'a ti bɛ bunibin ka fʋn bɛ gbɛɛmin, li anɛ nyan.
6Pʋpielnam na paam albareka pamm.
Nimbɛ'og pian'ad ziidi zabaa kenna.
7Ba ya'a tiɛn burikin yɛla li mɔri bareka kenna,
amaa nimbɛ'og yʋ'ʋr na pun'oe.
8Banɛ mɔr ya'am di'ednɛ sa'al sʋŋ,
amaa banɛ pian'ad nɛ zɔlimis la na ba'as yɔri.
9Sida dim kennɛ tuon ka dabiem kae,
amaa bugusim dim la ba na sɛnbigi ba.
10Onɛ amisid o nifʋ pa'an yɛlsu'ada ziidi yɛla kenna,
ka onɛ pian'ad pian'ayɛɛd na ba'as bɛ'ɛd.
11Pʋpiel pian'ad ziidnɛ vʋm kenna,
wʋʋ bulig ku'om bun si'em la;
amaa nimbɛ'og pian'ad ziidnɛ zaba kenna.
12 Kisidim mɔri yɛla kenna,
amaa nɔŋilim kɛtnɛ taab taali basid.
13Onɛ mi' yɛla bakid pian'ad nɛ ya'am,
amaa zi'ilim daan nya'aŋ tigid nɛ balaar.
14Ya'am sɔb paamidi baŋir kanɛ wʋsa ka o bɔɔd,
amaa zɔlʋg pian'ayɛɛd ziidnɛ san'auŋʋ kenna.
15Arezak sʋŋidi bʋndaan wʋʋ zaŋguom kpi'ema sʋŋid tempʋʋg si'em la,
amaa nɔŋ kɛtnɛ ka nɔŋdaan ba'asid yɔri.
16Tʋʋm sʋma sɔb yɔɔd anɛ vʋm,
amaa tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd yɔɔd anɛ tʋbtɛɛgir.
17Banɛ wʋm sa'alʋg na vʋe,
amaa banɛ yidig ka pʋ siak ye ba pa'ali ba la na zii ba taaba kpɛn' mɔɔg.
18Onɛ su'a mɔr kisidim o sʋʋnrin
anɛ dama'am sɔb,
onɛ ginnɛ yɛɛsid anɛ zɔlʋg.
19Fʋ ya'a pian'adi galis fʋ kʋ luak tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ,
amaa onɛ gban'ad o zilim anɛ ya'am sɔb.
20Pʋpiel pian'ad nwɛnɛ anzurifa sʋŋ nɛ,
nimbɛ'og pʋtɛn'ɛr anɛ zaalim.
21Pʋpielim dim pian'ad sʋŋid nidib bɛdegʋ,
amaa zɔn kpiidnɛ ba ya'amka'alʋg zug.
22Zugsɔb la albareka kɛt ka nid liebid arezak sɔb,
ka li pʋ ziid yɛla kennaa.
23Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nwɛnɛ di'ema tis zɔlʋg,
amaa nimbanɛ mɔr baŋir bɔɔdi ya'am.
24Bugusnamɛ zɔt si'el dabiem la nyaŋidi ba nɛ,
amaa pʋpielnam on na nyɛ ban bɔɔd si'el.
25Sisi'em ya'a da'ae li na mɔr nimbɛ'ɛdnam la gaad,
amaa pʋpielnam la zi'enɛ kiŋ-kiŋ saŋa wʋsa.
26Nwɛnɛ danmi'isʋgʋ mi'is nɔɔrin,
ka nyɔ'ɔs kpand nini si'em la,
ala ka gbanya'a aan tis onɛ tʋm o.
27Zugsɔb la zɔtim na kɛ ka fʋ vʋe yuug.
Nimbɛ'ɛdnam la kpiidnɛ ka ba daar pʋ paae.
28Ninsʋma ti'ir ziidi sumalisim kenna,
amaa nimbɛ'ɛdnam pʋ mɔr ti'ir si'a bɛogɔ.
29Zugsɔb la guri banɛ dɔl suosʋma la,
ka lɛɛ san'amid banɛ tʋm linɛ pʋ nara.
30Pʋpielnam na zi'e kiŋ-kiŋ saŋa wʋsa,
amaa nimbɛ'ɛdnam kʋ kpɛm bɛ teŋ la zugɔ.
31Pʋpielnam pian'adi ya'am,
amaa nɔɔr kanɛ pian'ad pian'abɛ'ɛd la na nyɛ san'auŋ.
32Pʋpielnam mi' linɛ nar ye ba pian',
amaa nimbɛ'ɛdnam pian'adnɛ pian'agɔlima.

english_text:
Watch What You Say and Do
1The Lord hates anyone
who cheats,
but he likes everyone
who is honest.
2Too much pride
can put you to shame.
It's wiser to be humble.
3If you do the right thing,
honesty will be your guide.
But if you are crooked,
you will be trapped
by your own dishonesty.
4When God is angry,
money won't help you.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
5If you are truly good,
you will do right;
if you are wicked,
you will be destroyed
by your own sin.
6Honesty can keep you safe,
but if you can't be trusted,
you trap yourself.
7When the wicked die,
their hopes die with them.
8Trouble goes right past
the Lord's people
and strikes the wicked.
9Dishonest people use gossip
to destroy their neighbors;
good people are protected
by their own good sense.
10When honest people prosper
and the wicked disappear,
the whole city celebrates.
11Good people bring prosperity
to their city,
but deceitful liars
can destroy a city.
12It's stupid to say bad things
about your neighbors.
If you are sensible,
you will keep quiet.
13A gossip tells everything,
but a true friend
will keep a secret.
14 A city without wise leaders
will end up in ruin;
a city with many wise leaders
will be kept safe.
15It's a dangerous thing
to guarantee payment
for someone's debts.
Don't do it!
16A gracious woman
will be respected,
but a ruthless man
will only get rich.
17Kindness is rewarded—
but if you are cruel,
you hurt yourself.
18Meanness gets you nowhere,
but goodness is rewarded.
19Always do the right thing,
and you will live;
keep on doing wrong,
and you will die.
20The Lord hates sneaky people,
but he likes everyone
who lives right.
21You can be sure of this:
All crooks will be punished,
but God's people won't.
22A beautiful woman
who acts foolishly
is like a gold ring
on the snout of a pig.
23Good people want what is best,
but troublemakers
hope to stir up trouble.
24Sometimes you can become rich
by being generous
or poor by being greedy.
25Generosity will be rewarded:
Give a cup of water,
and you will receive
a cup of water in return.
26Charge too much for grain,
and you will be cursed;
sell it at a fair price,
and you will be praised.
27Try hard to do right,
and you will win friends;
go looking for trouble,
and you will find it.
28Trust in your wealth,
and you will be a failure,
but God's people will prosper
like healthy plants.
29Fools who cause trouble
in the family
won't inherit a thing.
They will end up as slaves
of someone with good sense.
30Live right, and you will eat
from the life-giving tree.
And if you act wisely,
others will follow.
31 If good people are rewarded
here on this earth,
all who are cruel and mean
will surely be punished.
translation_text:
1Zugsɔb la kis zam makir,
amaa o ya'am bɔɔd linɛ ka li makir dɔl sida.
2Adʋ'ʋsi-m-mɛŋ ya'a gaad tuon, nyannɛ dɔl,
amaa a-sie-m-mɛŋ mɔri ya'am kenna.
3Ninsʋma sida la guri ba,
amaa banɛ ka' sida dim la, ba zam tʋʋma la na san'ami ba.
4Sʋnpɛɛn daar ya'a paae, kpan'am anɛ zaalim,
amaa pʋpielim yisid nid kumin.
5Pʋpielim dimi ka' gba'ar la,
zugʋ kɛ ka ba suor an sappi,
amaa bugusim dim la ka' alaa,
ba bugusim tʋʋma la vɛ'ɛgidi baa sigisid teŋin.
6Pʋpielim dim bɛllim sʋŋ la yisidi ba
amaa banɛ ka' sida la ya'amlɛogʋ gban'adi ba.
7Bugusim sɔb ya'a kpi o ti'ir wʋsa naae ya;
linɛ wʋsa ka o tɛn'ɛsid ye o tʋm nɛ o mɛŋ paŋ la na lieb zaalim.
8Wina'am yisid pʋpiel yɛla ni,
ka lɛɛ kɛ ka li keŋ bugusim sɔb la san'an.
9Onɛ zi' Wina'am la mɔr o nɔɔr pian'adi san'amid o kpi'a,
amaa baŋir na kɛ ka pʋpielim sɔb yii li pʋʋgin.
10Pʋpielim sɔb nu'ug ya'a mɔr, teŋ la mɔr sumalisim;
bugus ya'a kpi, nidib maannɛ sumalisim tansid agɔla.
11Albareka linɛ yit sida dim san'an na la zug ka teŋ la yʋ'ʋr na dʋ,
amaa bugus nɔɔri san'amidi li.
12Ninkanɛ nɛ'ɛsid o kpi'a la ka' ya'am,
amaa sida sɔb gban'ad o nɔɔr baanlimm.
13Bayɛʋg sɔb viigidnɛ nidib yɛlsu'ada,
amaa onɛ ka ba niŋ o yadda su'adi yɛla.
14Teŋ kanɛ pʋ mɔr banɛ sa'an la lit nɛ;
amaa banɛ sa'an ya'a bɛ, bi'esʋg kae ye ba kʋ nyaŋi.
15Onɛ kaanb ye o na di'e saan samme yɔ na nyɛ namisʋg,
onɛ wʋsa yis o nu'ugʋ li pʋʋgin mɔr yɔlisim.
16Pu'a kanɛ sʋnfʋ bʋgʋs la nyɛt na'asi,
amaa dap banɛ maannɛ ba ya'amin la na nyɛ nɛ kpan'am ma'aa.
17Pʋpiel sʋŋid o mɛŋ,
amaa zaba sɔb ieedi yɛla tisid o mɛŋ.
18Dau bugus di'edi ziri yɔɔd,
amaa onɛ bʋt pʋpielim di'edi yɛlsida yɔɔd.
19Pʋpielim sɔb amɛŋa nyɛt nyɔvʋr,
amaa onɛ kati dɔl bɛ'ɛd gbin la wa'anɛ kumin.
20Zugsɔb la kis banɛ an pʋkpɛnnim dim,
amaa o ya'am bɔɔd banɛ pʋ mɔr gbadaa.
21Li anɛ sida ye bugusim dim la kʋ nyɛ bʋʋd ka yi namisʋgʋ nɛ,
amaa pʋpielim dim la na nyɛ yɔlisim.
22Pu'a kanɛ vɛnl ka pʋ mɔr ya'am la
nwɛnɛ sanlima baŋi na tʋ kukur nyɔnya ni.
23Pʋpiel ya'am bɔɔdim naad nɛ sʋm,
amaa bugus ti'ir naad nɛ sʋnpɛɛn.
24Sɔ' bɛ ka o nu'us siakid tisib
la'an nɛ wala, ka o maligim nyɛt bɛdegʋ,
ka sɔ' mɛ nu'ug pʋ lakida,
amaa ka o la'an lieb nɔŋdaan.
25Onɛ piinid la na maligim nyɛ,
onɛ diisid o taaba la mɛ na nyɛɛ di.
26Nidib tʋ'ʋdnɛ onɛ vaad diibi su'ad
ye o ti kuosi nyɛ nyɔɔd,
amaa onɛ siaki kuosid la,
albareka bɛɛ o zugin bɛdegʋ.
27Onɛ ieed linɛ an sʋm na nyɛ yɛlsʋm,
amaa banɛ ieed bɛ'ɛd la, bɛ'ɛd na kɛɛn ba zugin na.
28Onɛ nɔk o ti'iri niŋ o kpan'amin la na li,
amaa pʋpiel na nwɛnɛ vanma'asir nɛ.
29Onɛ ieed yɛla tisid o mɛŋ yidim la,
pɛbisʋg ma'aa na aan o faar;
ka zɔlʋg mɛ na an ya'am sɔb sankpan'as.
30Pʋpiel tʋʋma anɛ vʋm tiig,
ka onɛ mɔr o taaba ken na ka ba dɔl Wina'am anɛ ya'am sɔb.
31 Pʋpiel ya'a di'e linɛ nar o dunia nwa' ni,
ka banɛ zi' Wina'am nɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim on kʋ di'e linɛ nari baa?

english_text:
You Can't Hide behind Evil
1 To accept correction is wise,
to reject it is stupid.
2The Lord likes everyone
who lives right,
but he punishes everyone
who makes evil plans.
3Sin cannot offer security!
But if you live right,
you will be as secure
as a tree with deep roots.
4A helpful wife is a jewel
for her husband,
but a shameless wife
will make his bones rot.
5Good people have kind thoughts,
but you should never trust
the advice of someone evil.
6Bad advice is a deadly trap,
but good advice
is like a shield.
7Once the wicked are defeated,
they are gone forever,
but no one who obeys God
will ever be thrown down.
8Good sense is worthy of praise,
but stupidity is a curse.
9It's better to be ordinary
and have only one servant
than to think you are somebody
and starve to death.
10Good people are kind
to their animals,
but a mean person is cruel.
11Hard working farmers have more
than enough food;
daydreamers are nothing more
than stupid fools.
12An evil person tries to hide
behind evil;
good people are like trees
with deep roots.
13We trap ourselves
by telling lies,
but we stay out of trouble
by living right.
14We are rewarded or punished
for what we say and do.
15Fools think they know
what is best,
but a sensible person
listens to advice.
16Losing your temper is foolish;
ignoring an insult is smart.
17An honest person
tells the truth in court,
but a dishonest person
tells nothing but lies.
18Sharp words cut like a sword,
but words of wisdom heal.
19Truth will last forever;
lies are soon found out.
20An evil mind is deceitful,
but gentle thoughts
bring happiness.
21Good people never have trouble,
but troublemakers
have more than enough.
22The Lord hates every liar,
but he is the friend of all
who can be trusted.
23Be sensible and don't tell
everything you know—
only fools spread
foolishness everywhere.
24Work hard, and you
will be a leader;
be lazy, and you
will end up a slave.
25Worry is a heavy burden,
but a kind word
always brings cheer.
26You are better off to do right,
than to lose your way
by doing wrong.
27Anyone too lazy to cook
will starve,
but a hard worker
is a valuable treasure.
28Living right is a pathway
that leads to life
and away from death.
translation_text:
1Onɛ siakid o gbɛlʋŋ nɛ sa'alʋg anɛ onɛ mɔr baŋir,
amaa onɛ pʋ siakid ye ba yɛl o gbɛlʋŋ anɛ yalim.
2Zugsɔb la sʋʋnr malis nɛ ninsʋma,
amaa o kʋʋs ya'ambɛ'ɛd sɔb la bɛ'ɛd.
3Nid kʋ dɔl bugusim suori nyɛ zi'esim,
amaa pʋpiel kʋ lii.
4Pu'a kanɛ mɔr zusʋŋ anɛ na'am zupibigi tis o sid,
amaa pu'a kanɛ diisid o sid nyan nwɛnɛ ban'as o sid kɔnba ni.
5Pʋpielim sɔb gban'ar anɛ sida,
bugusim sɔb sa'alʋg mɛ anɛ dama'am.
6Bugus pian'ad anɛ ninkʋʋr,
amaa pʋpielnam pian'adi faandi ba.
7Ba ya'a kad bugusim sɔbi yis, o kʋ lɛb na ya'asɛ;
amaa pʋpielim sɔb yir zi'enɛ kiŋ-kiŋ.
8Ba zun'od ninsaal nɛ o ya'am zug,
amaa ka nɛ'ɛsid banɛ pʋ tɛn'ɛsidi paad la.
9Li an sʋm nɛ nidi na an tadim
ka tʋmmi diisid o mɛŋ,
sɔn'oe onɛ dʋ'ʋs o mɛŋ ka diib kae.
10Pʋpielim sɔb tɛnr o bʋnkɔnbid yɛla,
amaa hali bugus nimbaanlzɔɔr anɛ zam.
11Onɛ kuod na paam diib bɛdegʋ,
amaa onɛ yaannɛ gin zaalim-zaalim pʋ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛrɛ.
12Bugus bɔɔdi la'abanɛ ka bugusim dim faand la,
amaa pʋpiel ba'a nya'a ka wan walsʋma.
13Nimbɛ'og mɛŋ pian'abɛ'ɛdi gban'ad o,
amaa pʋpiel yiti yɛla ni.
14Ninsaal nɔɔr pian'adi tisid o bʋnsʋŋ
wʋʋ o nu'ug tʋʋma tisid o nyɔɔd si'em la.
15Zɔlʋgʋ tɛn'ɛsid ye o suoya la an sʋm tis o,
amaa ya'am sɔb kɛlisidi sa'alʋg.
16Zɔlʋg sʋnf pʋ ya'asid pɛligirɛ,
amaa pʋtɛn'ɛsʋma sɔb pʋ nɔkid tʋ'ʋd ka li an si'ela.
17Sida sɔb ditnɛ kasɛta linɛ mɔr sida,
amaa ziri kasɛt sɔb pian'ad anɛ faad.
18Onɛ pʋ gu'usid la pian'ad kunsidi nwɛnɛ sʋ'ʋg nɛ
amaa ya'am sɔb pian'ad mɔri laafi kenna.
19Sida sɔb pian'ad zi'enɛ saŋa wʋsa,
amaa ziri sɔb pian'ad pʋ yuugida.
20Banɛ gban'e bɛ'ɛd la, ziri ma'aa bɛɛ ba sʋnya ni,
amaa banɛ pa'an yɔlisim yɛla la mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm.
21Yɛlbɛ'ɛd pʋ paad pʋpiela,
amaa bugus bɛ nɛ yɛla ni ma'aa.
22Zugsɔb la kis faad dim,
amaa o ya'am bɔɔdnɛ sida dim.
23Ya'am sɔb mɔr o baŋir o san'an baanlimm,
amaa zɔlʋg pian'ad o ya'amka'alʋg pian'ad paalʋ ni.
24Fʋ nu'us ya'a bɔɔd tʋʋma, li na kɛ ka fʋ lieb na'ab,
amaa gbanya'am na kɛ ka fʋ lieb yammʋg.
25Sʋnsa'aŋ tadigidnɛ nid,
amaa pian'asʋŋ bʋgʋn o sʋʋnr.
26Pʋpiel pa'an o zua suosʋma,
amaa bugus suor kpɛn'ɛsid o nɛ mɔɔg.
27Gbanya'a kʋ nyɛ wɛog ni'imi sɛn'ɛɛ,
amaa onɛ tʋm hali nɛ nimmua na paam mɔrim pamm.
28Pʋpielim suor mɔr vʋm;
ka fʋ ya'a dɔlli li, fʋ kʋ kpii.

english_text:
Wise Friends Make You Wise
1Children with good sense
accept correction
from their parents,
but stubborn children
ignore it completely.
2You will be well rewarded
for saying something kind,
but all some people think about
is how to be cruel and mean.
3 Keep what you know to yourself,
and you will be safe;
talk too much,
and you are done for.
4No matter how much you want,
laziness won't help a bit,
but hard work will reward you
with more than enough.
5A good person hates deceit,
but those who are evil
cause shame and disgrace.
6Live right, and you are safe!
But sin will destroy you.
7Some who have nothing
may pretend to be rich,
and some who have everything
may pretend to be poor.
8The rich may have
to pay a ransom,
but the poor don't have
that problem.
9The lamp of a good person
keeps on shining;
the lamp of an evil person
soon goes out.
10Too much pride causes trouble.
Be sensible and take advice.
11Money wrongly gained
will disappear bit by bit;
money earned little by little
will grow and grow.
12Not getting what you want
can break your heart,
but a wish that comes true
is a life-giving tree.
13If you reject God's teaching,
you will pay the price;
if you obey his commands,
you will be rewarded.
14Sensible instruction
is a life-giving fountain
that helps you escape
all deadly traps.
15Sound judgment is praised,
but people without good sense
are on the way to disaster.
16If you have good sense,
you will act sensibly,
but fools act like fools.
17Whoever delivers your message
can make things better
or worse for you.
18All who refuse correction
will be poor and disgraced;
all who accept correction
will be praised.
19It's a good feeling
to get what you want,
but only a stupid fool
hates to turn from evil.
20 Wise friends make you wise,
but you hurt yourself
by going around with fools.
21You are in for trouble
if you sin,
but you will be rewarded
if you live right.
22If you obey God,
you will have something
to leave your grandchildren.
If you don't obey God,
those who live right
will get what you leave.
23Even when the land of the poor
produces good crops,
they get cheated
out of what they grow.
24If you love your children,
you will correct them;
if you don't love them,
you won't correct them.
25If you live right,
you will have plenty to eat;
if you don't live right,
you will go away empty.
translation_text:
1Bikanɛ mɔr ya'am di'esid o ba' sa'alʋg,
amaa onɛ la'ad nidib pʋ wʋm tansʋgɔ.
2Ninsaal nɔɔr pian'adi tisid o bʋnsʋŋ,
amaa banɛ ka' sida dim la ieedi zaba ma'aa.
3Onɛ gban'ad o nɔɔr gu'ud o nyɔvʋr,
amaa onɛ pian'ad yɔri-yɔri la na ba'as yɔri.
4Gbanya'a ya'am bɔɔd si'el nɛ ya'amlɛog la, o kʋ nyɛɛ,
amaa onɛ bɔɔd tʋʋma hali la na nyɛ ka li sia'al o.
5Pʋpielim sɔb kisi linɛ an ziri,
amaa bugus diisid o mɛŋ nyan.
6Pʋpielim gur yɛlsida sɔb,
amaa bugusim lugidi tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb.
7Dau yinne niŋ o mɛŋ wʋʋ bʋmmɔr, amaa ka lɛɛ ka' si'ela;
ka yinne mɛ niŋ o mɛŋ wʋʋ nɔŋdaan, ka lɛɛ mɔr bɛdegʋ.
8Kpan'am sɔb na nɔk o kpan'am la faaɛn o nyɔvʋr,
amaa sɔ' kʋ vɔlis nɔŋdaana.
9Pʋpielim sɔb nɛɛsim nied nɛ nyain,
amaa bugusim sɔb fitir kpiisidnɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ.
10Nyɛɛsim sɔb ziidi zaba kenna,
amaa banɛ siakid sa'alʋg la mɔr ya'am.
11Zam ligidi pʋ ya'asid naarɛ;
amaa onɛ la'asid o ligidi bi'el-bi'el, li na nɔbig.
12Fʋ ya'a mɔr ti'ir ka ti kɔ'ɔŋ,
li tisidi susʋnya ban'as;
amaa fʋ ya'a ti nyɛ fʋ ya'amlɛog bʋn,
li sumalisim nwɛnɛ tikanɛ busid nɛ vʋm.
13Onɛ ka ba san'an o ka o gbiakid la na nyɛɛ li bɛ'ɛd,
amaa onɛ siakid sa'alʋg la na dii li nyɔɔd.
14Ya'am sɔb pa'alʋg anɛ nyɔvʋr bulig
ka yisid ninsaal kum bɛndis pʋʋgin.
15Onɛ gban'ad si'el gbin tɔ'ɔtɔ la nyɛt na'asi,
amaa ziri sɔb suor kennɛ san'auŋ zin'igin.
16Onɛ an ya'am sɔb wʋsa tɛn'ɛsidnɛ ka nyaan maan si'el,
amaa zɔlʋg tʋʋma pa'annɛ o zɔlim paalʋ ni.
17Fʋ ya'a tʋm nimbɛ'ɛd, o na kpɛn'ɛs o mɛŋ yɛla ni,
amaa tʋmtʋm onɛ an sida sɔb la mɔri laafi kenna.
18Onɛ pʋ siakid zamisʋg la na lieb nɔŋdaan ka di nyan,
amaa onɛ siakid pa'alʋg la nyɛti na'asi.
19Fʋ ya'am ya'a bɔɔd si'el ka fʋ ti nyɛɛ li, li ma'adnɛ sʋʋnr,
amaa zɔn la zan'as ye ba kʋ fɛndig ka bas linɛ an bɛ'ɛdɛ.
20Onɛ gɔɔnd nɛ ya'am dim la mɛ na mɔr ya'am,
amaa onɛ zuanamɛ an zɔn na paam yɛltɔɔg.
21Yɛlbɛ'ɛd dɔlli tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb gbin,
amaa yɛlsʋm anɛ pʋpielim sɔb din.
22Ninsʋŋ yaas na dii o faar,
amaa tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim kpan'am la su'anɛ gur pʋpielim dim.
23Nɔŋ daan pɔɔg na nyaŋi maal zʋʋd sʋ'ʋŋa,
amaa teŋ kanɛ ka nidib pʋ dɔl sida la, ba na zii li gaad.
24Onɛ zɔt sisanbig nyɔɔg kis o biig nɛ,
amaa onɛ nɔŋ o biig na sa'al o sʋ'ʋŋa.
25Pʋpielim dim la diti ba ya'am bɔɔd si'el,
amaa bugusnam la kennɛ ka kɔ'ɔm kʋʋdi ba.

english_text:
Wisdom Makes Good Sense
1A woman's family
is held together
by her wisdom,
but it can be destroyed
by her foolishness.
2By living right, you show
that you respect the Lord;
by being deceitful, you show
that you despise him.
3Proud fools are punished
for their stupid talk,
but sensible talk
can save your life.
4Without the help of an ox
there can be no crop,
but with a strong ox
a big crop is possible.
5An honest witness
tells the truth;
a dishonest witness
tells nothing but lies.
6Make fun of wisdom,
and you will never find it.
But if you have understanding,
knowledge comes easily.
7Stay away from fools,
or you won't learn a thing.
8Wise people have enough sense
to find their way,
but stupid fools get lost.
9Fools don't care
if they are wrong,
but God is pleased
when people do right.
10No one else can really know
how sad or happy you are.
11The tent of a good person
stands longer than the house
of someone evil.
12 You may think you are
on the right road
and still end up dead.
13Sorrow may hide
behind laughter,
and happiness may end
in sorrow.
14You harvest what you plant,
whether good or bad.
15Don't be stupid
and believe all you hear;
be smart and know
where you are headed.
16Only a stupid fool
is never cautious—
so be extra careful
and stay out of trouble.
17Fools have quick tempers,
and no one likes you
if you can't be trusted.
18Stupidity leads to foolishness;
be smart and learn.
19The wicked will come crawling
to those who obey God.
20You have no friends
if you are poor,
but you have lots of friends
if you are rich.
21It's wrong to hate others,
but God blesses everyone
who is kind to the poor.
22It's a mistake
to make evil plans,
but you will have loyal friends
if you want to do right.
23Hard work is worthwhile,
but empty talk
will make you poor.
24Wisdom can make you rich,
but foolishness leads
to more foolishness.
25An honest witness
can save your life,
but liars can't be trusted.
26If you respect the Lord,
you and your children
have a strong fortress
27and a life-giving fountain
that keeps you safe
from deadly traps.
28Rulers of powerful nations
are held in honor;
rulers of weak nations
are nothing at all.
29It's smart to be patient,
but it's stupid
to lose your temper.
30It's healthy to be content,
but envy can eat you up.
31If you mistreat the poor,
you insult your Creator;
if you are kind to them,
you show him respect.
32In times of trouble
the wicked are destroyed,
but even at death
the innocent have faith.
33Wisdom is found in the minds
of people with good sense,
but fools don't know it.
34Doing right brings honor
to a nation,
but sin brings disgrace.
35Kings reward servants
who act wisely,
but they punish those
who act foolishly.
translation_text:
1Pu'a kanɛ an ya'am sɔb la mɛɛd o yir,
amaa pu'a kanɛ ka' ya'am la nwa'ad o din.
2Ninkanɛ dɔl suor linɛ an sʋm ka nar zɔt Wina'am dabiem
amaa onɛ dɔl zam suoya la nɛ'ɛsid o nɛ.
3Zɔlʋg pian'adi kɛt ka o di'ed balaar o nya'aŋ;
amaa ya'am sɔb pian'ad gu'ud o nɛ yisid yɛla ni.
4Niigi kae zin'isi'a la, gariki la dignɛ zaalim
amaa niigi paŋi kɛt ka ti nyɛt zʋʋd bɛdegʋ bun.
5Kasɛta sɔb onɛ pian'ad sida la pʋ ma'ada
amaa ziri kasɛta la faad.
6Ninla'as la ieedi ya'am ka pʋ nyɛta,
amaa onɛ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr la nyɛti baŋir na'ana.
7Zɔm ka bas zɔlʋg,
ka fʋ kʋ nyɛ ya'am o san'anɛ.
8Ya'am sɔb ya'am kɛt ka o mi' linɛ nar
amaa zɔltita'ar la ma'ad o mɛŋ.
9Zɔn la'adnɛ onɛ sɔsid tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd suguru,
amaa ninsʋma mɔri Wina'am yɛlsʋm.
10Onɛ sʋnfʋ pɛligi mi' lin zabid o si'em,
ka sɔ' mɛ kae na nyaŋi pʋdig o sumalisim.
11Nimbɛ'og yir na san'am,
amaa ninsʋŋ din na nɔbigid.
12 Suosi'a bɛnɛ nwɛnɛ li anɛ sʋ'ʋŋa tis ninsaal,
amaa li naar la mɔr o nɛ ken kum zin'igin.
13Nid tun'e la'ad ka o sʋʋnr lɛɛ zabid,
sumalisim na tun'e naae nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ.
14Onɛ ka' yadda la na di'e yɔɔd linɛ nar o,
ka ninsʋŋ mɛ di'e o yɔɔd wʋʋ lin nar si'em.
15Onɛ ya'am pɔɔd la niŋidi si'el wʋsa yadda,
amaa onɛ mɔr ya'am la gu'usidi nɛ o nɔbir yakir.
16Ya'am sɔb zɔti Zugsɔb la dabiem ka luakid bɛ'ɛd,
amaa zɔlʋg on nɔkidnɛ o zugʋ kpa' ken.
17Sʋnpɛɛn sɔb tʋmnɛ tʋʋmyɔɔd,
ka sɔ' wʋsa kis pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd sɔb.
18Onɛ ya'am pɔɔd la ditnɛ zɔlim faar,
amaa ya'am sɔb di'ednɛ baŋir wʋʋ na'am zupibig nɛ.
19Nimbɛ'ɛdnam la na igin ninsʋma tuon,
ka bugusim dim la bɛ pʋpielim dim za'anɔya nii sɔsid.
20Onɛ an nɔŋdaan la, hali o kpi'es la'am luakid o nɛ,
amaa onɛ an kpan'a la zuanam anɛ bɛdegʋ.
21Onɛ nɛ'ɛs o kpi'a tʋm taal
amaa onɛ maan fara dim sʋ'ʋŋa la mɔr zusʋŋ.
22Banɛ gban'ad gban'abɛ'ɛd la bɔdigid nɛ.
Amaa banɛ gban'ad linɛ an sʋm la mɔr nɔŋilim nɛ sida.
23Tʋʋm kpi'euŋ wʋsa mɔri nyɔɔdi kenna,
amaa azin'i-sɔnsid ziidi nɔŋ na.
24Ya'am dim kpan'am anɛ na'am zupibig,
amaa zɔltitada la din anɛ zɔlim ma'aa.
25Kasɛta sɔb onɛ pian'ad sida la ziid vʋm kenna,
amaa ziri kasɛta anɛ faad ma'aa.
26Onɛ zɔt Zugsɔb la mɔr suak zin'ig linɛ mɔr kpi'euŋ,
ka li mɛ na an suak zin'igi tis o biis.
27Zugsɔb la zɔtim anɛ nyɔvʋr bulig
ka yisid ninsaal kum bɛndis pʋʋgin.
28Nidib bɛdegʋ dʋ'ʋsid na'am,
amaa nidib ya'a kae, san'auŋ na kpɛn' na'abiig.
29Suguru sɔb gban'ad si'el gbin,
amaa sʋnpɛɛn sɔb pa'annɛ zɔlimis.
30Fʋ sʋnf ya'a mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm linɛ tisid niŋgbiŋ laafi,
amaa fufum sɔb kɔnba na ba'asi pun'oe.
31Onɛ mugusid nɔŋ dim tʋ'ʋdi Onɛ Maali ba la,
amaa onɛ maan fara dim sʋ'ʋŋa la na'asid Wina'am.
32Bɛ'ɛd ya'a ti lɛb bugusim dim la zugin ba liig paae ya,
amaa hali baa kum zin'igin pʋpielim dim na nyɛ suak.
33Ya'am bɛ nɛ banɛ mɔr baŋiri ba sʋnfʋn,
amaa zɔn pʋn zi' linɛ buon ya'am.
34Pʋpielim dʋ'ʋsid teŋ yʋ'ʋr,
ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd diisid nidib wʋsa nyan.
35Na'ab bɔɔdi kpɛɛm kanɛ mɔr ya'am,
amaa o ya'a tʋm nyan tʋʋma li duodi na'ab sʋnf.

english_text:
The Lord Sees Everything
1A kind answer
soothes angry feelings,
but harsh words
stir them up.
2Words of wisdom
come from the wise,
but fools speak foolishness.
3The Lord sees everything,
whether good or bad.
4Kind words are good medicine,
but deceitful words
can really hurt.
5Don't be a fool
and disobey your parents.
Be smart! Accept correction.
6Good people become wealthy,
but those who are evil
will lose what they have.
7Words of wisdom
make good sense;
the thoughts of a fool
make no sense at all.
8The Lord is disgusted
by gifts from the wicked,
but it makes him happy
when his people pray.
9The Lord is disgusted
with all who do wrong,
but he loves everyone
who does right.
10If you turn from the right way,
you will be punished;
if you refuse correction,
you will die.
11If the Lord can see everything
in the world of the dead,
he can see in our hearts.
12Those who sneer at others
don't like to be corrected,
and they won't ask help
from someone with sense.
13Happiness makes you smile;
sorrow can crush you.
14Anyone with good sense
is eager to learn more,
but fools are hungry
for foolishness.
15The poor have a hard life,
but being content is as good
as an endless feast.
16It's better to obey the Lord
and have only a little,
than to be very rich
and terribly anxious.
17A simple meal with love
is better than a feast
where there is hatred.
18Losing your temper
causes a lot of trouble,
but staying calm
settles arguments.
19A lazy person refuses
to clear a thorny path,
but everyone who does right
walks on a smooth road.
20Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
despise them.
21Stupidity brings happiness
to senseless fools,
but everyone with good sense
follows the straight path.
22Without good advice
everything goes wrong—
it takes careful planning
for things to go right.
23Giving the right answer
at the right time
makes everyone happy.
24All who are wise follow a road
that leads upward to life
and away from death.
25The Lord destroys the homes
of those who are proud,
but he protects the property
of widows.
26The Lord hates evil thoughts,
but kind words please him.
27Being greedy causes trouble
for your family,
but you protect yourself
by refusing bribes.
28Good people think
before they answer,
but the wicked speak evil
without ever thinking.
29The Lord never even hears
the prayers of the wicked,
but he answers the prayers
of all who obey him.
30A friendly smile
makes you happy,
and good news
makes you feel strong.
31Healthy correction is good,
and if you accept it,
you will be wise.
32You hurt only yourself
by rejecting instruction,
but it makes good sense
to accept it.
33Showing respect to the Lord
will make you wise,
and being humble
will bring honor to you.
translation_text:
1Lɛbisʋg linɛ an baanlimm yisidnɛ sʋnpɛɛn,
amaa ɛndʋg pian'ad duodi sʋnf.
2Ya'am sɔb zilim pian'adnɛ baŋir yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa,
amaa gɛdʋg nɔɔr pɛ'ɛl nɛ zɔlim ma'aa.
3Zugsɔb la nini bɛ nɛ zin'ig wʋsa,
gɔsid bugusim dim nɛ banɛ tʋm sʋm wʋsa.
4Nɔɔr kanɛ pian'adi mɔr laafi na nwɛnɛ tiig linɛ wala an vʋm,
amaa nɔɔr kanɛ pian'ad ziri la tisidi sʋnsa'aŋ.
5Zɔlʋgʋ nɛ'ɛsid o ba' sa'alʋg,
amaa onɛ siakid sa'alʋg anɛ ya'am sɔb.
6Pʋpielim sɔb yin mɔri kpan'am bɛdegʋ;
amaa bugusim sɔbi nyɛt si'el la ziidi yɛla na.
7Ya'am sɔb pian'adnɛ baŋir pian'ad,
amaa li ka' ala nɛ zɔnnɛ.
8Zugsɔb la kis bugusim sɔb maan,
amaa onɛ bɛllim an sʋm la pʋ'ʋsim ma'ad o sʋʋnr.
9Zugsɔb la kis bugusim dim suoya
amaa o nɔŋ banɛ dɔl pʋpielim dim suor.
10Namisʋg digi gur onɛ bas suor dɔllim;
onɛ kis sa'alʋg na kpi.
11Kpi'im teŋ nɛ aba'as-yɔri dignɛ Zugsɔb la tuon
ka ninsaalib sʋnf na nyaŋi su'a o san'anɛɛ?
12Onɛ la'ad nidib kis ban na yɛl o gbɛlʋŋ;
o pʋ nwɛ'ɛd ya'am sɔb sɔɔraa.
13Onɛ sʋnfʋ malis la lɔdigid o nindaa,
amaa sʋnzabir mɔri sʋnsa'aŋʋ kenna.
14Onɛ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr la ieed baŋir
amaa banɛ an zɔn la zɔlim tʋʋma aan ba diib.
15Onɛ bɛ mugusʋg pʋʋgin la dabisa wʋsa anɛ tɔɔg,
amaa onɛ mɔr sumalisim la ditnɛ saŋa wʋsa.
16Fʋ ya'a mɔr bi'ela ka zɔt Zugsɔb dabiem
li sɔn'oe onɛ mɔr bɛdegʋ ka bɛ yɛla ni.
17Li an sʋm nɛ fʋn na ɔnb vaand ma'aa
gat fʋn na ɔnbid na'akanɛ mɔr kpaam ni'im ka kisidim bɛ.
18Sʋnpɛɛn sɔb ziidi nɔŋgbannwa'ari kenna,
amaa suguru sɔb kpiisidi nɔŋgbannwa'ar.
19Gbanya'a suor pɛ'ɛl nɛ gɔn'ɔs,
amaa onɛ bɛllim an sʋm la suor anɛ suoraug.
20Bikanɛ mɔr ya'am ma'ad o ba' sʋʋnr,
amaa zɔlʋg nɛ'ɛsid o ma.
21Zɔlʋg ya'am ka'alʋg ma'ad o mɛŋ sʋnf,
amaa ninkanɛ gban'ad si'el gbin la tʋmnɛ linɛ an sʋ'ʋŋa.
22Onɛ sa'an ya'a kae lin ka yɛla san'amid,
amaa sa'ansa'annib ya'a zu'oe ba na nyaŋi maal yɛla.
23Nid ya'a lɛbis bu'osʋg sʋ'ʋŋa li ma'ad o sʋʋnr,
ka pian'ʋk mɛ ya'a pian' saŋa kanɛ nar, li anɛ sʋ'ʋŋa!
24Mi'ilim sɔb suori tisid o nyɔvʋr
ka gur o ka o da sig kpi'im teŋa.
25Zugsɔb la san'amid nyɛɛsim sɔb yir,
amaa ka gur pʋkɔɔnr titɔndis sʋ'ʋŋa.
26Zugsɔb la kis bugusim sɔb tɛn'ɛsa,
amaa o sʋnf lɛɛ malisi nɛ pʋpielim sɔb.
27Kpian'asʋg sɔb ziidi yɛla kpɛn'ɛsid o yin,
amaa onɛ kʋ siak ye ba da' o la na vʋe yuug.
28Pʋpielim sɔb ɛɛnti tɛn'ɛs nɛ sʋ'ʋŋa ka nyaan gandig bu'osʋg,
amaa bugus nɔɔr yisidi bɛ'ɛd yɔri-yɔri.
29Zugsɔb la lal nɛ bugusim sɔb
amaa o wʋm pʋpiel winsɔsʋg.
30Onɛ pʋ lɔɔd nindaa li tisid o sʋnf malisim,
ka labasʋŋ mɛ tisid niŋgbiŋ wʋsa laafi.
31Onɛ kɛlisid sa'alʋg linɛ tisid vʋm la,
ba na kaal o paas ya'am dim san'an.
32Onɛ wʋsa nɛ'ɛs zamisʋg nɛ'ɛs nɛ o mɛŋ
amaa onɛ wʋsa siakid o gbɛlʋŋ maligim gban'ad si'el gbin.
33Zugsɔb la zɔtim pa'an ninsaal ya'am,
a-sie-m-mɛŋi gat tuon ka na'asi nyaan dɔl.

english_text:
The Lord Has the Final Word
1We humans make plans,
but the Lord
has the final word.
2We may think we know
what is right,
but the Lord is the judge
of our motives.
3Share your plans with the Lord,
and you will succeed.
4The Lord has a reason
for everything he does,
and he lets evil people live
only to be punished.
5The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is conceited—
you can be sure
they will be punished.
6 If we truly love God,
our sins will be forgiven;
if we show him respect,
we will keep away from sin.
7When we please the Lord,
even our enemies
make friends with us.
8 It's better to be honest
and poor
than to be dishonest
and rich.
9We make our own plans,
but the Lord decides
where we will go.
10Rulers speak with authority
and are never wrong.
11The Lord watches to see
if we are fair
or if we cheat others.
12Justice makes rulers powerful.
They should hate evil
13and like honesty and truth.
14An angry ruler
can put you to death.
So be wise!
Don't make one angry.
15When a ruler is happy
and pleased with you,
it's like refreshing rain,
and you will live.
16It's much better to be wise
and sensible
than to be rich.
17God's people avoid evil ways,
and they protect themselves
by watching where they go.
18Too much pride
will destroy you.
19You are better off
to be humble and poor
than to get rich
from what you take by force.
20If you know what you're doing,
you will prosper.
God blesses everyone
who trusts him.
21Good judgment proves
that you are wise,
and if you speak kindly,
you can teach others.
22Good sense is a fountain
that gives life,
but fools are punished
by their foolishness.
23You can persuade others
if you are wise
and speak sensibly.
24Kind words are like honey—
they cheer you up
and make you feel strong.
25 Sometimes what seems right
is really a road to death.
26The hungrier you are,
the harder you work.
27Worthless people plan trouble.
Even their words burn
like a flaming fire.
28 Gossip is no good!
It causes hard feelings
and comes between friends.
29Don't trust violent people.
They will mislead you
to do the wrong thing.
30When someone winks
or grins behind your back,
trouble is on the way.
31Gray hair is a glorious crown
worn by those
who have lived right.
32Controlling your temper
is better than being a hero
who captures a city.
33We make our own decisions,
but the Lord alone
determines what happens.
translation_text:
1Ninsaal sʋnfʋ gban'ad gban'ar,
amaa Zugsɔb la sʋ'oe maalʋg yɛla.
2Ninsaal suoya wʋsa anɛ sʋ'ʋŋa o mɛŋ nini ni,
amaa Zugsɔb la kpansid o sʋnfʋ an si'em.
3Zaŋim fʋn maan si'el wʋsa tis Zugsɔb la,
ka fʋ gban'ar wʋsa na maal sʋ'ʋŋa.
4Zugsɔb la maal si'el wʋsa mɔri li naar;
hali bugusim sɔb naar anɛ san'auŋ.
5Zugsɔb la kis banɛ wʋsa mɔr nyɛɛsim.
Baŋimi ye ba kʋ yi namisʋgʋnɛɛ.
6Nɔŋir nɛ sida kɛt ka Wina'am na kɛ taali bas;
Zugsɔb la zɔtim kɛt ka ninsaal na nyaŋi bas tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.
7Ninsaal suoya ya'a malis Zugsɔb la,
hali o na kɛ ka on nɛ o bi'emnam na la'am bɛ nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.
8Li an sʋm nɛ fʋn na mɔr bi'ela ka li an pʋpielim bunnɛ
gaad fʋn na nyɛ bɛdegʋ ka li an zam bʋn.
9Ninsaal gban'ad o sʋnfʋn on na keŋ si'em,
amaa Zugsɔb la pa'annɛ o nɔba yakid si'em.
10Na'ab pian'adi nɛ Wina'am ya'am;
li pʋ sʋm ye o kad saria ka li pʋ dɔl suorɛ.
11Makir linɛ an sʋm ka tu'al yitnɛ Zugsɔb ni na;
linɛ ka ba mɔri makid tɛbisim la
o ba'a bɛ nɛ li wʋsa.
12Na'anam kis linɛ pʋ dɔl suorɛ,
bɔzugɔ pʋpielim kɛt ka na'am la zi'e kiŋ-kiŋ.
13Na'anam bɔɔd ye ba wʋm pian'ad linɛ ka' zirii;
ninkanɛ pian'ad sida la ba nɔŋ o nɛ.
14Na'ab sʋnpɛɛn anɛ linɛ ziid kum na,
amaa onɛ mɔr ya'am la na ma'ae li.
15Na'ab ya'a ti yidig o nindaa, li mɔri vʋm kenna;
o sʋŋir nwɛnɛ saa na kʋ sigir saŋa kenna la.
16Fʋ ya'a paam ya'am li gat fʋn na paam sanlim!
Fʋ ya'a bɔ baŋir, li sɔn'oe fʋn na gaŋ anzurifa!
17Banɛ bɛllim an sʋ'ʋŋa la dɔlnɛ suoraug ka bɛ'ɛd kae;
onɛ gu'usid nɛ o ken pʋʋgin gu'ud o nyɔvʋr.
18Adʋ'ʋsi-m-mɛŋ ya'a dɛŋ tuonnɛ, san'auŋʋ dɔl,
ka nyɛɛsim mɛ ken ka liig kad o bugir.
19Fʋ ya'a sie fʋ mɛŋ ka ba kaali fʋ pɛ'ɛs nɔŋdimin,
li sɔn'oe fʋn na la'as nɛ banɛ dʋ'ʋsidi ba mɛŋ ka ya fan' la'adi pʋdig.
20Banɛ kɛlisid ka siakid pa'ala kennɛ tuon,
ka albareka mɛ bɛ nɛ onɛ niŋ Zugsɔb la yadda.
21Ba buon onɛ mɔr ya'am ye baŋir sɔb;
pian'ad linɛ malis la sʋŋid ka pa'alʋg ken tuon.
22Banɛ mɔr ya'am gban'ad si'el gbin tɔ'ɔtɔ la, li nwɛnɛ buligi bunnɛ tisidi ba nyɔvʋr,
amaa zɔlimis mɔri namisʋgʋ ken zɔn ni na.
23Ya'am sɔb gu'usid nɛ o nɔɔr pian'ad,
ka li kɛt ka nidib di'ed o pa'alʋg.
24Pian'asʋma malisnɛ nwɛnɛ siind,
li malisi tisi fʋ nɔɔr ka tisidi fʋ niŋgbiŋ wʋsa laafi.
25 Suosi'a bɛɛ nwɛnɛ li anɛ sʋ'ʋŋaa tis ninsaal,
amaa li naar mɔr o kennɛ kum zin'igin.
26Ya'amlɛogʋ kɛt ka tʋmtʋm nyidigid
ka kɔ'ɔm zabir kpɛmisid o ka o tʋm.
27Nimbɛ'og gban'adnɛ gban'abɛ'ɛd
ka o pian'ad dit nwɛnɛ bugum pielim nɛ.
28Ninkanɛ ieed yɛla tuginnɛ nidib,
bayɛʋg mɛ san'amidi zuod.
29Zaba sɔb bɛlisid o kpi'a
kpɛn'ɛsid o suobɛ'ɛdin.
30Onɛ amisid la gban'adi gban'abɛ'ɛd;
onɛ mi'ed nidib la tɛn'ɛsidi bɛ'ɛd.
31Zupielim anɛ na'am zupibig kanɛ vɛnl,
pʋpielim dim ma'aa nyɛti li.
32Sumbʋgʋsʋm sɔb sɔn'oe zabzabid onɛ kpi'em,
ka onɛ nyaŋi gban'ad o mɛŋ gat onɛ nyaŋ teŋ mum.
33Bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm dim bʋgʋlʋm ye ba gban'e gban'ar,
amaa gban'ar wʋsa yitnɛ Zugsɔb la san'an na.

english_text:
Our Thoughts Are Tested by the Lord
1A dry crust of bread eaten
in peace and quiet
is better than a feast eaten
where everyone argues.
2A wise slave
will be placed in charge
of a no-good child,
and that slave will be given
the same inheritance
that each child receives.
3Silver and gold are tested
by flames of fire;
our thoughts are tested
by the Lord.
4Troublemakers listen
to troublemakers,
and liars listen to liars.
5By insulting the poor,
you insult your Creator.
You will be punished
if you make fun
of someone in trouble.
6Grandparents are proud
of their grandchildren,
and children should be proud
of their parents.
7It sounds strange for a fool
to talk sensibly,
but it's even worse
for a ruler to tell lies.
8A bribe works miracles
like a magic charm
that brings good luck.
9You will keep your friends
if you forgive them,
but you will lose your friends
if you keep talking about
what they did wrong.
10A sensible person
accepts correction,
but you can't beat sense
into a fool.
11Cruel people want to rebel,
and so vicious attackers
will be sent against them.
12A bear robbed of her cubs
is far less dangerous
than a stubborn fool.
13You will always have trouble
if you are mean to those
who are good to you.
14The start of an argument
is like a water leak—
so stop it before
real trouble breaks out.
15The Lord doesn't like those
who defend the guilty
or condemn the innocent.
16Why should fools have money
for an education
when they refuse to learn?
17 A friend is there to help,
in any situation,
and relatives are born
to share our troubles.
18It's stupid to guarantee
someone else's loan.
19The wicked and the proud
love trouble and keep begging
to be hurt.
20Dishonesty does you no good,
and telling lies
will get you in trouble.
21It's never pleasant
to be the parent of a fool
and have nothing but pain.
22If you are cheerful,
you feel good;
if you are sad,
you hurt all over.
23Crooks accept secret bribes
to keep justice
from being done.
24Anyone with wisdom knows
what makes good sense,
but fools can never
make up their minds.
25Foolish children bring sorrow
and pain to their parents.
26It isn't fair
to punish the innocent
and those who do right.
27It makes a lot of sense
to be a person of few words
and to stay calm.
28 Even fools seem smart
when they are quiet.
translation_text:
1Fʋ ya'a di zɔ'ɔm ka mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm li sɔn'oe yir kanɛ ka fʋ dii tig ka nɔŋgbannwa'ar bɛ.
2Sankpan'as kanɛ mɔr ya'am na sʋ'oe yibiig kanɛ diisid o yidim nyan,
o na la'asi di faar wʋʋ o anɛ yibiig nɛ.
3Bugum ka ba mɔri nyɛligid anzurifa nɛ sanlima siligid,
amaa Zugsɔb la kpansid ninsaal sʋnf.
4Bugus kɛlisidi pian'ad linɛ an bɛ'ɛd
ka faad sɔb mɛ kɛlisid ziri kikɛung.
5Onɛ la' nɔŋ dim tʋ'ʋdi Onɛ Maali ba la;
onɛ ka yɛla paae sɔ' ka o sʋnf ma'ae la na nyɛ namisʋg.
6Yaas anɛ na'am zupibigi tis bʋnkʋdʋg,
ka biis mɛ dʋ'ʋsidi ba mɛŋi ba du'adib zug.
7Ya'am pian'ad pʋ nar nɛ zɔlʋgɔ;
ka li bɛ'ɛd wʋsa anɛ na'akanɛ faad!
8Onɛ da'ad kpi'emnam nɛ ligidi la tɛn'ɛs ye linɛ fɛndigid nidib ya'am;
ka on fɛndig zin'isi'a wʋsa o na di ya'an.
9Onɛ wʋsa lusid taal kɛt ka nɔŋilim bɛ,
amaa onɛ wʋsa tɛɛnsid yɛla san'amidi zuod.
10Fʋ ya'a zɛrig ya'am sɔb vugiri li na tiak o
gat zɔlʋgʋ na di'e kpa'asa kɔbiga.
11Ninvʋbɛ'ɛd anɛ onɛ zan'asid yɛlsida;
ka ba mɛ na tʋm onɛ pʋ zɔt nimbaanlig o san'an ka o vɛɛns o.
12Fʋ ya'a tʋ'ʋs bʋnyua kanɛ ka ba faaɛn o biis
sɔn'oe fʋn na tʋ'ʋs zɔlʋg ka o tʋmm o zɔlim tʋʋma.
13Nid ya'a maalif sʋ'ʋŋa ka fʋ lɛbis o bɛ'ɛd,
bɛ'ɛd kʋ naae fʋ yir pʋʋginɛ.
14Onɛ pin'il nɔŋgbannwa'ar li tɔɔg nwɛnɛ fʋn na bi'ed mu'ar;
alazug dɛŋim bas yɛl la ka li da lieb zabaa.
15Azɛrig bʋʋd sɔb ka tis bugus bʋʋd la
anɛ linɛ ka Zugsɔb la kisi li wʋsa.
16Zɔlʋg ya'a pʋ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr ye o ie ya'am,
o ligidi tʋʋm an bɔ?
17Zua anɛ onɛ nɔŋif saŋa wʋsa,
ka ba'abiig mɛ an onɛ sʋŋid yɛlpakir saŋa.
18Ninkanɛ ka' ya'am nɔkid o la'adi zi'en kasɛt
ye o kpi'a pɛ'ɛŋ.
19Onɛ nɔŋ nɔŋgbannwa'ar la nɔŋnɛ bɛ'ɛd
onɛ niŋid ala ieedi yɛla tisid o mɛŋ.
20Ninkanɛ an zam sɔb la pʋ ken tuonnɛ;
ka ziri sɔb mɛ kpɛn'ɛd yɛla ni.
21Fʋ ya'a du'a zɔlʋg li anɛ sʋnsa'aŋ,
zɔlʋg saam sʋʋnr ka' ma'arɛ.
22Onɛ sʋʋnri malis, li tisid o nɛ laafi
amaa sʋnsa'aŋ kpɛn'ɛsidi ban'as nid kɔnba ni.
23Ninkanɛ an bugus la su'adi di'esid ligidi
ye o san'am yɛlsida dim la suor.
24Onɛ pʋtɛn'ɛri vʋe la mɔr ya'am,
amaa zɔlʋg gi'esidnɛ yɔri-yɔri.
25Bikanɛ an zɔlʋg tisid o ba' sʋnsa'aŋ
ka kɛ ka onɛ du'a o la sʋʋnr zabid.
26Li ka' sʋm nɛ fʋn na namis sɔ' zaalim-zaalim,
bɛɛ fʋ bʋ' ninsʋŋ o yɛlsida zugɔ.
27Ninkanɛ mɔr baŋir pian'adi ka gu'usid
ka onɛ gban'ad yɛl gbin sʋnf pʋ pɛligid tɔ'ɔtɔɔ.
28Hali zɔlʋg ya'a ti an baanlimm ba na yɛl ye o mɔr ya'am,
ka o ya'a gban'e o nɔɔr ba na tɛn'ɛs ye o mɔri baŋir.

english_text:
It's Wrong To Favor the Guilty
1It's selfish and stupid
to think only of yourself
and to sneer at people
who have sense.
2Fools have no desire to learn,
instead they would rather
give their own opinion.
3Wrongdoing leads to shame
and disgrace.
4Words of wisdom
are a stream that flows
from a deep fountain.
5It's wrong to favor the guilty
and keep the innocent
from getting justice.
6Foolish talk will get you
into a lot of trouble.
7Saying foolish things
is like setting a trap
to destroy yourself.
8There's nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
9Being lazy is no different
from being a troublemaker.
10The Lord is a mighty tower
where his people can run
for safety—
11the rich think their money
is a wall of protection.
12Pride leads to destruction;
humility leads to honor.
13 It's stupid and embarrassing
to give an answer
before you listen.
14Being cheerful helps
when you are sick,
but nothing helps
when you give up.
15Everyone with good sense
wants to learn.
16A gift will get you in
to see anyone.
17You may think you have won
your case in court,
until your opponent speaks.
18Drawing straws is one way
to settle a difficult case.
19Making up with a friend
you have offended
is harder than breaking
through a city wall.
20Make your words good—
you will be glad you did.
21Words can bring death or life!
Talk too much, and you will eat
everything you say.
22 A man's greatest treasure
is his wife—
she is a gift from the Lord.
23The poor must beg for help,
but the rich can give
a harsh reply.
24Some friends don't help,
but a true friend is closer
than your own family.
translation_text:
1Ninkanɛ ka' zua la mɔɔdnɛ o mɛŋ yɛla ma'aa
ka zan'asid linɛ an sa'al sʋŋ wʋsa.
2Zɔlʋg pʋ mɔr ya'amlɛog nɛ ya'am zamisʋgɔ,
amaa o mɔɔdi ye o pa'al o mɛŋ pʋtɛn'ɛri gban'e si'el la ma'aa.
3Bugusim ya'a ti kena, ala ka nɛ'ɛsʋg dɔl,
ka nyan mɛ ken nɛ zuziid.
4Ninsaal pian'ad nwɛnɛ ku'ozuluŋ nɛ
amaa ya'am nwɛnɛ ku'okanɛ bun buligin.
5Li ka' sʋm nɛ fʋn na tis bugusim sɔb bʋʋd
ka lɛɛ mɔŋ sida sɔba.
6Zɔlʋg pian'ad mɔri zaba kennɛ o san'an na,
ka o nɔɔr ieed bʋ'ʋdi tisid o.
7Zɔlʋg nɔɔri san'amid o,
ka an baŋi gban'ad o mɛŋ.
8Bayɛʋg sɔb pian'ad malis nɛ nwɛnɛ sa'anwɛdir nɛ;
li sigid nɛ bɔlimm-bɔlimm paad pʋʋgin sa.
9Gbanya'am sɔb
nɛ la'asan'auŋ sɔb anɛ ba'abiis.
10Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr anɛ suak zin'ig;
Pʋpielnam la zɔti kpɛn'ɛdi su'adi ani ka paam faangir.
11Arezak sʋŋidi bʋndaan wʋʋ zaŋguom kpi'ema sʋŋid tempʋʋg si'em la,
o tɛn'ɛs ye li anɛ zaŋguom kanɛ ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi ianki kpɛn' naa.
12Nid ya'a ti dʋ'ʋsid o mɛŋ, o liigi dɔl,
amaa A-sie-m-mɛŋ ya'a kena, na'asi dɔl.
13Onɛ lɛbis pian'ad ka pʋ kɛlisɛ,
li anɛ gɛtim nɛ nyannɛ tis o.
14Ninsaal siigi tisid o kpi'euŋ o ban'as saŋa,
amaa anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi kpɛmis onɛ siigi tadigɛ?
15Onɛ mɔr ya'am ieednɛ baŋiri paasid;
ka o sɔb tʋba yɔ'ɔgi ieedi li zin'ig.
16Piini yɔ'ɔgidi suori tit Onɛ piinid la
ka vɛ'ɛgid o la'asid nɛ nintitada.
17Onɛ dɛŋ tuonnɛ tu'as o pian'ad la li nwɛnɛ on sɔba mɔr bʋʋd,
asɛɛ ka o tiraan la ti kena bu'os o bu'osa ka li nie.
18Pɔnsʋgʋ pansigid zaba
ka widigid paŋ dim banɛ zabid nɛ taaba la.
19Fʋ ya'a san'ami fʋ ba'abiig sʋʋnr, li tɔi pamm nɛ on na basi fʋ taali gaad fʋn na nyaŋ tempʋkanɛ mɔr kpi'euŋ,
ka zaba mɛ gu'ud nidibi lɛbisid wʋʋ teŋ kanɛ ka ba yɔ' nɛ kʋnt gam.
20Ninsaal nɔɔr pian'adi tisid o diib ka o pʋʋr pɛ'ɛn
ka o nɔŋgbannɛ tisid o si'el linɛ sia'al o.
21Zilimi mɔr kum nɛ vʋm paŋ,
ka banɛ nɔŋi li na dii li wala.
22Onɛ di pu'a sʋŋ nyɛ bʋnsʋŋ
ka na nyɛ sʋŋir Zugsɔb la san'an.
23Nɔŋ daan sɔsidi ye ba zɔɔ o nimbaanlig,
amaa bʋmmɔr on lɛbisidi nɛ nyinyiug.
24Sɔ' na tun'e mɔr zuanam bɛdegʋ ka ba pʋ nyaŋi sʋŋ o,
amaa ka zua si'a bɛɛ gati fʋ mabiig.

english_text:
It's Wise To Be Patient
1It's better to be poor
and live right
than to be a stupid liar.
2Willingness and stupidity
don't go well together.
If you are too eager,
you will miss the road.
3We are ruined
by our own stupidity,
though we blame the Lord.
4The rich have many friends;
the poor have none.
5Dishonest witnesses and liars
won't escape punishment.
6Everyone tries to be friends
of those who can help them.
7If you are poor,
your own relatives reject you,
and your friends are worse.
When you really need them,
they are not there.
8Do yourself a favor
by having good sense—
you will be glad you did.
9Dishonest witnesses and liars
will be destroyed.
10It isn't right for a fool
to live in luxury
or for a slave to rule
in place of a king.
11It's wise to be patient
and show what you are like
by forgiving others.
12An angry king roars
like a lion,
but when a king is pleased,
it's like dew on the crops.
13Foolish children bring disgrace
to their fathers.
A nagging wife goes on and on
like the drip, drip, drip
of the rain.
14You may inherit all you own
from your parents,
but a sensible wife
is a gift from the Lord.
15If you are lazy
and sleep your time away,
you will starve.
16Obey the Lord's teachings
and you will live—
disobey and you will die.
17Caring for the poor
is lending to the Lord,
and you will be well repaid.
18Correct your children
before it's too late;
if you don't punish them,
trouble will come their way.
19People with bad tempers
are always in trouble,
and they need help
over and over again.
20Pay attention to advice
and accept correction,
so you can live sensibly.
21We may make a lot of plans,
but the Lord will do
what he has decided.
22What matters most is loyalty.
It's better to be poor
than to be a liar.
23Showing respect to the Lord
brings true life—
if you do it, you can relax
without fear of danger.
24Some people are too lazy
to lift a hand
to feed themselves.
25Stupid fools learn good sense
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being corrected.
26Disgraceful children
rob their father
and chase their mother away.
27If you stop learning,
you will forget
what you already know.
28A lying witness makes fun
of the court system,
and criminals think crime
is really delicious.
29A stupid fool should expect
to be punished.
translation_text:
1Onɛ an nɔŋdaan ka ken nɛ burikinnim
sɔn'oe zɔlʋg kanɛ ka o nɔɔr pian'ad an ziri.
2Li ka' sʋm nɛ fʋn na mɔr nyɛlʋg ka baŋir kae
bɛɛ kir tɔ'ɔtɔ keŋ yidig suorɛ.
3Ninsaal mɛŋ zɔlimisi san'amid o,
la'an nɛ wala ka o sʋʋnr duod nɛ Zugsɔb la.
4Kpan'am mɔri zuanam bɛdegʋ kenna,
amaa nɔŋdaan zuanam widigidnɛ ka kɛt o.
5Onɛ dit ziri kasɛt kʋ keŋ zaalim ka da di'e namisʋgɔ,
ba mɛ kʋ bas faad sɔb ka o keŋ zaalim.
6Nidib bɛdegʋ la'asid onɛ an tuongat san'ani bɔɔd sʋŋir,
ka sɔ' wʋsa zua an onɛ tisid piini.
7Nɔŋ daan sizuop ya'a nɛ'ɛs o,
di na niŋ wala ka o zuanam wʋsa kʋ luak o!
La'an nɛ on bɛlimmi dɔlli ba la,
o ieedi ba ka pʋ nyɛtaa.
8Onɛ ieed ya'am la nɔŋ o mɛŋ;
ka onɛ mɛ gban'ad si'el gbin la kennɛ tuon.
9Onɛ dit ziri kasɛt kʋ keŋ zaalim ka da di'e namisʋgɔ,
ka faad sɔb na ba'as yɔri.
10Li pʋ nar ye zɔlʋg bɛ zin'isʋŋinɛ,
ka li bɛ'ɛd mɛ anɛ sankpan'asi na sʋ'oe na'abiis!
11Ninsaal ya'am kɛt ka o an suguru sɔb;
on pʋ zaŋid sɔ' taal la zugʋ kɛt ka o nyɛt girima.
12Na'ab sʋnf ya'a pɛlig o nwa'amnɛ wʋʋ gbigim,
amaa o nimbaanlzɔɔr nwɛnɛ mɛligim na lit mɔɔg zug.
13Bizɔlʋg kɛtnɛ ka o saam ba'as yɔri,
ka pu'a kanɛ nɔŋ zaba nwɛnɛ ku'om na nyun tuak-tuak nɛ.
14Ya' nɛ kpan'am anɛ faar linɛ yit du'adibin na,
amaa Zugsɔb la tisid pu'a kanɛ mɔr ya'am.
15Gbanya'a gbisidi tigid,
ka onɛ pʋ siakid ye o nɔbir yaki keŋ tʋʋma ni la,
on sɔb na dig nɛ kɔ'ɔm.
16Onɛ di'ed zi'ela na vʋe yuug,
amaa onɛ nɛ'ɛsi li na kpi.
17Onɛ sʋŋid tadimnam pɛ'ɛŋidnɛ tisid Zugsɔb la,
ka o na yɔɔ o on maal si'el la zug.
18Tɛɛgimi fʋ biig tʋbir saŋa kanɛ ka ti'ir nam bɛ la,
ka da bas o ka li kɛ ka o kpi tɔ'ɔtɔɔ.
19Sʋnpɛɛn galisʋg sɔb na nyɛɛ li yɔɔd;
fʋ ya'a sʋŋi yis o yɛla ni, o na lɛn kpɛn' ka fʋ lɛn yis o ya'as.
20Kɛlisim sa'alʋg ka di'e pa'alʋg,
ka li naarin la fʋ na an ya'am sɔb.
21Ninsaal pʋtɛn'ɛr gban'adi yɛla bɛdegʋ,
amaa Zugsɔb la bɔɔdim na zi'en.
22Ninsaali bɔɔd si'el anɛ nɔŋilim linɛ pʋ naada;
fʋ ya'a an nɔŋdaan li sɔn'oe fʋn na an faad sɔb.
23Zugsɔb zɔtim mɔri vʋm kenna:
ala ka fʋ na nyɛ vʋ'ʋsʋm ka yɛla kʋ paae fɔ.
24Gbanya'a na nɔk o nu'ugʋ tʋm laan;
amaa ka kʋ nyaŋi nɔki niŋ nɔɔrinɛ!
25Nwɛ'ɛm nintʋ'ʋs ka banɛ nan ka' ya'am la na zamis ya'am;
sa'alim onɛ gban'ad pian'ad gbin ka o na paam baŋiri pɛ'ɛs.
26Onɛ faaɛn o saam la'ad ka kad o maa yis la,
o sɔb mɔri nyan nɛ zuziigi kenna.
27M biiga, fʋ ya'a pʋ lɛn kɛlisid sa'alʋgɔ,
fʋ na yidig ka kʋ baŋ ya'am pian'adɛ.
28Onɛ tisid zam kasɛt tʋ'ʋdi yɛlsida,
ka bugusnam la vɔn tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd wʋʋ li anɛ diib.
29Namisʋg bɛɛ gur nintʋ'ʋsnam,
ka bʋ'ʋd mɛ digi gur banɛ an zɔn la.

english_text:
Words of Wisdom Are Better than Gold
1It isn't smart to get drunk!
Drinking makes a fool of you
and leads to fights.
2An angry ruler
is like a roaring lion—
make either one angry,
and you are dead.
3It makes you look good
when you avoid a fight—
only fools love to quarrel.
4If you are too lazy to plow,
don't expect a harvest.
5Someone's thoughts may be
as deep as the ocean,
but if you are smart,
you will discover them.
6There are many who say,
“You can trust me!”
But can they be trusted?
7Good people live right,
and God blesses the children
who follow their example.
8When rulers decide cases,
they weigh the evidence.
9Can any of us really say,
“My thoughts are pure,
and my sins are gone”?
10Two things the Lord hates
are dishonest scales
and dishonest measures.
11The good or bad
that children do
shows what they are like.
12Hearing and seeing
are gifts from the Lord.
13If you sleep all the time,
you will starve;
if you get up and work,
you will have enough food.
14Everyone likes to brag
about getting a bargain.
15Sensible words are better
than gold or jewels.
16You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
17The food you get by cheating
may taste delicious,
but it turns to gravel.
18Be sure you have sound advice
before making plans
or starting a war.
19Stay away from gossips—
they tell everything.
20Children who curse their parents
will go to the land of darkness
long before their time.
21Getting rich quick
may turn out to be a curse.
22Don't try to get even.
Trust the Lord,
and he will help you.
23The Lord hates dishonest scales
and dishonest weights.
So don't cheat!
24How can we know
what will happen to us
when the Lord alone decides?
25Don't fall into the trap
of making promises to God
before you think!
26A wise ruler severely punishes
every criminal.
27Our inner thoughts are a lamp
from the Lord,
and they search our hearts.
28Rulers are protected
by God's mercy and loyalty,
but they must be merciful
for their kingdoms to last.
29Young people take pride
in their strength,
but the gray hairs of wisdom
are even more beautiful.
30A severe beating can knock all
of the evil out of you!
translation_text:
1Daam anɛ ninla'ad ka dankpi'euŋ ziid zabbɔɔsim na
onɛ bas o mɛŋ ka daam kpɛn'ɛs o mɔɔg ka' ya'am sɔba.
2Na'ab sʋnpɛɛn nwɛnɛ gbigimi na nwa'am;
onɛ kɛ ka o sʋnf pɛlig na kɔ'ɔŋ o nyɔvʋr
3Onɛ gban'e o mɛŋ nɛ zaba mɔr girima,
amaa zɔlʋg on ieedi zaba tɔ'ɔtɔ.
4Gbanya'a pʋ kuod kuob saŋaa;
ala ka bunib saŋa ka o gɔsid o pɔɔg ka si'el kae.
5Ninsaal pʋtɛn'ɛr nwɛnɛ ku'ozuluŋ nɛ
amaa baŋir sɔb na gban'e li gbin.
6Nidib bɛdegʋ yɛti ye ba mɔr nɔŋir,
amaa anɔ'ɔn na nyɛ onɛ an yɛlsida sɔba?
7Pʋpielim sɔb bɛllim pʋ mɔr gba'arɛ;
o biis na nyɛ albareka bɛog sa.
8Na'ab ya'a ti zin'inɛ o na'am gbauŋ zug ye o kad saria,
o nɔkidnɛ o nini bakid bɛ'ɛd wʋʋ ki ka ba yɛligid nɛ.
9Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi yɛl ye, “Mam pʋʋg anɛ yinne;
man anɛ nyain ka pʋ mɔr tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ?”
10Nidib ya'a mak la'ad ka zam taaba kuosimin,
li anɛ linɛ ka Zugsɔb la kis hali.
11Hali biig gba' tʋʋma ni ka nidib baŋid
ye o pʋʋg anɛ yinne ka dɔl suor.
12Tʋba banɛ wʋm nɛ nini banɛ nyɛt la,
Li anɛ Zugsɔb la maali ba wʋsa.
13Da nɔŋ gbɛɛm ka fʋ na kilim nɔŋdaan;
duom tʋm, ka fʋ na nyɛ diibi di ka li kpɛlim.
14Onɛ da'ad la yɛt ye, “Ayei, li anɛ saada, li anɛ saada,”
ka li nya'aŋ ka o yʋ'ʋn nwɛ'ɛd nyɔ'ɔg on da' si'em la yɛla.
15Sanlima bɛnɛ ka kugvɛnla mɛ bɛ,
amaa ya'am pian'adi gati ba wʋsa.
16Nɔkim onɛ kaanb ye o na yɔ saan sam la fuug;
o ya'a niŋ ala tis teŋ zʋŋ nid yanam faanmi li!
17Nid ya'a zu diibi di, li malis nɛ o nɔɔrin,
amaa li nya'aŋ, o nɔɔr na pɛ'ɛl nɛ zigi.
18Fʋ ya'a gban'e ye fʋ tʋm si'el, fʋn ieem sa'alʋg;
da keŋ zaba ka pʋ gban'e fʋn na zab si'em.
19Onɛ ginnɛ yɛɛsid viigidi nidib pian'asu'ada paalʋ;
alazugɔ luakim pian'agalisʋg sɔb.
20Nid ya'a pɔ nɔɔrɛ tis o ba' bɛɛ o ma,
o bugum na kpiis lik amɛŋa ni.
21Kpan'am linɛ ka fʋ pʋ namis ka paam la
kʋ naae nɛ yɛlsʋmmɛ.
22Da yɛl ye, “Bɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka fʋ maalim la m na yɔ sammɛ!”
Gu'usim ka Zugsɔb la na yɔɔ li sʋ'ʋŋa lɛbisif.
23Zugsɔb la kis nidibi na zam taaba kuosim pʋʋgin,
zam makir anɛ linɛ pʋ malis o.
24Zugsɔb la sʋ'oe ti nɔbir yakir yɛla,
ka sɔ' na niŋ wala baŋ linɛ na niŋ o bɛllim pʋʋginɛ?
25Tɛn'ɛsim sʋ'ʋŋa ka nyaan pɔ nɔɔri zi'el ye fʋ na pɛsig si'eli tis Zugsɔb la,
ya'a ka' ala fʋ na ti lɛb nya'aŋ ka li an pakiri tisif.
26Na'akanɛ mɔr ya'am bakidnɛ nimbɛ'ɛdnam la,
ka namisidi ba wʋʋ ki ka ba bʋ' zieŋin yɛligid nɛ.
27Zugsɔb la fitiri ieed ninsaal siig,
o mɔri gɔsid o sʋʋnrin yɛla wʋsa.
28Nɔŋir nɛ yɛlsida na sʋŋ na'ab,
ka kɛ ka o zin'inɛ o na'am gbauŋ zugʋ yuug.
29Na'akim paŋi aan ba girima,
zuobpielim an bʋnkʋd vɛnlim.
30Bʋ'ʋkanɛ tisid dɛŋ la yisid tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd
ka nwɛ'ɛd mɛ tiakid ninsaal pʋtɛn'ɛr.

english_text:
The Lord Is In Charge
1 The Lord controls rulers,
just as he determines
the course of rivers.
2We may think we are doing
the right thing,
but the Lord always knows
what is in our hearts.
3Doing what is right and fair
pleases the Lord
more than an offering.
4Evil people are proud
and arrogant,
but sin is the only crop
they produce.
5If you plan and work hard,
you will have plenty;
if you hurry to get rich,
you will end up poor.
6Cheating to get rich
is a foolish dream
and no less than suicide.
7You destroy yourself
by being cruel and violent
and refusing to live right.
8All crooks are liars,
but anyone who is innocent
will do right.
9 It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
10Evil people want to do wrong,
even to their friends.
11An ignorant fool learns
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being instructed.
12God is always fair!
He knows what the wicked do
and will punish them.
13If you won't help the poor,
don't expect to be heard
when you cry out for help.
14A secret bribe will save you
from someone's fierce anger.
15When justice is done,
good citizens are glad
and crooks are terrified.
16If you stop using good sense,
you will find yourself
in the grave.
17Heavy drinkers and others
who live only for pleasure
will lose all they have.
18God's people will escape,
but all who are wicked
will pay the price.
19It's better out in the desert
than at home with a nagging,
complaining wife.
20Be sensible and store up
precious treasures—
don't waste them
like a fool.
21If you try to be kind and good,
you will be blessed with life
and goodness and honor.
22One wise person can defeat
a city full of soldiers
and capture their fortress.
23Watching what you say
can save you
a lot of trouble.
24If you are proud and conceited,
everyone will say,
“You're a snob!”
25If you want too much
and are too lazy to work,
it could be fatal.
26But people who obey God
are always generous.
27 The Lord despises the offerings
of wicked people
with evil motives.
28If you tell lies in court,
you are done for;
only a reliable witness
can do the job.
29Wicked people bluff their way,
but God's people think
before they take a step.
30No matter how much you know
or what plans you make,
you can't defeat the Lord.
31Even if your army has horses
ready for battle,
the Lord will always win.
translation_text:
1Na'ab la ya'am bɛ nɛ Zugsɔb la nu'ugin wʋʋ ku'osuor nɛ;
onɛ kɛ ka li ku'om pʋbidi ken on bɔɔd si'el.
2Ninsaal suoya wʋsa anɛ sʋm o mɛŋ nini ni,
amaa Zugsɔb la gban'adi li gbin wʋsa.
3Sida nɛ fʋn na tʋm linɛ dɔl suor la
ma'ad Zugsɔb la sʋʋnri gat maana.
4Nimpʋnannim nɛ dʋ'ʋsi-m-mɛŋ
ma'aa an nɛɛsim linɛ bɛɛ tisid tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim.
5Nimmua daan ya'a mɔdig o mɛŋi gban'e gban'asʋma li mɔri nyɔɔdi kenna
ka kikirʋg mɛ mɔr nɔŋi kenna.
6Nid ya'a dɔlis filim-filim suori paam kpan'am li na naae tɔ'ɔtɔ
nwɛnɛ walim nɛ kum bɛndig nɛ.
7Bugusnam banɛ nɔŋ zaba la linɛ na mɔri ba keŋ,
ban zan'as ye ba kʋ tʋm linɛ dɔl suor la zug.
8Onɛ tʋm taal suor anɛ suogɔnlima,
amaa banɛ pʋ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd la tʋʋma dɔlli suor.
9Fʋ ya'a gbɛɛnd gɔnnin
li sɔn'oe fʋn na gbɛɛnd nɛ pu'a kanɛ nɔŋ zaba.
10Bugus ieedi bɛ'ɛd daar wʋsa;
o pʋ zɔt o kpi'a nimbaanliga.
11Nintʋ'ʋs ya'a ti nyɛ namisʋg,
banɛ nan ka' ya'am na zamis ya'am;
ba ya'a pa'al ya'am sɔb, o paamidi mi'ilim.
12Wina'am onɛ an pʋpiel la mi' bugusim sɔbi maan si'el o yin,
ka na kɛ ka san'auŋ paae o.
13Nid ya'a li' o tʋba pʋ bɔɔd ye o wʋm nɔŋdaan kaasiga,
on mɛ na ti kaasid ka sɔ' kʋ kɛlisɛ.
14Piini linɛ ka ba su'a tis la bʋgʋn onɛ sʋnfʋ pɛlig la sʋʋnr;
ka nid sʋnf ya'a duoe hali, ba na tun'e su'a da' o nɛ ligidi ka li ma'ae.
15Ba ya'a tu'as yɛlsida, li bʋgʋnnɛ pʋpielim sɔb sʋʋnr
amaa ka kɛt ka dabiem mɔr tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim la.
16Ninkanɛ bie ka bas ya'am linɛ gban'ad si'el gbin la suorin
o na gaadi sig kpi'im teŋ.
17Onɛ di'emid ka maannɛ o ya'amin la na lieb nɔŋdaan.
Onɛ wʋsa nɔŋ daam nɛ dikpama kʋ tun'e nyɛ kpan'am.
18Bugusnam la na di'e pʋpielim dim namisʋg,
ka ziri dim la na paam burikinnam namisʋg.
19Fʋ ya'a bɛ pipirigini fʋ kɔn'ɔkɔn',
li sɔn'oe fʋn na bɛ nɛ pu'a kanɛ nɔŋ zaba ka mɔr sʋnpɛɛn.
20Ya'am dim yin ka arezak nɛ disʋma bɛ ka ba su'a,
amaa zɔn yin la ba diti si'el wʋsa naae.
21Onɛ ieed nɔŋilim nɛ pʋpielim tʋʋma
na paam nyɔvʋwɔk, nɛ pʋpielim, nɛ na'asi.
22Ya'am sɔb zabidi nyaŋid zabzabidib teŋ,
ka san'ami ba kpi'euŋ zin'ig linɛ ka ba ti'e la.
23Onɛ wʋsa gu'usid o zilim nɛ o nɔɔr yisidi
o mɛŋ yɛla ni.
24Onɛ an nyɛɛsim sɔb nɛ tita'al,
ba buon o sɔb yʋ'ʋr ye, “Nintʋ'ʋs”;
o tʋmnɛ si'el wʋsa, nɛ nyɛɛsim ma'aa.
25Ya'amlɛog ma'aa na kʋ gbanya'a,
bɔzugɔ o ye o nu'ug kʋ tʋm si'ela.
26Dabisir wʋsa o tɛn'ɛsidi on bɔɔd si'el la yɛla,
amaa pʋpiel on tisidi saŋa wʋsa ka kʋ mɔŋ sɔ'.
27Zugsɔb la kis bugusnam la maana;
ka li kas-kas anɛ on na maal nɛ pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd.
28Onɛ di ziri kasɛt la na paam san'auŋ,
ka onɛ wʋsa kɛlisid o na nyɛ san'auŋ linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.
29Ninkanɛ an bugus ma'anɛ lɔdigid o nindaa,
amaa onɛ an burikin tɛn'ɛsidi o yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa.
30Ya'am si'a kae, mi'ilim si'a kae, gban'asi'a mɛ kae
na nyaŋi gaad Zugsɔb la.
31Ba bɔb Wiefʋ gur zaba dabisir,
amaa Zugsɔb la sʋ'oe nyaŋir.

english_text:
The Value of a Good Reputation
1A good reputation and respect
are worth much more
than silver and gold.
2The rich and the poor
are all created
by the Lord.
3When you see trouble coming,
don't be stupid
and walk right into it—
be smart and hide.
4Respect and serve the Lord!
Your reward will be wealth,
a long life, and honor.
5Crooks walk down a road
full of thorny traps.
Stay away from there!
6 Teach your children
right from wrong,
and when they are grown
they will still do right.
7The poor are ruled by the rich,
and those who borrow
are slaves of moneylenders.
8Troublemakers get in trouble,
and their terrible anger
will get them nowhere.
9The Lord blesses everyone
who freely gives food
to the poor.
10Arguments and fights
will come to an end,
if you chase away those
who insult others.
11The king is the friend of all
who are sincere
and speak with kindness.
12The Lord watches over everyone
who shows good sense,
but he frustrates the plans
of deceitful liars.
13Don't be so lazy that you say,
“If I go to work,
a lion will eat me!”
14The words of a bad woman
are like a deep pit;
if you make the Lord angry,
you will fall right in.
15All children are foolish,
but firm correction
will make them change.
16Cheat the poor to make profit
or give gifts to the rich—
either way you lose.
Thirty Wise Sayings
17Here are some sayings
of people with wisdom,
so listen carefully
as I teach.
18You will be glad
that you know these sayings
and can recite them.
19I am teaching them today,
so that you
may trust the Lord.
20I have written thirty sayings
filled with sound advice.
