21You can trust them completely
to give you the right words
for those in charge of you.
–1–
22Don't take advantage
of the poor
or cheat them in court.
23The Lord is their defender,
and what you do to them,
he will do to you.
–2–
24Don't make friends with anyone
who has a bad temper.
25You might turn out like them
and get caught in a trap.
–3–
26Don't guarantee to pay
someone else's debt.
27If you don't have the money,
you might lose your bed.
–4–
28Don't move a boundary marker
set up by your ancestors.
–5–
29If you do your job well,
you will work for a ruler
and never be a slave.
translation_text:
1Yʋ'ʋsʋŋ gat kpan'am;
girima mɛ gat sanlima nɛ anzurifa.
2Bʋmmɔr nɛ nɔŋdaani an yinne si'em nwa':
Zugsɔb la maali ba wʋsa.
3Pʋtɛn'ɛr sɔb dɛŋidnɛ nyɛt yɛltɔɔg ka luakid,
amaa zɔlʋg on na gaad tuonnɛ nyɛ namisʋg.
4A-sie-m-mɛŋ nɛ Zugsɔb la zɔtim
mɔri kpan'am nɛ na'asi nɛ vʋm kenna.
5Gɔn'ɔs nɛ bɛndis dignɛ bugusnam suoya ni,
amaa onɛ gu'usid o mɛŋ na yi yɛlban la ni.
6Pa'alim biig on na bɛ si'em,
ka o ya'a ti nɔbig o kʋ tiak ka basi lii.
7Bʋndaane sʋ'oe nɔŋdaan,
ka onɛ pɛ'ɛŋ mɛ an on pɛ'ɛŋ sɔ' san'an la sankpan'as.
8Onɛ bʋd bɛ'ɛd na bun yɛltɔɔg,
ka kʋ lɛm mɔr kpi'euŋʋ na mugus nidiba.
9Onɛ tisid piini la mɛ na nyɛ bareka,
on pʋdigid o diib nɛ nɔŋ dim la zug.
10Kadim nintʋ'ʋs la yis ka sʋnpɛɛn gaad,
ka nɔŋgbannwa'ar nɛ zaba na naae.
11Onɛ an burikin ka o pian'ad mɛ tisid sumbʋgʋsʋm,
on sɔb na an na'ab zua.
12Zugsɔb la kpa'anɛ o nini gɔsid baŋir dim,
amaa o lɛɛ kati banɛ kae sida la pian'adi basid.
13Gbanya'a pʋ bɔɔd tʋʋma ka ma' ye, “Gbigim bɛ samannin,
m pa'a ti yii keŋ ka o kʋʋm!”
14Pu'agɔɔndir nɔɔr zulimnɛ nwɛnɛ bʋmbɔk;
onɛ ka Zugsɔb sʋnpɛɛn bɛɛ o zugin la na lii li pʋʋgin.
15Biig ya'a tʋm zɔlim tʋʋma
sisanbig na sa'al o ka o tiak ka basi li.
16Onɛ mugusid nɔŋ dim ye o nyɛ kpan'am paas
nɛ onɛ mɔr o la'adi tisid kpan'am dim,
babayi' la wʋsa na lieb nɔŋ dim.
Ya'am dim pian'ad
17An baanlimm ka kɛlis ya'am dim pian'ad;
kɛl ka fʋ ya'am gban'e man pa'anif si'el la,
18bɔzugɔ fʋ ya'a nɔki li niŋi fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛrin
ka mɔri li wʋsa fʋ nɔɔrin
ala ka li na niŋif malisim.
19Mam pa'anif nɛ'ɛŋa nɛ zina
ye li kɛ ka fʋ tis Zugsɔb la sida. Ɛɛn, fʋn ka m yɛt!
20M pʋ sɔb ya'am pian'ad pistan' tisi fɔɔ?
Li anɛ pian'ad linɛ mɔr sa'alʋg nɛ baŋir. Bɛɛ m ma'aanɛɛ?
21M pa'alif linɛ an sida ka pʋ mɔr viigirɛ,
ala ka fʋ na baŋ fʋn na gandig banɛ tʋmif la si'em.
22Da faaɛn nɔŋdaan si'el on an tadim la zugɔ
ka mɛ da mɔŋ fara sɔb bʋʋd kɔɔtʋ nii,
23bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la na zabi tisi ba
ka na fan' banɛ faaɛn ba la'ad la.
24Da dɔl sʋnpɛɛn galisʋg sɔb zuodɛ,
mɛ da la'asi fʋ mɛŋ nɛ onɛ sʋnfʋ pʋ ya'asid pɛligirɛ,
25ya'a ka' alaa fʋ na zamis o suoya la
ka ti kpɛn'ɛsi fʋ mɛŋ bɛndigin.
26Da an ninkanɛ bɔɔd ye fʋ zi'enɛ tis nidib ka ba pɛ'ɛŋ
bɛɛ fʋ nɔk la'adi zi'el ye fʋ na yɔ sɔ' sammɛ;
27fʋ ya'a ti kɔ'ɔŋ yɔɔb,
hali fʋ gadʋg linɛ ka fʋ mɔri dig la, ba na faaɛn li.
28Da tɔlisi fʋ kpi'a titɔndig kugir
kanɛ ka ba da digil kʋdimin sa laa.
29Fʋ nyɛ ninkanɛ mi' tʋʋma sʋ'ʋŋa laa?
O na tʋm na'anam yin;
o kʋ tʋm tis tadimnama.

english_text:
–6–
1When you are invited
to eat with a king,
use your best manners.
2Don't go and stuff yourself!
That would be just the same
as cutting your throat.
3Don't be greedy for all
of that fancy food!
It may not be so tasty.
–7–
4Give up trying so hard
to get rich.
5Your money flies away
before you know it,
just like an eagle
suddenly taking off.
–8–
6Don't accept an invitation
to eat a selfish person's food,
no matter how good it is.
7People like that take note
of how much you eat.
They say, “Take all you want!”
But they don't mean it.
8Each bite will come back up,
and all your kind words
will be wasted.
–9–
9Don't talk to fools—
they will make fun of you.
–10–
10Don't move a boundary marker
or take the land
that belongs to orphans.
11God All-Powerful is there
to defend them against you.
–11–
12Listen to instruction
and do your best to learn.
–12–
13Don't fail to correct
your children.
You won't kill them
by being firm,
14and it may even
save their lives.
–13–
15My children,
if you show good sense,
I will be happy,
16and if you are truthful,
I will really be glad.
–14–
17Don't be jealous of sinners,
but always honor the Lord.
18Then you will truly have hope
for the future.
–15–
19Listen to me, my children!
Be wise and have enough sense
to follow the right path.
20Don't be a heavy drinker
or stuff yourself with food.
21It will make you feel drowsy,
and you will end up poor
with only rags to wear.
–16–
22Pay attention to your father,
and don't neglect your mother
when she grows old.
23Invest in truth and wisdom,
discipline and good sense,
and don't part with them.
24Make your father truly happy
by living right and showing
sound judgment.
25Make your parents proud,
especially your mother.
–17–
26My son, pay close attention,
and gladly follow
my example.
27Bad women and unfaithful wives
are like a deep pit—
28they are waiting to attack you
like a gang of robbers
with victim after victim.
–18–
29Who is always in trouble?
Who argues and fights?
Who has cuts and bruises?
Whose eyes are red?
30Everyone who stays up late,
having just one more drink.
31Don't even look
at that colorful stuff
bubbling up in the glass!
It goes down so easily,
32but later it bites
like a poisonous snake.
33You will see weird things,
and your mind
will play tricks on you.
34You will feel tossed about
like someone trying to sleep
on a ship in a storm.
35You will be bruised all over,
without even remembering
how it all happened.
And you will lie awake asking,
“When will morning come,
so I can drink some more?”
translation_text:
1Fʋ ya'a zin'in nɛ na'ab ye fʋ di,
gban'ami fʋ mɛŋ ka baŋ banɛ nɔk diibi tisif la an sɔ'.
2Fʋ ya'a an dindiis,
fʋn gu'usimi fʋ mɛŋ.
3Da kɛ ka kʋkɔma'asim mɔrif
nɛ o diib la malis si'em la zugɔ,
ka daasi'erɛɛ o bɔɔdi makif nɛ gɔs.
4Da bɔɔdi fʋ tʋm kʋʋ fʋ mɛŋi paam kpan'am;
mɔr ya'am ka gu'usid.
5Fʋ ya'a nɔki fʋ nifi kpa' kpan'am, li na gaad
wʋʋ li busnɛ kpʋkpama ianknɛ,
li na ianki dʋʋ agɔla wʋʋ silʋg nɛ.
6Da di dasuŋ sɔb diibɔ,
da kɛ ka fʋ ya'am kpɛn' lii;
7bɔzugɔ o anɛ ninkanɛ buudi
tɛn'ɛsid o diib la samme an si'em;
o na yɛl ye, “Dim, dim, ka nuu fʋ bɔɔdim bɛn!”
Amaa ka o sʋnf lɛɛ kpɛnnɛf.
8Fʋ na tin linɛ ka fʋ di bi'ela la,
ka fʋn faas o si'em la lieb zaalim.
9Da pian'ad nɛ zɔlʋgɔ,
bɔzugɔ o na gɔsi ziemi fʋ ya'am pian'ad la.
10Da tɔlis kʋdimin sa titɔndig kugirɛ
bɛɛ fʋ kuaa kpɛn' kpiibig pɔɔginɛ,
11bɔzugɔ onɛ zabidi ba yɛla la kpi'em nɛ;
o na duoe zi'enɛ tu'a ba antu'a tisi ba.
12Kɛl ka fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛr di'e sa'alʋg
ka fʋ tʋba kɛlig linɛ an baŋir.
13Da bas biig sa'alʋgɔ;
fʋ ya'a fieb biig nɛ sisanbig o kʋ kpii.
14Fiebim biig la nɛ sisanbig
ka linɛ na kɛ ka fʋ faaɛn o yis kumin.
15M biiga, fʋ ya'a mɔr ya'am,
li na ma'ae mam sʋʋnr.
16Fʋ ya'a pian'ad linɛ dɔl suor
m sʋnf na malis hali.
17Da mɔr fufum nɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dima,
amaa an onɛ mɔr Zugsɔb la zɔtim saŋa wʋsa.
18Li anɛ sida ye fʋ na mɔr ti'ir bɛog sa,
ka fʋ ti'ir la kʋ naae.
19M biiga, kɛlisim ka baŋ ya'am,
ka kɛ ka fʋ ya'am gban'e linɛ dɔl suor.
20Da la'asi fʋ mɛŋ nɛ banɛ gban'e daam nu'us ayi' la
bɛɛ banɛ an dindiisnam laa;
21ka danuudib nɛ dindiisnam na lieb nɔŋ dim,
ka gbɛɛm sɔb na yɛɛd kparikɛɛnd ma'aa.
22Kɛlisimi fʋ ba' onɛ du'af la pian'ad,
ka fʋ ma ya'a kʋdig fʋn da nɛ'ɛs oo.
23Da'am sida ka da kuosi lii;
ieem ya'am, nɛ zamisʋg, nɛ pian'ad gbin gban'ar.
24Bikanɛ an pʋpielim sɔb, o saam mɔri sumalisim;
ka onɛ biigi mɔr ya'am o nif tigid o nɛ.
25Kɛl ka fʋ ba' nɛ fʋ ma sʋnf ma'ae;
kɛl ka pu'a kanɛ du'af la mɔr sumalisim!
26M biiga, pɛligimi fʋ pʋʋgʋ tisim
ka yɔ'ɔgi fʋ nini gɔsi m suoya la;
27ka pu'a pu'agɔɔndir anɛ bʋmbɔk zulʋŋ
ka pu'a bɛ'ɛd mɛ nwɛnɛ bulig kanɛ nɔɔri pʋ yalimma.
28O dig nɛ gu'ud wʋʋ banɛ faand,
ka gban'e dau kaŋa lɔ'ɔŋ dau kaŋa
ka kɛt ka banɛ tʋm bɛ'ɛd la zu'oe pɛ'ɛs.
29Anɔ'ɔnɛ mɔr tɔɔgɔ? Anɔ'ɔnɛ mɔr sʋnsa'aŋa?
Anɔ'ɔnɛ bɔɔd zaba? Anɔ'ɔnɛ fabin na?
Anɔ'ɔn ka o niŋgbina fieb zaalim-zaalim?
Anɔ'ɔn ka o nini mu'oe wii nɛ?
30Banɛ ka daam kʋʋli ba,
ka ba gɛndigid dankpi'ema kɔn'ɔb, kɔn'ɔbi nuud la.
31Da gɔsid daam mu'oe wii si'em laa,
bɛɛ lin zi'e nɛ nwammi fuud
ka fʋ nuud ka li malis ka sigid bɔlimm-bɔlimm sʋ'ʋŋa la!
32Li naarin la, li na dumif nwɛnɛ waaf,
ka li zɛɛnsim nwɛnɛ dunduug zɛɛnsim nɛ.
33Fʋ nini na nyɛt bʋnsaamis
ka fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛr pian'ad yɔri-yɔri tisidif.
34Fʋ na nwɛnɛ ninkanɛ gbisid atɛukʋn
ka dig nwiis banɛ ka ba lɔ anrʋŋ la zug.
35Fʋ na yɛl ye, “Ba nwɛ'ɛm,” amaa m pʋ pu'alim!
Ba bʋ'ʋm amaa li pʋ zabidima!
Bʋndaar ka m na tun'e duoe
ka lɛm paam daam nu?

english_text:
–19–
1Don't be jealous of crooks
or want to be their friends.
2All they think about
and talk about
is violence and cruelty.
–20–
3Use wisdom and understanding
to establish your home;
4let good sense fill the rooms
with priceless treasures.
–21–
5Wisdom brings strength,
and knowledge gives power.
6Battles are won
by listening to advice
and making a lot of plans.
–22–
7Wisdom is too much for fools!
Their advice is no good.
–23–
8No one but troublemakers
think up trouble.
9Everyone hates senseless fools
who think up ways to sin.
–24–
10Don't give up and be helpless
in times of trouble.
–25–
11Don't fail to rescue those
who are doomed to die.
12Don't say, “I didn't know it!”
God can read your mind.
He watches each of us
and knows our thoughts.
And God will pay us back
for what we do.
–26–
13Honey is good for you,
my children,
and it tastes sweet.
14Wisdom is like honey
for your life—
if you find it,
your future is bright.
–27–
15Don't be a cruel person
who attacks good people
and hurts their families.
16Even if good people
fall seven times,
they will get back up.
But when trouble strikes
the wicked,
that's the end of them.
–28–
17Don't be happy
to see your enemies trip
and fall down.
18The Lord will find out
and be unhappy.
Then he will stop
being angry with them.
–29–
19Don't let evil people
worry you
or make you jealous.
20They will soon be gone
like the flame of a lamp
that burns out.
–30–
21My children, you must respect
the Lord and the king,
and you must not make friends
with anyone who rebels
against either of them.
22Who knows what sudden disaster
the Lord or a ruler
might bring?
More Sayings That Make Good Sense
23Here are some more sayings
that make good sense:
When you judge,
you must be fair.
24If you let the guilty
go free,
people of all nations
will hate and curse you.
25But if you punish the guilty,
things will go well for you,
and you will prosper.
26Giving an honest answer
is a sign
of true friendship.
27Get your fields ready
and plant your crops
before starting a home.
28Don't accuse anyone
who isn't guilty.
Don't ever tell a lie
29or say to someone,
“I'll get even with you!”
30I once walked by the field
and the vineyard
of a lazy fool.
31Thorns and weeds
were everywhere,
and the stone wall
had fallen down.
32When I saw this,
it taught me a lesson:
33 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
34Suddenly poverty hits you
and everything is gone!
translation_text:
1Da mɔr fufum nɛ bugusnama,
da bɔɔd ye fʋ la'as nɛ baa;
2bɔzugɔ ba sʋnf gban'e nɛ zaba,
ka ba nɔɔr pian'ad la ieed yɛla.
3Ya'am mɛɛd yir,
ka agban'ad si'el gbin kɛt ka li zi'e.
4Baŋiri kɛt ka yir la dɔɔd la pɛ'ɛn
nɛ la'asʋma nɛ kpan'am wʋsa.
5Ninkanɛ mɔr ya'am mɔr paŋ,
ka ninkanɛ mɔr baŋir paŋ mɛ paasid.
6Fʋ ya'a wa'ae zaba ni ieemi li suoya,
ka nyaŋir anɛ fʋn na mɔr banɛ sa'an bɛdegʋ.
7Ya'am zu'oe galis nɛ zɔlʋgʋ na mɔri li;
bɔzugɔ o pʋ ya'ad o nɔɔr nidib sʋʋgin bɛɛ kɔɔtʋ nii.
8Onɛ tɛn'ɛsid bɛ'ɛd
ba na buon o ye, pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd sɔb.
9Zɔlʋg gban'ar anɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd,
ka nidib wʋsa kis nintʋ'ʋs.
10Fʋ ya'a tadig yɛla saŋa,
fʋ sid na tadig amɛŋa!
11Faanm banɛ wa'ae kum zin'igin la;
ka gban'e banɛ ka ba kʋʋsi ba bɛ'ɛd
ye asɛɛ ka ba kpi la.
12Fʋ ya'a yɛl ye, “Amaa tinam zi' nɛ' yɛlaa,”
onɛ mi' linɛ bɛ ninsaal pʋtɛn'ɛrin la kʋ baŋi lii?
Onɛ guri fʋ nyɔvʋr la kʋ baŋi lii?
O kʋ yɔ sɔ' wʋsa on tʋm si'el laa?
13M biiga, dim siind ka li an sʋm
siind linɛ an singbana la na malisi fʋ nɔɔrin.
14Baŋim ye ya'am mɛ an sʋm tisi fʋ siig;
fʋ ya'a nyɛɛ li, fʋ mɔr ti'ir bɛog sa,
ka fʋ ti'ir la kʋ naae.
15Da su'a digi gur ye fʋ keŋ san'am pʋpielim sɔb yir
wʋʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔbi tʋm si'em la,
da keŋ o yinnɛ faaɛn o la'adɛ;
16bɔzugɔ pʋpiel ya'a li nɔɔr ayɔpɔi, o na lɛn duoe,
amaa zam sɔb tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd na dii o.
17Fʋ dataa ya'a li da kɛ ka li ma'ae fʋ sʋnf ka fʋ dii tigɛ;
o ya'a tu'ug, fʋn da maal sumalisim.
18Ka ya'a ka' ala Zugsɔb la na nyɛ ka li pʋ malis oo
ka o yis o sʋnpɛɛnni fʋ dataa la san'an.
19Da kɛ ka fʋ sʋnf zabid nɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim la
bɛɛ fʋ bɛn'ɛd fufum nɛ bugusnam la zugɔ,
20bɔzugɔ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb pʋ mɔr bɛogɔ,
ka bugusnam la bugum na kpiis.
21M biiga, zɔm Zugsɔb la ka mɛ zɔ na'ab la,
ka da la'asi fʋ mɛŋ nɛ banɛ pʋ siakid bama nɔɔrɛ,
22ka bama ayi' la na kɛ ka san'auŋ paae ba,
ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na baŋ yɛltita'ar kanɛ yiti ba san'an na?
Ya'am dim pian'ad linɛ pɛ'ɛs
23Ya'am dim pian'ad linɛ pɛ'ɛsi nwa':
Da kad saria nɛ baregaŋa, ka li ka' sʋm.
24Onɛ wʋsa yɛl taal sɔb ye, “Fʋ mɔr bʋʋd,”
nidib na pɔ nɔɔri tis o ka tɛɛns wʋsa zan'as o.
25Amaa si'el wʋsa na an sʋ'ʋŋa tis banɛ tu'asid sida la,
ba na nyɛ albareka tita'ar.
26Nid ya'a pian' sida
li nwɛnɛ on na ʋk o fʋ zi.
27Kuomi fʋ saman yiiga naae ka naan lɔ'ɔŋ pɔɔg;
lin nya'aŋ ka fʋ nyaan mɛɛ fʋ yir.
28Da di ziri kasɛti zɛrigi fʋ kpi'a zaalim-zaalim
bɛɛ fʋ ya'ae fʋ nɔɔri faa tis oo.
29Da yɛl ye, “Asɛɛ m maal o wʋʋ on maal mam si'em la,
m na yɔ dau kaŋa lɛbis wʋʋ on tʋm si'em la.”
30M dɔl gbanya'a la pɔɔgin gaad,
ka dɔl zɔlʋg onɛ zi' gban'ar la tiis pɔɔgin;
31ka nyɛ ka gɔn'ɔs yi zin'ig wʋsa,
mɔɔd ma'aa di'e pɔɔg la zan',
ka li kuga zaŋguom la lii digi.
32M tɛn'ɛs man nyɛ si'el la
ka zamis ya'am li pʋʋgin, ye,
33 Onɛ yɛt ye, “Kɛl ka m gbis bi'ela, ka zɔɔnsim bi'ela
ka kpɛn'ɛsi m nu'us gɛɛgʋni vʋ'ʋs la.”
34Amaa on bɛ gbɛɛmin la, nɔŋ na kena wʋʋ na'ayiig nɛ
ka fara kpɛn' o nwɛnɛ faandibi kena faaɛn o nɛ.

english_text:
More of Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some more
of Solomon's proverbs.
They were copied by the officials
of King Hezekiah of Judah.
2God is praised
for being mysterious;
rulers are praised
for explaining mysteries.
3Who can fully understand
the thoughts of a ruler?
They reach beyond the sky
and go deep in the earth.
4Silver must be purified
before it can be used
to make something of value.
5Evil people must be removed
before anyone can rule
with justice.
6 Don't try to seem important
in the court of a ruler.
7It's better for the ruler
to give you a high position
than for you to be embarrassed
in front of royal officials.
Be sure you are right
8before you sue someone,
or you might lose your case
and be embarrassed.
9When you and someone else
can't get along,
don't gossip about it.
10Others will find out,
and your reputation
will then be ruined.
11The right word
at the right time
is like precious gold
set in silver.
12Listening to good advice
is worth much more
than jewelry made of gold.
13A messenger you can trust
is just as refreshing
as cool water in summer.
14Broken promises
are worse than rain clouds
that don't bring rain.
15Patience and gentle talk
can convince a ruler
and overcome any problem.
16Eating too much honey
can make you sick.
17Don't visit friends too often,
or they will get tired of it
and start hating you.
18Telling lies about friends
is like attacking them
with clubs and swords
and sharp arrows.
19A friend you can't trust
in times of trouble
is like having a toothache
or a sore foot.
20Singing to someone
in deep sorrow
is like pouring vinegar
in an open cut.
21 If your enemies are hungry,
give them something to eat.
And if they are thirsty,
give them something
to drink.
22This will be the same
as piling burning coals
on their heads.
And the Lord
will reward you.
23As surely as rain blows in
from the north,
anger is caused
by cruel words.
24It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
25Good news from far away
refreshes like cold water
when you are thirsty.
26When a good person gives in
to the wicked,
it's like dumping garbage
in a stream of clear water.
27Don't eat too much honey
or always want praise.
28Losing self-control
leaves you as helpless
as a city without a wall.
translation_text:
Solomon siilima banɛ paas
1Solomon siilima sieba nwa', ka Hezekia onɛ an Juda na'ab la kpɛɛmnam da la'asi li sɔbi digil:
2Wina'am nyɛt na'asi nɛ on su'a yɛla la zug;
na'anam mɛ nyɛt na'asi nɛ ban vɛɛnsidi baŋid pian'ad gbin la zug.
3Nwɛnɛ agɔla lal ka teŋ zulim si'em la,
ala ka fʋ kʋ baŋ linɛ bɛ na'anam pʋtɛnda nii.
4Nyɛligim anzurifa yis dian'ad linɛ bɛɛ ani la,
ka onɛ tʋm nɛ anzurifa la nɔki li maal la'asʋŋ.
5Yisim nimbɛ'ɛdnam la na'ab san'an,
ka o na'am la na ba'a zi'en nɛ pʋpielim.
6 Da dʋ'ʋsi fʋ mɛŋ na'ab tuonnɛ,
mɛ da dɛŋi gaŋ kpɛɛmnam zin'isiga;
7li an sʋm nɛ on na yɛl ye, “Dʋm kpɛla na zin'in,”
n gaad on na diisif nyan burikinnam la sʋʋgin.
Fʋ nini nyɛ si'el la
8da mɔɔd ye fʋ mɔri li tɔ'ɔtɔ keŋ kɔɔtʋ nii,
li nya'aŋ la fʋ kpi'a la ya'a ti diisif nyannɛ
fʋ na niŋ wala?
9Fʋn nɛ fʋ kpi'a ya'a mɔr nɔŋgbannwa'ar,
da viigi fʋ kpi'a la gbin ka kɛ ka li yi yiŋa.
10Ya'a ka' ala nidib na wʋmi li
ka yʋ'ʋbɛ'ɛd kanɛ bɛɛ fʋ san'an la kʋ yi na'anaa.
11Pian'ad linɛ mɔr gbin la,
nwɛnɛ sanlima na gɛndig nɛ anzurifa nɛ.
12Ya'am sɔb sa'alʋg nwɛnɛ sanlim tʋblɛm
bɛɛ sanlimsʋŋ baŋi tis onɛ kɛlisid nɛ.
13Bisʋŋ titʋmis ma'ad banɛ tʋm o la sʋʋnr
nwɛnɛ zʋʋd bunib saŋa ku'oma'asig nɛ;
o bʋgʋnnɛ o zugdaannam sʋʋnr.
14Onɛ dʋ'ʋsid o mɛŋ ye o na tis sɔ' piini ka pʋ tis o
nwɛnɛ saa na kʋʋ fuk ka pʋ nii.
15Suguru sɔb bɛlisidi tuongat,
ka onɛ kʋkɔri bʋgʋs nyaŋid yɛl.
16Fʋ ya'a nyɛ siind fʋn dim zemis;
fʋ ya'a dii galis fʋ na tiin li bas.
17Da kennɛ fʋ kpi'a yiri pɛndigida,
ka o yaama na yiif ka o kisigif.
18Onɛ di ziri kasɛti tis o kpi'a
li nwɛnɛ balaar bɛɛ zaba sʋ'ʋg
bɛɛ piim yabid ka o pu'alim o.
19Yɛla ya'a paaf ka fʋ bɔɔd sʋŋir onɛ ka' sida sɔb san'an,
li nwɛnɛ fʋ nyina na pun'oe
ka fʋ ye fʋ ɔnb si'el bɛɛ fʋ keŋ nɛ nɔbir kanɛ pɔn'ɔlim nɛ.
20Onɛ yʋ'ʋmmi tisid sʋnsa'aŋ sɔb
nwɛnɛ ban na kpa'ae bʋmmi'isʋgʋ gɛndig nɛ zɛɛm,
bɛɛ sɔ' na yɛɛg o fuug waad daar.
21 Fʋ dataa kɔ'ɔm ya'a zabid, fʋn tisim o diib ka o di,
ka ku'onuud ya'a mɔr o, fʋn tisim o ku'om ka o nu.
22Fʋ ya'a niŋ ala, li nwɛnɛ fʋn na vaae bugumsaana linɛ diti pa'al o sɔb zugin,
Zugsɔb la mɛ na yɔɔ fʋ li yɛla.
23Sisi'em mɔr saa kenna si'em la,
ala mɛn ka kikɛung mɔr sʋnpɛɛnni kenna.
24Samannin bɛllim sɔn'oe
fʋn na la'as dɔɔgin nɛ pu'a kanɛ bɔɔd zaba.
25Fʋ ya'a wʋm labasʋŋ ka li yi lalli na,
li nwɛnɛ ku'onuudi na wʋmif ka fʋ nyɛ ku'oma'asig.
26Pʋpiel ya'a ti siak nimbɛ'og sa'alʋg,
li nwɛnɛ bulig ku'om na gɛndig nɛ yabid.
27Li ka' sʋ'ʋm nɛ fʋn na di siindi galisɛ,
ka mɛ ka' sʋ'ʋm nɛ fʋ na ieed yʋ'ʋri galisɛ.
28Ninkanɛ pʋ gban'ad o mɛŋ
nwɛnɛ tempʋʋg kanɛ pʋ mɔr zaŋguoma.

english_text:
Don't Be a Fool
1Expecting snow in summer
and rain in the dry season
makes more sense
than honoring a fool.
2A curse you don't deserve
will take wings and fly away
like a sparrow or a swallow.
3Horses and donkeys
must be beaten and bridled—
and so must fools.
4Don't make a fool of yourself
by answering a fool.
5But if you answer any fools,
show how foolish they are,
so they won't feel smart.
6Sending a message by a fool
is like chopping off your foot
just to spite yourself.
7A fool with words of wisdom
is like an athlete
with legs that can't move.
8Are you going to honor a fool?
Why not shoot a slingshot
with the rock tied tight?
9A thornbush waved around
in the hand of a drunkard
is no worse than a proverb
in the mouth of a fool.
10It's no smarter to shoot arrows
at every passerby
than it is to hire a bunch
of worthless nobodies.
11 Dogs return to eat their vomit,
just as fools repeat
their foolishness.
12There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who says,
“I'm really smart!”
13Don't be lazy and keep saying,
“There's a lion outside!”
14A door turns on its hinges,
but a lazy person
just turns over in bed.
15Some of us are so lazy
that we won't lift a hand
to feed ourselves.
16A lazy person says,
“I am smarter
than everyone else.”
17It's better to take hold
of a mad dog by the ears
than to take part
in someone else's argument.
18It's no crazier to shoot
sharp and flaming arrows
19than to cheat someone and say,
“I was only fooling!”
20Where there is no fuel
a fire goes out;
where there is no gossip
arguments come to an end.
21Troublemakers start trouble,
just as sparks and fuel
start a fire.
22There is nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
23Hiding hateful thoughts
behind smooth talk
is like coating a clay pot
with a cheap glaze.
24The pleasant talk
of an enemy
hides more evil plans
25than can be counted—
so don't believe a word!
26Everyone will see through
those evil plans.
27 If you dig a pit,
you will fall in;
if you start a stone rolling,
it will roll back on you.
28Watch out for anyone
who tells lies and flatters—
they are out to get you.
translation_text:
1Nwɛnɛ saa pʋ nar ye li niid bunib saŋa
bɛɛ sakuga lit dɔnwalig saŋa si'em la,
ala ka zɔlʋg pʋ nar nɛ na'asii.
2Nɔpɔɔr linɛ ka' gbin la
na bus kpʋkpama iank wʋʋ lʋʋr bɛɛ lilaaliŋ.
3Wief din anɛ sisanbig, bʋŋ din anɛ ba li'e o,
ka zɔlʋg din mɛ an bʋ'ʋd!
4Zɔlʋg ya'a bu'osif zɔlim bu'osʋg,
fʋn da gandig o zɔlim gandigirɛ,
ya'a ka' alaa, fʋn nɛ on na nwɛn taaba.
5Lɛbisim zɔlʋg wʋʋ on bu'os si'em la
ya'a ka' ala o na tɛn'ɛs ye o mɔri ya'am.
6Fʋ ya'a tʋm zɔlʋg
li nwɛnɛ fʋn na ki'e fʋ nɔbir nɛ lieŋe bas, bɛɛ nu yabid.
7Nwɛnɛ pɔn'ɔr nɔbiri zaanlim si'em la,
ala ka zɔlʋg siiliŋ mɛ aɛn.
8Fʋ ya'a na'as zɔlʋg,
li nwɛnɛ fʋn na niŋ kugir luobigini vɛnlig.
9Zɔlʋg ya'a siilim siiliŋ,
li nwɛnɛ danuudi na yɛl ye o yis gun'a o nu'ugin nɛ.
10Onɛ buol zɔlʋg bɛɛ ningɔɔndir ye o kena tʋm baadi tʋʋma
nwɛnɛ onɛ tɔɔnd piema yɔri-yɔri pu'alim nidib.
11Baa tiind ka lɛbidi dit si'em la,
ala ka zɔlʋg mɛ tʋmm o zɔlim tʋʋma takid.
12Fʋ nyɛ ninkanɛ tɛn'ɛs ye on mɔr ya'am hali laa?
Zɔlʋg sɔn'oe ninkan la.
13Gbanya'a pʋ bɔɔd tʋʋma ka ma'aa ye,
“Gbigim bɛ suorin,
gbigim bɛɛ ani ka li mɔr dabiem hali!”
14Nwɛnɛ kʋlʋŋi yuulimi li tabidisin si'em la,
ala ka gbanya'a digi liebid ka dɔɔn o gadʋg zug.
15Gbanya'a na nɔk o nu'ugʋ tʋm laan;
amaa ka ʋkim niŋ nɔɔrin la an yɛl!
16Gbanya'a tɛn'ɛs ye on mɔr ya'am
gaad nidiba ayɔpɔi banɛ na tun'e gandig bu'osa nɛ ya'am la.
17Onɛ zɔti kpɛn'ɛd yɛlbanɛ pʋ paae o la
nwɛnɛ ninkanɛ sia'al baa suorin ka gban'e o tʋba.
18-19Ninkanɛ bɛlis o kpi'a faaɛn o
ka yɛl ye, “Mam maannɛ galima,”
nwɛnɛ gɛɛŋ kanɛ tɔɔnd piema yɔri-yɔri mɔɔd ye o pu'alim nidib.
20Daad ya'a kae, bugum na kpiis;
bayɛʋg mɛ ya'a kae, zaba naae ya.
21Nwɛnɛ bugumsaana kɛt ka bugum la'aŋid si'em,
ka daad mɛ kɛt ka bugum dit si'em la,
ala ka nɔŋgbannwa'ar dim mɛ kɛt ka zaba nɔbigid.
22Bayɛʋg sɔb pian'ad malis nɛ nwɛnɛ sa'anwɛdir nɛ;
li sigid nɛ bɔlimm-bɔlimm paad pʋʋgin sa.
23Biriku'an sɔb pian'ad nwɛnɛ sɔ' na ya'ab yʋʋr,
ka nyɛlig kɔlibire bʋligi li ka li vɛnl.
24Nimbɛ'og pian'ad anɛ linɛ malis,
amaa ka bugum zɔɔnd pʋʋgin.
25La'an nɛ o pian'adi malis la, da niŋ o yadda,
ka o pʋʋg pɛ'ɛli nɛ nɛnnim;
ka yɛlkisa ayɔpɔi bɛɛ o sʋʋnrin.
26On an nimbɛ'og la o na tun'e pian' nɛ kʋkɔmalisiŋi lusi li;
amaa o bugusim la na nie nidib sʋʋgin.
27Nid ya'a tu bʋmbɔk, o mɛŋ na lii anina;
ninkanɛ mɛ bilig kugir, li na lɛbi diinl o.
28Ziri sɔb kis nimbanɛ ka o ma'adi tisidi ba la
ka onɛ pan'asidi ba mɛ mɔɔdi ba san'auŋ.

english_text:
Don't Brag about Tomorrow
1 Don't brag about tomorrow!
Each day brings
its own surprises.
2Don't brag about yourself—
let others praise you.
3Stones and sand are heavy,
but trouble caused by a fool
is a much heavier load.
4An angry person is dangerous,
but a jealous person
is even worse.
5A truly good friend
will openly correct you.
6You can trust a friend
who corrects you,
but kisses from an enemy
are nothing but lies.
7If you have had enough to eat,
honey doesn't taste good,
but if you are really hungry,
you will eat anything.
8When you are far from home,
you feel like a bird
without a nest.
9The sweet smell of incense
can make you feel good,
but true friendship
is better still.
10Don't desert an old friend
of your family
or visit your relatives
when you are in trouble.
A friend nearby is better
than relatives far away.
11My child, show good sense!
Then I will be happy
and able to answer anyone
who criticizes me.
12Be cautious and hide
when you see danger—
don't be stupid and walk
right into trouble.
13You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
14A loud greeting
early in the morning
is the same as a curse.
15The steady dripping of rain
and the nagging of a wife
are one and the same.
16It's easier to catch the wind
or hold olive oil in your hand
than to stop a nagging wife.
17Just as iron sharpens iron,
friends sharpen the minds
of each other.
18Take care of a tree,
and you will eat its fruit;
look after your master,
and you will be praised.
19You see your face in a mirror
and your thoughts
in the minds of others.
20Death and the grave
are never satisfied,
and neither are humans.
21Gold and silver are tested
in a red-hot furnace,
but we are tested by praise.
22No matter how hard
you beat a fool,
you can't pound out
the foolishness.
23You should take good care
of your sheep and goats,
24because wealth and honor
don't last forever.
25After the hay is cut
and the new growth appears
and the harvest is over,
26you can sell lambs and goats
to buy clothes and land.
27From the milk of the goats,
you can make enough cheese
to feed your family
and all your servants.
translation_text:
1 Da dʋ'ʋsidi fʋ mɛŋ bɛog yɛllɛ,
ka fʋ zi' bɛogʋ saa na an si'em.
2Kɛl ka sɔ' dʋ'ʋsif
ka da dʋ'ʋsidi fʋ mɛŋa.
3Kugir tɛbis ka titan mɛ an zitɛbisʋg,
amaa zɔlʋg daamʋg gat bama ayi' la wʋsa.
4Sʋnpɛɛn nɛ ɛndʋg anɛ bɛ'ɛd ka na nyaŋi zi san'auŋ na,
amaa anɔ'ɔn na nyaŋi zi'en fufum sɔb tuonnɛ?
5Fʋ ya'a pian' nyain sa'al nid
li sɔn'oe fʋn na su'a nɔŋ o.
6Fʋ zua ya'a pu'alimif,
li sɔn'oe fʋ dataa na nɔk o nu'ugʋ kuaki fʋ niŋgɔɔnr.
7Onɛ dii tig la pʋ bɔɔd siindɛ,
amaa nid kɔ'ɔm ya'a zabid, hali bʋntɔɔg gba malis o nɔɔrin.
8Nid ya'a yidig o yisuor
li nwɛnɛ niiŋe na yidig o tɛog nɛ.
9Tudaar nɛ bʋnnyubisa ma'ad sʋʋnr,
ka sɔ' sumbʋgʋsʋm yit nɛ on nyɛɛ o zua sa'alʋg si'em.
10Da tami fʋ zuanam nɛ fʋ ba' zuanam yɛlaa
mɛ da kennɛ fʋ ba'abiisin saŋa kanɛ ka yɛla paaf ma'anɛ;
fʋ ya'a mɔr kpi'a onɛ an sʋm sɔn'oe fʋn na mɔr ba'abiig kanɛ bɛ lalli sa.
11M biiga, mɔr ya'am, ka kɛ ka m sʋnf malis;
ala ka sɔ' ya'a nɛ'ɛsim, m mi' mam na lɛbis o si'em.
12Pʋtɛn'ɛr sɔb dɛŋidnɛ nyɛt yɛltɔɔg ka luakid,
amaa zɔlʋg on na gaad tuonnɛ nyɛ namisʋg.
13Nɔkim onɛ kaanb ye o na yɔ saan sam la fuug;
o ya'a niŋ ala tis pu'agɔɔndir fʋn mɔr fuug la ka li zi'e sam la zi'esim!
14Fʋ ya'a tansi pʋ'ʋsi fʋ zua bɛkɛung asuba,
o na nɔki li ka li nwɛnɛ nɔpɔɔr ka fʋ tis o nɛ.
15Pu'a kanɛ nɔŋ zaba
nwɛnɛ saa na niid ka ku'om yun ka pʋ gu'oda.
16Fʋ ya'a ye fʋ gu' o, li nwɛnɛ fʋn na mɔɔd ye fʋ gu' sisi'em
bɛɛ fʋn na mak ye fʋ gban'e kpaam nu'ugin nɛ.
17Kunti saasid kʋnt si'em la,
ala ka nidib mɛ zamisidi yiti ba taaba san'an.
18Onɛ sɛ tiig onɛ na dii li nyɔɔd,
onɛ tʋmmi tisid o zugdaan na mɔr na'asi.
19Ninsaali gɔsid ku'omin ka nyɛt o nindaa si'em la,
ala mɛn ka sɔ' wʋsa mɛŋ sʋnf niedi pa'an on an sɔ'.
20Kum nɛ yaʋgʋ vɔn ka pʋ tigid si'em la,
ala ka ninsaal nini mɛ gɔsid ka pʋ tigida.
21Bugum ka ba mɔri nyɛligid anzurifa nɛ sanlima
siligid ka li yit nyain,
amaa ba makid ninsaal nɛ on nyɛt na'asi si'em.
22Fʋ ya'a bɔɔd fʋn tuom zɔlʋg tuodirin,
bɛɛ nɛɛm o wʋʋ zɔ'ɔm nɛ,
fʋ kʋ nyaŋi yis zɔlimis linɛ bɛɛ o pʋʋgin laa.
23Baŋimi fʋ kɔnbid la bɛllim an si'em,
ka guri fʋ niigi la sʋ'ʋŋa;
24ka kpan'am pʋ bɛ saŋa wʋsa,
bɛɛ na'am zi'e sʋ'ʋŋa zʋmaana wʋsa nii.
25Fʋ ya'a kie yaama ka mɔpaalig yina,
ka la'as mɔbanɛ bɛ kʋkʋna ni na,
26pɛ'ɛs la kɔnbid na tisif gum ka fʋ ʋg fuud
ka kuos bʋʋs la da' pɔɔg.
27Fʋ na mɔr bʋʋs bin'isim bɛdegʋ
ka fʋn nɛ fʋ yidim nuud
ka ugusi fʋ sankpan'asnam banɛ an bipumis la.

english_text:
The Law of God Makes Sense
1Wicked people run away
when no one chases them,
but those who live right
are as brave as lions.
2In time of civil war
there are many leaders,
but a sensible leader
restores law and order.
3When someone poor takes over
and mistreats the poor,
it's like a heavy rain
destroying the crops.
4Lawbreakers praise criminals,
but law-abiding citizens
always oppose them.
5Criminals don't know
what justice means,
but all who respect the Lord
understand it completely.
6It's better to be poor
and live right,
than to be rich
and dishonest.
7It makes good sense
to obey the Law of God,
but you disgrace your parents
if you make friends
with worthless nobodies.
8If you make money by charging
high interest rates,
you will lose it all to someone
who cares for the poor.
9God cannot stand the prayers
of anyone who disobeys
his Law.
10By leading good people to sin,
you dig a pit for yourself,
but all who live right
will have a bright future.
11The rich think highly
of themselves,
but anyone poor and sensible
sees right through them.
12When an honest person wins,
it's time to celebrate;
when crooks are in control,
it's best to hide.
13If you don't confess your sins,
you will be a failure.
But God will be merciful
if you confess your sins
and give them up.
14The Lord blesses everyone
who is afraid to do evil,
but if you are cruel,
you will end up in trouble.
15A ruler who mistreats the poor
is like a roaring lion
or a bear hunting for food.
16A heartless leader is a fool,
but anyone who refuses
to get rich by cheating others
will live a long time.
17Don't give help to murderers!
Make them stay on the run
for as long as they live.
18Honesty will keep you safe,
but everyone who is crooked
will suddenly fall.
19Work hard, and you will have
a lot of food;
waste time, and you will have
a lot of trouble.
20God blesses his loyal people,
but punishes all who want
to get rich quick.
21It isn't right to be unfair,
but some people can be bribed
with only a piece of bread.
22Don't be selfish
and eager to get rich—
you will end up worse off
than you can imagine.
23Honest correction
is appreciated
more than flattery.
24If you cheat your parents
and don't think it's wrong,
you are a common thief.
25Selfish people cause trouble,
but you will live a full life
if you trust the Lord.
26Only fools would trust
what they alone think,
but if you live by wisdom,
you will do all right.
27Giving to the poor
will keep you from poverty,
but if you close your eyes
to their needs,
everyone will curse you.
28When crooks are in control,
everyone tries to hide,
but when they lose power,
good people are everywhere.
translation_text:
1Onɛ an bugus la zɔti ka sɔ' pʋ kad oo,
amaa pʋpielim sɔb la na mɔr sʋnkpi'euŋ wʋʋ gbigim nɛ.
2Zaba ya'a ti kɔ' teŋin, banɛ sʋ'oe teŋ la anɛ bɛdegʋ,
amaa ninkanɛ mɔr ya'am nɛ baŋir la
na kɛ ka si'el wʋsa ken sʋ'ʋŋa.
3Nɔŋ daan onɛ mugusid o taaba la
nwɛnɛ saa na niidi da'ad nɛ paŋi san'amid zʋʋd.
4Banɛ pʋ dɔl wada la faasid bugusnam,
amaa banɛ dɔl wada la pʋ siakidi li'ennɛ baa.
5Nimbɛ'ɛdnam pʋ gban'ad sida gbinnɛ,
amaa banɛ zɔt Zugsɔb la gban'adi li gbin sʋ'ʋŋa.
6Fʋ ya'a an nɔŋdaan ka an burikin
sɔn'oe fʋn na mɔr kpan'am ka fʋ bɛllim pʋ dɔl suorɛ.
7Onɛ dɔl wada la anɛ bikanɛ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr,
amaa onɛ dɔl dindiisnam la diisid o ba' nyan.
8Onɛ di'esid nyɔɔd bɛdegʋ maan kpan'am digin la,
o sɔb la'asidnɛ diginɛ tisid onɛ na zɔt nɔŋ dim nimbaanlig.
9Onɛ li' o tʋba ka pʋ dɔl wada la,
hali o winsɔsʋg anɛ linɛ ka Zugsɔb la kis.
10Onɛ nɔk pʋpieli dɔlisid suobɛ'ɛd,
o sɔb na lii o mɛŋ baŋin;
amaa banɛ pʋ mɔr gba'ar la na di faar linɛ an sʋ'ʋŋa.
11Bʋmmɔr na tɛn'ɛs ye o mɔri ya'am,
amaa nɔŋdaan onɛ an ya'am sɔb la mi' o gbin.
12Pʋpiel ya'a ti paam paŋ, nidib maannɛ sumalisim;
amaa nimbɛ'og ya'a sʋ'oe teŋ, nidib zɔti su'ad.
13Onɛ su'ad o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kʋ keŋ tuonnɛ,
amaa onɛ viig o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi tu'as
ka zan'asi li na nyɛ nimbaanlzɔɔr.
14Albareka bɛ nɛ onɛ zɔt Zugsɔb la;
amaa onɛ digilim o sʋnf la na kpɛn' yɛla ni.
15Ninkanɛ sʋ'oe nidib ka an bugus la
nwɛnɛ gbigimi na nwa'am bɛɛ mɔɔgin bʋnyua.
16Onɛ sʋ'oe teŋ ka pʋ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛsʋma la mugusidi nidib,
amaa onɛ kis zam la nyɔvʋr na wa'am.
17Da mɔɔd ye fʋ sʋŋ ninkanɛ kʋ nida;
kɛl ka o kennɛ o kɔn'ɔkɔn' ti paae o kum daar.
18Onɛ ken ka pʋ mɔr gba'ar la na bɛ nɛ laafi,
amaa onɛ bɛllim pʋ dɔl suor la na nyɛ kʋʋsbɛ'ɛd.
19Onɛ kuod na paam diib bɛdegʋ,
amaa onɛ yaannɛ gin zaalim-zaalim nɔŋ na kʋʋ o.
20Ninkanɛ an sida sɔb na nyɛ bareka,
amaa onɛ mɔɔd ye o nyɛ kpan'am tɔ'ɔtɔ
kʋ keŋ zaalim ka da di'e namisʋgɔ.
21Fʋ ya'a maan baregaŋ li ka' sʋm;
la'an nɛ wala diib bi'ela yɛla ma'aa zug sɔ' na maal bɛ'ɛd.
22Ninkanɛ tɛn'ɛsid o mɛŋ yɛla ma'aa
ka mɔɔd on na niŋ si'em nyɛ kpan'am,
on sɔb zi' ye nɔŋ bɛ suori gur oo.
23Fʋ ya'a sa'al sɔ', li nya'aŋ fʋ na nyɛɛ li na'asi
gaad onɛ pian'ad nɛ nɔmalisim ka sida kae.
24Ninkanɛ zuu o ba' nɛ o ma
ka yɛl ye, “Li ka' bɛ'ɛdɛ”;
on nɛ na'ayiig anɛ yinne.
25Dindiis anɛ onɛ ieed yɛla,
amaa onɛ tis Zugsɔb la sida na ken tuon.
26Onɛ ti'e o mɛŋ paŋ la anɛ zɔlʋg,
amaa onɛ mɔr ya'am ken la, daamʋg kʋ paae oo.
27Onɛ tisid tadimnam piini, si'el kʋ pɔ'ɔg o;
amaa onɛ fɛndig o nindaa bidi ba la, ba na pɔɔ o nɔɔr.
28Nimbɛ'og ya'a ti sʋ'ʋg teŋ, nidib zɔtnɛ su'ad;
amaa bugusnam la ya'a ti paam san'auŋ
pʋpielnam la kpɛn kennɛ tuon.

english_text:
Use Good Sense
1If you keep being stubborn
after many warnings,
you will suddenly discover
you have gone too far.
2When justice rules a nation,
everyone is glad;
when injustice rules,
everyone groans.
3If you love wisdom
your parents will be glad,
but chasing after bad women
will cost you everything.
4An honest ruler
makes the nation strong;
a ruler who takes bribes
will bring it to ruin.
5Flattery is nothing less
than setting a trap.
6Your sins will catch you,
but everyone who lives right
will sing and celebrate.
7The wicked don't care
about the rights of the poor,
but good people do.
8Sneering at others is a spark
that sets a city on fire;
using good sense can put out
the flames of anger.
9Be wise and don't sue a fool.
You won't get satisfaction,
because all the fool will do
is sneer and shout.
10A murderer hates everyone
who is honest
and lives right.
11Don't be a fool
and quickly lose your temper—
be sensible and patient.
12A ruler who listens to lies
will have corrupt officials.
13The poor and all who abuse them
must each depend on God
for light.
14Kings who are fair to the poor
will rule a long time.
15Correct your children,
and they will be wise;
children out of control
disgrace their mothers.
16Crime increases
when crooks are in power,
but law-abiding citizens
will see them fall.
17If you correct your children,
they will bring you peace
and happiness.
18Without guidance from God
law and order disappear,
but God blesses everyone
who obeys his Law.
19 Even when servants are smart,
it takes more than words
to make them obey.
20There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who speaks
without thinking.
21Slaves that you treat kindly
from their childhood
will cause you sorrow.
22A person with a quick temper
stirs up arguments
and commits a lot of sins.
23Too much pride brings disgrace;
humility leads to honor.
24If you take part in a crime
you are your worst enemy,
because even under oath
you can't tell the truth.
25Don't fall into the trap
of being a coward—
trust the Lord,
and you will be safe.
26Many try to make friends
with a ruler,
but justice comes
from the Lord.
27Good people and criminals
can't stand each other.
translation_text:
1Ninkanɛ zugʋ kpi'em hali ka ba sa'ali gʋ'ʋŋ la;
o sɔb na gbirigi paam san'auŋ ka li maalʋg kae.
2Pʋpiel ya'a ken tuon, li malis nɛ nidib sʋnya;
nimbɛ'og ya'a di na'am, nidib la na unsidi nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ.
3Ninkanɛ mɔr ya'am la ma'ad o ba' sʋʋnr,
amaa onɛ dɔl pu'agɔɔnda la na dii o arezaki naae.
4Na'akanɛ tu'asid sida la, o sʋ'ʋlim la zi'enɛ kiŋ-kiŋ,
amaa onɛ an fufum sɔb ka di'esid ligidi la na san'am teŋ la.
5Onɛ wʋsa faasid o kpi'a ka sida kae la
bɛnd o nɛ baans linɛ na gban'e o.
6Nimbɛ'og tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi gban'ad o,
amaa onɛ an pʋpiel la na yʋ'ʋm ka mɔr sumalisim.
7Onɛ an pʋpiel tisid nɔŋ dim bʋʋd,
amaa bugusim sɔb on ba'a ka' nɛ ba.
8Ninla'asnam la tugunnɛ teŋ nidib,
amaa ya'am dim la ma'adnɛ nidib sʋnya.
9Ya'am sɔb ya'a mɔr zɔlʋgʋ keŋ kɔɔtʋ ni,
zɔlʋg la na pian'ad pian'ayɛɛd ka maan tʋkpiidʋg ka sumbʋgʋsʋm kae.
10Ninkʋʋdib kis onɛ an sida sɔb
ka mɔɔd ye ba kʋ burikinnam.
11Zɔlʋg pa'annɛ o sʋnpɛɛn nyain,
amaa ya'am sɔb gban'ad o mɛŋ.
12Na'ab ya'a kɛlisid ziri,
o na'ayikpɛm wʋsa mɛ na an nimbɛ'ɛdnam.
13Bʋn yinne bɛ ka nɔŋdaan nɛ onɛ mugusid o taab an yinne;
Zugsɔb la niedi ba wʋsa nini.
14Na'ab ya'a kad nɔŋdaan saria nɛ sida,
o na'am la na zi'en kiŋ-kiŋ.
15Sisanbig nɛ sa'alʋgʋ pa'an biig ka tisid o ya'am,
fʋ ya'a bas o ka o tʋm o bɔɔdim o na diis o ma nyan.
16Bugusnam ya'a ken tuon, tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd mɛ nɔbigidnɛ,
amaa pʋpielnam na nyɛɛ ba liig.
17Sa'alimi fʋ biig, ka o na kɛ ka fʋ nyɛt sumbʋgʋsʋm;
ka lɛn kɛ ka fʋ ya'amlɛog bɛɛ o san'an.
18Zin'ikanɛ ka Wina'am nied si'elnamɛ pa'an na
nidib la bɛllim an yɔri-yɔri;
amaa sumalisim bɛ nɛ onɛ dɔlisid wada la.
19Sankpan'as pʋ sʋm ka fʋ san'an o nɛ nɔɔr pian'ad ma'anɛ,
daasi'erɛ o na gban'e li gbin, ka lɛɛ kʋ tʋm wʋʋ lin nar si'em.
20Fʋ nyɛ ninkanɛ pian'ad ka pʋ gu'usid laa?
Zɔlʋg mɔr ti'iri sɔn'oe ninkan la.
21Fʋ ya'a pɔn'ɔli fʋ sankpan'as o biilimin,
li naarin la o na san'ami fʋ sʋʋnr.
22Ninkanɛ an sʋnpɛɛn sɔb la ziid nɔŋgbannwa'ar na,
sʋnpɛɛn galisʋg sɔb kpɛn'ɛdi tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdin.
23Tita'alim lugid ninsaal,
amaa onɛ sied o mɛŋ ka an baanlimm la nyɛt na'asi.
24Ninkanɛ sʋŋid na'ayiig la anɛ o mɛŋ dataa;
ba na kɛ ka o pɔ amaa ka kʋ tun'e dii li sida kasɛta.
25Fʋ ya'a zɔt ninsaal, fʋ bɛnd nɛ fʋ mɛŋ baans,
amaa onɛ tis Zugsɔb la sida na bɛ ka daamʋg kae.
26Nidib bɛdegʋ bɔɔd ye na'ab kɛlisi ba pian'ad,
amaa li anɛ Zugsɔb la tisid ninsaal sida.
27Pʋpiel kis onɛ an zam sɔb;
Ka bugusim sɔb mɛ kis burikin, o bɛllim an sʋ'ʋŋa la zug.

english_text:
The Sayings of Agur
1These are the sayings
and the message
of Agur son of Jakeh.
Someone cries out to God,
“I am completely worn out!
How can I last?
2I am far too stupid
to be considered human.
3I never was wise,
and I don't understand
what God is like.”
4 Has anyone gone up to heaven
and come back down?
Has anyone grabbed hold
of the wind?
Has anyone wrapped up the sea
or marked out boundaries
for the earth?
If you know of any
who have done such things,
then tell me their names
and their children's names.
5Everything God says is true—
and it's a shield for all
who come to him for safety.
6Don't change what God has said!
He will correct you and show
that you are a liar.
7There are two things, Lord,
I want you to do for me
before I die:
8Make me absolutely honest
and don't let me be too poor
or too rich.
Give me just what I need.
9If I have too much to eat,
I might forget about you;
if I don't have enough,
I might steal
and disgrace your name.
10Don't tell a slave owner
something bad about one
of the slaves.
That slave will curse you,
and you will be in trouble.
11Some people curse their father
and even their mother;
12others think they are perfect,
but they are stained by sin.
13Some people are stuck-up
and act like snobs;
14others are so greedy
that they gobble up
the poor and homeless.
15Greed has twins,
each named “Give me!”
There are three or four things
that are never satisfied:
16The world of the dead
and a childless wife,
the thirsty earth
and a flaming fire.
17Don't make fun of your father
or disobey your mother—
crows will peck out your eyes,
and buzzards will eat
the rest of you.
18There are three or four things
I cannot understand:
19 How eagles fly so high
or snakes crawl on rocks,
how ships sail the ocean
or people fall in love.
20An unfaithful wife says,
“Sleeping with another man
is as natural as eating.”
21There are three or four things
that make the earth tremble
and are unbearable:
22A slave who becomes king,
a fool who eats too much,
23a hateful woman
who finds a husband,
and a slave who takes the place
of the woman who owns her.
24On this earth four things
are small but very wise:
25Ants, who seem to be feeble,
but store up food
all summer long;
26badgers, who seem to be weak,
but live among the rocks;
27locusts, who have no king,
but march like an army;
28lizards, which can be caught
in your hand,
but sneak into palaces.
29Three or four creatures
really strut around:
30Those fearless lions
who rule the jungle,
31those proud roosters,
those mountain goats,
and those rulers
who have no enemies.
32If you are foolishly bragging
or planning something evil,
then stop it now!
33If you churn milk
you get butter;
if you pound on your nose,
you get blood—
and if you stay angry,
you get in trouble.
translation_text:
Agur siilima
1Jake biig Agur nimmua pian'akanɛ ka o pian' tis Itiel la nwa'. O pian'anɛ tis Itiel nɛ Ukal ye,
“Wina'am, m gɛnnɛ;
Wina'am, m gɛnnɛ ka ligid.
2Man anɛ zi'ilim sɔb ninsaalib wʋsa sʋʋgin;
M pʋ mɔr ya'am kanɛ ka ninsaalib mɔr laa.
3M pʋ zamis ya'am,
bɛɛ mɔr baŋir Onɛ an Kasi la yɛlaa.
4Anɔ'ɔnɛ dʋ arezana ni ka sig na?
Anɔ'ɔnɛ nam mi' gban'e pɛbisim nɛ o nu'ugɔ?
Anɔ'ɔnɛ nam mi' pɔnbil ku'om nɛ fuugɔ?
Anɔ'ɔnɛ digil teŋgbauŋ la bɛn wʋsa ɛɛnbirɛ?
O yʋ'ʋrɛ? Ka o biig la yʋ'ʋrɛ?
Fʋ ya'a mi' fʋn yɛlimim!
5Wina'am pian'ad wʋsa anɛ sida nyain;
o anɛ gbanti'edʋg banɛ ieed suak zin'ig o san'an la.
6Da paas si'el o pian'ad la zugɔ,
ya'a ka' ala o na tansif ka li pa'al ye fʋ anɛ ziri sɔb.
7Bʋnama ayi' ka m sɔsidif, O Zugsɔba;
tʋmmi li tisim man nan vʋe la.
8Kɛl ka faad nɛ dama'am lal nɛ m
ka da kɛ ka li bɛɛ m san'anɛ.
Mɛ da kɛ ka m an nɔŋdaan tapigif bɛɛ m mɔri galisɛ,
amaa tisimim linɛ na sia'alim dabisir wʋsa.
9Ya'a ka' ala m na mɔr bɛdegʋ ka tami fʋ yɛla
ka yɛl ye, ‘Zugsɔb la aan anɔ'ɔnɛ?’
Bɛɛ m an nɔŋdaan ka zu,
ka li san'ami m Wina'am la yʋ'ʋr.
10Da zɛrig tʋmtʋmi tis o zugdaana,
ka o na pɔ nɔɔri tisif, ka fʋ nyɛ li namisʋg.
11Ninsieba bɛɛ pɔɔd nɔya tisidi ba saamnam
ka pʋ kaanbid sʋ'ʋm tisidi ba manama.
12Nimban gɔsi ba mɛŋ ka ba anɛ kasi
ka zi' ye ba lɛɛ anɛ dian'ad dima.
13Ba anɛ nimpʋnannib
ka pʋ gɔsid nidibi nyɛta.
14Ba nyiidi nidib
ka ba yier mɔr linɛ nwɛnɛ zaba sʋ'ʋs nɛ.
Ka ba mugusid nɔŋ dim banɛ bɛ teŋin la
nɛ banɛ an fara dimi bɛ nidib sʋʋgin la.
15Adanyɔb mɔri bipumis ayi'
ka ba kaasidi yɛt ye, ‘Tisim! Tisim!’
Ka pʋ tigida.
Ala ka bʋnam atan' bɛɛ nan zi' tigɛ,
ka bʋnam anaasi nan zi' yɛl ye, ‘Li sia'al yaa!’
16Bama anɛ: yaʋg nɛ kʋndu'ar
nɛ teŋ kanɛ zi' tig ku'om.
Bugum mɛ nan zi' yɛl ye, ‘M dii sia'alɛ!’
17Ninkanɛ nɔk o ba' maal bʋnla'adir
ka nɛ'ɛsid o ma ka pʋ di'ed o nɔɔr la,
agaand na yi bɔn'ɔgin na nwɛ' ba gaad wʋʋ silʋg nɛ,
ka zʋʋnd dii ba.
18Bʋnama atan' bɛɛ an nyalima tisim,
anaasi ka m pʋ gban'e li gbinnɛ.
19Bama anɛ: silʋg suor saŋgbana ni,
waaf suor tampiing zug,
anrʋŋ tita'ar suor atɛukʋn,
nɛ dau nɛ pu'asadir nɔŋir suoya.
20Pu'a kanɛ maal o mɛŋ pu'agɔɔndir suoya an si'em nwa':
o ɛɛn dinɛ ka pie o nɔɔr.
Ka li pa'al ye o na san'am dau ka zɔɔ keŋ sʋ
ka ki'isi yɛl ye, ‘Mam pʋ maal si'ela.’
21Bʋnam atan' ka teŋgbauŋ la nyɛt ka kirid,
bʋnam anaasi ka o kʋ nyaŋi ba.
22Bama anɛ: Sankpan'asi na di na'am,
nɛ zɔlʋgʋ na di diibi tig,
23pu'a kanɛ ka nidib pʋ bɔɔd o la na kul sid,
nɛ pu'a-ɛliŋi na kad yipu'a ka lɛdig.
24Bʋnam anaasi bɛ teŋgbauŋ la zugʋ pɔɔd,
amaa ka ba paŋ lɛɛ galis nɛ.
Bama anɛ:
25salinsa'as banɛ ka ba paŋ pɔɔd
la'an nɛ wala ka ba su'adi ba diibi paad dɔnwalig;
26bʋnvʋbaanlʋg banɛ ka ba paŋ pɔɔd,
la'an nɛ wala ka ba maali ba gbɛɛnb zin'ig tampiins sian'asimin;
27na'azɔmnam pʋ mɔr na'aba,
la'an nɛ wala ba kennɛ salililili;
28fʋ na nyaŋi gban'e akɔn'ɔs nɛ nu'ug,
la'an nɛ wala ba bɛ na'ayin.
29Bʋnama atan' bɛ ka fʋ nanɛ ba ken,
bʋnama anaasi kennɛ ba ya'amin.
30Bama anɛ: gbigim onɛ kpi'emi gat bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa,
ka ken ka si'el pʋ vi'id o la;
31nɔraug kanɛ ken nɛ nyɛɛsim,
nɛ bʋraug nɛ na'ab kanɛ ka o soogianam gilig o.
32Fʋ ya'a an zɔlʋg ka dʋ'ʋsi fʋ mɛŋ,
bɛɛ fʋ gban'anɛ gban'abɛ'ɛd,
nɔkimi fʋ nu'usi pin' fʋ nɔɔr.
33Bɔzugɔ, nwɛnɛ bin'isgbisidim yisid bin'iskpaam,
ka nyɔnya nwɛ'ɛb yisid ziim si'em la,
ala mɛn fʋ ya'a kɛ ka sʋnpɛɛn duoe
li ziidnɛ zaba na.”

english_text:
What King Lemuel's Mother Taught Him
1These are the sayings
that King Lemuel of Massa
was taught by his mother.
2My son Lemuel, you were born
in answer to my prayers,
so listen carefully.
3Don't waste your life
chasing after women!
This has ruined many kings.
4Kings and leaders
should not get drunk
or even want to drink.
5Drinking makes you forget
your responsibilities,
and you mistreat the poor.
6Beer and wine are only
for the dying or for those
who have lost all hope.
7Let them drink and forget
how poor and miserable
they feel.
8But you must defend
those who are helpless
and have no hope.
9Be fair and give justice
to the poor and homeless.
In Praise of a Good Wife
10A truly good wife
is the most precious treasure
a man can find!
11Her husband depends on her,
and she never
lets him down.
12She is good to him
every day of her life,
13and with her own hands
she gladly makes clothes.
14She is like a sailing ship
that brings food
from across the sea.
15She gets up before daylight
to prepare food for her family
and for her servants.
16She knows how to buy land
and how to plant a vineyard,
17and she always works hard.
18She knows when to buy or sell,
and she stays busy
until late at night.
19She spins her own cloth,
20and she helps the poor
and the needy.
21Her family has warm clothing,
and so she doesn't worry
when it snows.
22She does her own sewing,
and everything she wears
is beautiful.
23Her husband is a well-known
and respected leader
in the city.
24She makes clothes to sell
to the shop owners.
25She is strong and graceful,
as well as cheerful
about the future.
26Her words are sensible,
and her advice
is thoughtful.
27She takes good care
of her family
and is never lazy.
28Her children praise her,
and with great pride
her husband says,
29“There are many good women,
but you are the best!”
30Charm can be deceiving,
and beauty fades away,
but a woman
who honors the Lord
deserves to be praised.
31Show her respect—
praise her in public
for what she has done.
translation_text:
Na'ab Lemuel ma sa'alʋg
1Na'ab Lemuel maa pa'al o pian'asieba nwa':
2“M biiga, m mɛŋ pʋʋgin biiga,
M nɔɔr kaanbʋg biiga,
3da mɔri fʋ paŋi san'amid nɛ pu'aba,
da mɔri fʋ daulim ken banɛ san'amid na'anam la san'anɛ.
4M biig Lemuel, li ka' na'anam tʋʋma la,
li ka' sʋm ye na'ab nuud daam,
bɛɛ banɛ sʋ'oe tɛɛns la bɔɔd dankpi'ema;
5ba ya'a nu, ba na tam wada la yɛl si'em la,
ka kad banɛ ka nidib mugusidi ba la saria ka mɔŋi ba bʋʋd.
6Nɔkim dankpi'ema tis banɛ bɔɔd kum la ka ba nu,
sʋnsa'aŋ dimi bɔɔd daam;
7kɛl ka ba nu ka tami ba nɔŋ la yɛla
ka mɛ da lɛn tiɛnri ba fara la yɛla ya'asɛ.
8Pian'am sʋŋ banɛ kʋ nyaŋi pian' ba mɛŋ yɛla la,
ka sʋŋ banɛ mɔr bʋʋd ka pʋ mɔr sʋŋir la.
9Pian'am ka kad saria ka li dɔl suor;
ka zabi sʋŋ nɔŋ nɛ fara dim.”
Pu'a kanɛ kik ka mi' o mɛŋ mɔrim
10Anɔ'ɔn kimm lɛɛ na nyaŋi paam pu'a kanɛ an pu'amɛŋa?
O gaad fʋn na mɔr sanlim.
11O sid ti'ir wʋsa bɛ nɛ o san'an
ka linɛ an bʋnsʋŋ wʋsa pʋ kɔ'ɔŋid o san'anɛ.
12O vʋm pʋʋgin wʋsa,
o maannɛ o sid sʋ'ʋŋa ka gbɛlʋŋ kae.
13O kpɛ'ɛŋid o mɛŋi gaansid gum sʋŋʋ
nwiid ka ʋgʋd piena.
14O nwɛnɛ anrʋŋ kanɛ ka ba mɔri kpiisid,
o ziidi diibi yit lalli sa kenna.
15O na dɛŋi duoe ka bɛog nam pʋ nie
maal diibi tis o yidim
ka pa'al o yir tʋmtʋm bipumis la sɔ' wʋsa nɛ o tʋʋma.
16O ɛɛnti gɔs nɛ paalʋ kanɛ an sʋm ka da' li:
on tʋm nyɛ si'el la ka o nɔki kuo pɔɔg.
17O anɛ onɛ tʋmm o tʋʋma nɛ nimmua;
o kpi'em o tʋʋma ni ka pʋ lɛbid nya'aŋa.
18O mi' ye o kpikpiŋ an sʋm ka li tisid o nyɔɔd;
o na tʋm ka yʋ'ʋŋ ti kena sɔb.
19Onɛ kaad o mɛŋ gum,
ka ʋgid o mɛŋ fuud.
20O sʋŋidi nɔŋ dim
ka mɛ pʋ mɔŋid fara dima.
21Waadi bɛ daasi'ɛr hali la, dabiem pʋ mɔr o, o yidim yɛlaa;
bɔzugɔ ba wʋsa mɔr waad fuud.
22O mɛŋi maan fubanɛ na yadig gadʋg;
ka sɔɔnd fuud banɛ pɔnri vɛnl.
23Ba na'asid o sid wʋrʋg sʋʋgin,
zin'ikanɛ ka o zin' nɛ teŋ la kpɛɛmnam la.
24O sɛɛnd fuudi kuosid,
ka banɛ kpiisid la kennɛ o san'an na da'ad sɛnbidis.
25O mɔr paŋ nɛ girima;
ka bɛog sa o saa na zin' ka dit ka maan sumalisim.
26O pian'adi nɛ ya'am
ka on pa'an si'el wʋsa an sida.
27O gɔsid o yir sʋ'ʋŋa
ka pʋ mɔr gbanya'am ka na kɔ'ɔŋ diibɔ.
28O biis na duoe na ka kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tis o;
ka o sid mɛ na faas o ka ye,
29“Pu'ab bɛdegʋ tʋm tʋʋm sʋma,
amaa fʋ gaadi ba wʋsa.”
30Fʋ ya'a bɔbi fʋ mɛŋ nɛ fusʋma, li bɛligidnɛ nidib
ka vɛnlim wʋsa mɛ na gaad;
amaa pu'a kanɛ na'asid Zugsɔb la nar ye ba zun'e o.
31Tisim o yɔɔd linɛ nar ye o di'e la,
ka kɛ ka o tʋʋma la tis o girima nidib la'asʋg zin'igin.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
Si'el wʋsa ka' gbinnɛ
1Labakaŋa yinɛ Pa'an onɛ an David biig ka da di na'am Jerusalem tempʋʋgin la na.
2Pa'an la yɛl ye,
“Li ka' gbinnɛ! Li ka' gbinnɛ
Asida si'el wʋsa ka' gbinnɛ!
3Ninsaal na nyɛ nyɔbɔ
yit tʋʋm kanɛ ka o tʋm dunia nwa' pʋʋginɛ?
4Zʋmaana kena ka gaad,
amaa dunia la on kpɛm bɛ nɛ saŋa wʋsa.
5Winnig tansid ka lɛm kpɛn'ɛd,
ka lɛbid on yi zin'isi'a la na tɔ'ɔtɔ.
6Pɛbisʋg la da'adnɛ ken ya-tuona
ka lɛbid ya-nya'aŋi giligid on yi zin'isi'a na.
7Ka kɔldaad wʋsa pʋbidi sigid Atɛukʋn,
amaa Atɛuk la pʋ pɛ'ɛnna.
Kɔldaad la yi zin'isi'a na la, ani ka ba na lɛb.
8Si'el wʋsa mɔri gɛɛnlis,
li tʋʋg ninsaal pian'ad bɛn;
sɔ' nini nan zi' gɔsi tigɛ,
bɛɛ sɔ' tʋbir wʋm tigɛ.
9Dinɛ pʋn kena la na lɛn kena,
ka dinɛ pʋn tʋm la na lɛn tʋm.
Si'el kae an bʋmpaal dunia kaŋa nii.
10Si'el kae ka sɔ' na nyaŋi yɛl ye
‘Gɔsima, nɛ'ɛŋa anɛ bʋmpaallɛ!’
Ayei, li da pʋm bɛ nɛ yʋʋm banɛ gaad la sa,
li da pʋm bɛ nɛ ka ti zʋmaʋŋ la nyaan kena.
11Sɔ' pʋ lɛn tɛn'ɛsid zʋmaʋŋ kanɛ gaad la nidib yɛla ya'asɛ;
hali ka banɛ na dɔl banɛ na ti kenna la nya'aŋ kʋ tiɛn ba yɛlaa.”
Baŋir ka' gbinnɛ
12Mam kanɛ an Pa'an la da anɛ Israel na'ab Jerusalem tempʋʋgin. 13Ka kpɛ'ɛŋi m mɛŋi zamis ye m baŋ ya'am an si'em, nɛ baŋiri zaŋi ken dunia nwa' pʋʋgin yɛla wʋsa. Abɔnam yɛla nwa' ka Wina'am zaŋi ziil ninsaaliba! 14M da gɔsi nyɛ linɛ maal dunia nwa' ni, ka li wʋsa anɛ zaalim wʋʋ fʋn na kad pɛbisʋg ye fʋ gban'e nɛ.
15Dinɛ pɔnd la kʋ nyaŋi tiɛn sappii.
Ka linɛ kae la kʋ nyaŋi kaalɛ.
16 M tɛn'ɛsi m sʋʋnrin sa ye, “Gɔsima, m nɔbig ya ka mɔr ya'am hali gaad na'abanɛ wʋsa nam mi' sʋ'oe Jerusalem. M paam ya'am nɛ baŋir bɛdegʋ.” 17Ka yʋ'ʋn nɔki m mɛŋi mak nɛ ya'am nɛ baŋir, ka lɛn vɛɛnsi mak gɛɛmis nɛ zɔn yɛla, ka yʋ'ʋn baŋ ye li wʋsa anɛ zaalim wʋʋ fʋn na kad pɛbisʋg ye fʋ gban'e nɛ. 18Ya'am galisʋg lɛn anɛ sʋnsa'aŋ,
ka fʋ ya'a mɔr baŋiri galis li anɛ namisʋg.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Yamlɛog tʋʋma ka' gbinnɛ
1Ka m tɛn'ɛsi m sʋnfʋn sa ye, “Tɔ', kɛl ka m tʋmim ya'amlɛog bɔɔdim ka gɔs ye bɔɔ na niŋɛ.” Amaa din wʋsa mɛ anɛ zaalim. 2Man nyɛ ka di'emyaalis anɛ zɔlimis, ka nyɔbɔɔ yit ya'amlɛog tʋʋma ni? 3Ka m yɛlim mɛŋ ye, m na bʋgʋli m sʋnf nɛ daam hali ka maali m mɛŋ wʋʋ zɔlʋg nɛ, amaa ka m ya'am nam kpɛn vʋe. M da bɔɔd ye m kpansi gɔs ye bɔɔ nar ye ninsaal tʋm saŋa bi'ela kanɛ ka o mɔr dunia nwa' ni. 4 Ka m tʋm tʋʋm kpi'ema ka mɛ' yaa tisim mɛŋ ka kua pɔɔd bɛdegʋ, 5ka maal lɔmbɔn'ɔdi sɛ tiwanna buudi wʋsa li pʋʋgin, 6ka ga mu'a mɔri dɔn'ɔsidi m tiis la. 7 M mɛ da lɛn da' yamdaad nɛ yampu'abi pɛ'ɛs, ka ba sieba la'an du'a m yin. Ka m mɛ mɔr niigi nɛ kɔnbidi gat nimbanɛ wʋsa da bɛ Jerusalem ka man nan kae. 8 M da paam anzurifa nɛ sanlima bɛdegʋ ka di'es areza'as tɛɛns bɛdegʋ na'anam san'an tisim mɛŋ; ka mɛ la'as dap nɛ pu'a banɛ yʋ'ʋmmi tisidim, nɛ pu'ab bɛdegʋ banɛ na ma'ae dau sʋnf. 9Ka m kpi'euŋ yʋ'ʋn da gat na'abanɛ wʋsa dɛŋi m tuon Jerusalem tempʋʋgin; ka la'an nɛ lin wʋsa m ya'am da nam kpɛn vʋe.
10Linɛ wʋsa ka m nif da nyɛ ka bɔɔd la, m da paamidi li,
ka pʋ zan'asi m ya'am bɔɔdim.
M sʋnf da ma'ae nɛ m tʋʋma wʋsa,
ka nwa' da aan m tʋʋma la wʋsa nyɔɔd.
11La'an nɛ wala wʋsa man da gɔsi m nu'ug tʋʋma
ka nyɛ man namisi paam si'el wʋsa la,
m nyɛ ka li wʋsa ka' gbinnɛ, wʋʋ fʋn na kad pɛbisim ye fʋ gban'e nɛ.
Si'el kae mɔr nyɔɔd dunia nwa' nii.
Ya'am nɛ zɔlimis wʋsa anɛ yɔri
12Ka m yʋ'ʋn pin'ili tɛn'ɛsid,
ya'am nɛ gɛɛmis nɛ zɔlimis yɛla.
Na'apaal na tʋm bɔ
ka li ka'anɛ linɛ pʋn tʋm sa?
13Ka m nyɛ ka ya'am mɔr nyɔɔdi gat yalimis,
nwɛnɛ nɛɛsim mɔr nyɔɔdi gat lik si'em la.
14Ya'am sɔb mɔr nini nyɛt, ka zɔlʋg on ken lik.
Amaa m kpansi baŋ ye bʋn yinne paadi ba wʋsa.
15Tɔ', ka m lɛn tɛn'ɛsi m sʋʋnrin sa ye yɛl linɛ paad zɔlʋg mɛ paad mam.
Dinzugɔ, nyɔbɔ ka man nyɛ m ya'am la pʋʋginɛ?
Ka m yɛli m sʋʋnrin sa ye, “Nɛ' mɛ ka' gbinnɛ.”
16Nwɛnɛ din kʋ yuugɛ ka ba tam zɔlʋg yɛla si'em la,
ala mɛn ka ba na tam ya'am sɔb yɛla;
Nwɛnɛ zɔlʋgʋ na kpi si'em la,
ala mɛn ka ya'am sɔb mɛ na kpi.
Tʋʋm galisʋg anɛ zaalim
17Alazug ka m kisig dunia nwa' bɛllim bɔzugɔ li anɛ namisʋg nɛ sʋnsa'aŋi tisim. Ka li wʋsa ka' gbinnɛ, wʋʋ fʋn na kad pɛbisim nɛ. 18Ka m kisig bʋn linɛ wʋsa ka m tʋm nyɛ dunia nwa' ni bɔzugɔ, m na basi li tis onɛ na dɔllim nya'aŋ na. 19Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na baŋ ye o sɔb na an ya'am sɔb bɛɛ zɔlʋgɔ? La'an nɛ wala o na sʋ'oe bʋn dinɛ wʋsa ka m zaŋi m ya'am tʋm namis ka nyɛ dunia nwa' ni la. Nɛ' mɛ ka' gbinnɛ. 20Ala ka m sʋnf pin'ili san'am m dunia namisʋg nwa' zug. 21Nid na nɔk o ya'am nɛ baŋir nɛ mi'ilim tʋm o tʋʋma, ka di an tilas ye o bas on paam si'el wʋsa la tis ninkanɛ pʋ namisi di yɛlaa. Nɛ' mɛ ka' gbinnɛ ka mɛ an zutɔɔg. 22Bɔ nyɔɔd ka ninsaal nyɛti yi o dunia nwa' fara nɛ namisʋg pʋʋginɛ? 23 Daar wʋsa o tʋʋma anɛ namisʋg nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ, la'an nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ wʋsa o ya'am pʋ dig ya. Nɛ' mɛ ka' gbinnɛ. 24 Nid kʋ tʋm bʋnsʋŋ si'a gaad on na di ka nu ka nyɛ sumalisim o tʋʋma nii. M mɛ nyɛ ka lina wʋsa yinɛ Wina'am san'an na 25bɔzugɔ, ya'a ka' onɛ, anɔ'ɔnɛ na di bɛɛ nyɛ malisim? 26 Dau kanɛ ma'ae Wina'am sʋnf la ka o tisid o ya'am nɛ mi'ilim nɛ sumalisim. Amaa o kɛtnɛ ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb namisid ka la'as areza'asi digili tis onɛ ma'ae Wina'am sʋnf la. Ka li wʋsa ka' gbin wʋʋ fʋn na ye fʋ kad pɛbisim gban'e nɛ.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.

1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Mukir nɛ namisʋg nɛ zuod ka'alim
1Ka m lɛn gɔs ya'as ka nyɛ mugusʋg buudi wʋsa dinɛ bɛ dunia nwa' ni.
M nyɛ bam mugusid sieba la ninta'am
ka sɔ' ka' bɛlisidi baa.
Paŋ bɛ nɛ banɛ mugusidi ba la nu'usin,
dinzug ka sɔ' ka' bɛlisidi baa.
2Ka m yɛl nyain ye banɛ pʋn kpi sa la
mɔr sumalisim gat banɛ vʋe la.
3Amaa onɛ sɔn'oe wʋsa anɛ onɛ ka ba nam pʋ du'a.
On sɔb nam pʋ nyɛ bɛ'ɛd kanɛ namisid nidib dunia ni laa.
4Ka m lɛn nyɛ ka baŋ ye fufum nɛ ti taaba zugʋ kɛ ka saalib pamm tʋm hali. Nɛ' mɛ ka' gbinnɛ. Li anɛ wʋʋ fʋn na kad pɛbisim nɛ.
5Zɔlʋg kaknɛ o nu'us ka kʋ siaki tʋmm
hali ka kɔ'ɔm kʋʋd o.
6Nid ya'a mɔr bi'ela ka mɔr sumalisim
sɔn'oe onɛ tʋm paam ka namisid
ka di an wʋʋ o katnɛ pɛbisim ye o gban'e nɛ.
7M lɛn nyɛ si'el ya'as ka li ka' gbin dunia nwa' nii:
8Dau da bɛ aan o kɔn',
ka ka' ba'abiig bɛɛ o mɛŋ biiga.
O tʋʋma da ka' bɛnnɛ.
Nɛ wala o nini daa pʋ tig o arezak la.
Ka o bu'os o mɛŋ ye, “Man tʋmmi tisid anɔ'ɔnɛ?
Bɔ ka m mɔŋi m mɛŋ sumalisim?”
Nɛ' mɛ anɛ namis zaalig ka ka' gbinnɛ.
9Nidib ayi' ya'a la'am bɛ sɔn'oe nid yinne
bɔzugɔ ba na tun'e tʋm paam nyɔɔd bɛdegʋ.
10Ayinne ya'a lu, o tiraan na nyaŋi sʋŋ o ka o duoe.
Amaa nid ya'a lu ka sɔ' kae na sʋŋ o ka o duoe, o bɛ nɛ yɛla ni.
11Nidib ayi' ya'a la'asi digi li anɛ wamm.
Amaa nid ya'a dig o kɔn'ɔkɔn', li na niŋ wala an wamm nɛ?
12Nid yinne nyaŋir pʋ tɔya,
Amaa nidib ayi' na tun'e sʋŋ taaba yi yɛla ni.
Hali nwiig kanɛ pan'am atan' pʋ kɛnsigid na'anaa.
13Dasaŋ onɛ an nɔŋdaan ka mɔr ya'am gat bʋnkʋdʋg onɛ an na'ab ka an zɔlʋg ka mɛ pʋ lɛn di'ed nimmua sa'alʋgɔ. 14Li tun'e anɛ ye dasaŋ nwa' yinɛ sanrega ni na di na'am la, bɛɛ ba mɛ tun'e du'a o nɛ nɔŋin. 15Ka m nyɛ ka banɛ wʋsa vʋe ka bɛ dunia nwa' ni la dɔl na'apaal la. 16Nimbanɛ dɔl o la ka' bɛnnɛ. Amaa ka zʋmaʋŋ kanɛ yuolim la kʋ mɔr sumalisim nɛ na'ab nwaa. Nɛ' mɛ ka' gbinnɛ. Li anɛ wʋʋ fʋn na kad pɛbisim ye fʋ gban'e nɛ.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
Gu'usim fʋn dɔl Wina'am si'em
1Fʋ ya'a keŋ Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin fʋn gu'usimi fʋ mɛŋ. Kem ka kɛlis sʋ'ʋŋa, gaad fʋn na maan maana wʋʋ zɔn banɛ zi' ye ba tʋm bɛ'ɛd la maan si'em la.
2Da kɛ ka fʋ nɔɔr pian'ad tɔ'ɔtɔ pa'an linɛ bɛɛ fʋ sʋnfʋn
ka gbirigi kaanbi zi'el Wina'am tuonnɛ.
Wina'am bɛ nɛ agɔl ka fʋn mɛ bɛ teŋin.
Alazug kɛl ka fʋ pian'ad an fiin.
3Nwɛnɛ yɛl babigi na bɛ sɔ' sʋnfʋn ka li kɛ ka o zaansim si'em la,
ala ka li na an nɛ zɔlʋgʋ na pian'ad pian'ayɛɛd.
4Fʋ ya'a kaanbi zi'el Wina'am tuon fʋn da yuug nɛ yɔɔbɔ. Baŋim ye o ba'a kae nɛ zɔnnɛ; mɔɔm ka yɔ fʋn kaanb si'el la. 5Fʋ ya'a pʋ kaanbɛ li sɔn'oe fʋn na kaanb ka pʋ yɔɔ. 6Da kɛ ka fʋ nɔɔr kɛ ka fʋ tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ. Mɛ da yɛl Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yir tʋmtʋm la ye fʋn daa kaanb la fʋ daa yidig nɛ. Bɔ ka fʋ na kɛ ka Wina'am sʋnf duoe nɛf ka o san'ami fʋ nu'ug tʋʋma? 7Zaansima bɛdegʋ nɛ pian'abɛdʋg anɛ zaalim. Gu'usim fʋn dɔl Wina'am si'em.
Zam arezak ka' nyɔɔdɛ
8Fʋ ya'a nyɛ ka ba namisid nɔŋdaan teŋ si'a ni ka mɔŋ o bʋʋd, fʋn da kɛ ka li lidigi fɔ. Bɔzugɔ kpɛɛm wʋsa mɔr onɛ sʋ'oe o, ka on mɛ mɔr sʋ'ʋd. 9Zʋʋd linɛ yit teŋin la na ka ba dit. Na'ab gba nyɔɔd yit nɛ pɔɔgin na.
10Onɛ nɔŋ ligidi pʋ nyɛt ligidi ka li siakida.
Onɛ bɔɔd areza'as o nini pʋ tigid on mɔr si'ela.
Nɛ' mɛ ka' gbinnɛ.
11Diibi paasid si'em la,
ditib mɛ paasid nɛ ala.
Ka nyɔbɔɔ bɛ tis o sɔba
gat o nini na gɔsidi li?
12Tʋmtʋm ya'a di fiin bɛɛ bɛdegʋ, o gbisidnɛ o ya'amin.
Amaa arezak daan pʋ gbisid baa bi'elaa o mɔrim la yɛla.
13M lɛn nyɛ tʋʋm kanɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd hali dunia nwa' ni.
Arezak sɔb la'asid kpan'am su'ad ka li lieb yɛla tis o hali,
14ka o zutɔɔg kɛ ka li widig ka bas o.
Ka o ya'a mɔr biig, faar kae ka o na basi tis oo.
15 Ba du'ad nid nɛ biel.
On kɛn si'em na la, ala ka o mɛ lɛbid.
O kʋ nɔk on tʋm nyɛ si'el la keŋɛ.
16Nɛ' mɛ anɛ yɛlpakir:
Nidi kɛn si'em na la, ala ka o mɛ lɛbid.
O namsisʋg la wʋsa nwɛnɛ onɛ tʋm tʋʋmzaal nɛ,
o kʋ tun'e paam si'eli yii li nii.
17O dii o dabisa wʋsa dunia nwa' ni nɛ namisʋg nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ,
ka nyɛt yɛltɔɔd nɛ sʋnpɛɛn gʋllim.
18Tɔ', ka m vʋʋg ye li an sʋm ka nar ye ninsaal dit ka nuud ka paam sumalisim o namisʋg tʋʋma la pʋʋgin dabisa bi'ela banɛ ka Wina'am tis o ka o vʋe la. Bɔzugɔ, lina aan o nyɔɔd. 19Linɛ paas, Wina'am ya'a nɔk arezak nɛ mɔrim tis sɔ', ka lɛn tis o suor ye o nyɛɛ o tʋʋma la malisim ka dii li nyɔɔd wʋsa, li anɛ Wina'am piini. 20Wina'am kɛnɛ ka on sɔb mɔr sumalisim daar wʋsa ka kʋ lɛn fabin o bɛllim yɛlaa.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
7We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied. 8We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right. 9It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
10Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us. 11The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk? 12Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_text:
1Ka m lɛn nyɛ yɛlbɛ'ɛsi'a linɛ tɛbis ka paad nidib dunia nwa' ni. 2Li anɛ ye Wina'am tis nid arezak nɛ mɔrim nɛ na'asi ka kɛ ka o pʋ kɔ'ɔŋid o ya'am bɔɔdim. Amaa Wina'am pʋ kɛ ka o dii li malisim, ka saan lɛɛ kena di li malisim. Nɛ' ka' gbinnɛ, ka an sʋnsa'aŋ pamm. 3Nid na tun'e mɔr biis kɔbiga ka o yʋma zu'oe. Ka la'an nɛ on yuug si'em la, o ya'a kʋ dii o areza'as la malisim o vʋm saŋa ka kpi ka pʋ nyɛ kʋʋrɛ, bikpi'iŋ sɔn'oe o. 4Bɔzugɔ ban du'a sɔ' la kennɛ yɔɔgʋ na ka lɛn lɛb yɔɔgʋ wʋʋ onɛ ken likin ka ba tam o yɛla la, 5la'an nɛ on pʋ nyɛ nɛɛsim bɛɛ baŋ vʋm an si'el la. O mɔr yɔlisim sɔn'oe ninkaŋa sɔb 6baa o ya'a vʋe yʋʋm tusir bɛɛ tusa ayi' ka pʋ dii o mɔrim malisim. Ba wʋsa pʋ wa'anɛ zin'ig yinnee?
7Ninsaal mɔɔr wʋsa anɛ m di la yɛla.
Amaa nɛ wala wʋsa o diib pʋ siakid oo.
8Bɔ ni ka ya'am sɔb sɔn'oe zɔlʋgɔ?
Nyɔbɔ ka nɔŋdaan na nyɛ o ya'a mi' o mɛŋ mɔrim nidibinɛ?
9Kɛl ka fʋ nif tig nɛ fʋn mɔr si'eli,
gaad linɛ ka fʋ nan tɛn'ɛsidi li yɛla.
Nɛ' mɛ anɛ zaalim wʋʋ fʋn na kad pɛbisʋg ye fʋ gban'e nɛ.
10Bʋn kanɛ bɛ la, ba pʋm pʋd o li yʋ'ʋr sa.
Ka ninsaali an si'em la, ba pʋm baŋ.
Nid kae na tun'e nwa'as nɔŋgbannwa'ari
nyaŋ onɛ paŋi gaad o.
11Pian'ad ya'a zu'oe, li gbin anɛ fiin
ka li nyɔɔd an bɔ tis sɔ'?
12Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ mi' linɛ an sʋm tis nid o vʋm saŋa. O dabisa banɛ an fiin ka ka' gbin la na gaad. Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na yɛl o linɛ na tʋm dunia nwa' ni o kum nya'aŋa?

english_text:
The Best in Life
1 A good reputation
at the time of death
is better than loving care
at the time of birth.
2It's better to go to a funeral
than to attend a feast;
funerals remind us
that we all must die.
3Choose sorrow over laughter
because a sad face
may hide a happy heart.
4A sensible person mourns,
but fools always laugh.
5Correction from someone wise
is better by far
than praise from fools.
6Foolish laughter is stupid.
It sounds like thorns
crackling in a fire.
7Corruption makes fools
of sensible people,
and bribes can ruin you.
8Something completed is better
than something just begun;
patience is better
than too much pride.
9 Only fools get angry quickly
and hold a grudge.
10It isn't wise to ask,
“Why is everything worse
than it used to be?”
11Having wisdom is better
than an inheritance.
12Wisdom will protect you
just like money;
knowledge with good sense
will lead you to life.
13Think of what God has done!
If God makes something crooked,
can you make it straight?
14When times are good,
you should be cheerful;
when times are bad,
think about what it means.
God makes them both
to keep us from knowing
what will happen next.
Some of Life's Questions
15I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper. 16So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart! 17Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool. 18Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
19Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
20No one in this world always does right.
21Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you. 22Haven't you cursed many others?
23I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me. 24The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep. 25So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
26Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for. 27With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together, 28but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman. 29I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_text:
1 Yʋ'ʋsʋŋ an sʋm gaad tudaar,
ka fʋ kum daar sɔn'oe fʋ du'am daar.
2Li an sʋm ka fʋ keŋ kʋyinnɛ
gat yikanɛ ka ba maan sumalisim.
Bɔzugɔ kum an sɔ' mɛkama ba'asʋg zin'ig.
Banɛ vʋe wʋsa tɛn'ɛsim nɛ'.
3Sʋnsa'aŋ an sʋm gat la'ad
bɔzugɔ sʋnsa'aŋ an sʋm tisi fʋ sʋnr.
4Ya'am sɔb sʋnf bɛ nɛ kʋyin.
Amaa zɔn sʋnya bɛ nɛ sumalisim zin'ig.
5Fʋ ya'a di'e ya'am sɔb tansʋg
li sɔn'oe fʋn na kɛlisid zɔn yʋʋma.
6Nwɛnɛ gɔn'ɔsi dit bugumini tansid si'em la,
ala mɛnɛ an zɔlʋg la'ad. Nɛ' mɛ ka' gbinnɛ.
7Filiŋʋ kɛt ka ya'am sɔb liebid zɔlʋg
ka zam san'amid nid sʋnf.
8Si'el mɛkama wʋsa naar an sʋm gati li pin'ilʋg.
Ka mɔdigir mɛ an sʋm gat nyɛɛsim.
9 Da kɛt ka fʋ sʋnf duod tɔ'ɔtɔ
ka sʋnduor anɛ zɔn din.
10Mid ka fʋ yɛl ye, “Bɔɔ lɛɛ kɛ ka kʋdimin la da an sʋm gat nannanna?”
Bɔzugɔ, bu'os kan ka' ya'am bu'osʋgɔ.
11Ya'am nwɛnɛ faar nɛ,
li anɛ bʋnsʋŋ ka mɔr nyɔɔdi tis banɛ bɛ dunia nwa' ni la.
12Ya'am anɛ linɛ lusidif
wʋʋ ligidi lusid si'em la,
Amaa mi'ilim an sʋm si'em nwa':
li faandi onɛ mɔr ya'am la nyɔvʋr.
13Tɛn'ɛsim gɔs Wina'am maal si'el.
Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi tiɛn on pɔnd si'ela?
14Saŋa ya'a ti an sʋm, fʋn mɔr sumalisim.
Saŋa ya'a mɛ ti an bɛ'ɛd fʋn baŋim ye li anɛ Wina'am maali li wʋsa.
Alazugɔ ninsaal kʋ nyaŋi baŋ o bɛogɔ.
15Mam bɛllim dinɛ ka' gbin nwa' ni, m nyɛ nɛ'ɛnam wʋsa:
ninsʋŋ kpiidi tɔ'ɔtɔ o pʋpielimin
ka bugis mɛ vʋe yuug nɛ o bugusim.
16Da an sʋm galisɛ, bɛɛ mɔr ya'am galisɛ:
bɔ ka fʋ san'amidi fʋ mɛŋa?
17Da mɔr pʋtɔɔgʋ galisɛ, mɛ da an zɔlʋgɔ:
bɔ ka fʋ kpiid ka fʋ daar pʋ paae?
18Li an sʋm ka fʋ gban'e yinne ka mɛ da bas ka yinne la gaadɛ.
Ninkanɛ zɔt Wina'am mɔr ayi' la wʋsa ka kʋ maali baa tʋʋgɛ.
19Ya'am kɛt nɛ ka li sɔb mɔr paŋi
gaad na'anam piiga.
20Ninsʋŋ kae dunia nwa' nii tʋm sʋm
ka bɛ'ɛd ka' o nii.
21Da kɛlisid dinɛ wʋsa ka nidib yɛta,
ka daasi'erɛɛ fʋ na ti wʋm ka fʋ yammʋg tʋ'ʋdif.
22Ka fʋ mi' ye saŋa bɛdegʋ fʋn mɛ tʋ'ʋd sieba. 23Man nɔki m ya'am kpans nɛ' wʋsa ka mɔɔd ye m lieb ya'am sɔb, amaa nɛ' gaad man nɛ. 24Ya'am ya'a an si'em wʋsa, li zulim nɛ hali ka ninsaal kae na iee nyɛɛ li. 25Ka m lɛm mɔ ye m tiaki m pʋtɛn'ɛri vɛɛnsi baŋ ya'am ka gban'e si'elnam gbin. M mɔ ye m pa'al ye pitɔɔlim anɛ zɔlimis ka gɛɛmis mɛ an yalimis.
26M nyɛ tɔɔg kanɛ gaad kum.
Linɛ an pu'a kanɛ an bɛndig,
ka o sʋnf nɛ o nu'us nwɛnɛ baŋ ka ba bɛnd.
Ninkanɛ ma'ad Wina'am sʋnf la ma'aa na pɔns,
amaa tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb la, o na bɛndi gban'e o. 27Gɔsima! Pa'an la yɛt ye, “Nɛ' anɛ linɛ ka m nyɛ:
m daa dɔlisnɛ suoya kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ye m baŋ yɛla wʋsa gbin. 28Ka man daa nan ieed ka nam pʋ nyɛ la,
m daa nyɛnɛ dau sʋŋ yinne tusir pʋʋgin,
ka lɛɛ pʋ nyɛ pu'a sʋŋ yinne hali tusir pʋʋginɛ. 29Nɛ' ma'aa ka man nyɛ:
Wina'am maal ninsaal nɛ sʋ'ʋŋa,
amaa sɔ' mɛkama ieed o mɛŋ pitɔya'am.”

english_text:
1Who is smart enough
to explain everything?
Wisdom makes you cheerful
and gives you a smile.
Obey the King
2If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise. 3Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind. 4The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?” 5If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it. 6Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything, 7though no one can tell the future. 8We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil. 9I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another?
Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
10I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense. 11When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime. 12They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying:
Everyone who lives right
and respects God
will prosper,
13but no one who sins
and rejects God
will prosper or live very long.
14There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens. 15So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
16Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world. 17I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_text:
1Anɔ'ɔn nwɛnɛ ya'am sɔba?
Anɔ'ɔn baŋid yɛla gbinnɛ?
Ya'am nied nɛ ninsaal nini
ka tiakid o ka o kʋ lɛn lɔɔd nindaa.
Siakim na'ab nɔɔr
2Siakim na'ab wʋʋ fʋn kaanbi zi'el Wina'am tuon si'em la. 3Da gɛn' ka duoe na'ab tuonnɛ. Mɛ da nwa'asid nɛ na'aba bɔzugɔ, o na tun'e tʋm on bɔɔd si'el. 4Na'ab pian'ʋk mɔri paŋ, ka sɔ' kʋ tun'e bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ maan nɛ'ɛŋa?”
5On mɛkama siak o, kʋ nyɛ dɛŋŋa.
Ya'am sɔb mi' o pʋtɛn'ɛrin saŋa kanɛ nar ka dɔl suor.
6Si'el wʋsa mɔri li saŋa nɛ li suor,
la'an nɛ ninsaal bɛllim an tɔɔg si'em la.
7Sɔ' sadigim zi' linɛ ken bɛog na la,
anɔ'ɔnɛ na tun'e yɛl linɛ saa na kena?
8Sɔ' ka' sisi'em paŋ ka na tun'e gu'oe li,
ala mɛn ka sɔ' ka' paŋ o kum daarɛ.
Nwɛnɛ zabzabidi ka' suori na zɔ ka bas zaba si'em la,
ala mɛn ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kʋ bas banɛ tʋmmi li la suorɛ.
9Nɛ' wʋsa ka m nyɛ saŋkan ka m nɔki m ya'am ye m baŋ dunia nwa' gbin la. Saŋa bɛ nɛ ka nid sʋ'oe o taaba tʋmmi ba pitɔɔg, ka li mɛ an mugusʋgʋ tis o mɛŋ. 10M lɛn nyɛ ka ba mum bugisnam nɛ girima. Ka banɛ mi' ba bugusim yɛla wɔ'ɔgidi ba ban daa bɛ teŋ si'a la.
