Nɛ' mɛn ka' gbinnɛ. 11Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb ya'a pʋ nyɛt tʋbtɛkir tɔ'ɔtɔ, li kɛtnɛ ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd yaligid. 12La'an nɛ bugisnamɛ tʋm bugisim bɛdegʋ ka mɔr nyɔvʋr wɔk la, li na an sʋm gat ala tis Wina'am nimbanɛ zɔt o. 13La'an nɛ bugisnam la pʋ zɔt Wina'am la, li kʋ an sʋm tisi ba, ka ba dabisa kʋ wa'am nwɛnɛ winnigi ɛɛnti bik ka fʋ siig wa'am laa. 14Si'el lɛm bɛ dunia nwa' ni ya'as ka ka' gbinnɛ. Ninsʋma di'esid bugisnam yɔɔd. Ka bugisnam mɛ di'esid ninsʋma yɔɔd. Nɛ' mɛn ka m yɛl ye li ka' gbinnɛ. 15Alazug dim sumalisim ya vʋm saŋa bɔzugɔ si'el kae an sʋm tis nidi gat on na di ka nu ka mɔr sumalisim. Ka sumalisim na bɛ nɛ o, o tʋʋma zin'igin, dabisban ka Wina'am tis o dunia nwa' pʋʋgin la. 16Man daa mɔɔd ye m baŋ linɛ maan dunia nwa' wʋsa ni ka nyɛ ka ninsaal namisid hali nintaŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ wʋsa ka pʋ gbisida. 17Ani ka m nyɛ linɛ wʋsa ka Wina'am maal. Sɔ' kae na nyaŋi gban'e linɛ tʋm dunia nwa' ni la gbinnɛ. La'an nɛ paŋ kanɛ ka o mɔɔd la wʋsa o kʋ gban'e li gbinnɛ. Baa ya'am sɔb ya'a ma' ye o mi', o kʋ nyaŋi gban'e li gbinnɛ.

english_text:
One Day at a Time
1I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad. 2But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
3It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die. 4As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion. 5We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten. 6Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
7So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do. 8Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best. 9Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth. 10Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
11Here is something else I have learned:
The fastest runners
and the greatest heroes
don't always win races
and battles.
Wisdom, intelligence, and skill
don't always make you healthy,
rich, or popular.
We each have our own share
of misfortune.
12None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap.
Better To Be Wise than Foolish
13Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me. 14It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls. 15But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten. 16So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
17Words of wisdom spoken softly
make much more sense
than the shouts of a ruler
to a crowd of fools.
18Wisdom is more powerful
than weapons,
yet one mistake can destroy
all the good you have done.
translation_text:
Sɔ' wʋsa na kpi
1Ka m tiɛn gɔs nɛ' wʋsa yɛla ka kʋ'ʋg giŋa ye ninsʋŋ nɛ ya'am sɔb nɛ ba tʋʋma wʋsa bɛ nɛ Wina'am nu'usin. Alazugɔ sɔ' zi' ye nɔŋilim bɛɛ kisidim gur oo.
2Bama wʋsa na naae zin'ig yinne:
pʋpiel nɛ bugis, ninsʋŋ nɛ nimbɛ'og,
banɛ an nyain nɛ banɛ ka' nyainnɛ,
banɛ maan maana nɛ banɛ pʋ maana.
Lin an si'em tis ninsʋŋ la, ala mɛn ka li na aaɛn tis nimbɛ'og.
Lin an si'em tis banɛ kaanbi zi'el la
mɛ anɛ ala tis banɛ zɔt kaanbʋg la.
3Nɛ'ɛŋa an bʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ tʋm dunia nwa' ni: Saal wʋsa gan'al si'em la linɛ diti ba. Ba sʋnya pɛ'ɛli nɛ bɛ'ɛd ka ba tʋm gɛɛntʋʋma ba vʋm saŋa wʋsa, ka li nya'aŋ ka ba kpi.
4Amaa onɛ wʋsa vʋe lɛm mɔr ti'ir;
hali bavʋt sɔn'oe gbigim kpiiluŋ.
5Bɔzugɔ banɛ vʋe la mi' ye ba na kpi,
amaa banɛ kpi zi' si'ela.
Ba pʋ lɛm mɔr yɔɔdɛ,
li kʋ yuugɛ ka nidib tami ba yɛla.
6Ka ba nɔŋilim nɛ ba kisidim nɛ ba ya'amlɛog gaad,
ka ba pʋ lɛm mɔr zin'isi'a dunia nwa' nii.
7Kem dii fʋ diib nɛ sumalisim ka nu ka kɛ ka fʋ sʋnf ma'ae. Ka Wina'am nini pʋn tig fʋn tʋm si'el la. 8Yɛɛm fupielig saŋa wʋsa, ka mɛ bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋi fʋ zug saŋa wʋsa. 9Dim malisim nɛ fʋ pu'a kanɛ ka fʋ nɔŋ la fʋ vʋm saŋa linɛ ka' gbinnɛ ka Wina'am tisif dunia nwa' ni la. Dim dabisbanɛ ka' gbin la wʋsa nɛ o, bɔzugɔ linɛ an namiskanɛ ka fʋ nyɛ dunia nwa' ni. 10Fʋ nu'ugʋ gban'e tʋʋm si'a wʋsa, fʋn tʋmmi li nɛ fʋ paŋ wʋsa, bɔzugɔ tʋʋma bɛɛ gban'ar bɛɛ mi'ilim bɛɛ ya'am kae yaʋgʋn, zin'ikan ka fʋ wa'ae la. 11M lɛn nyɛ si'el ya'as dunia nwa' ni:
Li ka'anɛ onɛ mi' zɔɔgʋ dit ya'an zɔɔginɛ,
bɛɛ onɛ mɔr paŋi nyaŋid zaba nii.
Li ka'anɛ ya'am sɔbi paamid diib bɛdegʋʋ,
bɛɛ onɛ mɔr baŋiri paamid arezaka.
Li ka'anɛ onɛ zamis hali paamid on bɔɔd si'ela:
ayei, li anɛ sia'alsʋŋ bɛɛ sia'albɛ'ɛdi tisidi ba wʋsa.
12Sɔ' mɛ zi' saŋa kanɛ ka o na kpii.
Asau gban'ad zimi si'em,
bɛɛ bɛndisi gban'ad niis si'em la,
ala ka ba bɛnd nidib
ka li gban'adi ba tɔ'ɔtɔ ka ba zi' li yɛla baa bi'elaa.
Ya'am nɛ yalimis yɛla
13Ka m lɛn nyɛ dunia nwa' ni ya'am si'a buudi ka li an sʋm tisim. 14Tembil si'a da bɛ ka li nidib pʋ zu'oe, ka na'atita'ar kena ye o gilig ka zab nɛ li nɛ o paŋ la wʋsa. 15Ka dau bɛ tembil nwa' nii an nɔŋdaan ka lɛɛ mɔr ya'am, o da nɔk o ya'am faaɛn teŋ nwa'. Amaa sɔ' da pʋ lɛn tiɛn dau kaŋa yɛlaa. 16Alazug ka m yɛl ye la'an nɛ ya'am an sʋm gat paŋ la, ba ziem nɔŋdaan ya'am la ka pʋ kɛlis o yɛlaa.
17Ya'am sɔb ya'a pian' bʋgʋsiga ka fʋ di'e,
li sɔn'oe na'abi na pian'adi tansidi tisid zɔn.
18Ya'am an sʋm gat zaba la'ad,
amaa tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb yinne san'amid bʋnsʋma bɛdegʋ.

english_text:
1A few dead flies in perfume
make all of it stink,
and a little foolishness
outweighs a lot of wisdom.
2Sensible thoughts lead you
to do right;
foolish thoughts lead you
to do wrong.
3Fools show their stupidity
by the way they live;
it's easy to see
they have no sense.
4Don't give up your job
when your boss gets angry.
If you stay calm,
you'll be forgiven.
5Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair: 6They honor fools, but dishonor the rich; 7they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
8 If you dig a pit,
you might fall in;
if you break down a wall,
a snake might bite you.
9You could even get hurt
by chiseling a stone
or chopping a log.
10If you don't sharpen your ax,
it will be harder to use;
if you are wise,
you'll know what to do.
11The power to charm a snake
does you no good
if it bites you anyway.
12If you talk sensibly,
you will have friends;
if you talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
13Fools begin with nonsense,
and their stupid chatter
ends with disaster.
14They never tire of talking,
but none of us really know
what the future will bring.
15Fools wear themselves out—
they don't know enough
to find their way home.
16A country is in for trouble
when its ruler is childish,
and its leaders
party all day long.
17But a nation will prosper
when its ruler is mature,
and its leaders
don't party too much.
18Some people are too lazy
to fix a leaky roof—
then the house collapses.
19Eating and drinking
make you feel happy,
and money can buy
everything you need.
20Don't let yourself think about
cursing the king;
don't curse the rich,
not even in secret.
A little bird might hear
and tell everything.
translation_text:
1Nwɛnɛ pʋmpɔɔsi na kpi tudaari pʋʋgin ka li nyuug san'am si'em la,
ala mɛn ka zɔlim ɛɛn paas ya'amin ka girima lɛn kae.
2Ya'am sɔb sʋnf gban'adi bʋnsʋŋ.
Amaa zɔlʋg sʋnf gban'adi bɛ'ɛd.
3Hali zɔlʋg ya'a dɔl pal zug, o ya'am kae,
ka on niŋid si'em la kɛtnɛ ka ba baŋ o gɛtim la yɛla.
4Na'ab sʋnf ya'a duoe nɛ na'ayikpɛɛm, on da bas o kpɛuŋɔ.
An baanlimm ka o sʋnpɛɛn la na ba'asi li ka o tami fʋ bɛ'ɛd la.
5Mam lɛn nyɛ bʋnsi'a dunia nwa' ka li pʋ nara, ka linɛ an na'anamɛ yidigid yidig sieba la.
6Ba nɔk zɔn ka ba gaad tuon,
ka mɛ lɛbis ya'am dim nya'aŋ.
7Man nyɛ yammis ka ba ban'ad widi
ka tuongatib ken nɔbteŋ.
8Onɛ mɛkama tu bʋmbɔk zulʋŋ na luu li pʋʋgin.
Onɛ nwa'ae guomi kpɛn' na, waaf na dum o.
9Onɛ nwa'ae kuga na nyɛ kuga sapu'ad.
Onɛ wia'arid daad na nyɛ li dɛŋ.
10Zɛnnir ya'a pʋ ditta ka fʋ pʋ saasɛ
asɛɛ ka fʋ wiak nɛ paŋ,
amaa mi'ilim na kɛ ka fʋ wiaki li na'ana.
11Waaf ya'a dumif ka tiimdaan kae yamminɛ
o tiim la nyɔɔd kae.
12Ya'am sɔb pian'adi kɛt ka nidib na'asid o,
amaa zɔlʋg nɔɔri dit o.
13Pin'ilʋgʋn la o pian'ad anɛ zɔlim pian'ad,
ka naarin la ka li an bugisim nɛ gɛɛŋ pian'ad.
14Ka zɔlʋg kpɛm pian'adi ken tuon, amaa sɔ' zi' dinɛ kennaa.
Anɔ'ɔnɛ mi' on na gaad ka dinɛ na lɛdigi tʋm?
15Zɔlʋg tʋʋma gɛɛnsid o nɛ,
ka la'an nɛ wala o zi' suokanɛ wa'ae tempʋʋginɛ.
16Yɛltɔɔg bɛɛ tis teŋ kanɛ na'abi an sankpan'as,
ka ba tuongatib nuud ka maan sumalisim bɛogʋn.
17Yɛlsʋm bɛɛ tis teŋ kanɛ na'ab ka ba du'a o nɛ na'am.
Ka li tuongatib dit saŋa dinɛ nar ye ba nyɛ paŋ
ka ka' ye ba nuu bugɛ.
18Nid ya'a an gbanya'a o yu'ada pun'odnɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ;
o nu'us ya'a pʋ bɔɔd tʋʋmaa, o yir nyunnɛ.
19Di'ema ziid sumalisim na. Ka daam ma'ae sʋnf.
Amaa ligidi wɛligid yɛla wʋsa.
20Da tɛn'ɛs na'ab yɛla bɛ'ɛdi fʋ sʋnfʋnɛ
bɛɛ zɛrig arezak sɔbi fʋ dɔɔginɛ,
ka niiŋ tun'e mɔri fʋ pian'ad la yi,
bʋn-ian'adir kanɛ bɛ ani na mɔɔli fʋ yɛla tis.

english_text:
It Pays To Work Hard
1Be generous, and someday
you will be rewarded.
2Share what you have
with seven or eight others,
because you never know
when disaster may strike.
3Rain clouds always bring rain;
trees always stay
wherever they fall.
4If you worry about the weather
and don't plant seeds,
you won't harvest a crop.
5No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
6Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce.
Youth and Old Age
7Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun. 8Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
9Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
10Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_text:
Ya'am tʋʋma
1Nɔkimi fʋ diibi lɔs ku'omin
ka dabisa bɛdegʋ nya'aŋ fʋ na lɛn di'e li.
2Pʋdigim tis nidib ayɔpɔi bɛɛ anii,
bɔzugɔ fʋ zi' yɛlbɛ'ɛd kanɛ na ti lu teŋ la zugɔ.
3Saŋgbana ya'a pɛ'ɛl nɛ ku'om, li niidnɛ saa basid teŋ zug.
Tiig ya'a lu dagɔbʋg bɛɛ datiuŋ, ani ka li digi.
4Onɛ mɛkama kpansid sisi'em kʋ bʋdɛ.
Onɛ gɔsid saŋgbana mɛ kʋ bunɛ.
5Fʋn zi' sisi'em suori an si'em la,
bɛɛ biigi kilimid o ma pʋʋgin si'em la,
ala mɛn ka fʋ kʋ baŋ Wina'am onɛ
maal si'el wʋsa la tʋʋmaa.
6Bʋdimi fʋ bʋmbʋʋda bɛogʋn,
ka mɛ da bas zaam bʋdiga,
ka fʋ zi' tʋʋm kanɛ na maal sʋ'ʋŋa
li tun'e an bɛogʋn bɛɛ zaam din la, bɛɛ ayi' la wʋsa.
Tɛnr onɛ maalif la fʋ dasannim saŋa
7Nɛɛsim malis,
li an sʋm nɛ fʋn na vʋe ka fʋ nini na nyɛt winnig.
8Baa nid ya'a vʋe yʋma bɛdegʋ, on kɛl ka li malis o.
Amaa o tiɛnm dabisbanɛ na ti an lik la bɔzugɔ dabisban la na ti zu'oe.
Bʋn kanɛ kenna wʋsa ka' gbinnɛ.
9Dasaŋa, mɔr sumalisim fʋn nam mɔr paŋ la,
ka kɛ ka fʋ sʋnf malisi fʋ dasannim saŋa.
Dɔlli fʋ sʋnf bɔɔdim nɛ fʋ nini nyɛ si'el ka bɔɔd.
Amaa tɛnr ye dabisir kenna ka Wina'am na kadi fʋ saria.
10Alazugɔ basimi fʋ sʋntɔɔg nɛ fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛyaalis la,
ka da kɛ ka fʋ niŋgbiŋ yɛla daami fɔ,
ka dasannim nɛ li paŋ wʋsa ka' gbinnɛ.

english_text:
1Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
2Someday the light of the sun
and the moon and the stars
will all seem dim to you.
Rain clouds will remain
over your head.
3Your body will grow feeble,
your teeth will decay,
and your eyesight fail.
4The noisy grinding of grain
and the voices of singers
will be shut out
by your deaf ears,
but even the song of a bird
will keep you awake.
5You will be afraid
to climb up a hill
or walk down a road.
Your hair will turn as white
as almond blossoms.
You will feel lifeless
and drag along
like an old grasshopper.
We each go to our eternal home,
and the streets here are filled
with those who mourn.
6The silver cord snaps,
the golden bowl breaks;
the water pitcher is smashed,
and the pulley at the well
is shattered.
7So our bodies return
to the earth,
and the life-giving breath
returns to God.
8Nothing makes sense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense.
Respect and Obey God
9I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied. 10Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
11Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together. 12My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these.
There is no end to books,
and too much study
will wear you out.
13Everything you were taught can be put into a few words:
Respect and obey God!
This is what life
is all about.
14God will judge
everything we do,
even what is done in secret,
whether good or bad.
translation_text:
1-2Tiɛnm Wina'am onɛ maalif la fʋ dasannim saŋa,
ka namisʋg dabisa la nam pʋ paae naa,
ka yʋma la da ti li'el na
ka fʋ yɛl ye, “Mam pʋ di malisimi li nii.”
Ka winnig la nɛ nɛɛsim nɛ nwadig
nɛ nwadbibis la nyaan sɔbigi lieb lik.
Ka saa nii naae ka saŋgbana na kpɛm bɛ.
3Saŋkan la fʋ nu'ubanɛ daa mɔr paŋ la na kirid gba-gba
ka fʋ nɔba tadig.
Fʋ nyina na vɔn' ka kpɛlim bi'ela
ka kʋ lɛn nyaŋi ɔnbid ya'asɛ,
ka fʋ nini kʋ lɛn nyɛta
ka banɛ gɔsid takoro ni la gɔsid ka li an paan.
4Fʋ tʋba na kpid ka fʋ kʋ wʋm suoraadin vuudɛ.
Fʋ mɛ kʋ lɛn wʋm nɛɛr bɛɛ yʋʋma vuudɛ;
amaa niimis kaasig na nief gbɛɛmin.
5Saŋkan la ka fʋ ya'a bɛɛ agɔl fʋ na zɔt dabiem,
ka mɛ zɔt dabiem nɛ suorin sapu'ad yɛla.
Saŋkanɛ ka fʋ zuobid pɛlig farr wʋʋ gum nɛ
ka fʋ gɛɛn kennɛ ku'usid bi'el-bi'el
ka kʋ lɛm mɔr si'el yamlɛogɔ.
Ka fʋ yʋ'ʋn na kuli fʋ yin ka kʋ lɛn lɛb naa,
ka kʋkaasidib dɔl suoya kaasid.
6Tiɛnmi Wina'am yɛla ka anzurifa zɔnt la nam pʋ kɛnsigɛ
bɛɛ sanlima laa la nwa'ae.
Ka ku'om yʋʋr la mɛ nam pʋ nwa'ae buliginɛ,
bɛɛ lɔbidiŋ nwiig la kɛnsigɛ.
7Ka tan la na lɛb tannin,
ka siig mɛ na lɛb Wina'am kanɛ maal o la ni.
8Pa'an la yɛl ye, “Li gbin kae! Li gbin kae! Si'el wʋsa ka' gbinnɛ.”
Naar yɛla
9Pa'an la da ka'anɛ ya'am sɔb ma'aanɛ; amaa o mɛ da pa'an nidib ka ba paamid baŋir, ka la'as siilima bɛdegʋ digil. 10O da ieednɛ ye o nyɛ pian'akanɛ an viki nɛ sida.
11Ya'am dim pian'ad nwɛnɛ kɔnbkem duor nɛ. Ka ba siilima nwɛnɛ kuusa banɛ kpa' gban'e sʋ'ʋŋa. Wina'am onɛ aan ti kɔnbkem la tis nɛ' wʋsa. 12M biiga, gu'usim ka da di'e pa'alsieba ka li ya'a ka' nɛ'.
Gbana bɛdegʋ sɔbir ka' bɛnnɛ, ka zamistɔɔg mɛ an gɛɛnlis.
13Nannanna ti wʋmi li wʋsa,
yɛl la kʋʋsʋgʋ nwa':
zɔm Wina'am ka di'e o zi'ela la,
ka linɛ nar ye ninvʋsaal tʋm.
14Bɔzugɔ Wina'am na kad si'el wʋsa saria,
la'an nɛ linɛ su'a wʋsa,
li ya'a an sʋm bɛɛ bɛ'ɛdɛ.

english_text:
Love Is Better than Wine
1 This is Solomon's
most beautiful song.
She Speaks:
2Kiss me tenderly!
Your love is better than wine,
3and you smell so sweet.
All the young women adore you;
the very mention of your name
is like spreading perfume.
* 4Hurry, my king! Let's hurry.
Take me to your home.
The Young Women Speak:
We are happy for you!
And we praise your love
even more than wine.
She Speaks:
Young women of Jerusalem,
it is only right
that you should adore him.
5My skin is dark and beautiful,
like a tent in the desert
or like Solomon's curtains.
6Don't stare at me
just because the sun
has darkened my skin.
My brothers were angry with me;
they made me work in the vineyard,
and so I neglected
my complexion.
7My darling, I love you!
Where do you feed your sheep
and let them rest at noon?
Don't let the other shepherds
think badly of me.
I'm not one of those women
who shamelessly follow
after shepherds.
He Speaks:
8My dearest, if you don't know,
just follow the path
of the sheep.
Then feed your young goats
near the shepherds' tents.
9You move as gracefully
as the pony that leads
the chariot of the king.
10Earrings add to your beauty,
and you wear a necklace
of precious stones.
11Let's make you some jewelry
of gold, woven with silver.
She Speaks:
12My king, while you
were on your couch,
my aroma was a magic charm.
13My darling, you are perfume
between my breasts;
14you are flower blossoms
from the gardens of En-Gedi.
He Speaks:
15My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
your eyes are those of a dove.
She Speaks:
16My love, you are handsome,
truly handsome—
the fresh green grass
will be our wedding bed
17in the shade of cedar
and cypress trees.
translation_text:
1Solomon Yʋʋm malisiŋ linɛ gaad o yʋʋma la wʋsa:
Pu'asadir la pian'ad dau kanɛ ka o nɔŋ la ye,
2Muakimim nɛ fʋ nɔɔr
ka fʋ nɔŋir la gaad damalisiŋ.
3Fʋ yʋ'ʋr la nwɛnɛ tudaar kanɛ nyuugʋ malis
ka ba kpa'ae ka li nyuug tiig zin'ig wʋsa nɛ.
Bi'esʋg kae nɛ pu'asada nɔŋif la!
4Mɔrim ka ti yi! Kɛl ka ti keŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ!
Kɛl ka m na'ab la mɔrimi keŋ o dɔɔgin.
Pu'asadir la zuanam yɛt dau la ye,
Ti bɔɔdi fʋ yɛla ka mɔr sumalisim fʋ yɛla;
ti na zun'e fʋ nɔŋilim gaad damalisiŋ.
Pu'asadir la mɛŋ:
Asida, li nar ye ba zʋn'ʋf!
5Mam anɛ sabilig, la'an nɛ wala m vɛnl hali.
Yanam Jerusalem pu'asada
sɔbig nɛ nwɛnɛ Kedar teŋ dim sʋga nɛ,
amaa ka nwɛnɛ Solomon dɔɔg fuvɛnla la.
6Da gɔsidim kii, man an sabilig la zugɔ,
nintaŋi nwɛ'ɛm la zug ka m sɔbig.
M tanp la wʋsa sʋnf daa pɛlig nɛ mam
ka ba kɛ ka m guri ba vain pɔɔd,
dinzug ka m basim mɛŋ vain pɔɔg la.
7Fʋn kanɛ ka m nɔŋ la,
yɛlimim fʋn kemmi fʋ kɔnbid la zin'isi'a,
nɛ winnigi ɛɛnti bul ka kɔnbid la vʋ'ʋsid zin'isi'a?
Bɔ ka m na nwɛnɛ pu'a kanɛ ka ba lus o nindaa ka o su'a
dɔlli ya'adi fʋ zuanam kɔnbidɛ.
O zuanam la yɛt, ye,
8Oi! Pu'a vɛnliŋa,
fʋ ya'a zi', asɛɛ fʋ kadi m kɔnbid la buga,
ka mɔri fʋ bʋbibis la keŋ
ka ba ɔnb yam kɔnbkemnib la sʋgaa bɛ si'el la.
9M ya'am bʋnnɛ, m nɔki fɔ maki nɛ wiednya'as banɛ gat Na'ab Faaro zaba tɛrekonam tuon la.
10Fʋ kpɛnda la vɛnli nɛ tʋblɛma hali,
ka sanlima niŋgɔnkɔris pɛ'ɛli fʋ niŋgɔɔnr.
Pu'asadir la zuanam ye,
11Ti na maal sanlima tʋblɛma,
nɛ anzurifa baansi tisif.
Pu'asadir la:
12Na'ab la daa zin'in ye o di la,
ka m tudaari la nyuug duoe.
13M ya'ambʋn la nwɛnɛ kpaam kanɛ nyuugʋ malis hali
ka li pa'ae m bin'isa zug.
14M nɔŋir la nwɛnɛ puum linɛ widigi vɛnl
ka bɛ Engedi vain pɔɔgin la.
Sabua, dau la:
15M ya'am bʋnnɛ, fʋ vɛnl woo!
Fʋ sid vɛnl hali!
Ka fʋ nini la nwɛnɛ dawan nini.
Pu'asadir la:
16Fʋ vɛnl hali, m nɔŋirɛ,
ka m nini sid tigif!
Mɔma'asa la na aan ti digisig zin'ig.
17Na'aziinr tiis la na aan ti dɔɔg la datitada;
ka dɔɔns la na aan li yu'ada.

english_text:
Love Makes Everything Beautiful
She Speaks:
1I am merely a rose
from the land of Sharon,
a lily from the valley.
He Speaks:
2My darling, when compared
with other young women,
you are a lily among thorns.
She Speaks:
3And you, my love,
are an apple tree
among trees of the forest.
Your shade brought me pleasure;
your fruit was sweet.
4You led me to your banquet room
and showered me with love.
5Refresh and strengthen me
with raisins and apples.
I am hungry for love!
6Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
7Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Winter Is Past
She Speaks:
8I hear the voice
of the one I love,
as he comes leaping
over mountains and hills
9like a deer or a gazelle.
Now he stands outside our wall,
looking through the window
10and speaking to me.
He Speaks:
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
11Winter is past,
the rain has stopped;
12flowers cover the earth,
it's time to sing.
The cooing of doves
is heard in our land.
13Fig trees are bearing fruit,
while blossoms on grapevines
fill the air with perfume.
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
14You are my dove
hiding among the rocks
on the side of a cliff.
Let me see how lovely you are!
Let me hear the sound
of your melodious voice.
15Our vineyards are in blossom;
we must catch the little foxes
that destroy the vineyards.
She Speaks:
16My darling, I am yours,
and you are mine,
as you feed your sheep
among the lilies.
17Pretend to be a young deer
dancing on mountain slopes
until daylight comes
and shadows fade away.
translation_text:
1M nwɛnɛ mɔɔd puum linɛ mu'oe
ka vɛnl hali bɛ bɔn'ɔgin la.
Dau la:
2Nwɛnɛ puum kanɛ vɛnl ka bɛ gɔn'ɔs sʋʋgin si'em la
ala ka m ya'am bʋn bɛ pu'asada sʋʋgin.
Pu'asadir la:
3Nwɛnɛ apʋl tiigi bɛ mɔɔgin tiis sʋʋgin si'em la
ala ka onɛ aan m ya'am bʋn la mɛ bɛ na'akim sʋʋgin.
M ya'am bɔɔdnɛ hali ye m zin' o ma'asim,
ka o wala mɛ malisi m nɔɔrin hali.
4O mɔrimi keŋ diib zin'igin,
ka pa'alim o nɔŋilim kanɛ nwɛnɛ fuugʋ lusim la.
5Tisimi m tiis wala ka m di ka paam paŋ,
tisimi m apʋl linɛ an tiig wala la ka m di ka m nini lak;
ka nɔŋir kɔ'ɔm ma'aa kɛ ka m nwi'e.
6O nɔk o dagɔbʋg nu'ug la kʋki m zug,
ka o datiuŋ nu'ug la kuakim.
7Yanam Jerusalem pu'asada,
pɔɔmi nɛ bʋnkɔnbkanɛ ka ya pɔɔd la ye,
ti nɔŋir la kʋ san'am.
Da tiɛnd nɔŋir yɛla ka li saŋa nam pʋ paae.
8Kɛlisima! M ya'am bʋnnɛ! Gɔsima, onɛ ka m nɔŋ la kenna,
o yi zuoya la nii kenna,
o ian'asid kʋkʋna nii kenna.
9Onɛ ka m nɔŋ la nwɛnɛ walig bɛɛ mɔlif nɛ.
Gɔsima! Onɛ zi'e ti yampʋn la.
O gbɛlisidi gɔsid takoro la ni na,
ka gɔsid vɔnya la ni.
10Onɛ ka m nɔŋ la yɛlim ye,
Dau la:
Duoma, m ya'am bʋnnɛ,
m sʋnf bʋnnɛ, kem na dɔllim.
11Gɔsima! Sɛɛung gaad ya
saa pʋ lɛn niida.
12Puum yit teŋin la;
yʋʋma saŋa paae ya,
ka dawana kaasidi
ti teŋ la zug.
13Kekama tiis pin'ili wan waldɛɛnna;
ka vain tiis la puum nyuug pɛ'ɛl zin'ig wʋsa.
Duom, kem na, m nɔŋirɛ;
m ya'ambʋnnɛɛ, kem na ye!
14Fʋ anɛ m dawan, onɛ bɛ tampiins lɛuŋʋn
ka kpɛn' suak zin'igin zuoya la ni.
Kɛl ka m nyɛ fʋ nindaa;
ka kɛ ka m wʋmi fʋ kʋkɔr
ka fʋ kʋkɔr malis nɛ hali,
ka fʋ nindaa vɛnl amɛŋa.
15Gban'am zaŋsiris la tisi ti,
gban'am zaŋsirbibis banɛ san'am vain tiis pɔɔg
saŋkanɛ ka tiis la puud la.
Pu'asadir la:
16Man anɛ m nɔŋir la din ka on mɛ aan m din;
ka mɔr o pɛ'ɛs la bɛ na'apu'a-kʋ-si'is-ku'om pʋʋgin ka ba ɔnbidi giligid.
17Sɛɛ bɛog ti nie
ka zibisʋg gaad;
fɛndigim na, m ya'am bʋnnɛ,
nwɛnɛ mɔlif bɛɛ walig
kanɛ bɛ kʋkʋna la ni.

english_text:
Beautiful Dreams
She Speaks:
1While in bed at night,
I reached for the one I love
with heart and soul.
I looked for him,
but he wasn't there.
2So I searched through the town
for the one I love.
I looked on every street,
but he wasn't there.
3I even asked the guards
patrolling the town,
“Have you seen the one
I love so much?”
4Right after that, I found him.
I held him and would not let go
until I had taken him
to the home of my mother.
5Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles,
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
The Groom and the Wedding Party
Their Friends Speak:
6What do we see approaching
from the desert
like a cloud of smoke?
With it comes the sweet smell
of spices, including myrrh
and frankincense.
7It is King Solomon
carried on a throne,
surrounded by sixty
of Israel's best soldiers.
8Each of them wears a sword.
They are experts at fighting,
even in the dark.
9The throne is made of trees
from Lebanon.
10Its posts are silver,
the back is gold,
and the seat is covered
with purple cloth.
You women of Jerusalem
have taken great care
to furnish the inside.
11Now come and see the crown
given to Solomon by his mother
on his happy wedding day.
translation_text:
1M diginnɛ m kɔn'ɔkɔn' gadʋg zug yʋ'ʋŋ la wʋsa
ka bɔɔd onɛ ka m ya'am nɔŋ hali la;
M iee o zin'ig hali ka pʋ nyɛ o.
2M na duoe nannanna gilig tempʋʋg la,
m na gilig suoraad la nɛ lɔdis la wʋsa;
mam na iee onɛ ka m nɔŋ nɛ m sʋnf wʋsa la.
M sid iee o hali ka pʋ nyɛ o.
3Dap banɛ gur tempʋʋg nyɛ mam, ban daa kaadi giligid la, ka m bu'osi ba ye,
“Ya nyɛ onɛ ka m nɔŋ hali laa?”
4Man fansigi gaad la nɔɔ,
ka keŋ tuon bi'ela ka nyɛ m ya'am bʋn la.
Man nyɛ o la.
M gban'e o nu'ug ka pʋ siak ye m bas o ka o keŋɛ,
ka mɔr o tat-tat nɛ man ti mɔr o paae m ma yin na
kpɛn' onɛ da nɔki m pʋʋg la dɔɔgin.
5Yanam Jerusalem pu'asada,
pɔɔmi nɛ bʋnkɔnbkanɛ ka ya pɔɔd la ye,
ti nɔŋir la kʋ san'am.
Da tiɛnd nɔŋir yɛla ka li saŋa nam pʋ paae.
6Anɔ'ɔnɛ nwa' yi pipirigini kenna
nwɛnɛ nyɔ'ɔsi duoda?
O nɔk tudaari nɛ bʋnnyubisa banɛ bɛ wʋsa,
linɛ ka banɛ kuosid la'ad mɔr la, mis o mɛŋ.
7Gɔsima! Li anɛ Solomon ka ba ziid
ka zabzabidib banɛ kpi'em ban pisyuobʋ dɔl o,
ba anɛ Israel zaba tuongatib kpɛɛmnam.
8Ba wʋsa mɔr zaba sʋ'ʋs,
ba wʋsa mɛ mi' zaba sʋ'ʋŋa.
Sɔ' wʋsa mɔr o sʋ'ʋg ka li bɛɛ o sakpidirin
gur zabaa na ti kɔ' yʋ'ʋŋ.
9Na'ab Solomon mɛŋi kpa' linɛ ka ba nɔki ziid o la;
dasʋma linɛ yi Lebanon na la ka o nɔki maal.
10Li daad la buligi nɛ anzurifa,
li gbinnin la ba bulig nɛ sanlima.
Fupipɛlʋg ka ba nɔki maali li zin'isa la.
Li anɛ Jerusalem pu'asada la ʋgi li nɛ nɔŋilim.
11Zion teŋ pu'asadaa, yimi naa
gɔsi Na'ab Solomon pid o na'am zupibig si'em.
Na'am zupibig kanɛ ka o ma da nɔki pil o
o pu'adiir malʋŋ dabisir daar la,
daakan la ka o sʋnf da ma'ae hali.

english_text:
What a Beautiful Bride
He Speaks:
1My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
as you look through your veil,
your eyes are those of a dove.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
2Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
3Your lips are crimson cords,
your mouth is shapely;
behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
4Your neck is more graceful
than the tower of David,
decorated with thousands
of warriors' shields.
5Your breasts are perfect;
they are twin deer
feeding among lilies.
6I will hasten to those hills
sprinkled with sweet perfume
and stay there till sunrise.
7My darling, you are lovely
in every way.
8My bride, together
we will leave Lebanon!
We will say goodbye
to the peaks of Mount Amana,
Senir, and Hermon,
where lions and leopards
live in the caves.
9My bride, my very own,
you have stolen my heart!
With one glance from your eyes
and the glow of your necklace,
you have stolen my heart.
10Your love is sweeter than wine;
the smell of your perfume
is more fragrant than spices.
11Your lips are a honeycomb;
milk and honey
flow from your tongue.
Your dress has the aroma
of cedar trees from Lebanon.
12My bride, my very own,
you are a garden, a fountain
closed off to all others.
13Your arms are vines,
covered with delicious fruits
and all sorts of spices—
henna, nard, 14saffron,
calamus, cinnamon,
frankincense, myrrh, and aloes
—all the finest spices.
15You are a spring in the garden,
a fountain of pure water,
and a refreshing stream
from Mount Lebanon.
She Speaks:
16Let the north wind blow,
the south wind too!
Let them spread the aroma
of my garden,
so the one I love
may enter and taste
its delicious fruits.
translation_text:
Dau la:
1M ya'ambʋnnɛɛ, fʋ vɛnl hali!
Fʋ sid vɛnl, oo!
Fʋ nini banɛ ka fʋ ligil la vɛnli nwɛnɛ dawan nini.
Fʋ zuobid la sɔbigi nwɛnɛ bʋʋsi
naan Gilead zuorin la wa'adi sigid na.
2Fʋ nyina la pɛlignɛ nwɛnɛ pɛpielʋg kɔnbid,
nwɛnɛ pɛ'og kanɛ ka ba sʋʋ o ka o nan dʋt na.
Baa yinne kae pʋ mɔr o bu'arɛ,
baa yinne pʋ zi'e o kɔn'ɔkɔn'.
3Fʋ nɔŋgban la mu'oenɛ vɛnl wʋʋ pien gum,
ka fʋ pian'ad la mɔr nɔŋilim.
Fʋ gbɛ'og la nie bɔbigin la naa vɛnl
ka gbilisi nwɛnɛ taba kiig.
4Fʋ niŋgɔɔnr la nwɛnɛ David girimbisa
linɛ ka ba mɛɛ li ka li vɛnl;
ka fʋ kɔr niŋgɔnkɔris
wʋʋ ban ya'an zaba la'ad za'antɔligin si'em la.
5Fʋ bin'isa ayi' la zi'enɛ sappi,
li nwɛnɛ walbibis banɛ an liiba
banɛ bɛ na'apu'a-kʋ-si'is-ku'om teŋsʋkʋ ɔnbid yam.
6Ya'a ka' bɛog ti nie
ka zibisim la gaadɛ,
m na bɛ zuoya la zin'ikanɛ ka bʋnnyubisa
linɛ an frankinsens nɛ mir bɛ la ni.
7M ya'ambʋnnɛɛ, fʋ vɛnlim la bɛ nɛ zin'ig wʋsa;
fʋ pʋ mɔr gba'arɛ.
8Dɔllim ka ti yi Lebanon teŋin,
ɛɛn, m pu'apaalaa, dɔllim ka ti yi Lebanon na.
Kɛl ka ti la'am naan Amana zuorin la sig na,
ka naan Senir nɛ Hemon zuoya la zugɔ sig na.
Yim gbigima buugin la
nɛ zuoya linɛ an wɛbaas gbɛɛnsir la ni.
9Fʋ fɛndigi m ya'am, m taʋn nɛ m pu'apaala;
fʋ fɛndigi m ya'am.
Fʋ gɔsig yimmʋ,
nɛ fʋ niŋgɔnkɔris la fɛndigi m ya'am.
10M taʋn nɛ m pu'apaala,
fʋ nɔŋir la mɔr ya'amlɛog!
Fʋ nɔŋir la malisi gaad damalisiŋ,
ka fʋ tudaari la nyuug malisi gaad bʋnnyubisa wʋsa!
11M pu'apaala,
fʋ nɔɔr malisi nwɛnɛ sinkpaam tu'asid nɛ;
bin'isim nɛ siind bɛɛ fʋ zilimin la.
Fʋ fuug la nyuug nwɛnɛ bʋnnyubisa
nɛ li buudi wʋsa banɛ bɛ Lebanon teŋin nɛ.
12M pu'apaal nɛ m taʋn,
fʋ nwɛnɛ lɔmbɔn'ɔg ka ba yɔɔ lɛbis;
fʋ anɛ bulkanɛ bɛ pʋʋgin,
bulkanɛ ka ba taasi li nɔɔr.
13Fʋ tiis pɔɔg la anɛ pomanganɛt linɛ vɛnl.
Li wan walsʋma ka mɔr nyuug linɛ malis.
14Bʋnnyubisa tiis buudi wʋsa bɛɛ ani,
la'an nɛ frankinsens nɛ mir
nɛ bʋnnyubisa banɛ bɛ wʋsa.
15Fʋ anɛ lɔmbɔn'ɔgin bulkanɛ ka ku'om bʋnnɛ
naanid Lebanon zuoya zugʋ pʋbidi sigid na.
Pu'asadir la:
16Pɛbisʋg kanɛ yit ya-datiuŋ naa, duom!
Pɛbiskanɛ yit ya-dagɔbʋgɔ, kem na!
Lɔmmi pɛbisim gɛɛlini m lɔmbɔn'ɔg la,
ka li nyuug la widigi gilig zin'ig wʋsa.
M ya'am bʋnnɛ, kemi m lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la na
lɛmim tiis la walmalisa linɛ bɛɛ ani la.

english_text:
He Speaks:
1My bride, my very own,
I come to my garden
and enjoy its spices.
I eat my honeycomb and honey;
I drink my wine and milk.
Their Friends Speak:
Eat and drink until
you are drunk with love.
Another Dream
She Speaks:
2I was asleep, but dreaming:
The one I love was at the door,
knocking and saying,
“My darling, my very own,
my flawless dove,
open the door for me!
My head is drenched
with evening dew.”
3But I had already undressed
and bathed my feet.
Should I dress again
and get my feet dirty?
4Then my darling's hand
reached to open the latch,
and my heart stood still.
5When I rose to open the door,
my hands and my fingers
dripped with perfume.
6And I yearned for him
while he spoke to me,
but when I opened the door,
my darling had disappeared.
I searched and shouted,
but I could not find him—
there was no answer.
7Then I was found by the guards
patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.

ka m ya'am pin'ili tuod o yɛla.

ba daa nyɛɛm,

ka sɔbigi nwɛnɛ agaung.

english_text:
He Speaks:
1My bride, my very own,
I come to my garden
and enjoy its spices.
I eat my honeycomb and honey;
I drink my wine and milk.
Their Friends Speak:
Eat and drink until
you are drunk with love.
Another Dream
She Speaks:
2I was asleep, but dreaming:
The one I love was at the door,
knocking and saying,
“My darling, my very own,
my flawless dove,
open the door for me!
My head is drenched
with evening dew.”
3But I had already undressed
and bathed my feet.
Should I dress again
and get my feet dirty?
4Then my darling's hand
reached to open the latch,
and my heart stood still.
5When I rose to open the door,
my hands and my fingers
dripped with perfume.
6And I yearned for him
while he spoke to me,
but when I opened the door,
my darling had disappeared.
I searched and shouted,
but I could not find him—
there was no answer.
7Then I was found by the guards
patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.
They beat me up
and stripped off my robe.
8Young women of Jerusalem,
if you find the one I love,
please say to him,
“She is weak with desire.”
Their Friends Speak:
9Most beautiful of women,
why is the one you love
more special than others?
Why do you ask us
to tell him how you feel?
She Speaks:
10He is handsome and healthy,
the most outstanding
among ten thousand.
11His head is purest gold;
his hair is wavy,
black as a raven.
12His eyes are a pair of doves
bathing in a stream
flowing with milk.
13His face is a garden
of sweet-smelling spices;
his lips are lilies
dripping with perfume.
14His arms are branches of gold
covered with jewels;
his body is ivory
decorated with sapphires.
15His legs are columns of marble
on feet of gold.
He stands there majestic
like Mount Lebanon
and its choice cedar trees.
16His kisses are sweet.
I desire him so much!
Young women of Jerusalem,
he is my lover and friend.

o bɛ nɛ o kɔn', tusa piiga la sʋʋgin.
11O zug la anɛ sanlim sʋŋ;
o zuobid la nwɛnɛ ba pan'ami li nɛ
ka sɔbigi nwɛnɛ agaung.
12O nini vɛnli nwɛnɛ dawan nɛ
bɛ kɔldaug nɔɔrin.
O nini pɛligi nwɛnɛ bin'isim ka o nɔki sʋʋd nɛ,
ka nwɛnɛ niŋgɔnkɔris ka o kɔr.
13O kpɛnda nwɛnɛ vugus ka ba sɛ bʋnnyubisa tiis
O nɔŋgban nwɛnɛ na'apu'a-kʋ-si'is-ku'om nɛ,
ka mir linɛ nyuugʋ malis hali la tu'asidi yiti lit.
14O kpʋkpama la nwɛnɛ sanlim daad
ka ba nɔki li bulig gɔtiŋin.
O niŋgbina nwɛnɛ wabʋg nyina ka ba saalimi li
ka maali li nɛ kugvɛnla.
15O nɔba nwɛnɛ kugpiela zan'antɔlis
ka ba ba'a li nɛ sanlima zi'esa
Fʋ ya'a nyɛ o, o nwɛnɛ Lebanon zuoya
ka nwɛnɛ na'aziinr wila yaadim si'em la.
16O nɔɔr muakir malis nɛ;
ka o si'el wʋsa mɔr ya'amlɛog.
Jerusalem pu'abaa,
m ya'ambʋn la an si'em nwa'.

english_text:
Their Friends Speak:
1Most beautiful of women,
tell us where he has gone.
Let us help you find him.
She Speaks:
2My darling has gone down
to his garden of spices,
where he will feed his sheep
and gather lilies.
3I am his, and he is mine,
as he feeds his sheep
among the lilies.
He Speaks:
4My dearest, the cities of Tirzah
and Jerusalem
are not as lovely as you.
Your charms are more powerful
than all of the stars
in the heavens.
5Turn away your eyes—
they make me melt.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
6Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
7Behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
8What if I could have
sixty queens, eighty wives,
and thousands of others!
9You would be my only choice,
my flawless dove,
the favorite child
of your mother.
The young women, the queens,
and all the others
tell how excited you are
as they sing your praises:
10“You are as majestic
as the morning sky—
glorious as the moon—
blinding as the sun!
Your charms are more powerful
than all the stars above.”
She Speaks:
11I went down to see if blossoms
were on the walnut trees,
grapevines, and fruit trees.
12But in my imagination
I was suddenly riding
on a glorious chariot.
Their Friends Speak:
13Dance! Dance!
Beautiful woman from Shulam,
let us see you dance!
She Speaks:
Why do you want to see
this woman from Shulam
dancing with the others?
translation_text:
Pu'asadir la taaba:
1Fʋ ya'ambʋn la keŋ yaanɛ,
fʋn kanɛ an pu'a kanɛ vɛnli gat pu'ab wʋsa la?
Fʋ ya'ambʋn la dɔl suokanɛ
ka ti iee o sʋŋi fɔ?
Pu'asadir la:
2M ya'ambʋn pʋn sig o lɔmbɔn'ɔgin
ye o kaae o bʋnnyubisa tiis la.
O ieed yam linɛ bɛɛ ani la
ka la'asid na'apu'a-kʋ-si'is-ku'om vɛnla.
3M ya'ambʋn la anɛ m din ka mam mɛ aan o din;
o gur o pɛ'ɛs la nɛ na'apu'a-kʋ-si'is-ku'om bɛ zin'isi'a la.
Dau la:
4M ya'ambʋnnɛ, fʋ vɛnli nwɛnɛ Tiza tempʋʋg nɛ,
ka fʋ nɔŋilim nwɛnɛ Jerusalem,
ka kpi'em nwɛnɛ zabzabidibi
zanl tuuta tʋ'ʋsid tanp.
5Fɛndigimi fʋ nindaa yii m san'an;
ka fʋ kɛ ka li maligim kpɛn'ɛm.
Fʋ zuobid la sɔbigi nwɛnɛ bʋʋsi
naan Gilead zuorin la wa'adi sigid na nɛ.
6Fʋ nyina la pɛligi nwɛnɛ pɛpielʋg kɔnbid,
nwɛnɛ pɛ'og kanɛ ka ba sʋʋ o ka o nan dʋt na.
Yinne wʋsa mɔr o buar,
yinne kae zi'e o kɔn'ɔkɔn'.
7Fʋ gbɛ'og la nie bɔbigin la vɛnl
ka gbilisi nwɛnɛ taba kiig.
8Na'apu'ab la bɛɛ paae pisyuobʋ,
ka pu'abibis an pisnii,
ka pu'asada zu'oe ka' kallɛ.
9Amaa la'an nɛ wala m dawan la bɛ nɛ o kɔn',
on ma'aa aan o ma bipuŋ,
onɛ ka o du'a o ka nɔŋ o hali la.
Pu'asada la wʋsa nyɛ o ka yɛl ye o anɛ zusʋŋ sɔb;
na'apu'ab nɛ pu'abibis la wʋsa zun'od o.
Pu'asadir la taaba:
10Anɔ'ɔnɛ nwa' nɔɔd wʋʋ bɛogʋ nie?
O pɛligi vɛnl wʋʋ nwadig,
ka nie nwɛnɛ winnig nɛ,
ka nɔɔd o ya'amin wʋʋ nwadbibisi kenna.
Dau la:
11M duoe keŋ tiis banɛ wan ka la'asi zi'e bɛdegʋ la ni
ye m gɔs tipɔla banɛ bɛ bɔn'ɔgin la,
Ye o gɔs vain vanmɛna banɛ busid la
nɛ pomanganɛt la puud bɛɛ.
12Man ti ye m baŋ la,
ka m ya'amlɛog kpɛn'
m nidib zaba tɛrekonamin la.
Pu'asadir taaba la:
13Lɛm na, lɛm na, fʋn kanɛ an Sulam teŋ nida!
Lɛm na lɛm na, ka ti gɔsif!
Dau la:
Bɔ ka ya bɔɔd ye ya gɔs Sulam dim pu'a la
nwɛnɛ onɛ wa'ad banɛ gɔsid la sʋʋginɛ?

english_text:
The Wedding Dance
He Speaks:
1You are a princess,
and your feet are graceful
in their sandals.
Your thighs are works of art,
each one a jewel;
2your navel is a wine glass
filled to overflowing.
Your body is full and slender
like a bundle of wheat
bound together by lilies.
3Your breasts are like twins
of a deer.
4Your neck is like ivory,
and your eyes sparkle
like the pools of Heshbon
by the gate of Bath-Rabbim.
Your nose is beautiful
like Mount Lebanon
above the city of Damascus.
5Your head is held high
like Mount Carmel;
your hair is so lovely
it holds a king prisoner.
6You are very beautiful,
so desirable!
7You are tall and slender
like a palm tree,
and your breasts are full.
8I will climb that tree
and cling to its branches.
I will discover that your breasts
are clusters of grapes,
and that your breath
is the aroma of apples.
9Kissing you is more delicious
than drinking the finest wine.
How wonderful and tasty!
She Speaks:
10My darling, I am yours,
and you desire me.
11Let's stroll through the fields
and sleep in the villages.
12At dawn let's slip out and see
if grapevines and fruit trees
are covered with blossoms.
When we are there,
I will give you my love.
13Perfume from the magic flower
fills the air, my darling.
Right at our doorstep
I have stored up for you
all kinds of tasty fruits.
translation_text:
1Na'ab pu'ayua, fʋ nɔba vɛnl nɛ ta'ada hali,
fʋn na'ab pu'ayua biiga!
Fʋ gbɛya ayi' saalimnɛ vɛnli nwɛnɛ niŋgɔnkɔris,
ka nwɛnɛ onɛ mi' kpi'eb hali kpi'a li nɛ nu'us.
2Fʋ nyu'ug la nwɛnɛ daam nwam kanɛ an gbiliga nɛ
ka damalisiŋ pʋ naadi li pʋʋginɛ.
Fʋ pʋʋr la nwɛnɛ ki dʋʋr
ka na'apu'a-kʋ-si'is-ku'om giligi li.
3Fʋ bin'isa ayi' la zi'enɛ sappi,
li nwɛnɛ walbibis banɛ an liiba
ka bɛ mɔɔd puum teŋsʋkʋ ɔnbid yam.
4Fʋ niŋgɔɔnr la nwɛnɛ zan'antɔlig
ka ba nɔk wabʋg nyina maali li.
Fʋ nini ian'adi pil-pil wʋʋ Hesbon teŋ bɛuŋ
linɛ kpi'e Bafirabim za'anɔɔr la.
Fʋ Nyɔnya la vɛnli nwɛnɛ Lebanon girimbisa
linɛ zi'e kpa' Damaskus tempʋʋg la.
5Fʋ zug la vɛnlim nwɛnɛ Kamel zuor.
Fʋ zuobid la sɔbig nɛ liŋ-liŋ ka nyɛɛn hali;
ka li vɛnlim la na nyaŋi fɛndig na'ab ya'am.
6Fʋ vɛnli hali ka li mɛ narif,
m ya'ambʋnnɛ, fʋ zi'esim la sid paae m ya'am!
7Fʋ zi'esim la nwɛnɛ kpʋkparig tiig,
ka fʋ bin'isa la nwɛnɛ wala nɛ li buudi ka ba la'as.
8Lin ka m ye, “M na dʋ kpʋkparig la
paae kpʋkpara la pɔn'.”
Fʋ bin'isa la nwɛnɛ vain tiig wala nɛ,
ka fʋ vʋ'ʋsʋm la nyuug malisi
nwɛnɛ apʋl wala nyuugʋ malis si'em la,
9ka fʋ nɔɔr nwɛnɛ damalisiŋ nɛ.
Pu'asadir la:
Kɛl ka daam la pʋbi paae m ya'ambʋn la san'an,
dɔlisidi sigid o nɔŋgban nɛ o nyina ni.
10M anɛ m ya'ambʋn la din
ka o ya'am bɔɔd si'el la an mam ma'aa.
11Kem na, m ya'ambʋnnɛɛ, kɛl ka ti keŋ kpikpɛŋ,
kɛl ka ti keŋ teŋkpɛŋi gbɛɛn ani.
12Kɛl ka ti isigi keŋ vain tiis pʋʋgin la
ka gɔs ye tiis la bus ya, bɛɛ?
Ka pomanganɛt la ya'a puud,
ani ka m na pa'ali fʋ m nɔŋir.
13Tipuum banɛ nyuugʋ malis hali la
tiig nɛ zin'ig wʋsa
ka bɛɛ ti dɔɔg za'anɔɔrin la.
Bʋnkʋda nɛ bʋmpaala wʋsa bɛ,
ka m la'asi ba wʋsa digili gurif, m ya'am bʋnnɛ.

english_text:
If Only You and I …
She Speaks:
1If you were my brother,
I could kiss you
whenever we happen to meet,
and no one would say
I did wrong.
2I could take you to the home
of my mother,
who taught me all I know.
I would give you delicious wine
and fruit juice as well.
3Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
4Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Their Friends Speak:
5Who is this young woman
coming in from the desert
and leaning on the shoulder
of the one she loves?
She Speaks:
I stirred up your passions
under the apple tree
where you were born.
6Always keep me in your heart
and wear this bracelet
to remember me by.
The passion of love
bursting into flame
is more powerful than death,
stronger than the grave.
7Love cannot be drowned
by oceans or floods.
It cannot be bought—
any offer would be scorned
no matter how great.
Their Friends Speak:
8We have a little sister
whose breasts
are not yet formed.
If someone asks to marry her,
what should we do?
9She isn't a wall
that we can defend
behind a silver shield.
Neither is she a room
that we can protect
behind a wooden door.
She Speaks:
10I am a wall around a city,
my breasts are towers,
and just looking at me
brings him great pleasure.
11Solomon has a vineyard
at Baal-Hamon,
which he rents to others
for a thousand pieces
of silver each.
12My vineyard is mine alone!
Solomon can keep his silver
and the others can keep
their share of the profits.
He Speaks:
13You are in the garden
with friends all around.
Let me hear your voice!
She Speaks:
14Hurry to me, my darling!
Run faster than a deer
to mountains of spices.
translation_text:
1M naan bɔɔdin ye fʋ aannɛ m taʋn
kanɛ mu'a m ma bin'isir!
Li ya'a aan na la ka m nyɛɛ nɛf zin'isi'a,
m naan muakinɛ fʋ nɔɔr,
ka sɔ' kʋ nɛ'ɛsi ma.
2M naan gaadini fʋ tuon
ka dɔlli fʋ kuli m ma yin.
M ma kanɛ pa'alim la san'an.
M naan tisi nɛf daam kanɛ nyuugʋ malis ka fʋ nu,
danmalisʋŋ kanɛ ka m nwiaki yisi m mɛŋ pomanganɛt tiis wala ni la.
3O nɔk o dagɔbʋg nu'ug la kʋki m zug,
ka o datiuŋ nu'ug la kuakim.
4Yanam Jerusalem pu'asada,
pɔɔmi ye ya kʋ kɛ ti taab bɔɔb kʋkɔr duoe
ka li saŋa nam pʋ paae.
Pu'asadir la taaba:
5Anɔ'ɔnɛ nwa' yi pipirisin kenna
ka nɔk o mɛŋi dɛllim o ya'ambʋn la?
Pu'asadir la:
Apʋl walsʋma tiig la gbinnin ka m duof;
ani ka fʋ ma da tʋki fʋ pʋʋg,
ani ka o da lɛn sa'ae du'af.
6Fɛndigimi fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛr sɔ' wʋsa ni
ka kɛ ka fʋ ya'am bɛ man ni ma'aa,
da lɛm gban'e sɔ' nu'ugɔ sɛɛ mam ma'aa;
ka nɔŋir kpi'emi nwɛnɛ kum nɛ,
li ya'amlɛog mɛ mɔr paŋ wʋʋ kpi'im teŋ.
Li la'aŋid nwɛnɛ bugum nɛ,
ka diti nwɛnɛ bugum pielim dit nɛ paŋ si'em la.
7Ku'om bɛdegʋ kʋ nyaŋi pie nɔŋiri basɛ
bɛɛ kɔldaad ku'om nyaŋi pʋbigi li gaadɛ.
Sɔ' ya'a nɔk o yin kpan'am wʋsa ye o da' nɔŋir,
ba na nɛ'ɛs o hali.
Pu'a la tanp:
8Ti mɔri ti taʋn bil,
ka o bin'isa nam pʋ nɔbigɛ.
Ti na niŋi ti taʋn la yɛla wala
daakanɛ ka dau kena ye o bɔɔd o?
9O ya'a aan zaŋguom,
ti naan nɔkin anzurifa mɛɛ gilig o.
O ya'a lɛn aan nɛ kʋlʋŋ,
ti naan nɔkin na'aziinr dalamma maali lus o lɛbis.
Pu'asadir la:
10Mam anɛ zaŋguom,
ka m bin'isa la zi'e sappi
wʋʋ dɔbanɛ wa'am nɛ.
O nini gɔsidim nɛ ka pʋ tigida
ka li nwɛnɛ ninkanɛ kɛ ka o ya'am digin.
11Solomon mɔr vain tiis pɔɔg ka li bɛ Baal-Hamon teŋin;
o nɔki li tis nidib ye ba di'e li gur ka tʋm.
Sɔ' wʋsa ya'a pɔn' tiis la wala naae
ba na mɔr anzurifa ligidi tusir-tusir na tis o.
12Amaa mam mɛŋ vain pɔɔg anɛ m mɛŋ din;
kɛl ka Solomon mɔr o anzurifa tusir-tusir la,
ka banɛ gur la mɛ mɔri ba kɔbisyi' yi la.
Dau la:
13Fʋn kanɛ bɛ lɔmbɔn'ɔgin
ka fʋ zuanam nɛ fʋ tʋmtʋmnib bɛɛ fʋ san'an la,
kɛl ka m wʋmi fʋ kʋkɔr!
Pu'asadir la:
14M sabua onɛ ka m nɔŋ hali,
kem tɔ'ɔtɔ na nwɛnɛ mɔlif,
bɛɛ waldaug kanɛ an bʋmpɔlli bɛ zuoya ni,
zin'ikanɛ ka bʋnnyubisa bɛ la.

english_text:
1 I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz.
And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah:
A Guilty Nation
2The Lord has said,
“Listen, heaven and earth!
The children I raised
have turned against me.
3Oxen and donkeys know
who owns and feeds them,
but my people won't ever learn.”
4Israel, you are a sinful nation
loaded down with guilt.
You are wicked and corrupt
and have turned from the Lord,
the holy God of Israel.
5Why be punished more?
Why not give up your sin?
Your head is badly bruised,
and you are weak all over.
6From your head to your toes
there isn't a healthy spot.
Bruises, cuts, and open sores
go without care
or oil to ease the pain.
A Country in Ruins
7Your country lies in ruins;
your towns are in ashes.
Foreigners and strangers
take and destroy your land
while you watch.
8Enemies surround Jerusalem,
alone like a hut
in a vineyard
or in a cucumber field.
9 Zion would have disappeared
like Sodom and Gomorrah,
if the Lord All-Powerful
had not let a few
of its people survive.
Justice, Not Sacrifices
10You are no better
than the leaders and people
of Sodom and Gomorrah!
So listen to the Lord God:
11 “Your sacrifices
mean nothing to me.
I am sick of your offerings
of rams and choice cattle;
I don't like the blood
of bulls or lambs or goats.
12“Who asked you to bring all this
when you come to worship me?
Stay out of my temple!
13Your sacrifices are worthless,
and your incense disgusting.
I can't stand the evil you do
on your New Moon Festivals
or on your Sabbaths
and other times of worship.
14I hate your New Moon Festivals
and all others as well.
They are a heavy burden
I am tired of carrying.
15“No matter how much you pray,
I won't listen.
You are too violent.
16Wash yourselves clean!
I hate your filthy deeds.
Stop doing wrong
17and learn to live right.
See that justice is done.
Defend widows and orphans
and help the oppressed.”
An Invitation from the Lord
18I, the Lord, invite you
to come and talk it over.
Your sins are scarlet red,
but they will be whiter
than snow or wool.
19If you willingly obey me,
the best crops in the land
will be yours.
20But if you turn against me,
your enemies will kill you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
21Jerusalem, you are like
an unfaithful wife.
Once your judges were honest
and your people lived right;
now you are a city
full of murderers.
22Your silver is fake,
and your wine
is watered down.
23Your leaders have rejected me
to become friends of crooks;
your rulers are looking
for gifts and bribes.
Widows and orphans
never get a fair trial.
24I am the Lord All-Powerful,
the mighty ruler of Israel,
and I make you a promise:
You are now my enemy,
and I will show my anger
by taking revenge on you.
25I will punish you terribly
and burn away everything
that makes you unfit
to worship me.
26Jerusalem, I will choose
judges and advisors
like those you had before.
Your new name will be
“Justice and Faithfulness.”
The Lord Will Save Jerusalem
27Jerusalem, you will be saved
by showing justice;
Zion's people who turn to me
will be saved
by doing right.
28But those rebellious sinners
who turn against me, the Lord,
will all disappear.
29You will be made ashamed
of those groves of trees
where you worshiped idols.
30You will be like a grove of trees
dying in a drought.
31Your strongest leaders
will be like dry wood
set on fire by their idols.
No one will be able to help,
as they all go up in flames.
translation_text:
1 Juda nɛ Jerusalem yɛla da nie pa'al Azaya onɛ da an Amoz biig la ka o nyɛ, saŋkanɛ ka Uzia nɛ Jotam nɛ Ahaz nɛ Hezekia da di Juda teŋ na'am tuunl taaba la.
Zugsɔb la sa'al o nidib la yɛla
2Azaya da yɛl Zugsɔb la labaar ye,
“Arezana, wʋmma!
Teŋgbauŋɔ, fʋn mɛ kɛlisim!
M ugus biis ka ba duoe na
amaa ka zan'asi m nɔɔr.
3Na'araug mi' o daan,
ka bʋŋ mɛ mi' o yam daka zin'ig,
amaa Israel dim zi';
man nidib la pʋ mɔr gbin gban'arɛ.”
4Ya anɛ buudkanɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim,
ka an nimbanɛ tʋʋma pʋ dɔl suorɛ,
ka wiakid tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd,
ka an bibanɛ bɔɔd bugusim,
ka zan'as Zugsɔb la.
Ya nɛ'ɛs Israel dim Wina'am Onɛ An Kasi la,
ka fɛndigi lɛb nya'aŋ ka bid o kudug.
5Bɔ ka ya lɛm bɔɔd bʋ'ʋd ya'asɛ?
Bɔ ka ya nan kpɛn zan'as ka aandi yita?
Ya zut wʋsa pu'alim nɛ,
ka ya ya'am wʋsa fɛndig.
6Din yii ya nɔba ni keŋ dʋʋ ya zugin laafi kae,
li anɛ sapu'ad nɛ fɛn'ɛd ma'aa.
Ba pʋ pie li bɛɛ viligi li piennɛ
bɛɛ ba ma' li nɛ kpaam.
7Nidib widig ya ka basi ya teŋ la.
Bugum dii ya tempʋʋd la.
Saam kena buni ya pɔɔd la ya nini ni,
ka basi ya zaalim nɛ namisʋg.
8Ba bas Zion tempʋʋg la ka li kpɛlimmi li kɔn',
wʋʋ Fuug Sʋgʋr kanɛ bɛ pɔɔgin,
bɛɛ linɛ zi'e yir sʋʋgin nɛ,
ala ka tempʋʋg la zi'e ka bi'emnam giligi li.
9Ya'a ka' Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la kɛ ka ti sieba vʋ'ʋgɛ,
ti teŋ la wʋsa naan nwɛnɛ Sodom teŋ nɛ,
ti naan nwɛnɛ Gomora dim nɛ.
Ba Wina'am pʋ'ʋsʋg pʋ dɔl suorɛ
10Yanam banɛ an wʋʋ Sodom na'anamaa,
kɛlisimi Zugsɔb la labaar!
Wʋmmi ti Wina'am wada la,
yanam Gomora dima!
11Zugsɔb la yɛl ye,
“Ya maana banɛ an bɛdegʋ la an bɔɔ tis mam?”
Mam di'esi ya pɛraad nɛ bʋnkɔnbid banɛ nɔb
ka ya mɔri maan nyu'or maana la tig.
Mam pʋ mɔr ya'amlɛog nɛ na'araad nɛ pɛribis nɛ bʋʋs ziim.
12Yanamɛ ɛɛnti kɛɛn m san'an na la,
anɔ'ɔnɛ yɛti ya ye ya mɔr nɛ'ɛnam na?
Bɔ ka ya giilimi m Pʋ'ʋsim Yir zakin la?
13Da lɛm mɔri malima linɛ ka' gbin la kennɛ m san'an naa.
M kis maan banɛ ka ya nyu'od la.
Ya nwadpaalig nɛ ya Vʋ'ʋsʋm Daar malima la ka' gbinnɛ;
m yaama yi nɛ ya la'as banɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la'asʋg la.
14Mam kisnɛ ya nwadpaalig malima
nɛ malima banɛ ka ya zi'el la.
Li daamidim nɛ, ka lieb ziidi tisim,
ka m zii li gɛn.
15Ya ya'a ʋki ya nu'us agɔla ye ya pʋ'ʋs,
m na fɛndigi m nindaa ka basi ya.
Hali ya ya'a sɔs si'el wʋsa m kʋ kɛlisɛ,
ya nu'usi pɛ'ɛl nɛ ziim la zug.
16Pieminɛ ya mɛŋ ka maali ya mɛŋ nyain.
Mɔri nɛ ya tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la tɔɔmi m san'an.
Basimi tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd;
17zamisimi tʋmi linɛ an sʋm,
ka iee zin'ikanɛ ka ba kad saria nɛ sida.
Sʋŋim banɛ ka ba mugusidi ba la,
ka sa'al banɛ wɛbidi ba la.
Sʋŋim banɛ an kpiibis la mɛn,
ka tu'as pʋkɔnya antu'a nɛ yɛlmɛŋir.
18Zugsɔb la yɛl ye,
“Kemi na ka ti la'asi tɛn'ɛs ka pian' li yɛla.
La'an nɛ ya tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la miligi mu'oe si'em la,
ya na lɛm pɛligi nwɛnɛ sakuga nɛ,
la'an nɛ lin kɛ ka ya miligi si' la,
ya na lɛm pɛligi nwɛnɛ gungum nɛ.
19Ya ya'a siaki m nɔɔr sʋ'ʋŋa,
ya na nyɛ disʋma teŋ la nii di.
20Amaa ya ya'a zan'asim,
ba na kʋʋ ya nɛ sʋ'ʋg zaba ni.”
Zugsɔb la nɔɔri pian' si'em la.
Jerusalem dim tʋbpʋwʋmnim yɛla
21Gɔsim teŋ sʋŋ la yʋ'ʋn nwɛnɛ pu'agɔɔndir nɛ.
O da anɛ sida nɛ pʋpielim sɔb,
amaa ka yʋ'ʋn lieb ninkʋʋd.
22Ya anzurifanam la liebnɛ zaalim;
daam kanɛ ka ya nɔŋ la, ba yaligi li nɛ ku'om.
23Ya tuongatib la zan'asi m nɔɔr,
ka ba zuanam an na'ayiis.
Ba wʋsa nɔŋ nɛ nidib la na da' ba,
ka zɔti dɔl nidibi bɔɔd ye ba di'es piini.
Ba pʋ pian'adi sʋŋid kpiibisɛ,
ka mɛ pʋ kɛlisid pʋkɔnya pian'adɛ.
24Dinzugɔ, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la,
Paŋ Sɔb onɛ sʋ'oe Israel la, pian' ya nyain ye;
“Alazugɔ, m na nyɛ yɔlisim m dataas san'an
ka yɔɔ m bi'emnam la sam.
25M na zan'asi ya,
ka siligi ya wʋʋ kpaam nɛ,
ka yis dian'ad linɛ bɛɛ ya san'an la.
26M na kɛ ka ya sariakatib maligim bɛ nwɛnɛ kʋdimin la,
ka banɛ san'anɛ ya la bɛ wʋʋ pin'ilʋgʋnɛ da an si'em la.
Lin nya'aŋ la ba na buonnɛ ya ye, ‘Pʋpielim Teŋ dim’,
ka ya teŋ yʋ'ʋr na an Tempʋʋg kanɛ an Sida.”
27Zugsɔb na faaɛn Zion teŋ nɛ sida,
banɛ siak ka lɛb na la na nyɛ faangir pʋpielim.
28Amaa o na san'am banɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim nɛ banɛ zan'as o la,
ka banɛ pʋ siak o la na bɔdig.
29Nyan na dii ya,
yanamɛ mɔr ya'amlɛog ye ya pʋ'ʋsid tiis la zug.
Ba na faki ya zut
yanamɛ gaŋ lɔmbɔn'ɔd sieba wɔ'ɔgid la zug.
30Ya na nwɛnɛ tikanɛ ka li vaand kʋdig ka sʋʋgid nɛ,
ka nwɛnɛ lɔmbɔn'ɔg kanɛ ka' ku'om.
31Nintitada la na nwɛnɛ sa'ad,
ka bugum na diti ba tʋʋma linɛ an bɛ'ɛd la
ka sɔ' kae na kpiisɛ.

english_text:
Peace That Lasts Forever
1This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
2In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills;
every nation will rush to it.
3Many people will come and say,
“Let's go to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
4 He will settle arguments
between nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never make war
or attack one another.
5People of Israel, let's live
by the light of the Lord.
Following Sinful Customs
6Our Lord, you have deserted
your people, Israel,
because they follow customs
of nations from the east.
They worship Philistine gods
and are close friends
of foreigners.
7They have endless treasures
of silver and gold;
they have countless horses
and war chariots.
8Everywhere in the country
they worship the idols
they have made.
9And so, all of them
will be ashamed and disgraced.
Don't forgive them!
A Day of Judgment
10 Every one of you,
go hide among the rocks
and in the ground,
because the Lord is fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious.
11When the Lord comes,
everyone who is proud
will be made humble,
and the Lord alone
will be honored.
12The Lord All-Powerful
has chosen a day
when those who are proud
and conceited
will be put down.
13The tall and towering
cedars of Lebanon
will be destroyed.
So will the oak trees of Bashan,
14all high mountains and hills,
15every strong fortress,
16all the seagoing ships,
and every beautiful boat.
17When that day comes,
everyone who is proud
will be put down.
Only the Lord will be honored.
18Idols will be gone for good.
19You had better hide
in caves and holes—
the Lord will be fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious
when he comes to terrify
people on earth.
20On that day everyone will throw
to the moles and bats
their idols of silver and gold
they made to worship.
21The Lord will be fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious
when he comes to terrify
people on earth—
they will hide in caves
and in the hills.
22Stop trusting the power
of humans.
They are all going to die,
so how can they help?
translation_text:
Zugsɔb zuor la yɛla
(Mai 4:1-3)
1Amoz biig Azaya da nyɛ si'eli zaŋi keŋ Juda teŋgbauŋ nɛ Jerusalem tempʋʋg yɛla la nwa':
2“Naar saŋa la,
zuokanɛ ka Zugsɔb Yir zi'e li zug la na zi'en kiŋ-kiŋ.
Li na wa'am hali gaad kʋkʋna la wʋsa.
Ka tɛɛns wʋsa nidib na la'as anina pʋ'ʋs.
3Nidib bɛdegʋ na la'as taaba yɛl ye,
‘Kemi na ka ti keŋ Zugsɔb zuorin la,
kem na ka ti keŋ Jakob Wina'am Yin la.
O na pa'ali ti o suori an si'em
ka ti na dɔlli li sʋ'ʋŋa.’
Wina'am wada na yit Zion zuorin,
ka Zugsɔb la nɔzi'elʋg na naan Jerusalem teŋin na ka ti siaki li.
4O na an tɛɛns wʋsa sariakat
ka na maal buudi wʋsa pian'adi tisi ba.
Ba na zan' ba zaba sʋ'ʋsi maal kʋnya,
ka nɔki ba kpana la maal gɔn'ɔd.
Ba kʋ lɛn tʋ'ʋsid tanp
bɛɛ ba zamisid zaba ya'asɛ.
5 Jakob yidima, kemi na!
Kɛlli ka ti keŋ Zugsɔb nɛɛsim la ni.”
Zugsɔb dabisir la yɛla
6Nɔdi'es Azaya n da lɛn yɛl si'eli nwa':
“Zugsɔba, fʋ basi fʋ nimbanɛ an Jakob yidim la.
Ba dɔlnɛ ya-nya'aŋ dim buudi malima la wʋsa,
ba bʋgʋdnɛ wʋʋ Filistia dimi bʋgʋd si'em la,
ka maan zuod nɛ nimbanɛ zi' fʋn Wina'am.
7Anzurifa nɛ sanlima pɛ'ɛli ba teŋin la;
ba kpan'am la pʋ mɔr bɛnnɛ.
Ba teŋ la pɛ'ɛli nɛ widi
ka ba tɛrekonam pʋ mɔr bɛnnɛ.
8Ba teŋ la pɛ'ɛl nɛ bada,
ka ba iginidi wɔ'ɔgid linɛ ka ba mɛŋ maal
ka mɔr girima tisidi ba nu'usi maal si'el.
9Alazug sigisimi ba wʋsa teŋin ka kɛ ka ba di nyan.
Da kɛɛ ba taali basɛ.
10 Kem kpɛn' tampinlɛma ni
ka tu bʋmbu'ad teŋinɛ su'a ya mɛŋ
Zugsɔb sʋnpɛɛn la nɛ o na'am paŋ la zug.
11Dau kanɛ an tita'alim sɔb la nini na ma'ae,
ka saalib nyɛɛsim na sie,
Zugsɔb la ma'aa ka ba na dʋ'ʋs o daakan la.
12Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la zi'el dabisiri
gur banɛ mɔr nyɛɛsim ka dʋ'ʋsidi ba mɛŋ la.
Ninkanɛ wʋsa nwɛ'ɛd o nyɔ'ɔg la na sig teŋin.
13O na san'am Lebanon na'aziinr tibanɛ wa'am la
nɛ tititada banɛ bɛ Basan ka dʋ'ʋsidi ba mɛŋ la,
14nɛ zuotitada wʋsa
nɛ kʋkʋna banɛ wa'am la,
15nɛ girimbisanam banɛ kpi'em la wʋsa,
nɛ suak dɔtitada banɛ zaŋguoma wa'am la,
16nɛ anrima banɛ ka ba mɔri ken lallisa kpiisid,
nɛ anrinvɛnla la wʋsa.
17Dau kanɛ an tita'alim sɔb la nini na ma'ae,
ka saalib nyɛɛsim na sie.
Zugsɔb la ma'aa ka ba na dʋ'ʋs o daakan la,
18ka bada la wʋsa na bɔdig nyain.
19Nidib na zɔɔ keŋ kpɛn' tampinlɛma ni
ka tu bʋmbu'ad teŋinɛ su'a ba mɛŋ,
Zugsɔb sʋnpɛɛn la nɛ o na'am paŋ la zug,
saŋkan ka o na duoe dam teŋgbauŋ la.
20Daakan la, nidib na nɔki ba anzurifa bada
nɛ ba sanlima wina banɛ ka ba maali pʋ'ʋsid la
lɔbi tis dayuud nɛ zinzana la.
21Ba na zɔɔ kpɛn' tampinlɛma ni
nɛ tampinyɔ'ɔdin ye ba su'a ba mɛŋ,
Zugsɔb sʋnpɛɛn la nɛ o na'am paŋ la zug,
saŋkan ka o na duoe dam teŋgbauŋ la.
22Da lɛn nɔki fʋ ti'iri niŋ ninsaal
onɛ vʋ'ʋsʋm pʋ lal ka bɛɛ o nyɔnya ni la.
O ka' vɔɔnr hali baa bi'elaa.”

english_text:
Judgment on Jerusalem and Judah
1The mighty Lord All-Powerful
is going to take away
from Jerusalem and Judah
everything you need—
your bread and water,
* 2soldiers and heroes,
judges and prophets,
leaders and army officers,
3officials and advisors,
fortunetellers and others
who tell the future.
4He will let children and babies
become your rulers.
5You will each be cruel
to friends and neighbors.
Young people will insult
their elders;
no one will show respect
to those who deserve it.
6Some of you will grab hold
of a relative and say,
“You still have a coat.
Be our leader and rule
this pile of ruins.”
7But the answer will be,
“I can't do you any good.
Don't make me your leader.
There's no food or clothing
left in my house.”
8Jerusalem and Judah,
you rebelled against
your glorious Lord—
your words and your actions,
made you stumble and fall.
9The look on your faces shows
that you are sinful as Sodom,
and you don't try to hide it.
You are in for trouble,
and you have brought it all
on yourselves.
The Wrong Kind of Leaders
10Tell those who obey God,
“You're very fortunate—
you will be rewarded
for what you have done.”
11Tell those who disobey,
“You're in big trouble—
what you did to others
will come back to you.”
12Though you are God's people,
you are ruled and abused
by women and children.
You are confused by leaders
who guide you
down the wrong path.
13The Lord is ready to accuse
and judge all nations.
14He will even judge
you rulers and leaders
of his own nation.
You destroyed his vineyard
and filled your houses
by robbing the poor.
15The Lord All-Powerful says,
“You have crushed my people
and rubbed in the dirt
the faces of the poor.”
The Women of Jerusalem
16The Lord says:
The women of Jerusalem
are proud and strut around,
winking shamelessly.
They wear anklets that jingle
and call attention
to the way they walk.
17But I, the Lord, will cover
their heads with sores,
and I will uncover
their private parts.
18-23When that day comes, I will take away from those women all the fine jewelry they wear on their ankles, heads, necks, ears, arms, noses, fingers, and on their clothes. I will remove their veils, their belts, their perfume, their magic charms, their royal robes, and all their fancy dresses, hats, and purses.
24In place of perfume,
there will be a stink;
in place of belts,
there will be ropes;
in place of fancy hairdos,
they will have bald heads.
Instead of expensive clothes,
they will wear sackcloth;
instead of beauty,
they will have ugly scars.
25The fighting men of Jerusalem
will be killed in battle.
26The city will mourn
and sit in the dirt,
emptied of its people.
translation_text:
Jerusalem nɛ Juda sariakadib
1Gɔsima, nannanna, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la bɔɔd ye o faaɛnnɛ sʋŋir kanɛ bɛɛ tis Jerusalem nɛ Juda la; linɛ an diib bɛɛ ku'om wʋsa,
2nɛ banɛ an gandaad nɛ zabzabidib la,
nɛ sariakatib nɛ nɔdi'esidib,
nɛ ba'akɔn dim nɛ kpɛɛmnam,
3nɛ soogianam banɛ sʋ'oe nidib pisnunu
nɛ yʋ'ʋr dim la wʋsa,
nɛ banɛ sa'an nidib nɛ banɛ mi' tʋʋma hali la,
nɛ banɛ tʋm tiim tʋʋma la wʋsa.
4M na kɛ ka na'akimbibis aan ba kpɛɛmnam,
ka bilies sʋ'oe ba.
5Nidib na mugusid taaba.
Dau na zabid nɛ o tiraan
ka nid nɛ o kpi'a na zabid nɛ taaba.
Biis na duoe ziem ninkʋda,
ka tadimnam mɛ zan'as banɛ aan ba kpɛɛmnam nɔɔr.
6Saŋa kenna ka nid na gban'e o ba'abiig
o saam yin ka yɛl o ye,
“Fʋn mɔr fuug,
alazug fʋnɛ na sʋ'oe ti,
ka maal dabɔɔg nwa' yɛla tisi ti!”
7Amaa o na tans agɔla ka lɛbis ye,
“Mam pɔya mɛnɛ, m pʋ mɔr paŋ kanɛ na nyaŋi sʋŋɛ!
Mam pʋ mɔr diib bɛɛ fuudi m yinnɛ;
Da nɔk mam ye m sʋ'oe nidib la!”
8Jerusalem yidig nɛ,
ka Juda bɔɔd liig.
Bɔzugɔ, ba pian'ad nɛ ba tʋʋma ka' sʋm tis Zugsɔb la,
ka ba mɛ ki'is Zugsɔb na'am girima la.
9Ban gɔsid si'em la pa'al ye ba tʋm taal.
Ba tʋmmi ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd paalʋ ni wʋʋ Sodom dim nɛ.
Yɛl bɛɛ ba zugin,
ba mɛŋ tʋʋma kɛt ka ba paam tʋbtɛɛgir.
10Yɛlim pʋpielim dim la ye,
si'el wʋsa na an sʋ'ʋŋa tisi ba
bɔzugɔ, ba na dii ba tʋʋm sʋma la nyɔɔd.
11Yɛl bɛ bugusnam la zugin,
yɛltɔɔg na paae ba.
Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka ba tʋm la, lin ka ba na lɛbisi yɔɔ ba.
12Biisi mugusidi m nidib la
ka pu'ab sʋ'oe ba.
M nidiba, banɛ guri ya la na bɔdisi ya,
ka fɛndigi ya yis suorin la.
13Zugsɔb la zin'inɛ o zin'isigin kɔɔtʋ ni.
O duoe zi'en ye o kad o nidib la saria.
14Zugsɔb la kad kpɛɛmnam nɛ tuongatib la saria
ka kʋʋsi ba wʋsa bɛ'ɛd ye,
“Ya di sɔ' wʋsa pɔɔg zʋʋd,
ka tadimnam la'abanɛ ka ya faaɛn la bɛɛ ya yaan.
15Ya gban'e ye bɔ ka san'amidi m nidib la?
Bɛɛ bɔ ka ya nɛɛmidi ba wʋʋ zɔ'ɔm?”
Zugsɔb Wina'am Paŋtita'ar Sɔb pian'ʋkʋ la.
Jerusalem pu'ab yɛla
16Zugsɔb la lɛn yɛl ye,
“Zion pu'ab la anɛ nyɛɛsim dim;
ba ken ka dʋ'ʋsidi ba ningɔnya
ka ba gɔsig pa'an ye ba anɛ pu'agɔɔnda.
Ba ken ka zia'asidi ba niŋgbina bɔɔd ye nidib gɔs,
ka ba nɔba baans kum saiin-saiin.”
17Dinzugɔ, Zugsɔb la na kɛ ka Zion pu'ab la zut mɔr fɛn'ɛd.
O na kɛ ka ba zut la kɔn.
18Dabisir kenna ka o na yisi ba la'avɛnla la, baans banɛ ka ba pid nɔba nɛ nu'usin nɛ niŋgɔnkɔris nɛ ban pan'ami ba zut si'em la; 19nɛ tʋblɛma nɛ piena banɛ ka ba zanl nu'usin nɛ bɔbis; 20linɛ ka ba mɔri maan zut, nɛ zɔnt banɛ ka ba pid nɔba ni, nɛ piena banɛ lɔɔd siaa, nɛ tudaari nɛ tima banɛ ka ba mɔri kɛt ka dap dɔlli ba la; 21nu'ubibis baans nɛ baans banɛ ga'an nyɔnya ni la; 22fuvɛnla nɛ fubibis nɛ futitada nɛ pɔtmaannam; 23nɛ gɔtis nɛ fubanɛ lusid zug, ankitanam, nɛ la'abanɛ ka ba mɔri bɔbid la wʋsa.
24Ka li nyuugi naan malisin la, li na nyuusid pɔn'ɔsʋg;
ka ban naan lɔɔdin pien sʋma la, ba na lɔɔd nwiis banɛ gbinigbin.
Ban naan mɔrin zuobidi maan ka li vɛnl la, ba zut na an kɔɔndkɔɔndi,
ka ban naan yɛɛdin fusʋma la, ba na yɛɛd bɔto fuud.
Ba vɛnlim la na lieb nyan.
25Ba na nwɛ' tanpi kʋʋ ya dap,
ka ya zabzabidib na kpi zaba ni.
26Zion za'anɔya ni nidib na kaasidi ba yɛla,
ka tempʋʋg la na an zaalim wʋʋ pu'a na zin' sanwɛɛr nɛ.

english_text:
1When this happens, seven women will grab the same man, and each of them will say, “I'll buy my own food and clothes! Just marry me and take away my disgrace.”
The Lord Will Bless His People Who Survive
2The time is coming when the Lord will make his land fruitful and glorious again, and the people of Israel who survive will take great pride in what the land produces. 3Everyone who is left alive in Jerusalem will be called special, 4after the Lord sends a fiery judgment to clean the city and its people of their violent deeds.
5 Then the Lord will cover the whole city and its meeting places with a thick cloud each day and with a flaming fire each night. God's own glory will be like a huge tent that covers everything. 6It will provide shade from the heat of the sun and a place of shelter and protection from storms and rain.
translation_text:
1Dabisban ya'a ti paae,
pu'aba ayɔpɔi na la'asi gban'e dau yinne ka yɛl o ye,
“Ti na tʋm diisi ti mɛŋ,
ka da'adi ti mɛŋ fuudi yɛɛd.
Tinamɛ bɔɔd si'el anɛ fʋ siak ka ti buonif ye ti sid
ka li yisi ti nyan pʋʋgin
ka nidib da yɛl ye, ti kɔ'ɔŋ sidibi kulɛ.”
Zugsɔb la na maligim sʋŋi ba
2“Saŋkan la Zugsɔb na kɛ ka ya tiis la nɔbig ka vɛnl hali, ka zʋʋd na maal teŋ la zug bɛdegʋ ka Israel dim banɛ kpɛlim la na nwɛ'ɛd nyɔ'ɔg ka mɔr si'ire li zug. 3Ba na buon banɛ kpɛlim Zion nɛ Jerusalem la ye banɛ an kasi. Ban banɛ wʋsa nan kpɛn vʋe Jerusalem tempʋʋgin ka ba sɔbi ba yʋda digil la. 4Zugsɔb la na pie dian'ad linɛ ka Zion pu'ab tʋm la, ka kad saria ka vaae ziim linɛ kpa'ae Jerusalem pɔɔgin la, ka o siig la na kadi li saria ka pie li nɛ bugum. 5 Zugsɔb la na kɛ ka saŋgbauŋ linɛ nwɛnɛ nyɔ'ɔs la lus banɛ la'as Zion zuorin la nintaŋ, ka an bugum nie tisi ba yʋ'ʋŋ. Ka Wina'am na'am pipilim la na nwɛnɛ sʋk nɛ lusi ba. 6Li na mɔr ma'asim tisi ba nintaŋ, ka an suak zin'igi tisi ba saa nɛ sisi'em saŋa.”

english_text:
A Song about a Vineyard
The Lord said:
1 I will sing a song
about my friend's vineyard
that was on the side
of a fertile hill.
2My friend dug the ground,
removed the stones,
and planted the best vines.
He built a watchtower
and dug a pit in rocky ground
for pressing the grapes.
He hoped they would be sweet,
but bitter grapes
were all it produced.
3Listen, people of Jerusalem
and of Judah!
You be the judge of me
and my vineyard.
4What more could I have done
for my vineyard?
I hoped for sweet grapes,
but bitter grapes
were all that grew.
5Now I will let you know
what I am going to do.
I will cut down the hedge
and tear down the wall.
My vineyard will be trampled
and left in ruins.
6It will turn into a desert,
neither pruned nor hoed;
it will be covered
with thorns and briars.
I will command the clouds
not to send rain.
7I am the Lord All-Powerful!
Israel is the vineyard,
and Judah is the garden
I tended with care.
I had hoped for honesty
and for justice,
but dishonesty
and cries for mercy
were all I found.
Isaiah Condemns Social Injustice
8You are in for trouble! You take over house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone else in all the land. 9But the Lord All-Powerful has made this promise to me:
Those large and beautiful homes will be left empty, with no one to take care of them. 10Four hectares of grapevines will produce only 27 liters of juice, and 180 liters of seed will produce merely 18 liters of grain.
11 You are in for trouble! You get up early to start drinking, and you keep it up late into the night. 12At your drinking parties you have the music of stringed instruments, tambourines, and flutes. But you never even think about all the Lord has done, 13and so his people know nothing about him. That's why many of you will be dragged off to foreign lands. Your leaders will starve to death, and everyone else will suffer from thirst.
14The world of the dead has opened its mouth wide and is eagerly waiting for the leaders of Jerusalem and for its noisy crowds, especially for those who take pride in that city. 15Its citizens have been put down, and its proud people have been brought to shame. 16But the holy Lord God All-Powerful is praised, because he has shown who he is by bringing justice. 17His people will be like sheep grazing in their own pasture, and they will take off what was left by others.
18You are in for trouble! The lies you tell are like ropes by which you drag along sin and evil. 19And you say, “Let the holy God of Israel hurry up and do what he has promised, so we can see it for ourselves.” 20You are headed for trouble! You say wrong is right, darkness is light, and bitter is sweet.
21You think you are clever and smart. 22And you are great at drinking and mixing drinks. But you are in for trouble. 23You accept bribes to let the guilty go free, and you cheat the innocent out of a fair trial.
24You will go up in flames like straw and hay! You have rejected the teaching of the holy Lord God All-Powerful of Israel. Now your roots will rot, and your blossoms will turn to dust.
25You are the Lord's people, but you made him terribly angry, and he struck you with his mighty arm. Mountains shook, and dead bodies covered the streets like garbage. The Lord is still angry, and he is ready to strike you again.
Foreign Nations Will Attack
26The Lord has signaled for the foreign nations to come and attack you. He has already whistled, and they are coming as fast as they can. 27None of them are tired. They don't sleep or get drowsy, and they run without stumbling. Their belts don't come loose; their sandal straps don't break. 28Their arrows are sharp, and their bows are ready. The hoofs of their horses are hard as flint; the wheels of their war chariots turn as fast as a whirlwind.
29They roar and growl like fierce young lions as they grab their victims and drag them off where no one can rescue them. 30On the day they attack, they will roar like the ocean. And across the land you will see nothing but darkness and trouble, because the light of day will be covered by thick clouds.
translation_text:
Vain tiis pɔɔg yʋʋma
1“M na yʋ'ʋm tis onɛ ka m nɔŋ la;
o vain tiis pɔɔg la yɛla ka m na yʋ'ʋm ye,
‘Onɛ ka m nɔŋ la mɔr tiis pɔɔg
ka li bɛ zuokanɛ mɔr kʋ'ʋlʋm la zug.
2O tuu li ka uusi yis kuga la wʋsa,
ka gaŋ tisʋma sɛ.
O mɛ' dɔwɔk kanɛ ka ba zin' gur,
ka tu zin'ikanɛ ka ba na nwi'asid wain la,
ka bɔ tibanɛ wan walsʋma,
amaa ka ba lɛɛ wan walbɛ'ɛdnam.
3Nannanna, yanam banɛ bɛ Jerusalem nɛ Juda,
kadimi mam nɛ m vain tiis pɔɔg la saria.
4Bɔ ka m naan maalinɛ m tiis pɔɔgin la
gat mam maal si'el la?
Man daa tɛn'ɛs ye li na wal walsʋma la,
li niŋ wala wan walbɛ'ɛdnam ma'aanɛ?
5Nannanna, m na yɛli ya mam na niŋi m pɔɔg la si'em;
m na yis linɛ ka m maali gu' li lɛbis la
ka kɛ ka li san'am.
M na nwa'ae li zaŋguom la
ka bʋnkɔnbid kpɛn' nɔɔ li.
6M na bas ka mɔɔg yi li pʋʋgin.
M kʋ pɛsi li maal sʋ'ʋŋa
bɛɛ m kua pɔɔg la,
ka na kɛ ka tutubɛ'ɛd nɛ gɔn'ɔs tiis yii ani.
M mɛ na yɛl saŋgbana la
ye ba da kɛ ka saa ni anina.’
7Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pɔɔg anɛ Israel,
ka Juda dim nwɛnɛ o lɔmbɔn'ɔg nɛ.
O bɔɔdi sida
amaa on nyɛt si'el anɛ ninkʋʋr ma'aa,
O ieedi pʋpielim nɛ sumalisim
amaa o lɛɛ wʋmnɛ banɛ namisid la kaasig nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ ma'aa.”
Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sa'alʋg
8Tɔɔg bɛ yanam banɛ ɛɛnti mɛ' yir
ka lɛn tɔlisi mɛ' yisi'a,
ka ɛɛnti kua pɔɔg ka lɛn tɔlisi kua pɔsi'a,
ka teŋ la wʋsa liebi ya sʋ'ʋlim
ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn nyɛ paalʋʋ mɛ' bɛɛ kua la,
ka ya yʋ'ʋn bɛɛ ya kɔn'ɔkɔn' teŋ la zugin.
9Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian' ya ka m wʋm. O yɛl ye,
“Sida, ya' titada la na lieb dabɔɔd
ka ya' vɛnla la na zi'e ka sɔ' kʋ kpɛn' li pʋʋginɛ.
10Vain tiis pɔɔd piiga linɛ ka ba sɛ la,
ba na nwiak daam pɛ'ɛl danyʋʋr yinne ma'aa.
Pɔkanɛ ka ba zaŋ bʋmbʋʋda bɛdegʋ bʋd la,
ba na buni li paam bi'ela.”
11Tɔɔg na paae banɛ ɛɛnti isig bɛkɛungʋ
zɔti ieed daam zin'ig la,
nɛ banɛ ɛɛnti zin'in daamin ka yʋ'ʋŋ ti sɔbi sʋdig
ka ba nuu kʋʋl ka ba niŋgbina wʋsa lieb daam la.
12Ba ya'a la'as ye ba di,
ba kɛti ka googinam nɛ siyada nwɛ'ɛd,
ka wiis piebid,
ka galana nɛ piris nwɛ'ɛd ka daam zi'e.
Amaa ka ba ba'a kae nɛ Zugsɔbi tʋm si'el la,
ka mɛ pʋ na'asid Zugsɔb la maal si'el la.
13Dinzugɔ, m na kɛ ka ba gban'e m nidib la keŋ teŋ zʋŋ
ka ba an sankpan'asnam,
ban pʋ gban'ad yɛla gbin la zug.
Kɔ'ɔm na kʋʋ ba kpɛɛmnam la,
ka ku'onuud kʋʋ ba tadimnam la wʋsa.
14Alazug, Ayaʋg mɔri ya ya'amlɛog hali bɔɔd ye o vɔli ya,
ka ya'ae o nɔɔri gur.
Ani ka ya kpi'emnam la nɛ tadimnam la wʋsa na sig
la'an nɛ nimbanɛ maan tʋkpiidʋg ka aan m ba'akae dim la.
15Ba na ti kɛ ka ninsaalib sig teŋin,
ba na sie saalib la wʋsa;
ba na diis tita'alim sɔb nyan.
16Amaa Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la ka ba na dʋ'ʋs
o ya'a namisi ba wʋʋ din nar si'em.
Wina'am Onɛ An Kasi la na pa'al ye o sid an kasi
ka li yinɛ o pʋpielim tʋʋma ni na.
17Din saŋa, pɛ'ɛs na ɔnbid yaama anina nwɛnɛ ba yam ɔnbsir zin'ig nɛ,
ka pɛbibis mɛ na ɔnbid yaama dabɔɔdin la.
18Tɔɔg na paae yanam banɛ mɔr dama'am
ka vɛ'ɛd tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nɛ bugusim mɔri kenna,
nwɛnɛ tɛreko ka ba vɛ'ɛd nɛ nwiis la.
19Banɛ yɛt ye, “Wina'am, niŋim tɔ'ɔtɔ!
O gbirigim tʋm o tʋʋma ka ti nini nyɛ!
O kɛl ka li li'el na!
Israel Wina'am Onɛ An Kasi la
kɛl ka on gban'e si'em la nie ka ti baŋ!”
20Tɔɔg na paae banɛ buon bɛ'ɛd ye sʋ'ʋm,
ka mɛ buon sʋ'ʋm ye bɛ'ɛd la,
ka zaŋ liki buon ye nɛɛsim
ka lɛɛ buol nɛɛsim ye lik la;
hali ba buon bʋmmalisiŋ ye bʋntɔɔg,
ka lɛɛ buon bʋntɔɔg ye bʋmmalisiŋ.
21Tɔɔg na paae banɛ tɛn'ɛs ye ba mɔri ya'am,
ka nwɛ'ɛd nyɔ'ɔg ye ba mi' yɛla wʋsa la.
22Tɔɔg na paae banɛ yʋ'ʋri yi
ka li anɛ ban nuud daam bugid hali la,
nɛ banɛ pa'annɛ ba gandaalim an si'em
ka li anɛ ban gɛndigid danma kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔbi nuud la yɛla.
23Banɛ di'esid ligidi ka kɛt ka onɛ tʋm taal keŋ zaalim,
ka lɛɛ mɔŋid sida sɔb bʋʋd la.
24Dinzugɔ, nwɛnɛ bugum dit kikan'a si'em la
bɛɛ lin lɛligid mɔɔd si'em la,
ala ka ba na an wʋʋ tiis ka ba nya'a pun'oe nɛ,
ka ba mɔpuum sʋʋg nwɛnɛ uusʋg
ka sisi'em da'adi ken nɛ.
Bɔzugɔ ban ki'is Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la zi'elʋg
ka zan'as Israel dim Wina'am Onɛ An Kasi pian'ad la zug.
25Alazug ka Zugsɔb la sʋnf la'aŋ wʋʋ bugum nɛ, o nidib la yɛla,
ka o zaŋ o mɛŋ-mɛŋ nu'ugʋ nwɛ' baa digil.
O kɛ ka zuoya dammid,
ka nidib kpii yadig suoya ni nwɛnɛ sa'ad nɛ.
La'an nɛ wala, o sʋnpɛɛn la kʋ tɔɔm ka basi baa,
li nan kpɛm bɛ nɛ ba zugin.
26O na ʋk tuuta ye tɛɛns banɛ bɛ lalli la kena,
ka vʋʋli buol banɛ bɛ dunia kpikpɛmis la.
Banɛ nwa' zɔt tɔ'ɔtɔ kenna!
27Ba sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ gɛn bɛɛ tu'ugɛ,
ka sɔ' pʋ zɔɔnsim bɛɛ gbisɛ.
Ba sɔ' sɛnbidiŋ pʋ yu'as o sien
bɛɛ sɔ' ta'ada nwiis kɛnsigɛ.
28Ba piema la pʋlimnɛ
ka ba tiraad la gʋdi gur tɔɔnb.
Ba widi tafɛɛd la kpi'emnɛ nwɛnɛ sataŋ nɛ,
ka ba zaba tɛrekonam la zɔti nwɛnɛ sisi'epiliŋ nɛ.
29Ba ya'a kaas li nwɛnɛ gbigim nɛ,
ba ya'a nwa'am li nwɛnɛ gbigimbibis nɛ.
Ba nyuunnɛ wʋʋ bʋnyua na gban'e bʋnkɔnbʋgʋ
mɔri wa'ae ka sɔ' kae na faaɛn o basɛ.
30Daakan la ya'a ti paae, ba na kaasi bas Israel zug
ka li vuudi nwɛnɛ atɛuk ku'opila vuud si'em la.
Ka nid ya'a gɔs teŋgbauŋʋn la, o nyɛti lik nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ,
hali ka saŋgbana la na vɔl nɛɛsim ka li lieb zibisʋg.

english_text:
A Vision of the Lord in the Temple
1 In the year that King Uzziah died, I had a vision of the Lord. He was on his throne high above, and his robe filled the temple. 2Flaming creatures with six wings each were flying over him. They covered their faces with two of their wings and their bodies with two more. They used the other two wings for flying, 3 as they shouted,
“Holy, holy, holy,
Lord All-Powerful!
The earth is filled
with your glory.”
4 As they shouted, the doorposts of the temple shook, and the temple was filled with smoke. 5Then I cried out, “I'm doomed! Everything I say is sinful, and so are the words of everyone around me. Yet I have seen the King, the Lord All-Powerful.”
6One of the flaming creatures flew over to me with a burning coal that it had taken from the altar with a pair of metal tongs. 7It touched my lips with the hot coal and said, “This has touched your lips. Your sins are forgiven, and you are no longer guilty.”
8After this, I heard the Lord ask, “Is there anyone I can send? Will someone speak for us?”
“I'll go,” I answered. “Send me!”
9 Then the Lord told me to go and speak this message to the people:
“You will listen and listen,
but never understand.
You will look and look,
but never see.”
The Lord also said,
10“Make these people stubborn!
Make them stop up
their ears,
cover their eyes,
and fail to understand.
Don't let them turn to me
and be healed.”
11Then I asked the Lord, “How long will this last?”
The Lord answered:
Until their towns are destroyed and their houses are deserted, until their fields are empty, 12and I have sent them far away, leaving their land in ruins. 13If only a tenth of the people are left, even they will be destroyed. But just as stumps remain after trees have been cut down, some of my chosen ones will be left.
translation_text:
Azaya tʋʋma pin'ilʋg
1 Na'ab Uzia da kpi yʋʋm si'a la, m da nyɛ Zugsɔb la ka o zin' o na'am gbauŋ zug ka bɛɛ agɔl, ka o fuug la yidigi pɛ'ɛl Pʋ'ʋsim Yir la wʋsa. 2 Ka Serafnam zi'e gilig o, ka yinne wʋsa mɔr kpʋkpama ayuobʋ; ka nɔk kpʋkpama ayi' lus o nindaa, ka nɔk ayi' lus o nɔba, ka mɔr kpʋkpama ayi' mɛ ian'ad. 3Ka ba buon taaba yɛt ye,
“Kasi, kasi, kasi!
Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la anɛ kasi:
dunia la wʋsa pɛ'ɛli nɛ o na'am paŋ nɛ girima!”
4Ka ba kʋkɔya la vuud kɛ ka dɔɔg la dalamma la nɛ kugbanɛ gban'e li la dam, ka Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yir la pɛ'ɛl nɛ nyɔ'ɔs.
5Ka m kaas kuŋʋ yɛl ye, “Yɛl paae mam, m pʋn san'am naae! Bɔzugɔ, mam pian'ad anɛ bɛ'ɛd ka m mɛ la'am bɛ nɛ nimbanɛ pian'adi an bɛ'ɛd, ka m nini nyɛ Na'ab onɛ an Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la!” 6Ka Serafnam la yinne nɔk ma'adiŋe mak bugumsaan kanɛ dit maan daka la zug, ka ianki kɛɛn m san'an na, 7ka nɔki li si'isi m nɔɔr ka yɛl ye, “Nɛ'ɛŋa si'isi fʋ nɔɔr si'em la, taal kanɛ bɛɛ fʋ zugin la yi ya; ba yɔɔ fʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la wʋsa sam.” 8Ka m wʋm Zugsɔb la bu'osid ye, “Anɔ'ɔn ka m na tʋm? Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na keŋ tisi ti?” Ka m yɛl ye, “Naa, manɛ nwa': tʋmmim.” 9Ka o yɛl ye, “Kem yɛl nimbama ye,
“Ya na wʋm ka lɛn wʋm
ka kʋ gban'e li gbinnɛ.
Ya na gɔs ka lɛn gɔs
ka kʋ nyɛ si'ela.”
10Ka o lɛn yɛlim ye,
“Kɛl ka nimbama nwa' sʋnya digilim,
ka kɛ ka ba tʋba ziank nɛ wʋm,
ka kɛ ka ba zu'om ka kʋ nyɛɛ.
Ya'a ka' ala ba naan nyɛɛn nɛ ba nini,
ka wʋmin nɛ ba tʋba,
ka baŋin nɛ ba pʋtɛnda,
ka tiaki lɛbi m san'an na ka m ti'ebi ba.”
11Ka m bu'os o ye, “M Zugsɔba, li na yuugi paae wala?” Ka o lɛbis ye,
“Asɛɛ tempʋʋd la ti lieb dabɔɔd,
ka nidib lɛn kae,
ka ya' la zi'e zaalim,
ka pɔɔd la san'am yɔɔg-yɔɔg.
12Asɛɛ Zugsɔb la ti kad nidibi naae
ka ba lalig ka bas teŋ la nyain.
13Baa nidib piiga pʋʋgin yinne ya'a kpɛlim teŋin la,
bugum na di teŋ la san'ami li.
Amaa nwɛnɛ tiig ka ba ɛɛnti nwaae
ka li gbi'ir kpɛlim si'em la,
ala mɛn ka bielim banɛ an kasi la na kpɛlim teŋin wʋʋ gbi'ir nɛ.”

english_text:
Isaiah Offers Hope to King Ahaz
1 Ahaz, the son of Jotham and the grandson of Uzziah, was king of Judah when King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah son of Remaliah of Israel went to attack Jerusalem. But they were not able to do what they had planned. 2When news reached the royal palace that Syria had joined forces with Israel, King Ahaz and everyone in Judah were so terrified that they shook like trees in a windstorm.
3Then the Lord said to me:
Take your son Shearjashub and go see King Ahaz. You will find him on the road near the cloth makers' shops at the end of the canal that brings water from the upper pool. 4Tell Ahaz to stop worrying. There's no need for him to be afraid of King Rezin and King Pekah. They are very angry, but they are nothing more than a dying fire. Ahaz doesn't need to fear 5their evil threats 6to invade and defeat Judah and Jerusalem and to let the son of Tabeel be king in his place.
7I, the Lord, promise that this will never happen. 8-9Damascus is just the capital of Syria, and King Rezin rules only in Damascus. Samaria is just the capital of Israel, and King Pekah rules only in Samaria. But in less than 65 years, Israel will be destroyed. And if Ahaz and his officials don't trust me, they will be defeated.
A Son Named Immanuel
10Once again the Lord God spoke to King Ahaz. This time he said, 11“Ask me for proof that my promise will come true. Ask for something to happen deep in the world of the dead or high in the heavens above.”
12“No, Lord,” Ahaz answered. “I won't test you!”
13Then I said:
Listen, every one of you in the royal family of David. You have already tried my patience. Now you are trying God's patience by refusing to ask for proof. 14 But the Lord will still give you proof. A virgin is pregnant; she will have a son and will name him Immanuel. 15-16Even before the boy is old enough to know how to choose between right and wrong, he will eat yogurt and honey, and the countries of the two kings you fear will be destroyed. 17But the Lord will make more trouble for your people and your kingdom than any of you have known since Israel broke away from Judah. He will even bring the king of Assyria to attack you.
The Threat of an Invasion
18When that time comes, the Lord will whistle, and armies will come from Egypt like flies and from Assyria like bees. 19They will settle everywhere—in the deep valleys and between the rocks, on every thornbush and all over the pastureland.
20The Lord will pay the king of Assyria to bring a razor from across the Euphrates River and shave your head and every hair on your body, including your beard.
21Anyone who is able to save only one young cow and two sheep, 22will have enough milk to make yogurt. In fact, everyone left in the land will eat yogurt and honey.
23Vineyards that had 1,000 vines and were worth 1,000 pieces of silver will turn into thorn patches. 24You will go there to hunt with your bow and arrows, because the whole country will be covered with thornbushes. 25The hills where you once planted crops will be overgrown with thorns and thistles. You will be afraid to go there, and your cattle, sheep, and goats will be turned loose on those hills.
translation_text:
Azaya n mɔr labaar na tis na'ab Ahaz la yɛla
1Ahaz onɛ da an Na'ab Jotam biig ka o yaab an Na'ab Uzia la da di na'am Juda sʋ'ʋlimin saŋsi'a la, Aram na'ab Rezin nɛ Remalaya onɛ an Israel na'ab la biig Peka da duoe keŋ ye ba zab nɛ Jerusalem teŋ dim, amaa ka da pʋ nyaŋi baa. 2Ba da yɛl David yidim banɛ an na'am tuŋ dim la ye, “Aram dim la la'as nɛ Efiram dimi naal nɔɔr”; ka Ahaz nɛ o nidib la wʋsa ya'am iank, ka ba susʋnya dammid wʋʋ sisi'em na da'ad tiis vaand ka li dammid si'em la.
3Ani ka Zugsɔb la yɛl Azaya ye, “Fʋn nɛ fʋ biig Sear-Jasuob yim keŋ tʋ'ʋs Na'ab Ahaz, ka o bɛ ku'osuokanɛ ka ku'om naanid bɛuŋ kanɛ bɛ zugin la pʋbidi dɔl la naarin.
